quote: Risks to patient safety or observed instances of harm (including indirect harm) are reported at a predetermined frequency to the developer and implementer organizations.
hazard: Harms not communicated to responsible parties

statement: Maintain processes to manage risk arising from changes to the AI system, environment, and data.
quote: There should be processes to manage risk arising from changes to the system, environment, and data.
hazard: Harms from unmanaged system or data changes

statement: Track serious adverse events from AI use separately from adverse events and in a timely fashion.
quote: Serious adverse events (SAEs) resulting from AI system use should be tracked, separately from adverse events (AEs), and in a timely fashion.
hazard: Serious AI-related harms delayed or obscured

statement: Define an organization-level standard definition of AI-related serious adverse events.
quote: In lieu of that, a common standard definition at the health AI solution level SAEs and at the implementer team’s organization level is key, as the latter are where the clinical risk is defined within the workflow.
hazard: Inconsistent classification of AI harms

statement: Maintain plans for sunsetting the AI system, triggering a back-up plan, and initiating a safety investigation.
quote: Determine if there are plans in place for sunsetting the AI system if needed (and triggering a back-up plan) and initiating a safety investigation.
hazard: No fallback when AI must be withdrawn

statement: Describe automation bias and mitigation strategies in the risk management plan, training materials, and interface instructions.
quote: Identify whether the potential for automation bias is described in the risk management plan, training materials, and/or interface use instructions, along with mitigation strategies.
hazard: Clinicians over-relying on incorrect AI output

statement: Measure automation bias as part of risk assessment, including whether incorrect AI output can be detected.
quote: Assess whether it is possible to measure automation bias, and if such measurement is included in the risk assessment process (for example, determining whether the incorrect AI system output can be detected and how it may have potential impact on subsequent decision making).
hazard: Undetected over-reliance on erroneous output

statement: Define how safety issues are reported to the developer, regulators, and other customers in a timely manner.
quote: The implementer team should clarify how these issues are reported to the developer team so that the responsible organization, the FDA/other relevant agencies, and all customers using the AI solution so notified in a timely manner.
hazard: Safety issues not propagated to other sites

statement: Define recall/correction procedures and a threshold for reporting potential patient harm.
quote: The team should also determine how recalls/corrections will happen and assess whether there is a defined threshold for reporting potential patient harm and processes in place to report on it.
hazard: Delayed response to harmful AI behavior

statement: Conduct qualitative and quantitative user acceptance testing and capture human factors in harm assessment during pilot.
quote: This step includes determining whether user acceptance testing is both qualitative and quantitative, as well as whether human factors are captured as part of the assessment of harm during the pilot deployment of the AI solution.
hazard: Human-factors harms missed during pilot

statement: Establish a process to identify incorrect or outdated AI knowledge and determine when a newer system should replace it.
quote: In addition, note whether there is a process to identify incorrect “knowledge” and to determine when a newer AI system should be used.
hazard: Outdated or medically obsolete AI output

statement: Develop and distribute training resources on AI functionality and limitations to end users during small-scale implementation.
quote: Determine whether educational resources and/or training courses have been developed and distributed to inform end users about functionality and limitations of the AI solution.
hazard: Users unaware of AI limitations

statement: Designate a point-person to champion AI training, implementation, and follow-up.
quote: In addition, note whether a particular “point-person” will champion training, implementation and follow-up.
hazard: No accountable owner for training and follow-up

statement: Establish a process for end users to identify and report unforeseen, unintended, or adverse outcomes of AI use.
quote: Note whether a process has been established so that key stakeholders/end users can identify and report any unforeseen, unintended, negative, and/or adverse outcomes and whether a process exists for determining whether such outcomes have been sufficiently assessed during the pilot.
hazard: Adverse outcomes go unreported

statement: Define and legally vet accountability for AI-assisted decision-making and establish a post-deployment monitoring strategy.
quote: Finally, determine whether accountability for decision-making has been defined and legally vetted and a post-deployment monitoring strategy established.
hazard: Unclear liability and unmonitored deployment

statement: Assess user experience with AI output through focus groups or surveys and implement user feedback.
quote: Determine whether user experience and interactions with AI solution output have been assessed (through focus groups, surveys, follow up studies, research, etc.) and note whether there is a process to collect, assess and implement user feedback.
hazard: Poor user experience left unaddressed

statement: Implement continuous monitoring and reporting of AI performance for subpopulations, especially vulnerable ones.
quote: Determine whether continuous monitoring and reporting processes are in place for subpopulations, especially vulnerable ones.
hazard: Undetected harm to vulnerable groups

statement: Detect and document model drift with a response plan for safety, efficacy, and ethical issues.
quote: Clarify whether it is possible to detect and document AI model drift to ensure that any potential safety, efficacy, and ethical issues are addressed through a response plan.
hazard: Performance degradation over time

statement: Document the AI solution's limitations and make them accessible to end users and patients.
quote: In addition, clarify whether the AI solution’s limitations have been documented and whether that information is accessible to end users and/or patients.
hazard: Users and patients unaware of AI limitations

statement: Perform a privacy risk assessment on AI systems to understand stakeholder privacy preferences.
quote: Determine whether the implementer organization has performed a privacy risk assessment (or similar exercise) on AI systems to understand stakeholder privacy preferences.
hazard: AI use conflicting with stakeholder privacy expectations

statement: Review AI system audit log records and ensure logs capture only the minimum data needed.
quote: In addition, note whether the implementer organization reviews AI system audit log records, and clarify whether audit log processes capture only the minimum of data needed.
hazard: Unreviewed logs and excessive data retention

statement: Formally record changes to the AI deployment environment, traceable to an owner.
quote: Determine whether the organization formally records and stores changes to the AI solution’s deployment environment. Clarify whether configuration change records, including details of the change, can be traced to the owner.
hazard: Untracked configuration changes causing harm

statement: Develop, document, and regularly update an incident response plan for the AI system.
quote: Determine if the implementer organization has developed and documented an incident response plan that is updated with appropriate frequency.
hazard: Uncoordinated response to AI incidents

statement: Document and test a contingency plan for critical AI services and train personnel on their responsibilities.
quote: For this step, determine whether the implementer organization has documented a contingency plan for critical AI services, and if so, whether the organization has trained personnel on contingency plan implementation responsibilities. In addition, ascertain whether the organization's records document that the contingency plan has been tested.
hazard: Service disruption when critical AI fails

statement: Evaluate privacy and security risks to both individuals and the organization in the AI risk management strategy.
quote: For this step, note whether relevant staff have been interviewed to determine security and privacy risks and clarify whether the risk management strategy includes evaluating risks to both individuals and to the organization.
hazard: Overlooked privacy risks to individuals

statement: Conduct end-user testing and documentation of risk levels across specific query types for LLM tools.
quote: The varying levels of risk associated with the tool’s use should be considered based on specific queries or intended use, necessitating end -user testing and documentation, which may burden clinicians.
hazard: Unrecognized high-risk query types

statement: Configure LLM retrieval tools to always display the source content supporting each AI response.
quote: Mitigating hallucination (confabulation) is relatively straightforward a nd is addressed by the system, as it always provides the actual content supporting the AI response.
hazard: Undetectable hallucinated content

statement: Instruct clinicians to use additional safety measures to confirm absence of critical data (e.g., severe allergies) not retrieved by the LLM.
quote: Instructions to clinicians should account for this risk, advising them to use additional safety measures to confirm the absence of critical data, such as a severe allergy to an antibiotic.
hazard: Missed critical information from retrieval false negatives

statement: Monitor whether users ignore or develop workarounds to the AI solution and whether it hinders patient-clinician interaction.
quote: In addition, evaluate whether users are ignoring or developing workarounds to deal with the solution, as well as whether the solution hinders patient-clinician interaction.
hazard: Unsafe workarounds and degraded patient-clinician interaction

statement: Maintain a feedback loop with triage for detecting AI issues and defects after deployment.
quote: For this step, note whether there is a feedback loop for consistent detection of issues and defects, including a triage process to facilitate continuous improvement and monitoring.
hazard: Defects persist undetected

statement: Maintain a governance plan documenting responsibilities for deployed AI solutions.
quote: Also note whether there is a governance plan and documentation of responsibilities, and clarify whether the needs of accountable users are supported.
hazard: Unclear ownership of deployed AI

statement: Solicit end-user feedback and use it to continuously refine the AI solution.
quote: Determine whether end user feedback has been solicited, considered, and used to continuously refine the AI solution.
hazard: Known issues not incorporated into improvements

statement: Give users access to transparency and safety information such as model cards.
quote: In addition, determine whether users have access to relevant transparency and safety information (e.g., Model Cards).
hazard: Users lack information to calibrate trust

statement: Define clear inclusion/exclusion criteria for use of the AI solution.
quote: Determine whether there are clear inclusion/exclusion criteria for use of the AI solution.
hazard: Use outside intended scope

statement: Evaluate whether the AI solution is more or less useful for specific patient populations.
quote: The team should also evaluate whether the solution is more or less useful for certain patient populations (e.g., pregnant women, low-risk patients, patients over age 50).
hazard: Poor performance for specific populations

statement: Monitor data drift in inputs, outputs, and outcomes across the entire deployment population.
quote: Determine whether data drift (inputs, outputs, and outcomes) in the AI system – along with impact on performance and clinical outcomes – will be monitored over the entire deployment population.
hazard: Undetected drift degrading outputs

statement: Put monitoring protocols in place for relevant sociodemographic subgroups.
quote: In addition, evaluate whether monitoring protocols are in place for relevant sociodemographic subgroups in order to minimize unfair or systemic impacts.
hazard: Unfair systemic impacts on subgroups

statement: Identify qualified persons responsible for monitoring AI bias and fairness, with access to relevant advisers.
quote: It is important to identify the parties responsible for data monitoring and note whether they are qualified for those tasks.
hazard: Bias monitoring without qualified ownership

statement: Provide automatic, easy-to-interpret drift notifications to responsible individuals on an ongoing basis.
quote: Note whether automatic, easy-to-interpret notifications are provided to signal model drift on an ongoing basis to responsible individuals.
hazard: Drift noticed too late

statement: Monitor AI system data drift in inputs, outputs, and outcomes, and its impact on performance and clinical outcomes, across the entire deployment population.
quote: whether data drift (inputs, outputs, and outcomes) in the AI system – along with impact on performance and clinical outcomes – will be monitored over the entire deployment population.
hazard: Undetected performance degradation harming patients after deployment

statement: Establish monitoring protocols for AI performance within relevant sociodemographic subgroups.
quote: In addition, evaluate whether monitoring protocols are in place for relevant sociodemographic subgroups in order to minimize unfair or systemic impacts.
hazard: Unfair or systemic impacts on specific subgroups going unnoticed

statement: Define technical criteria for 'significant' drift and document the justification for those criteria.
quote: Finally, ascertain whether there are technical definitions for “significant” drift along with adequate justification for those definitions.
hazard: Inconsistent or arbitrary judgments about when drift requires action

statement: Set the significant-drift criterion so drift is detected before it affects many people.
quote: Assess whether the criterion defining “significant model drift” allows it to be detected before it impacts many people.
hazard: Drift detected too late, after widespread patient harm

statement: Designate qualified persons responsible for monitoring bias and fairness of the AI solution.
quote: It is important to identify the parties responsible for data monitoring and note whether they are qualified for those tasks.
hazard: No accountable, competent owner for bias and fairness monitoring

statement: Ensure monitoring staff can access social, ethical, legal, human factors, and clinical advisers when specific problems arise.
quote: This includes verifying that responsible parties are able to access relevant social, ethical, legal, human factors and/or clinical stakeholders/advisers in the event that specific problems arise.
hazard: Monitoring problems unresolved due to lacking expert input

statement: Provide automatic, easy-to-interpret ongoing drift notifications to responsible individuals.
quote: Note whether automatic, easy-to-interpret notifications are provided to signal model drift on an ongoing basis to responsible individuals.
hazard: Drift unnoticed by responsible staff

statement: If drift is evaluated manually, define and justify specific evaluation time intervals.
quote: If not, and if model performance drift must be manually evaluated, determine whether specific time intervals have been defined, along with adequate justification.
hazard: Irregular manual checks missing performance degradation

statement: Define timescales for routinely evaluating AI system fairness and bias.
quote: Determine whether the AI system will be monitored to identify drift or bias and note timescales used to routinely evaluate AI system fairness.
hazard: Emerging bias undetected due to no routine fairness review

statement: Routinely monitor data and model security on a defined, justified schedule of security checks.
quote: Also note whether data and model security are routinely monitored, and whether the timescales and frequency of security checks have been defined and adequately justified.
hazard: Security compromise of data or model going undetected

statement: Provide a clearly defined, easy-to-access channel, independent of business interests, for affected individuals to give feedback or seek guidance after adverse events.
quote: In case of an adverse event or large-scale issue, determine whether there is a clearly defined, unbiased (to business interests), and easy-to-access 60 way that affected individuals or groups can provide feedback or seek guidance, and whether these processes are consistent with state and federal policies.
hazard: Harmed patients lacking recourse or guidance after AI-related incidents

statement: Offer patients a timely way to report satisfaction with AI-assisted care that is equally accessible to all subgroups.
quote: In addition, determine whether there is a way for impacted individuals to provide timely feedback about whether they were satisfied with the care/service that was provided with input from an AI solution, and whether it is equally accessible to all relevant subgroups.
hazard: Patient experience problems with AI-assisted care going unreported

statement: Assess whether any groups are systematically excluded from giving feedback due to language barriers, disability, or access factors.
quote: Finally, evaluate whether there are some individuals or groups who are systematically excluded from giving feedback due to language barriers or factors related to ability or access.
hazard: Feedback systems silencing limited-English or disabled patients

statement: Identify long-term risks, overall and by subgroup, that could not be measured in the pilot and measure them post-deployment.
quote: Identify whether there are long-term risks associated with the AI system or its performance (whether overall or by subgroup) that could not be measured during small-scale implementation, but that could be measured post-deployment.
hazard: Risks invisible in small pilots emerging at scale

statement: Define and justify criteria for significant performance shifts within subgroups and for parity gaps between subgroups.
quote: Determine whether specific criteria are defined for how "significant" shifts in model performance within subgroups (if differing from overall population due to sample size/error), or in parity between subgroups, should be defined, with adequate justification for the choice of criteria.
hazard: Growing disparities between subgroups not flagged

statement: Identify accountable parties for data or AI system breaches and performance drift, whether the solution is vendor-purchased or internally developed.
quote: Regardless of whether an AI solution is purchased from a third-party vendor or developed internally, determine whether accountable parties for data/AI system breaches have been identified.
hazard: Unclear responsibility when breaches or drift cause harm

statement: Evaluate whether AI performance varies by deployment site or deployment context before and during full rollout.
quote: Determine whether AI system performance varies as a function of deployment site (rural vs. urban, community clinic vs. academic medical center, etc.) or deployment context (type of device or source of device/assay for specific input data, type of population most seen, etc.).
hazard: Tool performing poorly at sites unlike the pilot setting

statement: Assess whether data quality differs across deployment sites and affects AI performance.
quote: Also assess whether data quality differs across various deployment sites and whether it affects the solution’s performance.
hazard: Poor local data quality degrading AI outputs

statement: Assess whether data quality issues affect monitoring or AI performance in some subgroups more than others.
quote: In addition, determine whether issues related to data quality affect AI system performance monitoring efforts or AI system performance in some subgroups more than others.
hazard: Uneven data quality producing hidden subgroup harms

statement: Reassess at full deployment whether end users act on AI output alone or combine it with other information.
quote: The team should once again assess whether end users will use output from the AI solution on its own to arrive at a decision or if that input will be used in tandem with other information.
hazard: Unchecked sole reliance on AI output in decisions

statement: Clearly define when end users can or must override AI outputs, and the impacts of overrides, in the full deployment context.
quote: Also, determine whether the end user is able or required to override an AI system decision and evaluate whether the specific conditions for such an override, along with its potential impacts, 61 have been defined clearly in the full deployment context.
hazard: Clinicians unable or unsure how to override erroneous AI output

statement: Assess pilot-to-deployment differences such as less time, more heterogeneous populations, or greater patient flow that alter human-AI decision processes.
quote: In addition, determine whether there are differences in the pilot and deployment setting/processes that could alter how shared or automated decision-processes affect fairness and/or bias (e.g., is there less time? Is the population more heterogeneous? Is the patient flow greater?).
hazard: Oversight eroding under real-world time and volume pressures

statement: Provide an accessible, easy-to-understand way for patients to know that AI contributed to their treatment.
quote: Determine whether there is an accessible, easy-tounderstand way for affected groups to know that part of their treatment was determined by an AI solution and also note whether providing this information could increase the risk of harm or reduce the potential benefit.
hazard: Patients unaware AI shaped their care

statement: Consult human factors or behavioral science experts on how to present AI-use disclosures to patients.
quote: In addition, ascertain whether human factors or behavioral science experts have been consulted to determine how to present this information in a way that improves trust and patient agency.
hazard: Disclosures that confuse patients or undermine trust and agency

statement: Enable end users to give timely feedback on AI performance, accuracy, and operational challenges.
quote: Determine whether end users or implementers can provide timely feedback about AI system performance, accuracy, or operational challenges that could increase harm or reduce benefit.
hazard: Frontline-observed errors not reaching those who can fix them

statement: Design end-user feedback mechanisms to be simple, informative, and quick to access and complete.
quote: In addition, assess whether feedback strategies are simple, informative, easy, and quick to access and complete, and whether feedback is reviewed in a timely manner (thereby preventing any existing issues from escalating/causing harm).
hazard: Burdensome feedback processes suppressing error reporting

statement: Review submitted end-user feedback in a timely manner to prevent issues from escalating.
quote: In addition, assess whether feedback strategies are simple, informative, easy, and quick to access and complete, and whether feedback is reviewed in a timely manner (thereby preventing any existing issues from escalating/causing harm).
hazard: Reported issues escalating into harm while unreviewed

statement: Report patient safety risks and observed harms, including indirect harm, at a predetermined frequency through local governance to developer and implementer organizations.
quote: Similar to Stage 5, risks to patient safety or observed instances of harm (including indirect harm) should be reported at a predetermined frequency to the developer and implementer organizations through a local governance process.
hazard: Safety issues not communicated to parties who can correct them

statement: Establish a process to report harms to the developer team, whether internal or external.
quote: A process should be established to report harms to the developer team, whether internal or external to the implementer organization, and the development team can share potential issues and expected risks and how those can be managed.
hazard: Developers unaware of harms occurring in deployment

statement: Monitor trends and patterns in safety events for each AI solution.
quote: Trends and pattern detection of safety events for a given solution should be monitored.
hazard: Recurring safety problems missed when events viewed individually

statement: Establish safety thresholds that determine whether an AI solution continues operating, is refined, or is sunsetted.
quote: If there are safety issues and/or poor outcomes, thresholds should be established to decide whether the Al solution should continue to operate, needs to be refined, or whether it should be sunsetted.
hazard: Unsafe AI tools remaining in use without decision criteria

statement: Maintain processes to manage risk arising from changes to AI system architecture, code, environment, and data.
quote: The implementer team should be aware of any effect that changes to architecture and code have to the level of risk, and there should be processes in place to manage risk arising from changes to system, environment, and data.
hazard: System or data changes silently introducing safety risk

statement: Design AI deployments to keep a human in the loop who can contest or override AI output.
quote: Finally, when possible, ensure that the AI solution is designed to keep a human in the loop to contest or override its output.
hazard: Erroneous AI outputs acted upon without human check

statement: Where human-in-the-loop review is infeasible, implement quality control processes to assess AI accuracy and safety.
quote: When this is not possible, quality control processes can be implemented to assess accuracy and safety.
hazard: Unreviewed automated outputs containing errors

statement: Monitor continuously for AI safety risks using clear thresholds for detecting safety issues.
quote: For this step, monitor continuously for safety risks and their frequently, adhering to clear thresholds for detecting safety issues.
hazard: Safety issues undetected between periodic reviews

statement: Report and mitigate adverse and serious adverse events consistently, classifying safety risks by severity and frequency.
quote: Adverse events, including serious adverse events, should be reported and mitigated consistently, while classifying safety risks by severity and frequency.
hazard: Inconsistent response to AI-related adverse events

statement: Track AI-related adverse events and serious adverse events separately using the organization's standard definitions.
quote: From a reporting perspective, when applicable, assess whether there is compliance with the organization’s standard for “adverse event” and “serious adverse event, ” and whether these are tracked separately and mitigated consistently.
hazard: Serious events obscured within general adverse event data

statement: Plan for sunsetting the AI solution with a back-up plan and a process to initiate a safety investigation.
quote: Finally, determine whether there are plans for sunsetting the AI solution (triggering a back-up plan) and initiating a safety investigation.
hazard: Care disruption when an unsafe AI tool must be withdrawn

statement: Review at frequent intervals whether the AI solution has become outdated or no longer medically relevant.
quote: At frequent intervals throughout its deployment, review whether the AI solution has become outdated or no longer medically relevant [49], [77].
hazard: Outdated AI providing obsolete clinical information

statement: Establish processes to identify incorrect or out-of-date knowledge or recommendations produced by the AI solution.
quote: In addition, clarify whether there are processes to identify incorrect or out-of-date knowledge/recommendations and to determine when a newer AI system should be used.
hazard: AI outputs based on obsolete or incorrect medical knowledge

statement: Maintain processes for exploring whether better AI solutions exist for given tasks.
quote: Also, note whether there are processes for exploring whether there are better AI solutions for given tasks.
hazard: Continued use of inferior tools when safer alternatives exist

statement: Maintain reporting and recall procedures to promptly notify developers, relevant agencies, and all users of discovered safety concerns.
quote: Maintain robust reporting and recall procedures for promptly notifying developer organizations, relevant agencies, and all users when safety concerns are discovered during implementation at multiple organizations [95], [126].
hazard: Known safety flaws continuing to harm patients at other sites

statement: Define a process and threshold for reporting potential patient harm and managing recalls or corrections.
quote: In addition, identify how recalls/corrections will be managed and ascertain whether there is a defined process and threshold for reporting potential patient harm.
hazard: Ad hoc, delayed reporting of potential patient harm

statement: Establish a process for developers to share recalls and corrections with implementer teams.
quote: Also, if safety concerns meet the defined risk threshold at one system, triggering a delay and reevaluation, clarify whether this will be shared with the developer team and regulators, and determine whether there is a process in place for developer teams to share recalls and corrections with implementer teams.
hazard: Implementers unaware of vendor recalls or fixes

statement: Implement access controls with an audit trail allowing an independent reviewer to determine who can access the AI interface.
quote: For this reason, the team should assess whether there are proper access controls in place for the AI solution, 63 including an audit trail that will allow an independent reviewer to determine who can access the interface.
hazard: Unauthorized access to AI tools and patient data

statement: Maintain an audit trail showing how decisions were made based on AI output.
quote: In addition, determine whether there is an audit trail that can determine how decisions are made based on the AI solution’s output.
hazard: Inability to trace AI influence on harmful decisions

statement: Enable end users and stakeholders to report off-label or unintended uses of the AI solution to local leadership.
quote: Determine whether there is a process to assess and report outcomes for unindicated or “off label” uses of AI solutions, as well as whether end users or other stakeholders are able to report such uses to local leadership.
hazard: Unvalidated uses of AI causing unrecognized harm

statement: Conduct intermittent audits comparing actual AI use against its intended purpose.
quote: In addition, ascertain whether there are intermittent audits of how the AI solution is used vs. its intended purpose.
hazard: Scope creep into unintended, unsafe applications

statement: Maintain an impact analysis plan for any AI solution changes, including planned software updates.
quote: Note whether an impact analysis plan is in place for any AI solution changes (e.g., for planned software updates), so that safety, effectiveness, and performance are not compromised.
hazard: Updates degrading safety or performance unnoticed

statement: Test all environment, application, and model updates to the AI solution before use.
quote: Also assess whether there is a process to ensure that all environment, application, and model updates to the AI solution are appropriately tested.
hazard: Untested model or software updates introducing errors

statement: Document AI version changes and the impact testing of each version change.
quote: Finally, determine whether version changes (and impact testing of version changes) are documented.
hazard: Inability to trace problems to specific model versions

statement: Measure the potential for automation bias, including whether users can detect incorrect AI output, as part of risk management.
quote: For this reason, it is important to determine whether the potential for automation bias is measured for risk assessment and management purposes (for example, determining whether the incorrect AI system output can be detected and how it may have potential impact on subsequent decision making).
hazard: Clinicians over-relying on incorrect AI suggestions

statement: Disclose AI limitations, contraindications, accuracy, error rates, generalizability, and clinical implications to users.
quote: Determine whether limitations, contraindications, accuracy, error rates, generalizability, robustness, reproducibility, clinical implications, and interpretation of results from the AI solution have been disclosed.
hazard: Users unaware of AI limitations and error rates

statement: Provide clinicians or end users an explanation of why the AI made or suggested a particular decision.
quote: Evaluate whether the implementer team incorporates an explanation to the clinician or end user regarding the reason(s) the solution made or suggested a particular decision.
hazard: Users unable to evaluate opaque AI recommendations

statement: Make it clear to end users that they are interacting with an AI system.
quote: In addition, determine whether the developer team incorporates a method (e.g., Model Cards) to make it clear to end users that they are interacting with an AI system.
hazard: Users mistaking AI output for human communication

statement: Label the AI system with a plain-language explanation of its development, intended purpose, limitations, safety risks, and underrepresented subpopulations.
quote: Assess whether the AI system is labeled with a plainlanguage explanation of how the AI model was developed, its intended purpose, and its limitations and safety risks (e.g., type of model, description of dataset used to create the model, results from clinical studies, and which subpopulations were underrepresented in the training and test sets).
hazard: Misuse due to misunderstanding of AI purpose and limits

statement: Establish a process to update transparency information with newly discovered limitations from local deployment.
quote: Along with that, there should be a process for updating information based on newly discovered limitations of local deployment in the implementer environment.
hazard: Users relying on outdated limitation information

statement: Monitor and sunset unsupported AI algorithms and plan for developer-driven end-of-life processes.
quote: It is important to clarify whether the implementer team’s organization monitors and sunsets AI algorithms that are no longer supported and assess whether there is a plan for handling developer-driven EOL processes.
hazard: Unsupported, unpatched AI remaining in clinical use

statement: Maintain an end-of-life plan for patient data migration and archival and for supporting end users after AI retirement.
quote: It is also important to have an EOL plan for patient data, data migration, archival, etc. and clarify whether end users will receive support in the AI solution’s absence (e.g., contact information, onboarding to a new solution, etc.).
hazard: Patient data loss or exposure when AI is retired

statement: For vendor-purchased AI, apply quality control techniques or technical standards supporting supply chain risk management, including how safety risks are reported.
quote: For solutions purchased from third-party vendors, the implementer team should engage in quality control techniques and/or technical standards to support the developer’s supply chain risk management that include describing how safety risks should be reported.
hazard: Unmanaged supply chain risks in vendor AI

statement: Require vendors to provide a clear list of key AI risks identified, addressed, and mitigated across the supply chain or other organizations.
quote: In addition, the team should ascertain whether the developer has provided a clear list regarding key AI system-related risks that have been identified, addressed, and mitigated across the supply chain or in other organizations.
hazard: Implementers unaware of known vendor AI risks

statement: Conduct and report a preliminary study of AI solution effectiveness to end users and stakeholders.
quote: Assess whether a preliminary study of AI solution effectiveness has been conducted and reported.
hazard: Deploying AI without evidence of real-world benefit

statement: Measure user understanding by checking whether actions taken in response to AI output are consistent with its defined limitations and intended use.
quote: Consider whether understanding of end users and key stakeholders can be measured by examining actions taken in 65 response to the AI solution and verifying the consistency of those actions against the defined limitations and intended use of the AI solution.
hazard: Users acting on AI beyond its intended use

statement: Establish a defined level of patient awareness regarding AI use in their care.
quote: It is important to establish a defined level of patient awareness regarding the AI solution’s use as part of their care.
hazard: Inconsistent or absent patient awareness of AI use

statement: Ensure clinicians using AI can give patients a satisfactory explanation of the AI output.
quote: If the end user is a healthcare provider, they should determine whether they are able to provide a satisfactory explanation of the AI solution output to a patient.
hazard: Patients receiving unexplained AI-influenced decisions

statement: Provide a clearly defined method for patients and end users to access documentation about the AI solution.
quote: Determine whether there is a clearly defined method for patients and end users to access documentation about the AI solution and other project-related information.
hazard: Lack of access to information about AI tools

statement: Tailor AI documentation for patients versus clinicians according to expertise and health literacy levels.
quote: Also determine whether end users and patients will receive the same documentation (given various levels of expertise and health literacy).
hazard: Documentation incomprehensible to patients with limited health literacy

statement: Establish, maintain, and test incident response plans for AI solutions.
quote: Determine whether incident response plans are established, maintained, and tested according to policies for AI solutions.
hazard: Uncoordinated response to AI security or safety incidents

statement: Train AI monitoring and incident response personnel on procedures for sharing incident impacts with stakeholders.
quote: In addition, ensure that personnel responsible for AI system monitoring and incident response activities are trained on procedures to share incident impacts with stakeholders.
hazard: Poor incident communication to affected stakeholders

statement: Assign personnel responsibility for reviewing, analyzing, and reporting incident impacts on the AI solution to stakeholders.
quote: Finally, assess whether personnel are responsible for reviewing, analyzing, and reporting incident impacts on the AI solution to stakeholders.
hazard: Incidents unanalyzed and unreported due to no owner

statement: Maintain a process aligned with legal and regulatory requirements to notify external stakeholders of AI cybersecurity incidents or privacy events.
quote: Determine whether a process aligned with legal, contractual, and regulatory requirements is in place to communicate to external stakeholders about cybersecurity incidents or privacy events.
hazard: Affected individuals not notified of data breaches

statement: Schedule privacy risk evaluations of the AI system environment at an agreed interval, such as quarterly or annually.
quote: Determine whether the implementer organization schedules privacy risk evaluations of its AI system environment according to an agreed upon interval (i.e., quarterly, annually, etc.).
hazard: Evolving privacy risks going unassessed

statement: Establish policies and processes for communicating progress on legal compliance and privacy risk management.
quote: Assess whether the implementer organization has established policies and processes for communicating progress on compliance with legal requirements and managing privacy risk.
hazard: Noncompliance with privacy law going unaddressed

statement: Maintain clear plans for updating and maintaining generative AI systems such as EHR query tools.
quote: Clear plans for updating and maintaining the AI system are crucial to ensure its ongoing effectiveness and security.
hazard: Generative AI degrading in effectiveness or security over time

statement: Establish a system to collect and incorporate user feedback on generative AI tools in real time.
quote: Establishing a system for collecting and incorporating user feedback in real-time can aid in continuously improving usefulness, transparency, and identifying safety risks.
hazard: Generative AI safety risks unidentified without user input

statement: Consider dynamic consent mechanisms letting patients adjust consent to data use by generative AI over time.
quote: Dynamic consent mechanisms, allowing patients to adjust their consent regarding data use over time and with emerging technologies or uses, can be considered as well.
hazard: Patient data used in new AI applications without current consent

statement: Continuously check and define update frequency for knowledge sources such as trials, indications, and guidelines powering the AI system.
quote: The data powering the AI system must reflect current knowledge, necessitating continuous checks to determine the frequency of data updates for open clinical trials, treatment indications, guidelines, and biomarker-selection criteria.
hazard: AI recommendations based on outdated clinical knowledge

statement: Ensure all LLM handling of patient data complies with applicable health privacy regulations such as HIPAA or GDPR.
quote: Regarding privacy concerns, since the model accesses sensitive patient information from electronic health records, it is imperative to ensure that all data handling complies with healthcare privacy regulations such as HIPAA in the United States or GDPR in the European Union.
hazard: Regulatory violations and unlawful exposure of sensitive patient information accessed by the LLM

statement: Build security controls into the EHR-connected LLM that block unauthorized access to patient data.
quote: To ensure patient privacy, the LLM must incorporate robust security measures that thwart unauthorized access to patient data.
hazard: Unauthorized access to patient records through the LLM system

statement: Encrypt LLM-accessed patient data both at rest and in transit, using secure transmission protocols.
quote: These measures include employing secure data transmission protocols, encrypting data both at rest and during transit, and implementing stringent access controls to guarantee that only authorized healthcare professionals can interact with the system.
hazard: Interception or theft of patient data flowing to or stored by the LLM

statement: Implement access controls so that only authorized health care professionals can interact with the EHR-connected LLM.

statement: Address significant disparities between development data and the intended deployment population.
quote: Assess for potential disparities between training and testing data and the target population [102]. It is important to consider significant representational disparities, like missing data, between the intended target population and the input or output distributions in the training or testing datasets. If there are significant disparities, they should be addressed.
hazard: Known population mismatches persisting into deployment.

statement: Define relevant sociodemographic subgroups and assess availability of data needed to evaluate their outcomes.
quote: Consider how relevant sociodemographic subgroups are defined and assess the availability of these data [102].
hazard: Fairness evaluation overlooking relevant patient groups.

statement: Verify that evaluation datasets contain subgroup information and representative deployment-setting data for fairness comparisons.
quote: Determine whether training and testing datasets provide information on relevant socio-demographic subgroups, as well as representative data from the deployment setting, that will eventually allow for fairness evaluation between them.
hazard: Inability to detect unfair performance across deployment subgroups.

statement: Evaluate differences in data quality and resulting distributions across deployment sites.
quote: For this step, the team should evaluate whether differences in data quality are likely across deployment sites, especially for clinical data (e.g., MRI scanner type, type/method of heart rate measurements, type of assay used, etc.), and whether such differences on data distributions have been evaluated.
hazard: Site-specific data differences causing unsafe or unequal performance.

statement: Assess whether data quality, missingness, or data type differs systematically across sociodemographic subgroups.
quote: Explore any statistical interactions between data quality or data type and relevant socio-demographic subgroups (e.g. are Black patients or older patients more likely to have different, missing, or lower-quality data, or have data on a 1.5 vs 3 Tesla MRI scanner, etc.?).
hazard: Subgroup-specific data deficiencies producing unequal AI performance.

statement: Evaluate proxies or composite scores used as AI inputs or outputs for bias across relevant subgroups.
quote: If proxies or composite scores are used as inputs or outputs of the AI model, clarify whether they have been evaluated for bias across relevant socio-demographic subgroups.
hazard: Biased proxies or scores influencing AI recommendations.

statement: Assess whether proxies or composite scores could exclude or differentially treat disadvantaged groups.
quote: Consider whether their use (as inputs or outputs of the AI model) could result in unintentional exclusion or differential treatment of already disadvantaged groups (e.g., cost/utilization of as a proxy for deciding on advance care coordination).
hazard: Disadvantaged patients being excluded from appropriate services.

statement: Determine whether a directly measurable quantity can replace a proxy or composite score.
quote: In addition, the team should determine whether there is a directly measurable quantity that could be used instead of a proxy or composite score.
hazard: Avoidable bias caused by indirect measures of patient needs.

statement: Evaluate unavoidable proxies for subgroup differences associated with access to care.
quote: If not, consider whether training, testing, and deployment data have been evaluated for systematic differences in proxies or composite scores by relevant sociodemographic subgroups that could be related to issues with access, especially if the model is intended to provide care coordination, clinical care, or need-based services.
hazard: Historical access barriers being reproduced in need-based service decisions.

statement: Assess whether representative, separable data are available to test handling of different scenarios and data variations.
quote: When considering overall robustness, it is important to ask if representative and separable data is available to training and test the model’s handling of different scenarios and data variations.
hazard: Fragile performance on scenarios or data variations absent from testing.

statement: Ensure local tuning data represent the current deployment population and setting.
quote: Ensure that local data for model tuning is representative of the present population and setting [27], [108].
hazard: Local adaptation worsening performance through unrepresentative data.

statement: Evaluate performance and fairness using data representative of the implementation population.
quote: It is important to evaluate the model’s performance and fairness based on data representing the population in which it will be implemented.
hazard: Deployment based on performance or fairness estimates that do not apply locally.

statement: Determine whether the model has been tuned to the local population using retrospective or current data.
quote: It is also important to ask if the model has been tuned to a local population using retrospective or current data.
hazard: Unexamined mismatch between the model and local population.

statement: Assess availability and suitability of training and testing data information for evaluating fairness and bias.
quote: Consider the availability of information about the data used to train and test the model as well as its appropriateness for evaluating fairness and bias [27], [73].
hazard: Adopting a model without adequate evidence to assess fairness.

statement: Determine whether training and testing sample representativeness can be compared with the intended deployment population.
quote: Developer and/or implementer teams should also determine whether they can compare the representativeness of training/testing samples to that of 40 the intended population for AI solution deployment.
hazard: Population mismatches remaining unknown to implementers.

statement: Share available training and testing data acquisition and purpose information with the implementation team.
quote: In addition, if information on training and test data acquisition and data purpose are available from the developer team, these should be shared with the implementer team.
hazard: Implementers misunderstanding the origins or intended uses of development data.

statement: Evaluate the justification for data selection and curation.
quote: Finally, the justification provided for data selection/curation should be evaluated.
hazard: Unsupported data-selection choices undermining safety or fairness.

statement: Assess whether the dataset is sufficiently large and representative of the deployment patient population.
quote: Ensuring a high-quality model will require the team to assess whether the dataset is sufficiently large and representative of the patient population in which it will be used.
hazard: Deployment supported by insufficient or unrepresentative evidence.

statement: Establish monitoring of data quality.
quote: Ensure that data governance and appropriate systems are in place to monitor data and data quality [5], [12], [14], [35], [49], [109], [110].
hazard: Data-quality deterioration causing unsafe outputs.

statement: Assess whether data latency is monitored.
quote: For these reasons, it’s important to determine whether there is a system in place to monitor data quality, latency, and security, as well as outcomes and drift.
hazard: Stale or delayed data compromising clinical outputs.

statement: Assess whether data security is monitored.
quote: For these reasons, it’s important to determine whether there is a system in place to monitor data quality, latency, and security, as well as outcomes and drift.
hazard: Security violations remaining undetected.

statement: Assess whether deployed AI outcomes are monitored.
quote: For these reasons, it’s important to determine whether there is a system in place to monitor data quality, latency, and security, as well as outcomes and drift.
hazard: Adverse real-world outcomes remaining unnoticed.

statement: Assess whether data and model-output drift are monitored.
quote: Monitoring data quality and dataset drifts can help detect drift in model output and effectiveness and prevent downstream safety risks. For these reasons, it’s important to determine whether there is a system in place to monitor data quality, latency, and security, as well as outcomes and drift.
hazard: Declining model effectiveness causing downstream safety failures.

statement: Identify data-governance and change-management plans for the AI solution.
quote: The team should also identify any data governance and change management plans to drive accountability and reduce safety risks, as well as roles and responsibilities that specify who will address issues as they arise, given that data input and AI model output deviations may create safety risks.
hazard: Uncontrolled data or system changes creating safety risks.

statement: Specify who is responsible for addressing data-input and model-output deviations.
quote: The team should also identify any data governance and change management plans to drive accountability and reduce safety risks, as well as roles and responsibilities that specify who will address issues as they arise, given that data input and AI model output deviations may create safety risks.
hazard: Safety issues remaining unresolved because ownership is unclear.

statement: Assess whether data-quality thresholds define when the AI solution can continue operating safely.
quote: Finally the team should consider whether thresholds for data quality have been established (i.e., the extent to which the AI solution will continue to be safe and operate if there is a defect noted in data quality).
hazard: Continued operation despite unsafe data quality.

statement: Identify organizational leadership accountable for data governance and quality.
quote: Leadership and accountability in the implementer team’s organization should be identified, as well as data governance, quality policies and internal audit processes.
hazard: Data-quality risks lacking accountable leadership.

statement: Identify data-quality policies and internal audit processes.
quote: Leadership and accountability in the implementer team’s organization should be identified, as well as data governance, quality policies and internal audit processes.
hazard: Data-quality failures persisting without policy or audit oversight.

statement: Assess whether independent third parties can audit data lineage and provenance.
quote: The team should also assess whether the AI system’s data lineage and provenance are auditable by independent third parties and whether there is a data quality issue management plan for the AI solution, so that risks and issues can be continually identified, assessed and managed.
hazard: Unverifiable data origins or transformations concealing safety issues.

statement: Assess whether a data-quality issue-management plan supports continuous identification, assessment, and management of risks.
quote: The team should also assess whether the AI system’s data lineage and provenance are auditable by independent third parties and whether there is a data quality issue management plan for the AI solution, so that risks and issues can be continually identified, assessed and managed.
hazard: Data-quality risks being handled inconsistently or left unresolved.

statement: Provide stakeholders a way to report and trace data-quality complaints, ethical concerns, and safety risks.
quote: Ensure that stakeholders can trace complaints, ethical concerns, and safety risks related to data quality [39], [42], [43].
hazard: Stakeholder-reported risks being lost or ignored.

statement: Check that corrective and preventative actions exist for data-quality complaints and other issues.
quote: In addition, the team should clarify whether stakeholders can report complaints, ethical concerns, and safety risks due to data quality, and whether Corrective and Preventative Actions (CAPAs) for these complaints and other issues exist.
hazard: Repeated data-quality incidents without remediation or prevention.

statement: Verify that internal staff, vendors, and consultants understand their change-management responsibilities for data governance, engineering, and quality.
quote: The team should also clarify whether all involved in the development and deployment of the AI solution, including third-party vendors and consultants, understand their roles and responsibilities as indicated in the change management plan pertaining to data governance, data engineering and data quality.
hazard: Responsibility gaps across organizational and vendor boundaries.

statement: Define clear inclusion and exclusion criteria for the deployment patient population.
quote: Apply clear inclusion/exclusion criteria for the targeted patient population [49]. AI models should have clear inclusion / exclusion criteria.
hazard: AI use in populations for which validity has not been established.

statement: Identify a protocol governing automated or manual changes to deployment-population inclusion and exclusion.
quote: In addition, the team should identify 41 whether there is a protocol for automating or altering the inclusion/exclusion of deployment populations for whom the AI solution does/does not apply.
hazard: Uncontrolled expansion or restriction of the population receiving AI-supported care.

statement: Maintain access audit trails that support breach detection and independent review of access to the AI solution.
quote: This entails an audit trail and governance structure that can ensure compliance with regulations, detect breaches, and allow for independent review of who can access the AI solution.
hazard: Unauthorized access lacking an auditable record.

statement: Make developer and implementer data-privacy and security requirements transparent.
quote: It is important to be transparent about data privacy and security requirements as defined by both the developer and implementer teams.
hazard: Misaligned or misunderstood privacy and security obligations.

statement: Assess whether the AI system supports monitoring for data breaches and violations.
quote: This also includes assessing whether the AI model is engineered to be monitored for data breaches or violations, and whether system performance can be measured as complexity increases.
hazard: A system architecture that prevents detection of privacy or security violations.

statement: Assess whether system performance can be measured as complexity increases.
quote: This also includes assessing whether the AI model is engineered to be monitored for data breaches or violations, and whether system performance can be measured as complexity increases.
hazard: Unmeasurable performance deterioration as deployment becomes more complex.

statement: Identify a data-monitoring committee or group with documented roles and reporting structure.
quote: Determine whether there is a committee or group that monitors training, testing and deployment data and whether their roles and reporting structure are established and documented.
hazard: Data monitoring lacking defined oversight or reporting accountability.

statement: Document the justification if a data-monitoring committee or group is deemed unnecessary.
quote: If such a committee/group has been deemed unnecessary, the team should find out if the justification for that decision has been documented.
hazard: Omission of data oversight without an accountable rationale.

statement: Document how training-data representation relates to the intended deployment population.
quote: Determine whether the AI model training data is representative of the intended deployment population, and whether the correlation between them is documented.
hazard: Undocumented population mismatches obscuring fairness and validity limitations.

statement: Assess whether comorbidities and sociocultural influences have been accounted for.
quote: In addition, consider whether comorbidities and sociocultural influences have been accounted for.
hazard: Overlooking clinical or social context relevant to safe and equitable performance.

statement: Keep records of training and testing data origins, transformations, usage, and dependencies.
quote: It is important to keep a record of training and testing data, including information on its origins, transformations, usage, and dependencies exist.
hazard: Inability to investigate how development data affected deployed behavior.

statement: Document data limitations, including incompleteness, errors, temporal bias, and sample size.
quote: Along with that, it is important to document data limitations (e.g. incompleteness, noise and errors, temporal bias, sample size, etc.).
hazard: Deployment decisions overlooking known data limitations.

statement: Document the data pipeline so model decisions can be traced to specific points and transformations.
quote: For this step, the team should identify whether the data pipeline has been documented in a way that allows decisions about the AI model to be traced back to specific points and transformations.
hazard: Errors or changes becoming impossible to trace to their data origins.

statement: Plan regular data-lineage audits to keep records accurate and current.
quote: The team should also determine whether there is a plan for regular audits of data lineage to ensure that it remains accurate and current.
hazard: Outdated lineage records undermining investigations and accountability.

statement: Implement dataset version control.
quote: Implement version control for datasets [81].
hazard: Untraceable data changes affecting AI performance.

statement: Establish a process to notify end users of dataset changes after deployment.
quote: Determine whether there is a tracking process to maintain dataset version control, as well as a process for notifying end users of changes made after deployment.
hazard: Users relying on outdated assumptions about the system’s data.

statement: Assess the AI solution’s impact on patients and the potential need for consent.
quote: Consider the impact on patients and the potential need for consent [111].
hazard: Patient-impacting AI use without appropriate consent consideration.

statement: Justify and document the extent of patients’ access to information about the AI system and its outputs.
quote: Determine whether the extent to which patients have access to information about the AI system and its output has been justified and documented.
hazard: Unjustified restrictions on patients’ understanding of AI-supported care.

statement: Justify and document data manipulations, including cleaning and text preprocessing.
quote: For this step, assess whether any types of data manipulation used (e.g., feature engineering, data cleaning, text preprocessing, etc.) have been justified and documented.
hazard: Unexplained data transformations altering clinical meaning or introducing bias.

statement: Implement controls addressing the AI system’s privacy and security requirements.
quote: Implement controls for privacy and security requirements for the AI system [3], [4].
hazard: Privacy and security requirements remaining unenforced.

statement: Trace AI system requirements to privacy and security risks and obligations.
quote: Privacy and security requirements are important in order to enable the implementer team’s organization to address privacy and security risks to individuals and operations as well as legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations, the team should determine whether there is traceability between AI system requirements and privacy and security risks and obligations.
hazard: Requirements failing to address identified risks or binding obligations.

statement: Have legal staff assess whether implementation requirements meet privacy and security legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations.
quote: In addition, find out whether legal staff have determined whether implementer team requirements meet relevant security and privacy legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations.
hazard: Deployment violating privacy or security obligations.

statement: Include risks to both individuals and the organization in privacy and security risk management.
quote: The team should also assess whether the risk management strategy includes evaluating risks to both individuals and the organization, and consider whether privacy and security risk assessments will be conducted again to assess whether the implementation has altered risks.
hazard: Organizational risk management overlooking harms to individuals.

statement: Consider repeating privacy and security risk assessments to identify risks altered by implementation.
quote: The team should also assess whether the risk management strategy includes evaluating risks to both individuals and the organization, and consider whether privacy and security risk assessments will be conducted again to assess whether the implementation has altered risks.
hazard: New implementation-related privacy or security risks remaining unassessed.

statement: Address data-processing authorization and revocation in policy, including individual consent where appropriate.
quote: This step includes determining whether policies address the management of data processing authorization and revocation, including individual consent where appropriate.
hazard: Continued data processing without valid authorization.

statement: Address data retention and data-quality management in policies informed by privacy risks and system requirements.
quote: Also note whether policies address how data will be managed to minimize privacy and cybersecurity risks and meet AI system requirements, including data retention and data quality management.
hazard: Unsafe retention or handling of patient data.

statement: Establish policies for managing individuals’ privacy and data-processing preferences.
quote: In addition, consider whether policies address the management of individuals’ privacy and data processing preferences, and whether the AI system enables compliance with those policies.
hazard: Data processing contrary to individuals’ stated preferences.

statement: Assess whether the AI system enables compliance with privacy-preference policies.
quote: In addition, consider whether policies address the management of individuals’ privacy and data processing preferences, and whether the AI system enables compliance with those policies.
hazard: Privacy policies that cannot be enforced technically.

statement: Assess mechanisms and results for obtaining stakeholder feedback about privacy preferences.
quote: Also assess whether there are means for obtaining feedback about privacy preferences (e.g. surveys, focus groups) and if so, what the results are.
hazard: Privacy decisions made without understanding affected stakeholders’ preferences.

statement: Verify that AI data stores protect data confidentiality and integrity.
quote: Determine whether AI system data stores protect confidentiality and data integrity, as well as whether the AI system network protects the confidentiality and integrity 43 of data transfer.
hazard: Disclosure or alteration of stored patient data.

statement: Verify that AI network controls protect the confidentiality and integrity of data transfers.
quote: Determine whether AI system data stores protect confidentiality and data integrity, as well as whether the AI system network protects the confidentiality and integrity 43 of data transfer.
hazard: Interception or alteration of patient data in transit.

statement: Verify that user-access and network controls separate AI development and testing environments.
quote: Also note whether AI system user access and network controls maintain separation between AI development and testing environments.
hazard: Cross-environment access compromising data or testing integrity.

statement: Evaluate whether data inputs and provenance support accuracy, completeness, and bias management.
quote: Evaluate whether data inputs and provenance enable accuracy, ensure completeness, and facilitate the management of bias in datasets [3], [4].
hazard: Incomplete or poorly sourced data producing inaccurate or biased outputs.

statement: Document data-acquisition sources, methods, circumstances, and consent mechanisms where appropriate.
quote: As part of this step, the team should identify documentation regarding how, from what source(s), and under what circumstances data elements were acquired for the AI solution (including manner and mechanism of consent where appropriate).
hazard: Use of data with unclear origins or consent status.

statement: Identify data collectors and the categories of individuals whose data the AI solution uses.
quote: Also identify those persons involved in the data collection, and the categories of individuals whose data are being used.
hazard: Unclear accountability for collection or understanding of represented populations.

statement: Assess how dataset composition, collection, and processing constrain future uses.
quote: Note whether there is anything about the composition of the dataset or the way it was collected or processed that might affect future uses, and whether there are tasks for which the data should not be used.
hazard: Repurposing data in contexts for which it is unsuitable.

statement: Identify tasks for which the dataset should not be used.
quote: Note whether there is anything about the composition of the dataset or the way it was collected or processed that might affect future uses, and whether there are tasks for which the data should not be used.
hazard: Use of data for contraindicated or unsupported tasks.

statement: Determine whether the dataset needs updating and at what intervals.
quote: Finally, consider whether the dataset should be updated and if so, after what interval(s)?
hazard: Outdated data degrading deployed AI relevance or reliability.

statement: Test local barriers to AI use, including access pathways and interface usability.
quote: During testing, it is crucial to assess barriers to AI tool utilization in the local environment. This includes evaluating how the AI is accessed and whether the interface is user -friendly.
hazard: Local interface or access barriers causing poor adoption or misuse.

statement: Preserve engineering decision rationales for generative AI tools through document control and records management.
quote: Document control and records management are essential for preserving the rationale behind decisions made during the engineering of the solution, particularly concerning patient safety and risk management related to the AI tool.
hazard: Loss of safety-related decision rationales needed for accountability or investigation.

statement: Audit clinicians’ use of generative AI EHR tools by recording document access and system questions and answers.
quote: Implementing a solution that audits the tool’s use by clinicians, tracking EHR document access and the questions and answers provided by the system, is critical.
hazard: Inability to reconstruct AI-supported clinical decisions or investigate adverse events.

statement: Define end-user roles within the workflow.
quote: It is crucial to define the term “end -user” and specify their role in the workflow.
hazard: Unclear responsibilities for interpreting and acting on AI outputs.

statement: Identify patient subgroups especially susceptible to missing data.
quote: It is essential to address these cases equitably by identifying which subgroups are more susceptible to data gaps, finding ways to address these gaps, and managing care coordination efforts for individuals lacking key data necessary for appropriate risk categorization.
hazard: Patients with systematically incomplete records receiving inequitable care.

statement: Develop ways to address subgroup-specific data gaps.
quote: It is essential to address these cases equitably by identifying which subgroups are more susceptible to data gaps, finding ways to address these gaps, and managing care coordination efforts for individuals lacking key data necessary for appropriate risk categorization.
hazard: Known missing-data disparities persisting in AI-supported care.

statement: Manage care coordination for individuals lacking key data needed for appropriate risk categorization.
quote: It is essential to address these cases equitably by identifying which subgroups are more susceptible to data gaps, finding ways to address these gaps, and managing care coordination efforts for individuals lacking key data necessary for appropriate risk categorization.
hazard: Individuals with incomplete records being overlooked for care coordination.

statement: Complete and document a workflow-integration assessment.
quote: Once again, it is important to ensure that a workflow integration assessment has been completed and documented.
hazard: Deployment disrupting clinical workflows in unanticipated ways.

statement: Assess how AI affects the flow of people and tasks through physical and digital environments.
quote: It is also important to assess how the AI solution accounts for the flow of people and tasks through physical and digital environments and how the solution may hinder patient-clinician interactions.
hazard: Workflow disruption or task failures caused by poor integration.

statement: Assess potential effects of AI on clinician–clinician and patient–clinician interactions.
quote: This includes determining whether relevant team activities (e.g., clinician-clinician, patient-clinician interactions) have been studied and the possible effects of the solution on team activities have been assessed.
hazard: AI use hindering communication and collaborative care.

statement: Identify end users and other people whose work will be affected by the AI solution.
quote: In addition, determine whether end users and others whose work will be affected by use of the AI solution have been defined or identified.
hazard: Implementation overlooking affected staff and their work requirements.

statement: Reassess whether the AI solution addresses its stated use case.
quote: This includes reevaluating whether the AI solution addresses the stated use case, is consistent with organizational objectives, and whether it potentially improves the standard of care or existing practice.
hazard: Deploying a tool that does not solve the defined problem.

statement: Reassess whether the AI solution is consistent with organizational objectives.
quote: This includes reevaluating whether the AI solution addresses the stated use case, is consistent with organizational objectives, and whether it potentially improves the standard of care or existing practice.
hazard: Investment in AI that conflicts with organizational priorities.

statement: Reassess whether the AI solution could improve the standard of care or existing practice.
quote: This includes reevaluating whether the AI solution addresses the stated use case, is consistent with organizational objectives, and whether it potentially improves the standard of care or existing practice.
hazard: Deploying AI without a credible improvement over existing care.

statement: Reevaluate and document AI usability.
quote: Reevaluate the usability of the AI solution [12], [86]. This step includes determining whether the usability of the AI solution has been assessed and documented in prior stages, as well as whether human factors principles and usability heuristics have been explicitly considered and applied.
hazard: Usability problems causing errors or ineffective use.

statement: Apply human-factors principles and usability heuristics to the AI solution.
quote: This step includes determining whether the usability of the AI solution has been assessed and documented in prior stages, as well as whether human factors principles and usability heuristics have been explicitly considered and applied.
hazard: Interfaces or workflows that increase human error.

statement: Document potential trust in the AI solution through a risk-benefit assessment.
quote: Because trust is essential for successful adoption and impact of an AI solution, it is important to document potential trust in the AI solution using a risk-benefit assessment.
hazard: Trust or adoption unsupported by an assessment of benefits and risks.

statement: Verify that thorough robustness testing and its results are documented.
quote: The team should ascertain whether the AI solution has undergone thorough robustness testing, and whether this process and its outcomes have been documented.
hazard: Fragile system behavior remaining undiscovered before deployment.

statement: Assess development–implementation environment differences to determine necessary local tailoring.
quote: Assess how the tool will need to be tailored for the specific work context of the implementing organization [56]. This includes an assessment evaluating differences between the development and implementation environments.
hazard: Unsafe transfer of a tool into a materially different work environment.

statement: Assess whether counterfactual tests evaluate performance with and without relevant sociodemographic subgroup information.
quote: This step includes assessing whether counterfactual tests are conducted both with and without relevant sociodemographic subgroups in order to evaluate AI model performance.
hazard: Performance differences caused by sociodemographic information remaining undetected.

statement: Assess whether training and test datasets are independent.
quote: Assess whether training and test datasets are independent, and note whether the AI system is calibrated by producing outcomes independent of protected classes such as race, gender (or their proxies), disability, or other variables that correlate highly with protected classes.
hazard: Evaluation contamination overstating deployed model performance.

statement: Select accuracy, parity, and fairness measures based on the scope, degree, and direction of error impacts on individuals and subgroups.
quote: Determine whether measures of parity, overall accuracy, and fairness are chosen, by accounting for the scope, degree, and direction of impact that errors or inaccurate predictions can have on individuals or subgroups.
hazard: Evaluation metrics concealing clinically important or unequal harms.

statement: Ensure fairness measures match the fairness definition established during problem definition and planning.
quote: Determine whether measures of fairness are consistent with any definition of fairness stated during the problem definition and planning phase.
hazard: Changing fairness criteria obscuring whether intended equity goals were met.

statement: Plan evaluation of resource distribution, access, operations, and real-world outcomes using available data.
quote: Note whether a plan is in place and data available for evaluating how the AI system may improve the balance of resource distribution, access to care, clinical operations, and/or real-world clinical outcomes.
hazard: Technical performance masking inequitable real-world impact.

statement: Evaluate local performance and safety even when the AI solution has been evaluated in other populations.
quote: Evaluate performance and safety at the local level, even if impact and safety have been evaluated for a given AI solution in other populations [49].
hazard: Assuming external validation guarantees safety in the local setting.

statement: Integrate human factors into AI safety and harm assessments.
quote: In order to inform risk management practices for the deployment of the AI solution, human factors should be integrated into safety and harm assessments.
hazard: Safety assessments overlooking user behavior and interaction risks.

statement: Assess safety and efficacy on the local target population in a deployment-site test population or environment.
