hazard: Uncontrolled drift or poisoning in periodically retrained machine learning models.

statement: Capture what sources are included, criteria for inclusion, and update cadence in register entries for RAG systems.
quote: Register entries for RAG systems should capture what sources are included, the criteria for inclusion, and the update cadence — since a stale or poorly governed retrieval corpus introduces the same quality and bias risks as a poorly prepared training dataset.
hazard: Grounding generative AI on stale or inappropriate retrieval corpora.

statement: Document permitted data categories, prohibited categories, and the legal basis for including PHI in generative AI prompts.
quote: This should be documented, including the data categories permitted, any categories that are prohibited, and the legal basis for including PHI where applicable.
hazard: Inappropriate exposure of sensitive patient data in LLM context windows.

statement: Create a distinct register entry with access controls, defined retention periods, and BAA coverage confirmed for agentic AI persistent memory stores.
quote: If an agentic system maintains memory across sessions (e.g. retaining clinical context, user preferences, or prior interactions) that memory store should have its own register entry, with access controls, a defined retention period, and BAA coverage confirmed.
hazard: Ungoverned accumulation of PHI in persistent cross-session AI memory.

statement: Document which systems, databases, and external APIs an agentic AI system is authorized to access at runtime.
quote: For agentic AI that queries multiple systems or APIs to complete tasks, the register should document which systems, databases, and external APIs the agent is authorized to access — not only the datasets used to develop it.
hazard: Agents improperly retrieving or exfiltrating data across multiple APIs.

statement: Review the authorization scope for agentic AI systems whenever their capabilities or integrations change.
quote: This authorization scope should be reviewed whenever the system's capabilities or integrations change.
hazard: Agent capabilities exceeding initial privacy and authorization approvals.

statement: Inventory existing AI-related data by documenting data currently used in higher-risk AI tools or tools that touch sensitive data sources.
quote: Inventory existing AI-related data. Begin by documenting data currently used in higher-risk AI tools or tools that touch sensitive data sources.
hazard: Undocumented transmission of sensitive data to external AI vendors.

statement: Assign a named individual responsible for keeping each dataset entry accurate as a data steward.
quote: Assign data stewards. Each dataset entry should have a named individual responsible for keeping the record accurate.
hazard: Orphaned or outdated records in the AI data acquisition register.

statement: Link the data acquisition register to the organization's AI Inventory Registry.
quote: Integrate with the AI Inventory Registry. The data acquisition register should link to the AI Inventory Registry maintained under Domain 3
hazard: Disconnect between AI solutions tracked and the datasets they access.

statement: Establish a review cadence and specify triggers for updating the data register.
quote: Establish a review cadence and specify triggers for data register updates.
hazard: Failure to capture new data sources accessed as AI systems evolve.

statement: Review and update the data register when new AI tools are procured, vendors change practices, or new data sources are accessed.
quote: Review and update the register when new AI tools are procured, when vendors change their data practices, or when new data sources are accessed.
hazard: Operating on outdated documentation regarding vendor data use.

statement: Establish a retention period for the data register after the AI solution itself is decommissioned.
quote: Establish a retention period for the data register after the AI solution itself is decommissioned.
hazard: Premature deletion of audit trails needed for regulatory inquiries.

statement: Establish comprehensive Data Use Agreements or Business Associate Agreements detailing permitted uses, security compliance, audit rights, and data destruction terms.
quote: Control 4.3.2: Establish comprehensive Data Use Agreements and/or Business Associate Agreements that includes information on permitted and prohibited uses, compliance with organization’s security and privacy requirements, rights to audit, consequences of non-compliance, and data return/destruction terms at end of use.
hazard: Absence of legal mechanisms governing vendor use of healthcare data.

statement: Ask vendors requesting patient data to document in writing the specific data elements needed and the reason each is required.
quote: ask vendors requesting patient data to document, in writing, the specific data elements needed and the reason each element is required for the contracted service.
hazard: Over-sharing of patient data beyond what the vendor actually requires.

statement: Explicitly state whether the vendor is permitted to train or fine-tune models on organizational data.
quote: AI training restriction: If the vendor is not permitted to train or fine-tune models on your data, this must be stated explicitly.
hazard: Vendors implicitly assuming the right to train models on client data.

statement: Define the scope and resulting IP rights if the vendor is permitted to train models on organizational data.
quote: Conversely, if training is permitted, define its scope and any resulting IP rights.
hazard: Disputes over ownership of data-derived intellectual property.

statement: Contractually forbid the vendor from attempting to re-identify de-identified data or linking datasets to enable re-identification.
quote: Contractually forbid the vendor from attempting to re-identify de-identified data or linking datasets in ways that could enable re-identification.
hazard: Vendors employing advanced techniques to re-identify anonymized patient data.

statement: Require vendors to use only the minimum data necessary for the specified purpose.
quote: Data Minimization: Require vendors to use only the minimum data necessary for the specified purpose.
hazard: Unnecessary exposure of extensive patient records.

statement: Prohibit the vendor from retaining data beyond what is required.
quote: Prohibit the vendor from retaining data beyond what is required.
hazard: Indefinite storage of sensitive data in vendor systems.

statement: Specify minimum vendor security standards including encryption, role-based access controls, and regular independent security assessments.
quote: Security requirements: Specify minimum standards including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and regular independent security assessments (e.g., SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST).
hazard: Vulnerability of organizational data in insecure vendor environments.

statement: Reserve the right to audit vendor compliance with the DUA, including access logs, security practices, and data handling procedures.
quote: Audit rights: Reserve the right to audit vendor compliance with the DUA, including access logs, security practices, and data handling procedures.
hazard: Inability to verify vendor adherence to data protection terms.

statement: Require vendors to return or certifiably destroy all raw datasets, stop further training, and delete fine-tuned models upon contract termination.
quote: Data return and destruction: Require vendors to return or certifiably destroy all raw datasets, stop further training, and delete any models fine-tuned on your organizations data (if feasible) — upon contract termination.
hazard: Continued use of proprietary data within vendor AI systems after termination.

statement: Review all current AI tool agreements for required provisions, identifying gaps and prioritizing remediation based on risk and data volume.
quote: Audit existing vendor contracts. Review all current AI tool agreements for the provisions above. Identify gaps and prioritize remediation based on risk level of the tool and volume of data involved.
hazard: Legacy AI deployments operating under outdated or weak data protections.

statement: Create a standard AI DUA or BAA addendum that can be appended to existing agreements for vendors handling AI data.
quote: Develop a standard AI DUA and/or BAA addendum. Rather than renegotiating all contracts, create a standard addendum that can be appended to existing DUAs/BAAs for vendors handling data used in AI systems.
hazard: Inconsistent contractual guardrails across multiple AI vendors.

statement: Create a standardized vendor security assessment questionnaire that all AI vendors must complete before contracting.
quote: Establish/modify a vendor security assessment process. Create a standardized questionnaire that all AI vendors must complete before contracting.
hazard: Procuring AI software without verifying foundational cybersecurity practices.

statement: Give procurement and legal teams a checklist of AI-specific provisions to verify before signing any new AI vendor agreement.
quote: Create a contract review checklist. Give procurement and legal teams a checklist of AI-specific provisions to verify before signing any new AI vendor agreement.
hazard: Omission of critical data use clauses during contract negotiation.

statement: Establish written HIPAA-compliant de-identification policies that consider applicable state privacy laws.
quote: Control 4.3.3: Establish written HIPAA-compliant de-identification policies (Safe Harbor or Expert Determination) considering applicable state privacy laws
hazard: Violations of overlapping federal and state data privacy regulations.

statement: Evaluate each PHI-containing dataset to select the de-identification method that minimizes re-identification risk.
quote: where relevant, evaluate each PHI-containing dataset to select the method that minimizes re-identification risk
hazard: Applying insufficient de-identification methods to highly specific or rare datasets.

statement: Validate de-identification before any dataset is used in AI training or model development.
quote: validate de-identification before any dataset is used in AI training or model development
hazard: Accidental exposure of sensitive identifiers during AI model training.

statement: Maintain oversight of de-identified datasets and reassess re-identification risk whenever datasets are linked or new identifiers emerge.
quote: maintain oversight of de-identified datasets, reassessing re-identification risk whenever datasets are linked or new identifiers emerge.
hazard: Re-identification of patients caused by linking previously disparate datasets.

statement: Implement risk mitigation controls for identified hazards, then re-evaluate the risk level to determine whether residual risk is acceptable.
quote: Organizations should implement risk mitigation controls (i.e., specific actions taken to reduce identified hazards) and then re-evaluate the risk level to determine if the residual risk is acceptable.
hazard: Deploying AI with unacceptable residual risk after controls

statement: Evaluate whether each AI solution meets FDA Software as a Medical Device criteria, implicates CMS conditions, or triggers HIPAA obligations as part of the formal risk assessment.
quote: In addition to ISO 14971:2019, HDOs should evaluate whether the AI solution: Meets criteria for U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-regulated Software as a Medical Device (SaMD);
hazard: Regulatory noncompliance from unrecognized device, CMS, or HIPAA obligations

statement: Require formal governance committee review for AI solutions categorized as higher risk.
quote: Higher risk categorization should trigger defined governance actions, including: formal committee review, enhanced post-deployment monitoring, documented residual risk acceptance by designated governance authority, and defined re-review triggers (e.g., after a system update, incident, or drift detection).
hazard: High-risk AI deployed without adequate governance scrutiny

statement: Apply enhanced post-deployment monitoring to AI solutions categorized as higher risk.
quote: Higher risk categorization should trigger defined governance actions, including: formal committee review, enhanced post-deployment monitoring, documented residual risk acceptance by designated governance authority, and defined re-review triggers (e.g., after a system update, incident, or drift detection).
hazard: Undetected harms from high-risk AI after deployment

statement: Define re-review triggers for higher-risk AI, such as system updates, incidents, or drift detection.
quote: Higher risk categorization should trigger defined governance actions, including: formal committee review, enhanced post-deployment monitoring, documented residual risk acceptance by designated governance authority, and defined re-review triggers (e.g., after a system update, incident, or drift detection).
hazard: Outdated risk assessments after model updates, incidents, or drift

statement: Block deployment of AI solutions with unmitigated high-severity harm potential that available controls cannot reduce.
quote: Additionally, HDOs should define explicit conditions under which an AI solution will not proceed to deployment, including: Unmitigated high-severity harm potential that cannot be reduced through available controls; Vendor refusal to provide certain AI Intake/procurement documentation (e.g., model cards); Residual risk exceeding predefined organizational tolerance thresholds.
hazard: Deploying AI capable of severe uncontrollable patient harm

statement: Block deployment when a vendor refuses to provide required intake or procurement documentation such as model cards.
quote: Additionally, HDOs should define explicit conditions under which an AI solution will not proceed to deployment, including: Unmitigated high-severity harm potential that cannot be reduced through available controls; Vendor refusal to provide certain AI Intake/procurement documentation (e.g., model cards); Residual risk exceeding predefined organizational tolerance thresholds.
hazard: Deploying opaque vendor AI without adequate documentation

statement: Define predefined organizational risk tolerance thresholds and block deployment when residual risk exceeds them.
quote: Additionally, HDOs should define explicit conditions under which an AI solution will not proceed to deployment, including: Unmitigated high-severity harm potential that cannot be reduced through available controls; Vendor refusal to provide certain AI Intake/procurement documentation (e.g., model cards); Residual risk exceeding predefined organizational tolerance thresholds.
hazard: Accepting residual risk beyond organizational tolerance

statement: Block deployment of continuously adaptive AI unless the vendor defines when calibration changes require governance notification, how they are disclosed, and whether they trigger re-categorization.
quote: A continuously adaptive or self-calibrating AI system for which the vendor cannot provide defined governance procedures specifying: (a) the criteria under which a calibration change constitutes a governance notification event, (b) the disclosure mechanism for such events, and/or (c) whether such changes trigger re-risk-categorization.
hazard: Silent model changes altering behavior without governance awareness

statement: Assign decisions to halt deployment to the designated AI governance authority.
quote: Decisions to halt deployment under these conditions should be made by the designated AI governance authority (e.g., AI governance committee), and organizations should define a documented appeal or reconsideration pathway (e.g., who may submit an appeal, what new evidence or mitigations would warrant re-review, and the body responsible for the final determination).
hazard: Unclear accountability for stopping unsafe AI deployments

statement: Define a documented appeal pathway for halted deployments specifying who may appeal, what evidence warrants re-review, and the final decision body.
quote: Decisions to halt deployment under these conditions should be made by the designated AI governance authority (e.g., AI governance committee), and organizations should define a documented appeal or reconsideration pathway (e.g., who may submit an appeal, what new evidence or mitigations would warrant re-review, and the body responsible for the final determination).
hazard: Arbitrary or inconsistent deployment halt decisions

statement: Define quantitative subgroup performance disparity thresholds that trigger escalation or deployment pause when not met.
quote: Organizations should define quantitative subgroup performance disparity thresholds that trigger escalation or deployment pause when thresholds aren’t met.
hazard: AI performing worse for specific patient subgroups

statement: Assess whether training and testing data represent the organization's specific patient populations.
quote: Data Sufficiency: Is the training and testing data representative of the specific patient populations the organization serves?
hazard: Poor performance on unrepresented local populations

statement: Assess the AI's exposure to security vulnerabilities such as data poisoning or adversarial inputs given its technical deployment.
quote: Security Resilience: How exposed is the model to security vulnerabilities, such as data poisoning or adversarial examples, based on its technical deployment?
hazard: Manipulation of AI outputs through adversarial attacks

statement: When high risk of bias or error is identified, specify controls such as increased human oversight or restricted use cases.
quote: Mitigation Strategy: If a high-risk of bias or error is identified, what specific controls (e.g., algorithmic adjustments, increased human oversight, or restricted use cases) are being put in place?
hazard: Known bias or error risks left unmitigated

statement: Review vendor contracts for acceptable risk allocation, indemnification, and incident notification requirements before deployment.
quote: For vendor-provided or co-developed AI systems, have contractual risk allocation, indemnification provisions, and/or incident notification requirements been reviewed and found acceptable?
hazard: Unallocated liability and missed vendor incident notifications

statement: Establish a plan to temporarily or permanently remove the AI tool if necessary.
quote: What plan is in place to temporarily or permanently remove the AI in the event that becomes necessary?
hazard: Inability to quickly withdraw a malfunctioning AI tool

statement: Document risk assessment results including testing against predefined metrics, identified data gaps, and effectiveness of mitigation controls.
quote: Documentation should include the results of testing against predefined metrics, identified data gaps, and the effectiveness of implemented risk mitigation controls.
hazard: Undocumented risks and unverifiable mitigation effectiveness

statement: Update risk assessment documentation whenever the system undergoes significant changes such as retraining or a use-case shift.
quote: This documentation should be updated whenever the system undergoes significant changes, such as retraining or a shift in use case setting.
hazard: Stale risk assessments after model or use changes

statement: Require documented sign-off by the designated governance authority to accept residual risk for higher-risk AI systems.
quote: Residual risk acceptance for higher risk AI systems should require documented sign-off by the designated governance authority, consistent with organizational risk governance policies.
hazard: Residual risk accepted without accountable authorization

statement: Make residual risk acceptance decisions time-bound and re-evaluate them at defined intervals or upon material changes.
quote: Acceptance decisions should be time-bound and subject to re-evaluation at defined intervals or when material changes occur.
hazard: Indefinite acceptance of risks that have changed

statement: Consult established control libraries such as NIST AI RMF to develop AI-specific risk mitigation controls.
quote: Organizations may consult established control libraries to inform the development of AI-specific risk mitigation controls.
hazard: Inconsistent or incomplete mitigation controls

statement: Define how the organization will measure whether implemented risk mitigation controls achieve their intended effect.
quote: Organizations should define how they will measure whether implemented risk and mitigation controls are achieving their intended effect.
hazard: Ineffective controls going unnoticed

statement: Track AI output override rates to measure control effectiveness.
quote: Approaches may include: tracking AI output override rates; monitoring incident reports and near-miss events; reviewing performance drift indicators; conducting periodic stakeholder feedback surveys; and comparing pre/postmitigation performance metrics against predefined thresholds.
hazard: Unrecognized poor output quality or user distrust

statement: Monitor incident reports and near-miss events involving AI tools.
quote: Approaches may include: tracking AI output override rates; monitoring incident reports and near-miss events; reviewing performance drift indicators; conducting periodic stakeholder feedback surveys; and comparing pre/postmitigation performance metrics against predefined thresholds.
hazard: Undetected AI-related safety events

statement: Conduct periodic stakeholder feedback surveys on deployed AI tools.
quote: Approaches may include: tracking AI output override rates; monitoring incident reports and near-miss events; reviewing performance drift indicators; conducting periodic stakeholder feedback surveys; and comparing pre/postmitigation performance metrics against predefined thresholds.
hazard: Missed user-reported problems with AI tools

statement: Maintain a version history of risk assessments documenting timing, assumptions, and system changes that triggered reassessment.
quote: Is there a clear version history that documents when the risk assessment was conducted, what assumptions were made, and what system changes (e.g., retraining, new integrations, expanded user groups) triggered reassessment?
hazard: Untraceable changes to AI risk posture

statement: Maintain a documented plan for detecting and responding to output anomalies, drift, or security breaches.
quote: Incident Response: Is there a documented plan for detecting and responding to output anomalies, drift, or security breaches?
hazard: Slow or absent response to anomalous AI outputs

statement: Designate an authority with predefined conditions to pause, restrict, or deactivate an AI system if performance degrades or safety risks emerge.
quote: Accountability & Escalation Authority: Who is the designated governance authority (and under what predefined conditions) to pause, restrict, or fully deactivate the system if performance degrades or emergent safety risks arise?
hazard: Continued use of degraded or unsafe AI

statement: Define a timeline (e.g., quarterly, annually, post-incident) for formally re-reviewing each AI risk assessment.
quote: Review Cadence: Is there a defined timeline (e.g., quarterly, annually, post-incident) for formally re-reviewing the risk assessment to ensure it remains accurate in the current clinical and technical environment?
hazard: Risk assessments becoming inaccurate over time

statement: Include intended and unintended consequences, such as shifts in decision-making or patient-provider interactions, in AI impact assessments.
quote: An impact assessment should consider both intended and unintended consequences, such as shifts in decision-making patterns, changes in patient-provider interactions, or downstream financial incentives among other examples.
hazard: Unanticipated system-level harms from AI deployment

statement: Define internal thresholds (risk level, deployment scale, patient-facing functionality) that trigger a formal AI impact assessment.
quote: Not all AI solutions will require a formal impact assessment; however, organizations should define clear internal thresholds (e.g., risk level, scale of deployment, patient-facing functionality) that trigger one.
hazard: High-impact AI deployed without broader impact review

statement: Document criteria distinguishing when a full impact assessment is required versus a lighter-weight review.
quote: Specifically, organizations should articulate when a full impact assessment is required (typically for higher-risk, patient-facing, or broadly deployed solutions) versus when a lighter-weight review is sufficient, and document the criteria that distinguish the two paths.
hazard: Inconsistent review depth across AI solutions

statement: Periodically evaluate cumulative AI risk where multiple AI solutions affect the same workflow, patient population, or staff.
quote: HDOs should periodically evaluate cumulative AI risk across all deployed systems, particularly where multiple AI solutions influence the same workflow, patient population, or workforce staff (e.g., clinicians, nurses, or other employees who participate in multiple AI-supported workflows simultaneously).
hazard: Compounding risks from multiple interacting AI systems

statement: Review portfolio-level AI risk at defined intervals and report it to the designated governance authority.
quote: Portfolio-level risk should be reviewed at defined governance intervals (e.g., semi-annually or annually) and reported to the designated governance authority.
hazard: Aggregate AI risk invisible to leadership

statement: Assess whether combined AI systems create interaction effects, compounding errors, or population-level automation bias.
quote: (2) Develop a Core Assessment Question(s): e.g., “Does the combined operation of these systems create risks not present in any individual system, including interaction effects, compounding errors, or population-level automation bias?”
hazard: Automation bias and compounding errors across AI tools

statement: Cross-reference the risk-benefit assessment with third-party management processes to align with vendor selection decisions.
quote: Cross-referencing this assessment with the Subdomain 4.4: Third Party Management Playbook is encouraged to ensure alignment between risk-benefit and vendor selection decisions.
hazard: Vendor selection misaligned with risk-benefit findings

statement: Assess how the AI affects stakeholders who do not interact with it directly but are impacted by its outputs.
quote: Stakeholder Impact: How does this AI affect different groups, including those who may not interact with it directly but are impacted by its outputs?
hazard: Overlooked harms to indirectly affected groups

statement: Address in the impact assessment how the AI system might exacerbate or reduce existing health disparities.
quote: Bias and Disparity Considerations: Does the impact assessment specifically address how the system might exacerbate or reduce existing health disparities?
hazard: Worsening health disparities through AI deployment

statement: Verify AI output is presented in a way comprehensible and usable by the clinicians or patients receiving it.
quote: Accessibility: Is the AI's output presented in a way that is comprehensible and usable for the clinicians or patients receiving the information?
hazard: Recipients misunderstanding or unable to use AI outputs

statement: Assess whether the AI deployment creates financial incentives influencing clinical behavior, documentation practices, or resource allocation.
quote: Does the deployment of this AI solution create or alter financial incentives that could influence clinical behavior, documentation practices, or care resource allocation?
hazard: AI-driven incentives distorting documentation or care

statement: Explicitly identify, document, and address potential sources of bias in the AI system within the impact assessment.
quote: Have potential sources of bias in the AI system been explicitly identified, documented, and addressed as part of the impact assessment (separate from, but complementary to, risk categorization and assessment)?
hazard: Unaddressed bias in AI outputs

statement: Route AI tools with automated or agentic behavior lacking human-in-the-loop design to full committee review.
quote: Automation/agentic behavior: Any tool that does not rely on human-in-the-loop design.
hazard: Autonomous AI actions without human oversight

statement: Require a review packet including workflow map, model card, validation evidence, human-in-the-loop controls, rollback plan, and monitoring metrics like unsafe recommendation rate.
quote: Minimum packet: use case description, workflow map, data flows, vendor model card, validation evidence, human-in-the-loop controls, downtime/rollback plan, monitoring metrics (override rate, unsafe recommendation rate, etc.)
hazard: Approving AI without evidence, oversight, or rollback plans

statement: Allow expedited review only for supportive tools with clear mitigations such as required user sign-off, audit logs, and easy rollback.
quote: Low–to-moderate severity if wrong and clear mitigations (required user sign-off, audit logs, easy rollback).
hazard: Unreviewed AI outputs acted on without sign-off

statement: Limit exempt review to commodity tools without patient data, such as generic meeting transcription not used for clinical documentation.
quote: Commodity functionality (i.e., generic meeting transcription not used for clinical documentation).
hazard: Clinical-use tools escaping governance review

statement: Staff AI assessments with SMEs across cybersecurity, utility and validity, compliance, risk, ethics, and educational impact.
quote: The TGH Assessment team is made up of SMEs from 6 different evaluation domains: (1) Cybersecurity, (2) Utility & Validity, (3) Compliance, (4) Risk, (5) Ethics, (6) Educational Impact.
hazard: Narrow reviews missing critical risk dimensions

statement: Establish formal governance decision gates with a defined advancement decision, named accountable owner, and documented evidence of completion.
quote: An illustrative example that highlights how an organization may approach establishing a formal decision gate within the organization's governance framework, including a defined decision required to advance, a named accountable owner, and documented evidence of completion.
hazard: AI advancing through lifecycle without accountable approval

statement: Prioritize state and federal regulatory requirements, especially for AI solutions meeting the FDA SaMD definition.
quote: Organizations should prioritize state and federal regulatory requirements, especially for AI solutions that meet the definition of a Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), as defined by the FDA.
hazard: Regulatory violations for device-regulated AI

statement: Establish and maintain a structured data acquisition register for data used in AI systems.
quote: Data Documentation & Stewardship Establish and maintain a structured data acquisition register for data used in AI systems.
hazard: Untracked data sources and uses in AI systems

statement: Execute vendor agreements defining permissible uses, re-identification and redistribution terms, security compliance, audit rights, and data return/destruction.
quote: Data Use Agreements & Vendor Compliance Establish comprehensive agreements defining terms for permissible/nonpermissible uses, re-identification and redistribution preferences, requirements for vendor security compliance, audit rights, and data return/destruction terms.
hazard: Vendor misuse, redistribution, or retention of patient data

statement: Establish written HIPAA-compliant de-identification policies and validate de-identification before data is used for AI.
quote: De-identification & Privacy Compliance Establish written HIPAA-compliant de-identification policies; evaluate PHI datasets to select the appropriate method; validate de-identification before AI training use; maintain oversight of linked datasets.
hazard: Re-identification of patients from AI data

statement: Assign an owner and process for recurring AI data quality and bias evaluation.
quote: Data Quality & Bias Establish a process and owner for recurring AI data quality and bias evaluation to help identify quality gaps and known sources of bias.
hazard: Undetected data quality gaps and bias

statement: Identify the data types each AI system uses and the legal agreements that apply before deployment.
quote: Before implementing the controls in this playbook, organizations need to identify what types of data their AI systems use, and what legal agreements apply.
hazard: Improper data sharing without required agreements

statement: Use a DUA or other contractual controls when sharing de-identified data in AI contexts.
quote: DUA or other contractual controls (not required by HIPAA, but strongly recommended for AI contexts)
hazard: Uncontrolled downstream use of de-identified data

statement: Execute a Business Associate Agreement with any AI vendor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI.
quote: A BAA is required whenever a vendor creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI on behalf of a covered entity.
hazard: PHI processed by vendors without HIPAA protections

statement: Limit permitted PHI uses in AI vendor BAAs to defined functions and explicitly list AI-specific uses.
quote: Permitted Uses and Disclosures: Must be limited to defined functions (e.g., data hosting, analytics). AIspecific uses should be explicitly listed.
hazard: Vendor repurposing PHI for unauthorized AI uses

statement: Require AI vendors to report impermissible uses, disclosures, or security incidents within a defined timeframe, typically 10–15 days.
quote: Breach Notification: Timely reporting (typically within 10–15 days) of any impermissible use, disclosure, or security incident.
hazard: Delayed awareness of vendor data breaches

statement: Require flow-down of all BAA obligations to vendor subcontractors who access PHI.
quote: Subcontractors: Flow-down of all BAA obligations to any subcontractors who access PHI.
hazard: PHI exposure through unbound AI subprocessors

statement: Require return or destruction of PHI at contract termination, including model weights or embeddings trained on PHI.
quote: Return or Destruction of PHI: Required upon contract termination, including AI model weights or embeddings trained on PHI.
hazard: Retention of PHI in vendor model artifacts after termination

statement: Do not waive indemnification and liability provisions entirely in AI vendor agreements.
quote: Indemnification and Liability Caps: Important for risk allocation; often negotiated heavily with vendors but should not be waived entirely.
hazard: Organization bearing full liability for vendor AI failures

statement: Explicitly identify AI-specific use cases in Data Use Agreements for Limited Data Sets.
quote: AI-specific use cases must be explicitly identified.
hazard: Unauthorized AI uses of limited data sets

statement: Prioritize applicable state and federal regulatory requirements, especially for AI solutions classified as Software as a Medical Device.
quote: Organizations should prioritize state and federal regulatory requirements, especially for AI solutions that meet the definition of a Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), as defined by the FDA.
hazard: Deployment that fails to meet applicable regulatory requirements.

statement: Consult qualified legal counsel, clinical experts, and relevant professional advisors before acting on the playbook.
quote: Readers should consult with qualified legal counsel, clinical experts, and other appropriate professional advisors before taking, or refraining from taking, any action based on the information in this playbook.
hazard: Applying generalized guidance without considering local clinical and legal circumstances.

statement: Assess the resources available and needed to support AI governance.
quote: As organizations think about how to utilize existing and develop new organizational structures to support health AI governance, it is important to be aware of the resources available and needed, and to define who will be responsible and accountable for each of the functions necessary.
hazard: Governance responsibilities exceeding available organizational resources.

statement: Operationalize responsible AI principles across the AI lifecycle.
quote: Organizations should operationalize Responsible AI principles across the AI lifecycle (an example displayed below; See Subdomain 4.1: Responsible AI Lifecycle Management & Use Playbook).
hazard: Responsible AI safeguards being confined to only one lifecycle stage.

statement: Use a standard AI risk assessment.
quote: A standard risk, bias/fairness, and impact evaluation, and a risk-based governance approach supports safe, consistent, and accountable AI governance (See Subdomain 4.2: Risk & Impact Assessments Playbook).
hazard: Inconsistent identification of AI deployment risks.

statement: Use a standard AI bias and fairness evaluation.
quote: A standard risk, bias/fairness, and impact evaluation, and a risk-based governance approach supports safe, consistent, and accountable AI governance (See Subdomain 4.2: Risk & Impact Assessments Playbook).
hazard: Undetected bias or unfair effects on affected populations.

statement: Use a standard AI impact evaluation.
quote: A standard risk, bias/fairness, and impact evaluation, and a risk-based governance approach supports safe, consistent, and accountable AI governance (See Subdomain 4.2: Risk & Impact Assessments Playbook).
hazard: Deployment without understanding the solution's potential impacts.

statement: Use tiered governance processes that match oversight intensity to AI risk.
quote: A tiered risk categorization process, and a tiered governance process can help reduce burden on the organization, and speed up review and implementation where risks are low and benefits high.
hazard: Insufficient oversight of high-risk tools or unnecessary review burdens for low-risk tools.

statement: Establish risk-based validation requirements for AI usefulness, efficacy, safety, and fairness.
quote: Establishing requirements for risk-based validation and monitoring of usefulness, efficacy, safety, and bias/fairness (supported internally, by an external third-party, and/or vendor/developer).
hazard: Deployment of ineffective, unsafe, or unfair AI solutions.

statement: Establish risk-based monitoring requirements for AI usefulness, efficacy, safety, and fairness.
quote: Establishing requirements for risk-based validation and monitoring of usefulness, efficacy, safety, and bias/fairness (supported internally, by an external third-party, and/or vendor/developer).
hazard: Post-deployment deterioration in usefulness, safety, efficacy, or fairness.

statement: Standardize disclosure procedures for applicable AI solutions.
quote: Standard documentation requirements for vendors/developers, standard disclosures/consent procedures for certain AI solutions, and use-case specific training and feedback requirements (transparency) (e.g. Applied Model Card and AI Intake Questionnaire).
hazard: Affected people not receiving consistent information about AI use.

statement: Standardize consent procedures for applicable AI solutions.
quote: Standard documentation requirements for vendors/developers, standard disclosures/consent procedures for certain AI solutions, and use-case specific training and feedback requirements (transparency) (e.g. Applied Model Card and AI Intake Questionnaire).
hazard: AI use without appropriate, consistently obtained consent.

statement: Establish use-case-specific AI training requirements.
