statement: Require vendors to demonstrate HITRUST certification or SOC 2 Type II compliance prior to contracting.

statement: Establish a freshness and update schedule for the RAG retrieval corpus.

statement: Specify which actions or data access attempts by agentic systems require prior human confirmation.

statement: Evaluate AI tool performance across subgroups rather than relying exclusively on aggregate metrics.

statement: Require documentation in the data acquisition register explaining why each field is needed.

statement: Contractually require vendors to document and justify the specific data elements they request via the DUA addendum.

statement: Scope contractual audit rights to specific elements like access logs to reduce vendor resistance.

statement: Apply enhanced post-deployment monitoring to higher-risk AI solutions.

quote: k-anonymity (see related article here ): each record in a dataset should be indistinguishable from at least k−1 other records across the combination of quasi-identifiers retained.
hazard: Unique combinations of quasi-identifiers reveal patient identities.

statement: Use k=10 or higher when applying k-anonymity to sensitive-condition data.
quote: k=5 is a common minimum; k=10 or higher is preferred for sensitive conditions.
hazard: Re-identification exposes sensitive patient conditions.

statement: Suppress or perturb subgroup cells before release when fewer than 10–15 individuals share the attribute combination.
quote: Cell suppression — for any subgroup analysis where fewer than 10–15 individuals share a combination of attributes, those cells are typically suppressed or perturbed before release.
hazard: Disclosure of identifiable information from small subgroups.

statement: Adopt a risk-based approach to AI data governance and use.
quote: As with many of the controls described in these playbooks, it is recommended that organizations take a risk-based approach to responsible data governance and use in the context of AI.
hazard: Data governance effort is misaligned with deployment risks.

statement: Calibrate data-control rigor using both AI solution risk and the sensitivity of data used throughout its lifecycle.
quote: This approach may include taking both the risk of the AI solution and the sensitivity of the data sources used in training (if applicable), tuning, testing, or using the model to help prioritize how rigorously to apply a specific control.
hazard: High-risk systems or sensitive data receive insufficient controls.

statement: Align responsible AI lifecycle SOPs with responsible data management and use SOPs.
quote: Organizations may want to align responsible lifecycle management standard operating procedures (SOPs) with responsible data management and use SOPs to simplify processes and procedures.
hazard: Fragmented procedures create governance gaps.

statement: Implement methods to monitor and track compliance with AI policies.
quote: It’s one thing to have AI policies in place, but implementing these policies effectively, necessitates methods for monitoring and tracking compliance.
hazard: AI policies remain unenforced and violations go undetected.

statement: Design lifecycle and data-management procedures to implement and enforce AI policies.
quote: This means that both processes and procedures for Responsible Lifecycle Management and Use (see Subdomain 4.1: Responsible Lifecycle Management & Use Playbook), and Responsible Data Management and Use, should enable policy implementation and enforcement.
hazard: Operational processes fail to enforce organizational AI restrictions.

statement: Track prompt metadata to identify prohibited PHI use in general-purpose models.
quote: For example, if a policy prohibits the use of PHI in general purpose models, are organizations able to track metadata associated with prompts used, to identify where and when PHI was inappropriately used?
hazard: Undetected PHI disclosure through prompts.

statement: Establish and maintain a structured data acquisition register for data used in AI systems.
quote: Control 4.3.1: Establish and maintain a structured data acquisition register for data used in AI systems.
hazard: Unknown data sources and flows prevent effective governance.

statement: Prohibit unregistered datasets from being used for AI training, validation, or inference.
quote: Some organizations choose to prohibit the use of unregistered datasets for training, validation, or inference.
hazard: Unreviewed datasets bypass privacy, legal, and quality controls.

statement: Include training, fine-tuning, testing, and operational data in the data acquisition register.
quote: Data acquisition registers ideally document data across training, fine-tuning, testing, and operational use, but most organizations only reliably capture the first two, since training/validation data tends to be a discrete, bounded extract while inference data (the continuous daily flow through deployed models) is the least documented and carries the biggest governance gaps.
hazard: Operational inference data escapes lifecycle governance.

statement: Log data access comprehensively for AI systems whose data-access scope changes over time or at runtime.
quote: For any AI system where the full scope of data it acts on shifts over time or at runtime, comprehensive logging of data access (see Control 5, Section 8) is an important complement to the register.
hazard: Actual AI data access cannot be reconstructed or audited.

statement: Document authorized data access and its conditions in the register.
quote: The register documents what the system is authorized to access and under what conditions; logs record what it actually accessed.
hazard: Unclear authorization boundaries for AI data access.

statement: Determine register detail using organizational maturity, documentation capabilities, AI risk, and data sensitivity.
quote: The maturity of the organization and data documentation methods, the risks of the AI system, and sensitivity of the data used to train, tune, test, or use the AI solutions, should be considered when determining the breadth and depth of information is captured in a data register.
hazard: Documentation is inadequate for risk or impractical to maintain.

statement: Record each dataset's name, description, and purpose.
quote: Dataset name, description, and purpose
hazard: Datasets cannot be reliably identified or interpreted.

statement: Record each dataset's geographic or institutional scope.
quote: Geographic or institutional scope (e.g., which facilities, which patient populations)
hazard: Unknown population or facility coverage obscures deployment limitations.

statement: Document each dataset's structure, including formats, field definitions, variable types, units, and coding standards.
quote: Structural metadata: How data is organized File format, schema, and field definitions Variable types, units of measurement, and coding standards used (e.g., ICD-10, SNOMED, LOINC)
hazard: Misinterpreted data fields or coding conventions produce incorrect AI inputs.

statement: Record each dataset's record count and covered time period.
quote: Number of records and time period covered
hazard: Unknown dataset scale or age impedes suitability assessment.

statement: Document dataset access controls and authorized users.
quote: Access controls and authorized users
hazard: Unclear access permissions enable unauthorized data use.

statement: Maintain dataset version histories with the date of the latest update.
quote: Version history and date of last update
hazard: Untraceable dataset changes undermine audits and error investigation.

statement: Document data provenance and movement through systems.
quote: Where the data originated and how it moved through systems
hazard: Data lineage gaps prevent tracing errors or unauthorized transfers.

statement: Document transformations, cleaning, and de-identification applied to each dataset.
quote: What transformations, cleaning steps, or de-identification processes were applied
hazard: Unknown processing history hides privacy or data-quality failures.

statement: Link register entries to related datasets and derived outputs.
quote: Links to related datasets or derived outputs
hazard: Derived or linked data escapes governance.

statement: Record known data gaps, missingness rates, and quality flags.
quote: Known gaps, missingness rates, or data quality flags
hazard: Poor-quality inputs are used without awareness of their limitations.

statement: Document represented populations and known representativeness limitations.
quote: Population represented and any known representativeness limitations
hazard: Population mismatch produces inequitable AI performance.

statement: Record each dataset's validation status.
quote: Validation status
hazard: Unvalidated data is mistaken for validated data.

statement: Document cautioned uses for each dataset.
quote: Cautioned uses
hazard: Datasets are used outside their appropriate scope.

statement: Adapt and update existing data-documentation processes when implementing the register.
quote: See the following examples of what a basic data acquisition register might look like, noting that organizations should adapt and update existing processes, and that more mature organizations may want to build on this structure.
hazard: AI data documentation remains disconnected from established organizational processes.

statement: Record each data source's name and type.
quote: Data source name and type (e.g., EHR, claims, lab, imaging, external registry, wearable device)
hazard: Unidentified data sources prevent privacy and suitability review.

statement: Record each dataset's acquisition date and method.
quote: Date of acquisition and method (e.g., EHR extract, vendor API, manual upload)
hazard: Untraceable acquisition obscures data provenance and authorization.

statement: Identify the organizational unit or individual owning each data source.
quote: Data owner (the organizational unit or individual responsible for the source system)
hazard: Unclear ownership impedes accountability for data governance.

statement: Identify the individuals accountable for governance of each dataset.
quote: Data steward (the individual(s) accountable for governance of this dataset)
hazard: Dataset governance responsibilities remain unassigned.

statement: Record the legal basis for using each dataset.
quote: Legal basis for use (e.g., Business Associate Agreement, Data Use Agreement, de-identification, patient consent)
hazard: AI systems use data without a valid legal basis.

statement: Classify dataset sensitivity, including PHI, de-identified, synthetic, and publicly available data.
quote: Sensitivity classification (PHI, de-identified, synthetic, publicly available)
hazard: Data receives protections inappropriate to its sensitivity.

statement: Identify sensitive data categories subject to heightened legal or organizational protections.
quote: Other types of sensitive data categories may include: payment or financial data; data subject to heightened protections under state or federal law (e.g., behavioral health records, substance use disorder treatment records, reproductive health information, HIV/AIDS-related data, or data about minors); or other confidential categories defined in the organization's data classification policy.
hazard: Especially sensitive information is handled without required additional protections.

statement: Record which AI systems or models use each dataset.
quote: Linked AI systems or models using this dataset
hazard: Dataset use across AI systems cannot be traced.

statement: Document a retention period for each dataset.
quote: Retention period and disposition plan (when will data be destroyed or archived?)
hazard: Patient data is retained indefinitely or longer than justified.

statement: Document each dataset's destruction or archiving plan.
quote: Retention period and disposition plan (when will data be destroyed or archived?)
hazard: Data persists without a governed disposition process.

statement: Document secondary data flows when AI outputs feed back into model updating or performance assessment.
quote: If feedback loops exist, organizations may want to additionally include information on the secondary data flow, document its legal basis, and note whether the feedback loop generates new types of data.
hazard: Feedback-loop data use escapes the original data inventory.

statement: Document the legal basis for feedback-loop data use.
quote: If feedback loops exist, organizations may want to additionally include information on the secondary data flow, document its legal basis, and note whether the feedback loop generates new types of data.
hazard: Secondary use of AI outputs lacks legal authorization.

statement: Record whether AI feedback loops generate new data types.
quote: If feedback loops exist, organizations may want to additionally include information on the secondary data flow, document its legal basis, and note whether the feedback loop generates new types of data.
hazard: Newly generated data categories remain unclassified and ungoverned.

statement: Document the data sources and fields accessed by live inference systems.
quote: the register should document which data sources and fields are accessed, the legal basis for that access (noting that operational BAAs may not automatically cover all AI-specific uses), and what happens when expected data fields are missing or anomalous.
hazard: Runtime data access is omitted from governance records.

statement: Document the legal basis for runtime data access rather than assuming operational BAAs cover AI-specific uses.
quote: the register should document which data sources and fields are accessed, the legal basis for that access (noting that operational BAAs may not automatically cover all AI-specific uses), and what happens when expected data fields are missing or anomalous.
hazard: Live AI data access exceeds existing contractual authorization.

statement: Document system behavior when expected runtime data fields are missing or anomalous.
quote: the register should document which data sources and fields are accessed, the legal basis for that access (noting that operational BAAs may not automatically cover all AI-specific uses), and what happens when expected data fields are missing or anomalous.
hazard: Unspecified handling of missing or anomalous inputs causes unreliable outputs.

statement: Use live input distributions to inform ongoing data-quality monitoring.
quote: The live data distribution feeding the model at runtime may also inform ongoing data quality and bias monitoring under Control 4.
hazard: Changes in operational data quality go undetected.

statement: Use live input distributions to inform ongoing bias monitoring.
quote: The live data distribution feeding the model at runtime may also inform ongoing data quality and bias monitoring under Control 4.
hazard: Runtime population changes introduce undetected bias.

statement: Record how new data enters continuously learning or periodically updated models.
quote: the register should capture not only the original training dataset but also the mechanism by which new data enters the model, the cadence and criteria for updates, and who is responsible for approving those updates.
hazard: Post-deployment learning introduces undocumented data.

statement: Record the cadence and criteria for updates to continuously learning or periodically retrained models.
quote: the register should capture not only the original training dataset but also the mechanism by which new data enters the model, the cadence and criteria for updates, and who is responsible for approving those updates.
hazard: Model changes occur without documented update rules.

statement: Identify who approves updates to continuously learning or periodically retrained models.
quote: the register should capture not only the original training dataset but also the mechanism by which new data enters the model, the cadence and criteria for updates, and who is responsible for approving those updates.
hazard: Model updates proceed without accountable approval.

statement: Record the sources included in each RAG retrieval corpus.
quote: Register entries for RAG systems should capture what sources are included, the criteria for inclusion, and the update cadence — since a stale or poorly governed retrieval corpus introduces the same quality and bias risks as a poorly prepared training dataset.
hazard: Unknown retrieval sources undermine output grounding and traceability.

statement: Document inclusion criteria for RAG retrieval corpora.
quote: Register entries for RAG systems should capture what sources are included, the criteria for inclusion, and the update cadence — since a stale or poorly governed retrieval corpus introduces the same quality and bias risks as a poorly prepared training dataset.
hazard: Unsuitable or biased sources enter retrieval corpora.

statement: Document the update cadence for RAG retrieval corpora.
quote: Register entries for RAG systems should capture what sources are included, the criteria for inclusion, and the update cadence — since a stale or poorly governed retrieval corpus introduces the same quality and bias risks as a poorly prepared training dataset.
hazard: Stale retrieval content produces outdated or biased outputs.

statement: Document the patient-data categories permitted in generative AI prompts or context windows.
quote: Data categories permitted in prompts or context windows: For generative AI systems, what patient data may be included in prompts or passed to the model as context is itself a data governance decision. This should be documented, including the data categories permitted, any categories that are prohibited, and the legal basis for including PHI where applicable.
hazard: Users provide patient information beyond authorized prompt scope.

statement: Document patient-data categories prohibited from generative AI prompts or context windows.
quote: This should be documented, including the data categories permitted, any categories that are prohibited, and the legal basis for including PHI where applicable.
hazard: Sensitive data enters prompts because exclusions are unspecified.

statement: Document the legal basis for including PHI in generative AI prompts or context.
quote: This should be documented, including the data categories permitted, any categories that are prohibited, and the legal basis for including PHI where applicable.
hazard: PHI is disclosed to generative AI without legal authorization.

statement: Create a separate register entry for each agentic system's persistent memory store.
quote: Persistent memory stores: If an agentic system maintains memory across sessions (e.g. retaining clinical context, user preferences, or prior interactions) that memory store should have its own register entry, with access controls, a defined retention period, and BAA coverage confirmed.
hazard: Persistent agent memory becomes an ungoverned patient-data repository.

statement: Establish access controls for persistent agent memory stores.
quote: Persistent memory stores: If an agentic system maintains memory across sessions (e.g. retaining clinical context, user preferences, or prior interactions) that memory store should have its own register entry, with access controls, a defined retention period, and BAA coverage confirmed.
hazard: Unauthorized access exposes retained clinical context or interactions.

statement: Define a retention period for persistent agent memory.
quote: Persistent memory stores: If an agentic system maintains memory across sessions (e.g. retaining clinical context, user preferences, or prior interactions) that memory store should have its own register entry, with access controls, a defined retention period, and BAA coverage confirmed.
hazard: Agent memory retains patient information indefinitely.

statement: Confirm BAA coverage for persistent agent memory stores.
quote: Persistent memory stores: If an agentic system maintains memory across sessions (e.g. retaining clinical context, user preferences, or prior interactions) that memory store should have its own register entry, with access controls, a defined retention period, and BAA coverage confirmed.
hazard: Persistent patient context is stored outside contractual privacy protections.

statement: Document all systems, databases, and external APIs an agent is authorized to access at runtime.
quote: For agentic AI that queries multiple systems or APIs to complete tasks, the register should document which systems, databases, and external APIs the agent is authorized to access — not only the datasets used to develop it.
hazard: Agent access expands beyond documented authorization boundaries.

statement: Review agent data-access authorization whenever system capabilities or integrations change.
quote: This authorization scope should be reviewed whenever the system's capabilities or integrations change.
hazard: New capabilities or integrations enable unauthorized data access.

statement: Begin data inventory work with higher-risk AI tools and tools accessing sensitive data.
quote: Begin by documenting data currently used in higher-risk AI tools or tools that touch sensitive data sources.
hazard: The most consequential undocumented data flows remain unaddressed.

statement: Include vendor-deployed tools that transmit data to vendors in the AI data inventory.
quote: This should include vendor-deployed tools where data is transmitted to the vendor.
hazard: External vendor data flows escape organizational oversight.

statement: Select a register format appropriate to organizational size, capacity, and industry best practices.
quote: Select a register format appropriate to your organization's size, capacity, and industry best practices.
hazard: An impractical register cannot be maintained reliably.

statement: Assign a named individual to keep each dataset's register entry accurate.
quote: Each dataset entry should have a named individual responsible for keeping the record accurate.
hazard: Register entries become inaccurate because maintenance responsibility is unclear.

statement: Link the data acquisition register to the organizational AI Inventory Registry.
quote: The data acquisition register should link to the AI Inventory Registry maintained under Domain 3: Organizational Resources Playbook.
hazard: Disconnected inventories prevent tracing AI systems to governed data.

statement: Reference accessed datasets in every AI inventory entry, or at minimum in entries for higher-risk tools.
quote: Each AI solution in the inventory, or at minimum, each higher risk tool, should reference the datasets it touches.
hazard: AI tool data dependencies cannot be identified.

statement: Establish a regular review cadence for the data register.
quote: Establish a review cadence and specify triggers for data register updates.
hazard: Register information becomes stale between deployment changes.

statement: Update the register when procuring AI tools, when vendor data practices change, or when accessing new data sources.
quote: Review and update the register when new AI tools are procured, when vendors change their data practices, or when new data sources are accessed.
hazard: New or changed data flows remain undocumented.

statement: Align register review frequency with AI tool risk and data sensitivity.
quote: Consider aligning review frequency to the risk level of the AI tool and data involved: higher-risk tools (e.g., tools supporting clinical decision-making, tools with access to large volumes of PHI, etc.) may warrant more frequent data governance review, while lower-risk administrative tools may be reviewed annually or upon significant operational change.
hazard: High-risk data flows are reviewed too infrequently.

statement: Define how long the data register is retained after the AI solution is decommissioned.
quote: Establish a retention period for the data register after the AI solution itself is decommissioned.
hazard: Premature record disposal prevents retrospective accountability.

statement: Ensure BAAs cover data leaving the organization for AI vendors.
quote: Focus is on documenting data flows to external AI vendors, particularly ensuring BAAs are in place for any data leaving the organization.
hazard: External AI data transmissions lack contractual privacy protections.

statement: Integrate the data catalog with the EHR platform.
quote: Uses a data catalog integrated with the EHR platform.
hazard: Disconnected cataloging misses EHR-related AI data flows.

statement: Supplement manual register entries with automated metadata capture for structured data.
quote: Automated metadata capture supplements manual entries for structured data.
hazard: Manual metadata capture leaves incomplete or outdated records.

statement: Add documentation steps specifically for unstructured data such as clinical notes and imaging.
quote: Unstructured data (clinical notes, imaging) requires additional documentation steps.
hazard: Structured-data documentation practices miss unstructured-data risks.

statement: Review the register quarterly with the IT governance team.
quote: Register reviewed with IT governance team quarterly; major updates triggered by new AI procurement.
hazard: Data register inaccuracies persist without governance review.

statement: Integrate the enterprise data catalog with the MLOps platform.
quote: Enterprise data catalog fully integrated with the MLOps platform and AI inventory.
hazard: Data governance records become disconnected from operational AI lifecycle changes.

statement: Link data register entries to applicable IRB protocols.
quote: Register linked to IRB protocols, model cards, and data use agreement status.
hazard: Research authorization cannot be traced to AI data use.

statement: Link data register entries to model cards.
quote: Register linked to IRB protocols, model cards, and data use agreement status.
hazard: Model documentation is disconnected from data provenance and limitations.

statement: Review register information in real time through automated dashboards.
quote: Reviewed in real-time via automated dashboards.
hazard: Rapid changes in AI data use remain unnoticed.

statement: Assign an AI Domain Steward responsibility for assessing data classification and quality requirements.
quote: The AI Domain Steward is responsible for assessing data requirements for classification and quality, facilitating model adoption by partnering with use case owners, ensuring proper documentation of use cases and implementation procedures, and coordinating compliance with responsible AI principles.
hazard: Data classification and quality requirements lack an accountable owner.

statement: Have the AI Domain Steward partner with use-case owners during model adoption.
quote: The AI Domain Steward is responsible for assessing data requirements for classification and quality, facilitating model adoption by partnering with use case owners, ensuring proper documentation of use cases and implementation procedures, and coordinating compliance with responsible AI principles.
hazard: Model adoption proceeds without coordination between governance and use-case owners.

statement: Assign the AI Domain Steward responsibility for ensuring use cases are documented.
quote: The AI Domain Steward is responsible for assessing data requirements for classification and quality, facilitating model adoption by partnering with use case owners, ensuring proper documentation of use cases and implementation procedures, and coordinating compliance with responsible AI principles.
hazard: Undocumented use cases prevent scope and accountability review.

statement: Assign the AI Domain Steward responsibility for ensuring implementation procedures are documented.
quote: The AI Domain Steward is responsible for assessing data requirements for classification and quality, facilitating model adoption by partnering with use case owners, ensuring proper documentation of use cases and implementation procedures, and coordinating compliance with responsible AI principles.
hazard: Undocumented implementation practices hinder oversight and reproducibility.

statement: Assign the AI Domain Steward responsibility for coordinating compliance with responsible AI principles.
quote: The AI Domain Steward is responsible for assessing data requirements for classification and quality, facilitating model adoption by partnering with use case owners, ensuring proper documentation of use cases and implementation procedures, and coordinating compliance with responsible AI principles.
hazard: Responsible AI compliance responsibilities are fragmented.

statement: Coordinate data-governance domains through a central Data Governance Council.
quote: Their governance domains span Consumer, Clinical, Finance, Payer, Provider, Workforce, Location, and Technical Artifact categories, which are coordinated through a central Data Governance Council.
hazard: Cross-domain data governance decisions lack coordination.

statement: Include organizational security and privacy requirements in AI DUAs or BAAs.
quote: Control 4.3.2: Establish comprehensive Data Use Agreements and/or Business Associate Agreements that includes information on permitted and prohibited uses, compliance with organization’s security and privacy requirements, rights to audit, consequences of non-compliance, and data return/destruction terms at end of use.
hazard: Vendor contracts omit organizational data-protection requirements.

statement: Confirm that vendor data sharing is necessary for the use case before negotiating a DUA.
quote: Before negotiating a Data Use Agreement, organizations benefit from first confirming that sharing data with a vendor is the right approach for the specific use case.
hazard: Patient-level data is shared when the service could operate without it.

statement: Determine the minimum data the vendor needs before legal review.
quote: Asking 'what is the minimum data this vendor actually needs for the contracted service?' before engaging legal review often results in a narrower data scope, lower compliance risk, and stronger negotiating leverage.
hazard: Overbroad vendor requests expose unnecessary patient data.

statement: Codify the previously agreed data-sharing scope in the DUA.
quote: The DUA should codify the outcome of this decision — it should not be the first place the decision gets made.
hazard: Contract negotiations establish data scope without prior necessity assessment.

statement: Ask vendors to document each requested patient-data element and its service-specific justification in writing.
quote: One practical starting step is to ask vendors requesting patient data to document, in writing, the specific data elements needed and the reason each element is required for the contracted service.
hazard: Unjustified data requests enter contracts without scrutiny.

statement: Explicitly enumerate permitted vendor data uses rather than relying on general service-purpose language.
quote: Permissible use definition: Explicitly list what the vendor is permitted to do with the data. General language such as “for services purposes” is insufficient and may permit unauthorized model training.
hazard: Vague contract language permits unauthorized model training or secondary use.

statement: Explicitly prohibit vendor training or fine-tuning on organizational data when those uses are not permitted.
quote: AI training restriction: If the vendor is not permitted to train or fine-tune models on your data, this must be stated explicitly.
hazard: Vendors reuse organizational data for unauthorized model development.

statement: Define the scope of vendor training when training on organizational data is permitted.
quote: Conversely, if training is permitted, define its scope and any resulting IP rights.
hazard: Permitted model training expands beyond the organization's intended authorization.

statement: Define resulting intellectual-property rights when permitting vendor training on organizational data.
quote: Conversely, if training is permitted, define its scope and any resulting IP rights.
hazard: Rights over models trained on organizational data remain disputed or unclear.

statement: Contractually prohibit vendors from linking datasets in ways that could enable re-identification.
quote: Re-identification prohibition: Contractually forbid the vendor from attempting to re-identify de-identified data or linking datasets in ways that could enable re-identification.
hazard: Vendor dataset linkage reconstructs patient identities.

statement: Require vendors to use only the minimum data necessary for the specified purpose.
quote: Data Minimization: Require vendors to use only the minimum data necessary for the specified purpose.
hazard: Excessive vendor processing increases privacy exposure.

statement: Prohibit vendors from retaining data beyond what is required.
quote: Prohibit the vendor from retaining data beyond what is required.
hazard: Unnecessary vendor retention prolongs breach and misuse risks.

statement: Specify vendor encryption requirements for data at rest.
quote: Security requirements: Specify minimum standards including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and regular independent security assessments (e.g., SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST).
hazard: Stored patient data is exposed through compromised storage.

statement: Specify vendor encryption requirements for data in transit.
quote: Security requirements: Specify minimum standards including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and regular independent security assessments (e.g., SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST).
hazard: Patient data is intercepted during transmission.

statement: Require vendors to implement role-based access controls.
quote: Security requirements: Specify minimum standards including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and regular independent security assessments (e.g., SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST).
hazard: Vendor personnel access data beyond their authorized roles.

statement: Require regular independent vendor security assessments, such as SOC 2 Type II or HITRUST.
quote: Security requirements: Specify minimum standards including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and regular independent security assessments (e.g., SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST).
hazard: Vendor security weaknesses remain unverified or undetected.

statement: Reserve rights to audit vendor DUA compliance, including access logs, security practices, and data handling.
quote: Audit rights: Reserve the right to audit vendor compliance with the DUA, including access logs, security practices, and data handling procedures.
hazard: Vendor compliance claims cannot be independently checked.

statement: Include a contractual right to terminate the agreement for breach.
quote: Penalties for non-compliance: Define remedies for breach, including the right to terminate the agreement and seek financial damages.

statement: Include a contractual right to seek financial damages for breach.
quote: Penalties for non-compliance: Define remedies for breach, including the right to terminate the agreement and seek financial damages.
hazard: Data misuse lacks enforceable financial remedies.

statement: Require vendors to return or certifiably destroy all raw datasets upon contract termination.
quote: Data return and destruction: Require vendors to return or certifiably destroy all raw datasets, stop further training, and delete any models fine-tuned on your organizations data (if feasible) — upon contract termination.
hazard: Vendor data persists after termination without verifiable disposal.

statement: Require vendors to stop further training on organizational data upon contract termination.
quote: Data return and destruction: Require vendors to return or certifiably destroy all raw datasets, stop further training, and delete any models fine-tuned on your organizations data (if feasible) — upon contract termination.
hazard: Vendor training continues after contractual authorization ends.

statement: Require vendors to delete models fine-tuned on organizational data at contract termination, where feasible.
quote: Data return and destruction: Require vendors to return or certifiably destroy all raw datasets, stop further training, and delete any models fine-tuned on your organizations data (if feasible) — upon contract termination.
hazard: Fine-tuned models retain organizational data after the vendor relationship ends.

statement: Require vendors to disclose subcontractors and downstream processors that will access organizational data.

statement: Develop and maintain an incident response plan for data breaches and security incidents.
quote: Incident Response Plan: Develop and maintain an incident response plan to address data breaches and other security incidents promptly.

statement: Review organizational rights in vendor models, features, and analytical outputs derived from organizational data.

statement: Prevent vendor data uses that could harm patients or the organization.

statement: Consider IP co-ownership terms when the organization has unique data assets and capacity to enforce complex provisions.

statement: Consider revenue-sharing terms when the organization has unique data assets and capacity to enforce complex provisions.
quote: IP co-ownership or revenuesharing terms may be worth pursuing for organizations with unique data assets and the legal capacity to enforce complex provisions, but should be approached with realistic expectations about negotiating leverage, particularly for smaller HDOs or community health organizations.
hazard: Vendor commercialization of organizational data produces no negotiated organizational benefit.

statement: Assess negotiating leverage realistically before pursuing IP co-ownership or revenue-sharing provisions.
quote: IP co-ownership or revenuesharing terms may be worth pursuing for organizations with unique data assets and the legal capacity to enforce complex provisions, but should be approached with realistic expectations about negotiating leverage, particularly for smaller HDOs or community health organizations.
hazard: Unrealistic contracting objectives consume limited legal and organizational resources.

statement: Clarify the contractual definition of derivatives, including whether models count as derivatives.

statement: Clarify whether vendors may retain embeddings, feature vectors, or synthetic data generated from organizational data.

statement: Identify the specific models or features vendors develop using organizational data.

statement: Assess whether vendor product improvements materially depend on organizational data.

statement: Clarify the disposition of data derivatives upon contract termination.

statement: Require vendors of agentic AI to disclose persistent memory retained across sessions and mechanisms to scope or expire it.

statement: Enumerate and govern each sub-agent when an AI system orchestrates other agents.

statement: Require agentic AI audit logs granular enough to reconstruct incidents.

statement: Specify in the contract the frequency and format of vendor monitoring reports.

statement: Specify vendor obligations when performance degradation, model drift, or safety signals are detected.

statement: Define and document manual workarounds for each workflow that degrades if the AI tool is unavailable.

statement: Require vendors to provide recurring disaster recovery summaries.

statement: Set SLA notification timelines for outages, including failures of upstream foundation model or cloud providers.

statement: Define KPIs such as model performance thresholds and incident response times up front in the contract or statement of work.

statement: Hold a recurring accountability review of vendor KPI performance, separate from contract renewal, with escalation and documented corrective actions.

statement: Ensure the contract identifies whether the AI solution has or may require FDA clearance or approval.

statement: Specify which party is responsible for pursuing, maintaining, or reporting changes to FDA authorization.

statement: Document pre-defined triggers, decision-makers, and timelines for each enforcement tier in the contract.

statement: Define the scope of use, constraints, and dependencies before deploying AI products.

statement: Define technical performance targets and real-world measures of success for AI products.

statement: Design and test optimal workflows for integrating clinician-facing AI products.

statement: Locally validate AI products before clinical use and identify foreseeable risks.

statement: Disseminate information about AI products to the affected clinicians.

statement: Implement mechanisms to prevent the inappropriate use of AI products beyond their intended scope.

statement: Continuously monitor deployed AI solutions and the affected work environments over time.

statement: Conduct audits of AI products to complement ongoing monitoring and proactively identify emerging risks.

statement: Plan for and minimize disruptions and harms that may result from decommissioning AI products.

statement: Default to Safe Harbor de-identification for most AI use cases.

statement: Explore pooled de-identification expertise through HCCNs, regional HIEs, or state hospital associations.

statement: Work with vendors to accept de-identified data instead of PHI wherever technically feasible.

statement: Implement a formal AI data-request review process requiring documented justification for every requested data element.

statement: Document why each field is necessary for its intended purpose in the data acquisition register.

statement: Assign a privacy officer or legal counsel to monitor state privacy-law developments.

statement: Use modular DUA addenda that permit state-specific provisions to be updated without renegotiating the entire agreement.

statement: Subscribe to privacy-law tracking or guidance updates, such as IAPP or HHS OCR resources.

statement: Include state-law review in the annual AI contract-monitoring cycle.

statement: Prioritize state and federal regulatory requirements for AI deployments, especially solutions qualifying as Software as a Medical Device.

statement: Consult clinical, technical, compliance, ethics, and patient/community advisors when designing and stewarding AI programs.

statement: Obtain vendors' commitment to notify the organization of embedded AI features, artifacts, and significant updates before activation.

statement: Establish acceptable blanket standard operating procedures for AI solutions introduced through enterprise platforms.

statement: Risk-categorize embedded AI features to prioritize deeper oversight.

statement: Govern AI solutions across a defined lifecycle for every relevant ingestion modality.

statement: Inventory AI features in existing enterprise platforms on a recurring schedule.

statement: Assign an explicit owner for each enterprise platform's AI-feature inventory.

statement: Use vendor administration consoles and release notes to discover embedded AI features.

statement: Set a recurring re-review schedule for embedded AI features in the AI Vendor Register.

statement: Invoke contractual change-notification clauses during embedded AI governance review.

statement: Request deletion of organizational content where the vendor offers that option.

statement: Request available vendor opt-outs for use of organizational content.

statement: Add AI disclosure clauses to standard vendor contract templates.

statement: Use comparative vendor-performance data to justify negotiated service-level agreements or protections.

hazard: Known AI risks remaining unaddressed in operational practice.

statement: Record each AI vendor relationship's solution name, ingestion modality, use-case type, applicable contracts, and expiration or renewal date.

statement: Start AI vendor inventory work with the existing EHR vendor in smaller organizations.

hazard: Staff unaware they are relying on AI outputs

statement: Inform patients, where appropriate, when a third-party AI solution is involved in their interactions.
quote: When a third party AI solution is used in direct workflows or patient interactions, the HDO should ensure that end users (clinical, operational, or administrative staff, and where appropriate, patients) are made aware that a third party AI solution is involved.
hazard: Patients unknowingly interacting with AI

statement: Disclose to end users the known AI limitations relevant to them and how to report unexpected AI behavior.
quote: Transparency disclosures may include: the nature of the AI solution and its role in the workflow; the fact that a third party vendor is involved; known limitations that are relevant to users; and how to report unexpected behavior.
hazard: Users over-rely on AI or cannot report malfunctions

statement: Provide education and training to end users of AI solutions as a risk mitigation.
quote: Education and training of end users is an important risk-mitigator.
hazard: Inappropriate use of AI by untrained users

statement: Contractually require vendors to disclose known limitations, subgroup performance variability, out-of-distribution behavior, contraindicated conditions, and known safety concerns.
quote: Vendors should be contractually obligated to disclose known limitations, risks, and performance characteristics of their AI solutions or systems — including subgroup performance variability, out-of-distribution behavior, conditions under which the model should not be used, and any known safety concerns identified during validation.
hazard: Deployment in populations or conditions where the model fails

statement: Contractually require vendors to notify the organization of material model changes, including version updates, retraining, or newly identified limitations.
quote: Disclosure obligations should be ongoing: vendors should be required to notify the organization when material changes to the model occur, including version updates, retraining events, or newly identified limitations.
hazard: Silent model changes altering behavior without review

statement: Contractually require vendors to notify the HDO if the solution's FDA classification changes, as an explicit disclosure trigger.
quote: Vendors should also be contractually obligated to notify HDOs if the vendor’s FDA classification changes (e.g., moves into SaMD). Regulatory reclassification needs to be an explicit disclosure trigger.
hazard: Unrecognized regulatory obligations after reclassification

statement: Require vendors to identify at intake the third-party foundation model (e.g., LLM) provider underlying their solution.
quote: For vendor-built AI solutions that incorporate third party foundation model (e.g., large language models licensed from external providers) or open-source components, the vendor should provide at intake: (a) The identity of the third party model provider.
hazard: Hidden foundation model dependencies and associated risks

statement: Require vendors to disclose foundation model license terms and any restrictions relevant to healthcare data.
quote: (b) The license terms under which the component is used and any restrictions relevant to healthcare data.
hazard: License terms permitting inappropriate use of healthcare data

statement: Require vendors to disclose constraints they apply to the foundation model's behavior for the healthcare deployment context.
quote: (c) Any vendor-applied constraints on the foundation model's behavior specific to the healthcare deployment context.
hazard: Unknown or absent guardrails on LLM behavior

statement: Require vendors to describe their process for monitoring and disclosing foundation model provider changes that affect system behavior.
quote: (d) The vendor's process for monitoring and disclosing changes made by the foundation model provider that affect system behavior.
hazard: Upstream LLM updates silently changing outputs

statement: Treat missing foundation model documentation from a vendor as equivalent to undisclosed model limitations in risk assessment.
quote: HDOs should treat absence of this documentation as equivalent to undisclosed model limitations.
hazard: Underestimating risk of poorly documented LLM solutions

statement: Factor the depth of vendor-provided documentation into organizational AI risk assessment.
quote: HDOs should factor the depth of available documentation into their risk processes
hazard: Risk tiering ignores documentation gaps

statement: Require vendors of agentic AI to disclose which actions the agent takes without confirmation and which require human approval.
quote: the vendor should additionally disclose: Scope of autonomy: Which actions can the agent take without confirmation? Which require human approval?
hazard: Autonomous agent actions taken without appropriate human approval

statement: Require vendors of agentic AI to disclose which systems the agent can read, write, or invoke and its external API dependencies.
quote: Tool and integration access: Which systems can the agent read from, write to, or invoke? Which external APIs or third party services does it depend on?
hazard: Agents accessing or altering systems beyond intended scope

statement: Require vendors of agentic AI to disclose which agent actions are reversible and which are irreversible.
quote: Action reversibility: Which actions are reversible and which are not (e.g., medication orders, billing submissions, external communications)?
hazard: Irreversible harmful actions like erroneous medication orders

statement: Require vendors of agentic AI to disclose conditions that trigger human escalation or automatic halt.
quote: Escalation and circuit breakers: What conditions trigger human escalation or automatic halt?
hazard: Runaway agent behavior without escalation or shutdown

statement: Require vendors of agentic AI to disclose persistent memory retained across sessions and mechanisms to scope or expire it.
quote: Memory and context boundaries: What persistent memory does the agent retain across sessions, and what mechanisms exist to scope or expire it?
hazard: Inappropriate retention or leakage of patient data across sessions

statement: Enumerate and govern each sub-agent orchestrated by a multi-agent AI system.
quote: Multi-agent considerations: If the system orchestrates other agents, each should be enumerated and governed.
hazard: Ungoverned sub-agents acting within the system

statement: Require agentic AI audit logs granular enough to reconstruct incidents.
quote: Audit trail granularity: Logs sufficient for incident reconstruction.
hazard: Inability to investigate agent-caused incidents

statement: Include in vendor contracts an explicit monitoring plan specifying performance metrics tracked and reported, and report frequency and format.
quote: Vendor contracts should include an explicit monitoring plan specifying: What performance metrics the vendor will track and report. The frequency and format of monitoring reports shared with the HDO.
hazard: Undetected performance degradation after deployment

statement: Specify in contracts the vendor's obligations when performance degradation, drift, or safety signals are detected, and the HDO's right to request monitoring data.
quote: The vendor’s obligations when performance degradation, model drift, or safety signals are detected. The HDO’s right to request monitoring data.
hazard: Drift or safety signals detected but not acted upon

statement: Include concrete contractual remedies (service credits, fee withholding, expanded audit rights, feature suspension) for missed monitoring reporting obligations.
quote: Contracts should include concrete remedies such as service credits, fee withholding or refund rights, expanded audit rights, and, for repeat or sustained failures, suspension of new feature activation or new use cases pending remediation.
hazard: Monitoring obligations treated as optional by vendors

statement: Condition contract renewal on the vendor's demonstrated record of meeting monitoring reporting obligations and KPI performance.
quote: Renewal should be conditioned on the vendor's demonstrated record of meeting reporting obligations during the prior term, and KPI performance over the term should be formally considered in the renewal decision.
hazard: Renewing contracts with vendors who fail monitoring duties

statement: Define Recovery Time and Recovery Point Objectives per AI service in SLAs, graduated for critical patient safety solutions.
quote: Down-time planning and recovery objectives: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) defined per AI service, with a graduated approach for critical patient safety solutions.
hazard: Prolonged AI outages disrupting critical care

statement: Define manual workarounds for each clinical or operational workflow degraded if the AI becomes unavailable.
quote: Business continuity: Defined manual workarounds for each clinical or operational workflow that becomes degraded if the AI is unavailable; the contract should recommend the vendor surface and document these workarounds.
hazard: Care disruption when AI service fails

statement: Require vendors to provide recurring disaster recovery summaries.
quote: Vendor should provide recurring disaster recovery summaries.
hazard: Untested vendor recovery capabilities

statement: Require vendors to provide a written map of upstream dependencies (e.g., foundation models, hosted inference) and functionality lost if each goes offline.
quote: AI dependency map: The vendor should provide a written map of upstream dependencies (e.g., foundation models, hosted inference services, cloud regions, identity providers, data lakes, and third party APIs) and identify what functionality becomes unavailable if each dependency goes offline.
hazard: Unanticipated failures from upstream LLM or cloud outages

statement: Define SLA notification timelines for outages, including failures of upstream cloud or foundation model providers.
quote: Notification timelines for outages and dependency failures: Including outages of upstream providers (e.g., the cloud or foundation model vendor) not owned directly by the AI vendor.
hazard: HDO unaware of upstream outages affecting AI functionality

statement: Define KPIs up front in the contract, such as model performance thresholds, incident response times, and update cadence.
quote: Defined KPIs up-front in the contract or statement of work (e.g., model performance thresholds, incident response times, update cadence, training/support responsiveness).
hazard: No measurable standard for vendor performance

statement: Tie AI vendor KPIs to SLAs with defined remedies such as service credits, fee reductions, or termination rights.
quote: KPIs tied to Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with defined remedies such as service credits, fee reductions, and/or termination rights.
hazard: Unenforceable performance expectations

statement: Hold a recurring KPI review cadence, separate from contract renewal, to escalate issues and document corrective actions.
quote: A recurring accountability cadence at which KPI performance is reviewed, issues are escalated, and corrective actions are documented. This should occur separately from contract renewal
hazard: Weak KPI enforcement over multi-year contracts

statement: Ensure the contract identifies whether the AI solution has or may require FDA clearance and which party maintains FDA authorization.
quote: Ensure the contract clearly identifies whether the solution has been or may require FDA clearance or approval. Specify which party is responsible for pursuing, maintaining, or reporting changes to FDA authorization.
hazard: Unclear regulatory obligations for device-like AI

statement: Have legal counsel familiar with FDA SaMD regulations review contracts for AI tools that may be regulated devices.
quote: Legal counsel familiar with FDA SaMD regulations should review any contracts involving tools that may fall under this framework.
hazard: Regulatory noncompliance in AI device contracts

statement: Include an explicit tiered enforcement mechanism (notice and cure, remediation plan, access suspension, termination) with defined timelines in AI vendor contracts.
quote: Contracts should include an explicit tiered enforcement mechanism with defined timelines:
hazard: Ad hoc, ineffective response to vendor noncompliance

statement: Document pre-defined triggers, decision-makers, and timelines for each enforcement tier in the contract.
quote: Each tier should have pre-defined triggers, decision-makers, and timelines documented in the contract so enforcement does not depend on ad hoc escalation.
hazard: Enforcement stalled by ad hoc escalation

statement: Include bankruptcy or insolvency triggers granting code escrow access, accelerated data return or destruction, and termination rights.
quote: Bankruptcy or insolvency triggers: Filing of bankruptcy, assignment for the benefit of creditors, or similar action(s) should trigger access to (a) source code escrow or operating documentation, (b) accelerated data return / destruction obligations, and (c) the right to terminate without further notice.
hazard: Loss of service and data exposure upon vendor insolvency

statement: Require written notice of vendor change of control with rights to re-review, terminate without penalty, and require acquirer ratification of the AI addendum.
quote: Change-of-control or acquisition provisions: Written notice to the customer of any proposed change of control, with the customer's right to (a) re-review the deal for AI governance compatibility (e.g., new owner's data practices, new owner's foundation model dependencies), (b) terminate without penalty if AI governance posture materially worsens
hazard: Acquirer weakens data practices or changes foundation model dependencies

statement: Define a product sunset notice period and transition support, including export of customer data and configurations in usable form.
quote: Product sunset or discontinuation: Defined notice period and required transition support, including export of customer data and any organization-specific configurations in usable form.
hazard: Abrupt discontinuation disrupting workflows and stranding data

statement: For high-risk or critical patient safety AI, require escrow of model weights, inference code, and documentation released upon vendor failure.
quote: Source code and model escrow: For high-risk or critical patient safety solutions, require escrow of model weights, inference code, documentation, and/or runbooks, with release triggers tied to vendor failure events.
hazard: Loss of critical AI capability upon vendor failure

statement: Contractually prohibit vendors from remotely disabling the product without honoring wind-down terms allowing continued use of the latest version.
quote: the contract should specify that the customer may continue using the most recent version (e.g., under a perpetual, royalty-free license for a defined wind-down period) and that the vendor cannot remotely disable the product without honoring the wind-down terms.
hazard: Sudden loss of AI function when vendor ends support

statement: Ensure the BAA for PHI-processing AI solutions includes an AI-specific appendix or addendum.
quote: For AI solutions that involve protected health information (PHI), organizations should ensure that a BAA with the vendor includes an AI-specific appendix or addendum that covers components of this playbook.
hazard: Standard BAA fails to govern AI use of PHI

statement: Update the AI BAA addendum when the AI is materially modified, PHI access scope changes, or new risks are identified.
quote: This AIspecific appendix or addendum should be treated as a living document and updated when the AI solution is materially modified, when the scope of PHI access changes, or when new risks are identified.
hazard: Outdated contractual protections after AI changes

statement: Do not rely on standard BAA language to cover AI model disclosure, AI responsibilities, and AI risk mitigation.
quote: HDOs should not assume that standard BAA language adequately addresses AI model disclosure, roles and responsibilities pertinent to the AI system and known risk, or contractual and operational risk mitigation provisions.
hazard: False assurance from generic BAA terms

statement: Obtain patient or end-user consent before the AI solution is used, captured in the record in plain language rather than boilerplate.
quote: Consent and disclosure at activation: Patient (or end user) consent obtained before the solution is used; consent captured into the record in plain language rather than as boilerplate.
hazard: Patients subjected to AI use without informed consent

statement: Disable the AI solution by default for sensitive encounter types, with a documented case-by-case enablement procedure.
quote: Default-off for sensitive contexts: The solution is disabled by default for encounter types or workflows where the risks outweigh the benefits, with a documented procedure to enable it on a case-by-case basis.
hazard: AI use in sensitive encounters where risks outweigh benefits

statement: Present AI outputs as drafts requiring affirmative human sign-off for designated use cases.
quote: Human review of outputs: for certain use cases, AI outputs are presented as drafts; sign-off requires affirmative human action; override and edit rates are tracked.
hazard: Erroneous AI outputs acted on without human review

statement: Track clinician override and edit rates of AI-drafted outputs.
quote: Human review of outputs: for certain use cases, AI outputs are presented as drafts; sign-off requires affirmative human action; override and edit rates are tracked.
hazard: Undetected output quality problems or rubber-stamping

statement: Assign a named clinical informatics, IT, or operational owner to each designated AI solution with documented contacts and vendor counterparts.
quote: Named owner and escalation path: A clinical informatics, IT, or operational owner is identified for certain AI solutions, with documented contact information and vendor-side counterparts.
hazard: No accountable owner to respond to AI problems

statement: Maintain the ability to disable the AI solution independently of the vendor for safety or privacy concerns.
quote: Independent rollback procedure: The HDO can disable the solution independently of the vendor for a safety or privacy concern.
hazard: Inability to stop a harmful AI tool promptly

statement: Configure vendor tenant settings to the lowest retention, lowest data sharing, and tightest data residency options available.
quote: Configuration to minimum data exposure: Tenant settings are configured to the lowest retention, lowest data sharing, and tightest residency options the vendor permits.
hazard: Excess retention or sharing of patient data by vendors

statement: Re-review AI solutions at a defined cadence and upon triggers such as material modification, foundation model change, or incident.
quote: Periodic re-review: At a defined cadence and on triggers (material modification, foundation model change, incident).
hazard: Unreviewed changes in AI behavior over time

statement: Capture AI-related incidents in the HDO incident system with an AI tag for review.
quote: AI-tagged incident reporting: Incidents are captured by the HDO with an AI tag for review.
hazard: AI-related incidents lost among general safety reports

statement: For autonomous AI agents, implement action allow-lists, environment isolation, dry-run modes for high-impact actions, and per-action audit logs.
quote: Agent-specific guardrails (for autonomous solutions): Develop action allow-lists, environment isolation, dryrun modes for high-impact actions, and per-action audit logs.
hazard: Autonomous agents taking unintended high-impact actions

statement: Establish escalation criteria for walking away from a contract when a vendor refuses risk responsibility or declines to disclose limitations.
quote: How will you handle situations where a vendor refuses to accept responsibility for certain risks or declines to disclose limitations? Do you have escalation criteria for walking away from a contract?
hazard: Accepting opaque vendors with unallocated risk

statement: Require disclosure of model cards or equivalent documentation as a condition of contract execution.
quote: Is your organization prepared to require disclosure of model cards or equivalent documentation as a condition of contract execution, and how will you evaluate what vendors provide?
hazard: Deploying AI without documentation of performance or limits

statement: Define which organizational roles monitor AI vendor compliance with contract terms after deployment.
quote: Have you defined which roles within your organization are responsible for ongoing monitoring of AI vendor compliance with contract terms after the solution is deployed?
hazard: Contract obligations unenforced post-deployment

statement: Ensure staff are aware of AI capabilities embedded in the solutions they use and understand their accountability under contract terms.
quote: Are relevant clinical, operational, or administrative staff aware of the AI capabilities embedded in solutions they use? Do they understand their accountability (if any) under current contract terms?
hazard: Staff unknowingly relying on embedded AI

statement: Maintain a central repository of approved AI contract clause templates for consistency across departments.
quote: As you build or update AI terms / contract language, how are you ensuring consistency across departments? Do you have a central repository for approved clause templates?
hazard: Inconsistent AI protections across departments

statement: Inventory AI features embedded in existing enterprise platforms and review each platform's data processing terms for AI model training provisions.
quote: Have you run an inventory of AI features embedded in your existing enterprise platforms, and re-read each platform's data processing terms for AI model training provisions?
hazard: Unknown embedded AI using organizational data for training

statement: Require updated vendor documentation and governance review before activating AI features introduced through routine vendor software updates.
quote: When a major EHR vendor announces an AI-powered clinical documentation feature as part of a routine software update, the AI Governance Committee invokes the change notification clause and requires the vendor to submit updated documentation before the feature is activated.
hazard: AI features activated through updates without review

statement: Contractually require vendors to provide updated model cards within a defined period after any retraining or model update.
quote: the vendor to provide updated model cards within 30 days of any retraining or model update;
hazard: Outdated documentation after model changes

statement: Develop or adopt a reusable clause library for AI-specific BAA appendices or addenda.
quote: CHAI recommends organizations develop or adopt a reusable clause library for AI-specific BAA appendices or addenda.
hazard: Inconsistent, ad hoc AI contract terms

statement: Include AI responsibility allocation between vendor and HDO in Concept of Operations documents.
quote: Include AI responsibility allocation in Concept of Operations (CONOPS) documents to define accountability across development, deployment, and monitoring.
hazard: Unclear ownership of lifecycle obligations

statement: Contractually require vendors to give prior written notice and obtain approval before using AI, including generative AI, in delivering services.
quote: Service Provider shall not use artificial intelligence, machine learning, generative AI, or similar technologies (collectively, “AI”) in the performance of the Services without first providing prior written notice to Customer and obtaining Customer’s prior written approval to the extent such AI:
hazard: Vendors deploying undisclosed generative AI in services

statement: Require vendor approval before using AI that interacts directly with patients or generates communications delivered to patients.
quote: (c) interacts directly with patients or consumers, or generates content or communications delivered to patients or consumers;
hazard: Unvetted AI-generated content reaching patients

statement: Assess the suitability of AI as a technical approach to address specific organizational problems.
quote: Also includes guides for determining different dimensions of problems and assessing the suitability of AI as a technical approach to address problems.
hazard: Adopting AI tools for problems better solved by non-AI methods.

statement: Assess the legal risks associated with adopting an AI product.
quote: Also includes guides for conducting preliminary assessments of AI products, assessing legal risks of AI product adoption, and auditing the process by which AI product investments are made.
hazard: Exposure to legal liability or regulatory violations from AI deployment.

statement: Audit the organizational process by which AI product investments are made.
quote: Also includes guides for conducting preliminary assessments of AI products, assessing legal risks of AI product adoption, and auditing the process by which AI product investments are made.
hazard: Unaccountable, unsystematic, or biased AI procurement processes.

statement: Define the scope of use, constraints, and dependencies before deploying AI products.
quote: This decision point features guides for defining the scope of use, constraints, and dependencies of AI products.
hazard: Unintended negative consequences from out-of-scope usage or unmanaged system dependencies.

statement: Define technical performance targets and real-world measures of success for AI products.
quote: Also includes guides for defining technical performance targets for AI products as well as measures of success for AI products used in practice.
hazard: Deploying ineffective AI tools with no clear benchmark to evaluate success.

statement: Design and test optimal workflows for integrating clinician-facing AI products.
quote: This decision point features guides for how organizations design and test optimal workflows for clinician-facing AI products.
hazard: Friction, inefficiency, or errors caused by poorly integrated clinical workflows.

statement: Locally validate AI products before clinical use and identify foreseeable risks.
quote: This decision point features guides for locally validating AI products before clinical use and identifying foreseeable and unresolved risks resulting from AI use in clinical care.
hazard: Model performance degradation or unforeseen harms due to local population differences.

statement: Disseminate information about AI products to the affected clinicians.
quote: This decision point features guides for disseminating information about AI products to affected clinicians and managing changes in the work environment caused by AI products put into clinical use.
hazard: Clinician distrust, confusion, or misuse due to lack of transparency.

statement: Implement mechanisms to prevent the inappropriate use of AI products beyond their intended scope.
quote: Also includes guides for preventing inappropriate use of AI products beyond their intended scope.
hazard: Patient harm from off-label or out-of-scope AI application.

statement: Continuously monitor deployed AI solutions and the affected work environments over time.
quote: This decision point features guides for monitoring AI solutions and affected work environments over time and sustaining improved outcomes achieved through AI use.
hazard: Unnoticed performance drift or ongoing adverse impacts on clinical workflows.

statement: Conduct audits of AI products to complement ongoing monitoring and proactively identify emerging risks.
quote: Also includes guides for conducting audits of AI products that complement ongoing monitoring and proactively identifying risks not envisioned at the time of clinical integration.
hazard: Unforeseen risks emerging after clinical integration that routine monitoring misses.

statement: Plan for and minimize disruptions and harms that may result from decommissioning AI products.
quote: Also includes guides for minimizing disruptions and harms that result from decommissioning AI products and disseminating information about AI product updates to affected clinicians.
hazard: Patient harm or severe workflow disruption when an AI system is retired.

statement: Assess available vendor training support before deployment and plan internal training capacity accordingly.
quote: HDOs should assess available vendor training support before deployment and plan for internal training capacity accordingly.
hazard: Inadequate vendor training leaves staff unprepared to use the AI tool safely

statement: Define minimum AI training requirements by role and AI risk tier, including required completion, refresh frequency, and competency validation for higher-risk solutions.
quote: Organizations should define minimum training requirements by role and AI risk tier, including required completion, refresh frequency, and competency validation for higher-risk AI solutions.
hazard: Staff using higher-risk AI without sufficient, validated competency

statement: Include explicit contractual obligations for vendors to proactively notify the organization of AI incidents.
quote: Organizations should ensure vendor contracts include explicit obligations for proactive incident notification, performance reporting, and communication of model changes.
hazard: Vendor-known incidents not communicated, leaving the organization unaware of risks

statement: Include explicit contractual obligations for vendors to provide ongoing performance reporting.
quote: Organizations should ensure vendor contracts include explicit obligations for proactive incident notification, performance reporting, and communication of model changes.
hazard: Performance degradation undetected due to lack of vendor reporting

statement: Include explicit contractual obligations for vendors to communicate model changes to the organization.
quote: Organizations should ensure vendor contracts include explicit obligations for proactive incident notification, performance reporting, and communication of model changes.
hazard: Unannounced model updates change behavior without training or governance adjustment

statement: Examine upstream human-factor contributors such as insufficient onboarding and production pressure in root cause analyses of AI incidents.
quote: Root cause analysis should examine upstream human-factor contributors (e.g., insufficient onboarding, role-skill mismatch, production pressures that discourage critical review).
hazard: Automation bias and training gaps recur because root causes go unaddressed

statement: Escalate data-related AI incidents through the data governance channel and AI Governance Committee, engaging data stewards in root cause analysis.
quote: Data incidents should trigger escalation through the HDO’s data governance channel alongside the AI Governance Committee, with data stewards engaged in root cause analysis.
hazard: Data drift or biased data causing harm without appropriate governance response

statement: Record the model version and data vintage active at the time of each AI incident in incident reports.
quote: AI incident reports should reference the model version and data vintage active at the time of the incident to enable traceability.
hazard: Inability to trace incidents to specific model versions after updates

statement: Add an 'AI involvement' tag or category to existing incident reporting workflows rather than building a parallel system.
quote: Adding an “AI involvement” tag or category to existing workflows can significantly reduce implementation burden.
hazard: AI incidents unidentifiable within general safety reporting

statement: Establish a process ensuring all relevant staff receive training on each AI solution's purpose and limitations.
quote: Develop a process to ensure all relevant staff receive training on AI solutions, including their purpose, limitations, and related information.
hazard: Staff misuse AI tools due to unfamiliarity with purpose and limitations

statement: Reinforce AI training through recurring briefings and optional seminars.
quote: Reinforce training via recurring briefings and optional seminars for deeper engagement.
hazard: Training knowledge decays over time

statement: Provide all patients a Notice of Privacy Practices by first service delivery that describes how PHI may be used by AI solutions.
quote: Provide all patients, no later than the date of first service delivery, with a comprehensive Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP), including how protected health information (PHI) may be used by AI solutions, in compliance with HIPAA.
hazard: Undisclosed AI use of PHI violating HIPAA and patient trust

statement: Develop a process for patient transparency and/or consent for relevant AI solutions.
quote: Develop a process for patient transparency and/or consent where appropriate for relevant AI solutions.
hazard: Patients unaware of AI involvement in their care

statement: Develop a process to document, escalate, and notify relevant parties about AI incidents.
quote: Develop a process to document, escalate, and notify relevant parties about AI incidents.
hazard: AI incidents unreported or not escalated, allowing ongoing harm

statement: Communicate clearly that all parties involved in an AI incident share responsibility for reporting it.
quote: Ensure it is clearly communicated that all parties involved in an AI incident share responsibility for reporting any voluntary or mandatory incidents.
hazard: Underreporting because staff assume someone else will report

statement: Ensure AI incident communications comply with relevant federal and state laws and protections.
quote: Ensure information included in AI incident communication falls under relevant federal and state laws and protections.
hazard: Incident communications creating legal exposure or losing protections

statement: Provide whistleblower protections for AI reporting, including anonymity, confidentiality, non-retaliation, and disclosure of data retention policies.
quote: Provide whistleblower protections for both internal and external reporting, including anonymity, confidentiality, non-retaliation assurances, and clear disclosure of data retention policies.
hazard: Fear of retaliation suppresses reporting of AI safety concerns

statement: Create safe, accessible internal channels for staff to report AI performance concerns, bias, and safety issues.
quote: Creating safe, accessible channels for this type of feedback (e.g., whistleblower protections) is critical for surfacing issues that may not be visible through technical monitoring alone.
hazard: Issues invisible to technical monitoring go undetected

statement: Establish a structured, recurring training program covering the purpose, intended use, and known limitations of each deployed AI system.
quote: HDOs should establish a structured, recurring training program that ensures all relevant staff (across clinical, administrative, technical, and leadership roles) understand the purpose, intended use, and known limitations of each AI system deployed within their environment.
hazard: Staff unaware of AI limitations over-rely on outputs

statement: Differentiate AI training by role and deliver it through multiple modalities.
quote: Training should be role-differentiated and delivered through multiple modalities, as applicable.
hazard: Generic training fails to address role-specific risks
