statement: Deliver use case training at or before go-live and refresh it whenever the system is updated or performance concerns arise.
quote: A "just-in-time" approach is recommended, with training triggered at or before system go-live and refreshed whenever a system is updated or performance concerns arise.
hazard: Staff use updated or new systems without current training

statement: Embed AI training within existing role-based education and competency frameworks instead of separate tracks per solution.
quote: Where workflows incorporate multiple AI solutions, organizations should embed AI training within existing role-based education programs and competency frameworks rather than creating parallel tracks for each solution.
hazard: Fragmented training burden reduces completion and retention

statement: Keep AI fact sheets, model cards, or solution documentation accessible to staff between formal training cycles.
quote: Supporting resources such as AI fact sheets, model cards (such as the CHAI Applied Model Card), or solution documentation should remain accessible to staff between formal training cycles for self-directed review, if interested.
hazard: Staff lack reference information on AI limitations when needed

statement: Maintain AI training records and review them on a recurring basis.
quote: To sustain accountability and consistency over time, training records should be maintained and reviewed on a recurring basis, training responsibilities should be clearly assigned within each department, and organizations should consider designating AI Governance Champions (or equivalent) to provide ongoing peer support and serve as a first point of escalation for staff questions.
hazard: Untracked training gaps among AI users

statement: Clearly assign AI training responsibilities within each department.
quote: To sustain accountability and consistency over time, training records should be maintained and reviewed on a recurring basis, training responsibilities should be clearly assigned within each department, and organizations should consider designating AI Governance Champions (or equivalent) to provide ongoing peer support and serve as a first point of escalation for staff questions.
hazard: No accountability for ensuring staff are trained

statement: Designate departmental AI Governance Champions to provide peer support and serve as first point of escalation for staff questions.
quote: To sustain accountability and consistency over time, training records should be maintained and reviewed on a recurring basis, training responsibilities should be clearly assigned within each department, and organizations should consider designating AI Governance Champions (or equivalent) to provide ongoing peer support and serve as a first point of escalation for staff questions.
hazard: Staff questions and concerns about AI go unanswered or unescalated

statement: Require completion of required training before granting access to AI systems.
quote: Completion of required training should be a prerequisite for accessing or using AI systems.
hazard: Untrained users operating AI tools in patient care

statement: Train staff in non-patient environments such as sandboxes or simulations before go-live to surface limitations and failure modes.
quote: When able, training staff in non-patient environments (e.g., sandbox systems, test EHR instances, or simulation settings) allows organizations to assess system performance, surface known limitations and failure modes, and train end users on how to interact with the solution before patient safety is at stake.
hazard: Failure modes discovered only after patient harm

statement: Implement tiered competency validation calibrated to each AI solution's risk level and workflow impact.
quote: To validate that training is achieving its intended goals, HDOs should implement a tiered competency validation approach calibrated to the risk level and workflow impact of each AI solution.
hazard: Training completed without achieving actual competency

statement: Require knowledge assessments or scenario-based checks for staff using higher-risk or workflow-changing AI solutions.
quote: For staff who directly interact with higher-risk or workflow-changing AI solutions, a knowledge assessment or scenario-based check is recommended.
hazard: Inadequate competency for high-risk AI use

statement: Trigger re-certification or refresher training whenever an AI system undergoes material updates.
quote: Whenever a system undergoes material updates, a re-certification or refresher training should be triggered to ensure continued competency.
hazard: Staff unaware of changed behavior after updates

statement: Train clinicians on AI system use, updates, override protocols, and known risks.
quote: Clinicians: AI system use, updates, override protocols, and known risks.
hazard: Clinicians unable to recognize and override erroneous AI outputs

statement: Gate AI go-live on formal readiness criteria spanning IT, leadership, administrative, and training domains.
quote: No hospital was authorized to go live without meeting formal readiness criteria spanning IT, leadership, administrative, and training domains which ensured deployment authorization was a deliberate gate.
hazard: Premature deployment without operational readiness

statement: Hold daily debriefs for at least two weeks after launch to capture feedback and refine workflows.
quote: Daily debriefs continued for at least two weeks post-launch to capture feedback and refine workflows.
hazard: Early workflow problems persist unaddressed after go-live

statement: Involve end users in piloting before full rollout and formally collect and act on their feedback.
quote: Are end users involved in piloting before full rollout? Is their feedback formally collected and acted on?
hazard: Workflow issues undiscovered until full-scale deployment

statement: Document known limitations and failure modes and communicate them to staff before go-live.
quote: Are known limitations and failure modes documented and communicated to staff prior to go-live?
hazard: Staff unaware of failure modes over-trust outputs

statement: Audit training on a recurring basis to confirm user adherence and training effectiveness.
quote: Are training audits maintained and reviewed on a recurring basis to ensure users are adherent and the training itself is effective?
hazard: Ineffective training persists undetected

statement: Review and update the Notice of Privacy Practices to explicitly describe AI-related use of PHI.
quote: As AI systems increasingly use PHI to generate recommendations, predict risk, or support clinical decisions, organizations should review and update their NPP to explicitly describe AI-related data use.
hazard: Undisclosed AI processing of PHI constituting HIPAA violation

statement: Train staff or provide standard documentation so they can explain AI-related privacy practices to patients with questions.
quote: Are staff trained, or is there standard documentation in place, to understand and explain organizational privacy practices related to AI-enabled systems to patients who have questions about the written notice?
hazard: Patients' privacy questions about AI go unanswered

statement: Reserve formal patient consent for AI uses that change standard of care, introduce discrete clinical risk, or collect new data categories.
quote: Formal consent should be reserved for AI uses that materially change the standard of care, introduce discrete clinical risk, or require collection of a new category of patient data.
hazard: Patients exposed to material AI risks without informed consent

statement: Obtain formal consent when AI requires collecting a new category of patient data such as voice or biometric capture.
quote: The AI requires collection of a new category of patient data (e.g., voice or biometric capture).
hazard: Recording patient voice or biometrics without consent

statement: Obtain formal consent when the AI use is investigational or part of a research protocol.
quote: The AI use is investigational or part of a research protocol.
hazard: Patients unknowingly subjected to investigational AI

statement: Obtain formal consent when AI substitutes for clinician judgment in a discrete decision.
quote: The AI materially changes the standard of care or substitutes for clinician judgment in a discrete decision.
hazard: AI replacing clinician judgment without patient agreement

statement: Inform patients of reasonable non-AI alternatives when an AI solution materially influences a clinical recommendation.
quote: Where an AI solution materially influences a clinical recommendation, patients should also be informed of any reasonable non-AI alternatives available to them.
hazard: Patients denied choice of non-AI care options

statement: Identify patient touchpoints with AI-informed decisions or outputs and ensure existing handouts, consent forms, and portal content accurately describe AI use.
quote: Organizations can start by identifying where patients are most likely to encounter AIinformed decisions or AI-generated outputs, and ensuring that materials already in use, such as printed handouts, consent forms, and patient portal content, accurately reflect how AI is being used in those contexts.
hazard: Patient materials misrepresent or omit AI involvement

statement: Update existing patient documents incrementally to include plain-language descriptions of AI use.
quote: Where possible, existing workflows and documents can be updated incrementally to include plain-language AI descriptions, rather than building new materials from scratch.
hazard: Patients cannot understand technical AI disclosures

statement: Provide a 'Request Human Assistance' option in patient-facing AI tools such as scheduling assistants or triage support.
quote: In settings where patients may interact directly with AI solutions, such as scheduling assistants or triage support, a simple "Request Human Assistance" option can go a long way toward building trust and accommodating patients who prefer a different experience.
hazard: Patients trapped in AI interactions without access to a human

statement: Build a lightweight review of patient transparency materials into existing deployment and update workflows.
quote: Keeping materials current may not require a heavy lift if a lightweight review process is built into existing deployment and update workflows.
hazard: Transparency materials become outdated after AI changes

statement: Review and update patient transparency materials whenever new AI systems are deployed or existing ones materially updated.
quote: Are patient transparency materials reviewed and updated whenever new AI systems are deployed or when existing systems are materially updated?
hazard: Patients given inaccurate information about current AI use

statement: Consult Patient and Family Advisory Councils when designing or reviewing patient-facing AI transparency materials.
quote: Where capacity allows, consulting Patient and Family Advisory Councils or similar groups can help ensure that transparency materials reflect what patients actually want to know, which could lead to simpler, more effective communication than organizations might develop on their own.
hazard: Transparency materials miss what patients need to know

statement: Use use case-specific training to prepare front-line staff to answer patient questions about AI in their care.
quote: Staff play a natural role here as well: use casespecific training helps clinical and front-line staff answer patient questions about AI in their care setting, drawing on the same knowledge they already use day-to-day.
hazard: Staff unable to answer patient questions about AI

statement: Display visual cues such as signage where AI is actively used in patient-facing interactions.
quote: Are visual cues (e.g., signage, posters in waiting areas or clinical settings) present where AI is actively used in patient-facing interactions?
hazard: Patients unaware they are interacting with AI

statement: Provide AI transparency materials in accessible formats for patients with disabilities and limited AI literacy.
quote: Are transparency materials available in accessible formats for patients with disabilities and for patients with limited AI literacy?
hazard: Disabled or low-literacy patients excluded from AI disclosures

statement: Provide a consistent, accessible mechanism for patients to ask questions or raise concerns about AI in their care.
quote: Is there a consistent, accessible mechanism for patients to ask questions or raise concerns about AI in their care at any point during their visit or episode?
hazard: Patient concerns about AI go unvoiced or unaddressed

statement: Establish a process for handling patient requests to opt out of AI uses.
quote: HDOs should also address how patient opt-out requests are handled.
hazard: Patient preferences to avoid AI ignored

statement: Designate each AI solution in the AI inventory as opt-out eligible or not.
quote: The HDO maintains an AI inventory of its AI solutions with a clear designation for each: opt-out eligible or not.
hazard: Inconsistent handling of opt-out requests across AI tools

statement: Include plain-language statements in admission paperwork and patient rights notices that AI may be used and patients may request opt-out.
quote: Admission paperwork and the patient rights notice include plainlanguage statements informing patients that AI solutions may be used in their care and that they may request to opt out of certain uses.
hazard: Patients unaware of AI use or their opt-out rights

statement: Train admissions staff to briefly explain AI use and opt-out options during admission.
quote: Staff are trained to briefly explain this during the admissions process.
hazard: Written notices alone fail to inform patients

statement: Document patient opt-out requests in internal systems and flag them for the care team.
quote: When a patient opts out, the request is documented in the internal system(s) and flagged for the care team.
hazard: AI used on patients who opted out

statement: Tell patients which AI uses cannot be opted out of and explain why in accessible terms.
quote: The HDO is transparent that some AI uses are not eligible for opt-out, and explains why in accessible terms.
hazard: Patients misled about their ability to avoid AI

statement: Establish that all parties involved in an AI incident, not only the most senior staff member, are expected to report it.
quote: HDOs should establish that incident reporting is a shared responsibility: all parties involved, not just the most senior staff member present, are expected to report, and department head(s) should be formally notified following any mandatory reporting event.
hazard: Incidents unreported due to hierarchical diffusion of responsibility

statement: Formally notify department heads following any mandatory AI incident reporting event.
quote: HDOs should establish that incident reporting is a shared responsibility: all parties involved, not just the most senior staff member present, are expected to report, and department head(s) should be formally notified following any mandatory reporting event.
hazard: Leadership unaware of serious AI incidents

statement: Add AI-specific incident categories to current incident reporting systems.
quote: In practice, HDOs can build this into existing incident management workflows by adding AI-specific incident categories to current reporting systems, developing standard communication templates for common AI incident types to ensure speed and legal consistency, and defining clear internal service level agreements; for example, internal notification within 24 hours and regulatory notification within 72 hours, where applicable.
hazard: AI incidents not captured or distinguished in reporting systems

statement: Develop standard communication templates for common AI incident types.
quote: In practice, HDOs can build this into existing incident management workflows by adding AI-specific incident categories to current reporting systems, developing standard communication templates for common AI incident types to ensure speed and legal consistency, and defining clear internal service level agreements; for example, internal notification within 24 hours and regulatory notification within 72 hours, where applicable.
hazard: Slow or legally inconsistent incident communications

statement: Define incident notification service level agreements, e.g., internal notification within 24 hours and regulatory notification within 72 hours.
quote: In practice, HDOs can build this into existing incident management workflows by adding AI-specific incident categories to current reporting systems, developing standard communication templates for common AI incident types to ensure speed and legal consistency, and defining clear internal service level agreements; for example, internal notification within 24 hours and regulatory notification within 72 hours, where applicable.
hazard: Delayed notification allows AI harm to spread

statement: Inform staff who report AI incidents of outcomes and corrective actions taken.
quote: Equally important is closing the loop: staff who report incidents should be informed of outcomes and corrective actions taken, which reinforces a proactive reporting culture rather than a reactive one.
hazard: Reporting fatigue and declining incident reports

statement: Maintain a documented process for closing the feedback loop on AI incident reports with visible follow-up actions.
quote: HDOs should implement and maintain a documented process for closing the feedback loop on AI incident reporting, including communicating outcomes and visible follow-up actions to staff.
hazard: Loss of trust suppresses early identification of AI risks

statement: Have the treating clinician notify patients of AI-related adverse events affecting them.
quote: AI-related adverse event affecting a specific patient, and where the patient was aware of the AI's involvement; material near-misses or workflow changes that affect care.
hazard: Patients uninformed of AI-related harm to them

statement: Notify the vendor of suspected software defects or performance issues via IT or technical teams.
quote: Vendor Suspected software defect or performance issue.
hazard: Defects persist because vendor is not informed

statement: Define mandatory versus voluntary reportable AI incidents and communicate the definitions to staff.
quote: Has your organization defined what constitutes a “mandatory” vs. “voluntary” reportable AI incident, and are those definitions clearly communicated to relevant staff?
hazard: Staff unsure which AI incidents must be reported

statement: Document an internal AI incident notification chain with escalation pathways if the department head is unavailable.
quote: Is there a documented internal notification chain, including escalation pathways if the department head is unavailable?
hazard: Incident escalation stalls when key person unavailable

statement: Communicate performance findings, clinical concerns, workflow friction, and incident data back to the AI vendor.
quote: The HDO communicates performance findings, clinical concerns, workflow friction points, and incident data back to the vendor.
hazard: Vendor unaware of real-world performance problems

statement: Collect and act on patient and caregiver feedback about AI use in their care.
quote: Collecting and acting on patient feedback supports trust-building and informed consent processes.
hazard: Patient concerns about AI use ignored, eroding trust

statement: Enable frontline staff to discuss AI use with patients, clarify outputs, and surface non-AI alternatives.
quote: In a clinical context, frontline staff may communicate directly with patients about how AI may have been used in their care, answer questions, clarify outputs, and surface non-AI alternatives where appropriate.
hazard: Patients confused or distrustful about AI involvement

statement: Share AI performance data and incident learnings with peer organizations through collaborative networks.
quote: HDOs may share AI-related performance data, incident learnings, and governance practices with peer organizations through regional networks, shared governance models, or collaborative learning communities.
hazard: Systemic AI issues invisible within a single organization

statement: Provide dedicated AI orientation to new hires before they encounter AI systems in practice.
quote: Rather than waiting for the next scheduled general training cycle, onboarding training ensures new employees develop baseline AI literacy before they encounter these systems in clinical or operational practice.
hazard: New staff using AI without baseline literacy

statement: Provide scenario-based incident response training on recognizing, escalating, and documenting AI incidents.
quote: Scenario-based training that prepares staff to recognize, escalate, and document AIrelated incidents when they occur.
hazard: Staff do not recognize or escalate harmful AI outputs

statement: Provide leadership and governance committee training on AI risk management, regulatory trends, and ethical obligations.
quote: This covers risk management, regulatory trends, ethical obligations, and how to evaluate AI governance program performance.
hazard: Leaders unable to oversee AI risk effectively

statement: Offer patient and community AI literacy education through plain-language explainers, town halls, or PFAC curricula.
quote: Examples may include plain-language explainers and FAQs, community town halls or listening sessions, and structured curricula delivered through Patient and Family Advisory Councils (PFACs) or related councils.
hazard: Patients unable to engage meaningfully with AI governance

statement: Implement and maintain a documented process that informs staff of the outcomes and follow-up actions taken on AI incident reports.
quote: HDOs should implement and maintain a documented process for closing the feedback loop on AI incident reporting, including communicating outcomes and visible follow-up actions to staff.
hazard: Staff stop reporting AI concerns when reports seem ignored, delaying early detection of AI risks.

statement: Define mandatory versus voluntary reportable AI incidents and communicate those definitions to relevant staff.
quote: Has your organization defined what constitutes a “mandatory” vs. “voluntary” reportable AI incident, and are those definitions clearly communicated to relevant staff?
hazard: Inconsistent or missed reporting of AI incidents due to unclear reporting thresholds.

statement: Communicate to everyone involved in an AI incident that each person individually shares responsibility for reporting it.
quote: Is it explicitly communicated to all parties involved in an AI incident that they share individual responsibility for reporting (not only the most senior person in the chain)?
hazard: Incidents go unreported because staff assume a senior colleague will report.

statement: Notify and document notification of the relevant department head after every mandatory AI incident report.
quote: Is the head of the relevant department(s) notified after every mandatory reporting incident, and is this notification documented?
hazard: Leadership unaware of serious AI incidents, delaying corrective action.

statement: Maintain a documented internal notification chain for AI incidents, with escalation pathways when the department head is unavailable.
quote: Is there a documented internal notification chain, including escalation pathways if the department head is unavailable?
hazard: AI incident notifications stall when key personnel are unavailable.

statement: Configure the incident reporting system to capture severity, frequency, incident type, how AI was involved, and reporter contact information for follow-up.
quote: Does your incident reporting system capture information, such as: (a) severity of the incident; (b) frequency; (c) type of incident; (d) how AI was involved; and (e) contact information for follow-up by a supervisor?
hazard: Incomplete incident data prevents pattern detection and root-cause analysis of AI failures.

statement: Define and enforce time-bound AI incident notification requirements, such as internal notification within 24 hours and regulatory notification within 72 hours.
quote: Are time-bound notification requirements defined and enforced (e.g., internal notification within 24 hours, regulatory notification within 72 hours for applicable incidents)?
hazard: Delayed internal and regulatory notification of AI-related harms.

statement: Provide standard communication templates for common AI incident types.
quote: Are standard communication templates available for common incident types to ensure consistency, appropriate legal framing, and speed of response?
hazard: Inconsistent, slow, or legally problematic incident communications.

statement: Empower staff to report early AI concerns before they escalate into formal incidents.
quote: Is incident reporting designed to be proactive rather than reactive (e.g., are staff empowered to report early concerns before they escalate to formal incidents)?
hazard: Emerging AI problems reach patients before being flagged.

statement: Ensure information included in AI incident communications complies with relevant federal and state laws and protections.
quote: Control 4.5.5: Ensure information included in AI incident communication falls under relevant federal and state laws and protections.
hazard: Unlawful disclosure of protected health information in AI incident communications.

statement: Have legal and compliance teams review the data documented in AI incident reports and confirm alignment with HIPAA and applicable state law.
quote: HDOs should ensure their legal and compliance teams have reviewed what gets documented in AI incident reports and confirmed it aligns with HIPAA and applicable state law.
hazard: Incident reports containing patient identifiers or model outputs violate privacy law.

statement: Add AI incident data categories to the organization's standard annual HIPAA risk assessment.
quote: Much of this work can be embedded into existing compliance review cycles: legal teams can add AI incident data categories to their standard annual HIPAA risk assessments, and staff training on incident communication can be updated to include a brief module on what can, and cannot, be shared externally.
hazard: AI incident data escapes routine privacy risk review.

statement: Add a training module on what AI incident information can and cannot be shared externally.
quote: Much of this work can be embedded into existing compliance review cycles: legal teams can add AI incident data categories to their standard annual HIPAA risk assessments, and staff training on incident communication can be updated to include a brief module on what can, and cannot, be shared externally.
hazard: Staff inappropriately disclose protected information when discussing AI incidents externally.

statement: Identify state-specific mandatory AI or patient safety reporting obligations applicable to AI incidents.
quote: Have you identified your state-specific mandatory AI or patient safety reporting obligations (e.g., MCARE Act in Pennsylvania, NYPORTS in New York, and similar state regimes)?
hazard: Failure to meet state-mandated adverse event reporting deadlines for AI-related events.

statement: Train staff on their legal obligations and limitations when communicating about AI-related incidents internally and externally.
quote: Are staff trained on their legal obligations, and limitations, when communicating about AI-related incidents internally and externally?
hazard: Staff violate legal obligations when discussing AI incidents.

statement: Identify and document external regulatory reporting requirements for AI systems, such as FDA reporting for Software as a Medical Device.
quote: Are external regulatory reporting requirements identified and documented (e.g., FDA for AI systems classified as Software as a Medical Device)?
hazard: Missed FDA or other regulatory reporting for AI device incidents.

statement: Maintain a process to review and update incident communication protocols as new AI-specific state or federal regulations emerge.
quote: Is there a process to review and update incident communication protocols as new AI-specific regulations emerge at the state or federal level?
hazard: Outdated protocols fail to comply with newly enacted AI regulations.

statement: Maintain an accessible AI incident reporting system that staff, patients, and other relevant parties can use to flag AI-related incidents and concerns.
quote: HDOs should ensure a robust, accessible incident reporting system is in place. This system should be one that staff, patients, and other relevant parties can use to flag AI-related incidents and concerns.
hazard: AI-related harms to patients or staff go unreported and unaddressed.

statement: Audit existing reporting channels to identify which systems staff, patients, and other parties already use and trust before adding AI reporting.
quote: Audit existing reporting channels. Review current patient safety platforms, compliance hotlines, and peer review processes to identify which systems staff, patients, and other relevant parties already use and trust.
hazard: AI reporting placed in channels reporters do not use or trust.

statement: Add an AI-related concern tag or category to existing reporting tools rather than building a separate AI reporting system.
quote: Add AI-specific categories rather than building a new system. Incorporate an AI-related concern tag or category into existing reporting tools, with a few structured prompts such as which AI solution was involved, what the concern was, and any surrounding context.
hazard: Parallel reporting systems fragment data and burden reporters, reducing AI incident capture.

statement: Include structured prompts in AI incident reports asking which AI solution was involved, what the concern was, and surrounding context.
quote: Incorporate an AI-related concern tag or category into existing reporting tools, with a few structured prompts such as which AI solution was involved, what the concern was, and any surrounding context.
hazard: AI incidents cannot be attributed to specific tools or investigated effectively.

statement: Confirm AI incident reporting pathways are available to all relevant staff and to patients.
quote: Ensure accessibility across reporter types. Confirm that reporting pathways are available to all relevant HDO staff and patients.
hazard: Patients or some staff groups cannot report AI-related harms.

statement: Inform staff how and where to report AI concerns during training, onboarding, and in AI fact sheets or model cards.
quote: Communicate the pathway broadly. Inform staff of how and where to report AI-related concerns during training, onboarding, and through supporting documentation such as AI fact sheets or model cards.
hazard: Staff unaware of how to report AI problems, leading to underreporting.

statement: Route AI-related reports to a designated individual or governance body responsible for review, pattern identification, and follow-up.
quote: Assign clear ownership for review. Route AI-related reports to a designated individual or governance body responsible for reviewing concerns, identifying patterns, and ensuring follow-up action.
hazard: AI reports languish without an owner; recurring patterns go undetected.

statement: Extend whistleblower protection frameworks to explicitly cover AI-related disclosures by staff and external parties, including patients and vendors.
quote: This control calls on HDOs to extend their whistleblower protection frameworks to explicitly cover AI-related disclosures, ensuring that both HDO staff and external parties (including patients and vendors) can report concerns safely, anonymously, and without fear of retaliation.
hazard: Fear of retaliation suppresses reporting of AI bias, unexplained outputs, or safety risks.

statement: Provide an anonymous AI reporting channel, such as a third-party hotline or no-login form, that captures no identifying metadata.
quote: A truly anonymous channel (for example, a third party hotline or a no-login web form) accepts a report about an AI system without capturing names, employee IDs, IP addresses, badge data, or any metadata that could re-identify the source.
hazard: Reporters fear professional consequences and withhold AI safety concerns.

statement: Specify in confidentiality protections that reporter identifying information will not be shared with the AI vendor during root-cause analysis.
quote: Confidentiality protections typically need to specify that identifying information will not be shared with the AI vendor during rootcause analysis, since vendor contracts often create indirect channels back to a reporter's employer.
hazard: Reporter identity leaks back to employer through vendor channels, enabling retaliation.

statement: Issue written non-retaliation commitments covering anyone who reports AI concerns, participates in investigations, or refuses to use an AI solution reasonably believed unsafe.
quote: Non-retaliation assurances are formal, written commitments by the HDO that no adverse action will be taken against anyone who in good faith reports a concern about a health AI system, attempted to report one, participates in an investigation, or refuses to use an AI solution they reasonably believe is unsafe.
hazard: Staff pressured to use unsafe AI or punished for reporting concerns.

statement: Publish in plain language, before reports are made, what whistleblower submission data is collected, stored, accessed, retained, and destroyed.
quote: Clear disclosure of data retention policies means the HDO publishes, in plain language and before a report is made, exactly what happens to the data generated by a whistleblower submission.
hazard: Reporters deterred by uncertainty about how long identifying report data persists.

statement: Update non-retaliation language in existing HR policies to reference AI specifically.
quote: Rather than building entirely new infrastructure, much of this can be embedded into what HDOs already have: non-retaliation language can be updated to reference AI specifically within existing HR policies, AI-related reporting categories can be added to current compliance hotline intake forms, and whistleblower protections can be incorporated into the AI modules of onboarding and annual training programs.
hazard: Existing policies ambiguously protect AI-related disclosures.

statement: Add AI-related reporting categories to compliance hotline intake forms.
quote: Rather than building entirely new infrastructure, much of this can be embedded into what HDOs already have: non-retaliation language can be updated to reference AI specifically within existing HR policies, AI-related reporting categories can be added to current compliance hotline intake forms, and whistleblower protections can be incorporated into the AI modules of onboarding and annual training programs.
hazard: AI concerns submitted via hotlines are not identifiable or tracked.

statement: Cover whistleblowing protocols and legal protections in AI modules of onboarding and annual staff training.
quote: Are whistleblowing protocols and legal protections covered in staff AI training programs, including at onboarding?
hazard: Staff unaware of protections and reluctant to report AI safety issues.

statement: Assign reporters a case code rather than identifying them by name to staff handling the report.
quote: Is anonymity protected throughout the reporting and investigation process (e.g., reporters assigned a case code rather than identified by name to staff handling the report)?
hazard: Reporter identity exposed during investigation, enabling retaliation.

statement: Establish response service level agreements for AI reports by urgency level, such as responding to critical reports within 24 hours.
quote: Is there a defined response service level agreement (SLA) by urgency level (e.g., critical reports responded to within 24 hours)?
hazard: Critical AI safety reports receive delayed responses.

statement: Automatically escalate unaddressed AI reports to the Chief AI Officer or similar staff after a specified timeframe, such as 14 days.
quote: Is there a defined escalation pathway if a report is not addressed within a specified timeframe (e.g., automatic escalation to the Chief AI Officer or similar staff if not responded to within 14 days)?
hazard: Unresolved AI concerns stall indefinitely without accountability.

statement: Develop semi-automated priority systems for routing and responding to AI incident reports.
quote: HDOs may develop semi-automated priority systems for routing and responding to incident reports.
hazard: High-severity AI incident reports are not prioritized.

statement: Offer multiple channels for AI reports, including online forms, telephone, and in-person options, to accommodate different preferences and accessibility needs.
quote: Are multiple channels available for submitting reports (including online forms, telephone, and in-person options) to accommodate reporters with different preferences or accessibility needs?
hazard: Reporters with disabilities or preferences excluded from reporting AI concerns.

statement: State non-retaliation explicitly in both the whistleblower policy and the reporting interface itself.
quote: Is non-retaliation explicitly stated in the policy and in the reporting interface itself, covering demotion, dismissal, harassment, and other adverse actions?
hazard: Reporters unaware of protections at the point of reporting.

statement: Provide reporters a tracking mechanism showing report status, estimated timelines, and escalation paths.
quote: Are reporters provided with a tracking portal or mechanism to follow the status of their report, including estimated timelines and escalation paths?
hazard: Reporters lose trust when report status is opaque.

statement: Clearly disclose data retention timelines to reporters, such as records archived up to 7 years.
quote: Are data retention timelines clearly disclosed to reporters (e.g., records archived for up to 7 years for legal compliance and audit purposes)?
hazard: Reporters uninformed about how long their submission data persists.

statement: Include an explicit acknowledgment of protections and reporter obligations, such as an "I accept" checkbox, on the reporting form.
quote: Does the reporting form include an explicit acknowledgment of protections and reporter obligations (e.g., “I accept” checkbox)?
hazard: Reporters unaware of their protections and obligations when submitting.

statement: Have legal confirm the whistleblower policy addresses federal anti-retaliation statutes, including the False Claims Act, where AI supports billing, coding, documentation, or prior authorization.
quote: Has your legal team confirmed that your whistleblower policy addresses applicable federal anti-retaliation statutes (including the False Claims Act) particularly where AI tools are used in billing, coding, clinical documentation, or prior authorization workflows?
hazard: Retaliation against reporters of AI-driven billing or documentation fraud violates federal law.

statement: Pilot AI tools in silent mode against live EHR data before surfacing outputs to clinicians.
quote: Models were piloted in silent mode against live EHR data before alerts were surfaced to clinicians, satisfying the playbook's pre-deployment testing expectation without a dedicated sandbox.
hazard: Unvalidated AI outputs reach clinicians and patients before local performance is known.

statement: Scope AI training to the specific staff who act on the tool's outputs and reinforce it in existing clinical workflows.
quote: Rather than rolling out broad "AI literacy" curricula, training was scoped tightly to the case managers and hospitalists who actually acted on the risk score, and was reinforced in existing multidisciplinary rounds.
hazard: Generic training fails to prepare actual users to act on AI outputs appropriately.

statement: Capture staff feedback on AI tools within the same workflow where the AI output appears.
quote: Staff feedback was captured in the same rounding and case-management workflow where the score appeared, and concerns were triaged by Parkland Center for Clinical Innovation (PCCI) engineers back into retraining cycles.
hazard: User concerns about AI outputs go uncollected and uncorrected.

statement: Provide role-differentiated training tailored to each user group's specific use of the AI tool.
quote: Training was role-differentiated: ED nurses were trained on the specific alert triage pathway, physicians received use-case-specific guidance on how COMPOSER differed from the prior rules-based screen, and the model was accompanied by plain-language documentation describing its inputs and known limitations.
hazard: Users misapply AI tools because training ignores role-specific workflows.

statement: Accompany deployed AI tools with plain-language documentation describing their inputs and known limitations for clinicians.
quote: Training was role-differentiated: ED nurses were trained on the specific alert triage pathway, physicians received use-case-specific guidance on how COMPOSER differed from the prior rules-based screen, and the model was accompanied by plain-language documentation describing its inputs and known limitations.
hazard: Clinicians over-rely on AI outputs without understanding limitations.

statement: Use a phased go-live for AI tool deployment after silent-mode testing.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Organization-wide rollout exposes all patients to undetected AI failures.

statement: Log whether clinicians acted on, deferred, or overrode each AI output and review these logs to recalibrate the tool and retrain staff.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Declining AI usefulness or inappropriate reliance goes undetected after deployment.

statement: Reassess an AI tool's health equity impact locally whenever it is considered for a new setting, even if evaluated elsewhere.
quote: An AI solution that is evaluated by one setting through HEAAL should be reassessed when a different setting considers implementation.
hazard: Tool that advanced equity elsewhere worsens inequities in a different patient population or workflow

statement: Conduct a structured health equity assessment (e.g., HEAAL) every time the organization considers adopting an AI solution.
quote: Thus, to ensure health equity, HEAAL should be applied every time a healthcare organization considers using an AI solution.
hazard: AI adoption worsens health inequities without assessment

statement: Register AI product equity assessments in an independent registry and report progress on assessment procedures.
quote: Similar to the registration of clinical trials, healthcare organizations can register AI product assessments and report progress in conducting HEAAL procedures.
hazard: Equity assessments used as rubber stamp; cherry-picked populations or results

statement: Understand the legal and internal policy constraints for the AI solution and proactively develop intervention plans.
quote: It suggests that the governance committee or designated stakeholders should have a clear understanding of the legal and internal policy constraints that the solution is subject to comply and proactively develop intervention plans.
hazard: Unmanaged legal, policy, or safety violations.

statement: Devise strategies for ongoing monitoring, feedback, and evaluation of the AI solution.
quote: Additionally, they should devise strategies for ongoing monitoring, feedback, and evaluation.
hazard: Failure to adapt to emerging health equity concerns and degrading performance.

statement: Engage intended users and patient community members from the target population in the evaluation process.
quote: The fitness for purpose assessment emphasizes the engagement of its intended users and patient community members from the target population in the evaluation process.
hazard: Misalignment with the goals and needs of intended users and communities.

statement: Disclose information related to potential harms, risks, limitations, and impacts associated with the AI solution.
quote: It should entail the disclosure of information related to potential harms, risks, limitations, and impacts associated with the solution.
hazard: Users and stakeholders making uninformed decisions due to lack of transparency.

statement: Analyze current health inequity by reviewing epidemiology literature and consulting personnel who understand patient experiences.
quote: First, it begins with an analysis of the current state of health inequity through conducting a literature review on epidemiology and consulting with personnel who have a deep understanding of patient experiences, such as healthcare providers, patient navigators, and patient community members.
hazard: Unrecognized baseline health inequities in the target population.

statement: Scrutinize local retrospective healthcare data to determine the presence of identified health inequities.
quote: Then, local healthcare retrospective data is scrutinized to determine the presence of identified health inequities within the local healthcare delivery setting.
hazard: Implementing AI without understanding local baseline disparities.

statement: Identify the most suitable fairness metrics for the AI product to attain established equity goals.
quote: Defining the equity objectives involves identifying the most suitable fairness metrics for the AI product to attain the established goals.

statement: Retain liability-cap provisions rather than waiving them entirely.
quote: Indemnification and Liability Caps: Important for risk allocation; often negotiated heavily with vendors but should not be waived entirely.

statement: Execute a DUA before sharing a Limited Data Set.

quote: It must specify: Permitted Uses and Disclosures: Only for research, public health, or health care operations.

statement: Explicitly identify AI-specific use cases in Limited Data Set DUAs.

statement: Prohibit Limited Data Set recipients from re-identifying individuals.

statement: Prohibit Limited Data Set recipients from contacting individuals.
quote: Recipient Obligations: No re-identification or contact of individuals; use only for purposes specified in the DUA; implement safeguards to prevent unauthorized use or disclosure.

statement: Restrict Limited Data Set recipients to purposes specified in the DUA.

statement: Require Limited Data Set recipients to implement safeguards against unauthorized use or disclosure.
quote: Recipient Obligations: No re-identification or contact of individuals; use only for purposes specified in the DUA; implement safeguards to prevent unauthorized use or disclosure.

statement: Require recipients to notify the covered entity of data misuse or unauthorized disclosure.

statement: Use live input-data distributions to inform ongoing data-quality monitoring.

statement: Document how new data enters models that update after deployment.

statement: Record who approves post-deployment model updates.

statement: Document patient-data categories prohibited in generative AI prompts or context windows.

statement: Apply access controls to persistent agent memory stores.

hazard: Unrecognized baseline health inequities in the target population.

statement: Scrutinize local retrospective healthcare data to determine the presence of identified health inequities.
quote: Then, local healthcare retrospective data is scrutinized to determine the presence of identified health inequities within the local healthcare delivery setting.
hazard: Implementing AI without understanding local baseline disparities.

statement: Identify the most suitable fairness metrics for the AI product to attain established equity goals.
quote: Defining the equity objectives involves identifying the most suitable fairness metrics for the AI product to attain the established goals.
hazard: Using inappropriate metrics that fail to capture health equity progress.

statement: Document the rationale behind the selection of specific fairness metrics.
quote: Additionally, it requires documenting the rationale behind the selection of these specific fairness metrics.
hazard: Lack of transparency and justification for chosen fairness measures.

statement: Provide communication and education to end-users and stakeholders affected by the clinical integration of the AI solution.
quote: At the sixth decision point, the focus is on communication and education provided to end-users, members of disadvantaged patient subgroups, and other stakeholders affected by the clinical integration of the AI solution.
hazard: Lack of awareness about existing health inequities, potential biases, and consequences.

statement: Update or decommission the AI solution if monitoring results diverge from equity objectives.
quote: If the monitoring results diverge from these objectives, the AI solution undergoes either updates or decommissioning.
hazard: Continued use of AI that worsens health inequities over time.

statement: Reassess an AI tool's health equity impact locally whenever it is considered for a new setting, even if evaluated elsewhere.
quote: An AI solution that is evaluated by one setting through HEAAL should be reassessed when a different setting considers implementation.
hazard: Tool that advanced equity elsewhere worsens inequities in a different patient population or workflow

statement: Conduct a structured health equity assessment (e.g., HEAAL) every time the organization considers adopting an AI solution.
quote: Thus, to ensure health equity, HEAAL should be applied every time a healthcare organization considers using an AI solution.
hazard: AI adoption worsens health inequities without assessment

statement: Register AI product equity assessments in an independent registry and report progress on assessment procedures.
quote: Similar to the registration of clinical trials, healthcare organizations can register AI product assessments and report progress in conducting HEAAL procedures.
hazard: Equity assessments used as rubber stamp; cherry-picked populations or results

statement: Monitor generative AI outputs for confabulated content when integrating GAI into applications that inform consequential decisions, such as summarizing patient information.
quote: Risks of confabulated content may be especially important to monitor when integrating GAI into applications involving consequential decision making.
hazard: Confabulated patient summaries leading clinicians to incorrect diagnoses or wrong treatments

statement: Tailor how GAI risks are measured to the model's architecture, training data, access level, and use-case context.
quote: Organizations may choose to tailor how they measure GAI risks based on these characteristics.
hazard: Generic risk measurement missing risks specific to the model or use case

statement: Allocate risk management resources in proportion to the severity and likelihood of each GAI deployment's potential negative impacts.
quote: They may additionally wish to allocate risk management resources relative to the severity and likelihood of negative impacts, including where and how these risks manifest, and their direct and material impacts harms in the context of GAI use.
hazard: Under-resourcing oversight of high-severity, high-likelihood GAI harms

statement: Restrict model outputs for certain content or prompt types, and test whether less-explicit or novel prompts can still circumvent these controls.
quote: Many current systems restrict model outputs to limit certain content or in response to certain prompts, but this approach may still produce harmful recommendations in response to other less-explicit, novel prompts
hazard: Jailbreaks or novel prompts eliciting dangerous recommendations, including self-harm content

statement: Reassess an AI solution's health equity impact when considering implementation in a new or different setting.
quote: An AI solution that is evaluated by one setting through HEAAL should be reassessed when a different setting considers implementation.
hazard: Unanticipated inequities caused by variations in patient population or workflow across settings.

statement: Apply the HEAAL framework every time the healthcare organization considers using a new AI solution.
quote: Thus, to ensure health equity, HEAAL should be applied every time a healthcare organization considers using an AI solution.
hazard: Deployment of biased AI solutions that worsen health inequities.

statement: Register AI product assessments and report evaluation progress to independent registries to ensure transparency.
quote: Similar to the registration of clinical trials, healthcare organizations can register AI product assessments and report progress in conducting HEAAL procedures.
hazard: Outward projection of equity commitment without genuine accountability or changes to practices.

statement: Implement the AI solution prospectively with proactive outreach to provide medical and social support for all high-risk patients.
quote: Prospective implementation of the AI solution with proactive outreach to provide medical and social support for all high-risk patients can improve health equity.
hazard: Worsening of health inequities due to systemic racism or inequitable diagnosis processes.

statement: Ensure the AI governance committee or designated stakeholders understand the legal and internal policy constraints the AI solution must comply with.
quote: It suggests that the governance committee or designated stakeholders should have a clear understanding of the legal and internal policy constraints that the solution is subject to comply and proactively develop intervention plans.
hazard: Deployment of AI tools that violate legal or internal policy requirements

statement: Have the governance committee proactively develop intervention plans for potential adverse consequences of AI solution use before deployment.
quote: It suggests that the governance committee or designated stakeholders should have a clear understanding of the legal and internal policy constraints that the solution is subject to comply and proactively develop intervention plans.
hazard: Unmanaged negative consequences arising after AI solution integration

statement: Devise strategies for ongoing monitoring, feedback, and evaluation of each deployed AI solution.
quote: Additionally, they should devise strategies for ongoing monitoring, feedback, and evaluation.
hazard: Undetected performance degradation or emerging equity harms after deployment

statement: Identify named stakeholders responsible for managing and controlling the AI solution throughout its lifecycle.
quote: This assessment domain entails overseeing potential substantial adverse impacts that may arise after the solution is integrated, identifying stakeholders responsible for managing and controlling the solution throughout its lifecycle, and developing plans for continuous monitoring.
hazard: No accountable owner for AI tool outcomes and adverse impacts

statement: Define the intended use, unintended uses, constraints, and target population for the AI solution before adoption.
quote: It involves defining the intended and unintended use, constraints, and the target population for the solution.
hazard: AI tool used outside its appropriate scope or population

statement: Evaluate whether the AI solution is more suitable than a simpler heuristic approach for the identified problem.
quote: It also encompasses evaluating the suitability of a ML model compared to a simpler heuristic model for addressing the problem at hand.
hazard: Adopting complex AI where simpler, safer alternatives would suffice

statement: Engage intended users and patient community members from the target population in evaluating the AI solution's fitness for purpose.
quote: The fitness for purpose assessment emphasizes the engagement of its intended users and patient community members from the target population in the evaluation process.
hazard: Solution misaligned with needs of users and affected patient communities

statement: Establish fairness criteria for both model performance and the work environment in which the AI solution operates.
quote: It involves establishing and evaluating fairness criteria for the model performance and its work environment.
hazard: Unjust or discriminatory outcomes from AI use

statement: Test whether the AI solution produces consistent, reproducible output for the same or similar input across multiple instances.
quote: A reliable model produces consistent and reproducible output with the same input or similar data over multiple instances.
hazard: Inconsistent outputs undermining safe and trustworthy use

statement: Pre-specify technical and clinical performance targets and verify the AI solution consistently achieves them.
quote: The assessment of reliability and validity ensures that the solution consistently achieves pre-specified performance targets across technical and clinical measures.
hazard: Inaccurate or unreliable AI performance in clinical use

statement: Disclose potential harms, risks, limitations, and impacts of the AI solution to users and affected stakeholders, beyond technical specifications and intended use.
quote: Effective communication should go beyond providing details about the technical specifications of the model and its intended use. It should entail the disclosure of information related to potential harms, risks, limitations, and impacts associated with the solution.
hazard: Users and patients unable to make informed decisions about AI use

statement: Communicate about the AI solution with affected stakeholders, including members of disadvantaged patient subgroups.
quote: This assessment domain highlights the importance of comprehensive communication with users and other affected stakeholders, including members of disadvantaged and advantaged patient subgroups.
hazard: Disadvantaged patients excluded from understanding AI affecting their care

statement: Monitor federal and local regulators, including state Attorney General offices and health departments, for evolving AI requirements.
quote: For the time being, healthcare delivery organizations need to monitor federal and local regulators, including offices of state Attorney Generals and departments of health.
hazard: Noncompliance with changing AI regulations

statement: Assess baseline health inequity via epidemiologic literature review and consultation with providers, patient navigators, and patient community members before adoption.
quote: First, it begins with an analysis of the current state of health inequity through conducting a literature review on epidemiology and consulting with personnel who have a deep understanding of patient experiences, such as healthcare providers, patient navigators, and patient community members.
hazard: Unrecognized existing inequities worsened by AI deployment

statement: Analyze local retrospective data to confirm whether identified health inequities exist in the local care setting.
quote: Then, local healthcare retrospective data is scrutinized to determine the presence of identified health inequities within the local healthcare delivery setting.
hazard: Missing local inequities relevant to the AI use case

statement: Compile a list of relevant health inequities and identify disadvantaged patient subgroups for the AI use case.
quote: The information obtained from both procedures is synthesized to compile a comprehensive list of health inequities and to identify disadvantaged patient subgroups.
hazard: Failure to evaluate AI impact on vulnerable subgroups

statement: Establish equity objectives for the AI solution covering both health and economic outcomes.
quote: Following the measurement of the current state of health inequity, the third decision point entails establishing equity objectives for implementing the AI solution in terms of both health and economic outcomes.
hazard: No benchmark to judge whether AI worsens health inequities

statement: Select fairness metrics suited to the established equity objectives for the AI product.
quote: Defining the equity objectives involves identifying the most suitable fairness metrics for the AI product to attain the established goals.
hazard: Inappropriate metrics masking inequitable AI performance

statement: Document the rationale for selecting specific fairness metrics.
quote: Additionally, it requires documenting the rationale behind the selection of these specific fairness metrics.
hazard: Opaque, unaccountable fairness evaluation choices

statement: Inform AI solution design with input from end-users and members of disadvantaged patient subgroups.
quote: Solution design is informed by input from both end-users and members of disadvantaged patient subgroups.
hazard: Inaccessible solutions that fail to meet disadvantaged patients' support needs

statement: Evaluate AI solution performance using both retrospective and prospective local data before full deployment.
quote: At the fifth decision point, there is a strong emphasis on evaluating the performance of the model using both retrospective and prospective data sourced from local healthcare providers.
hazard: AI performing poorly in the local setting despite external validation

statement: Evaluate AI solution performance against fairness metrics across disadvantaged and advantaged patient subgroups.
quote: This assessment entails conducting a thorough evaluation of the model performance against fairness metrics across disadvantaged and advantaged patient subgroups.
hazard: Worse AI performance for disadvantaged subgroups going undetected

statement: Apply additional context-alignment procedures when evaluating an existing or externally developed AI solution for local implementation.
quote: When evaluating an existing solution, additional procedures are required in the second and fifth decision points to make sure that the solution aligns with the implementation context.
hazard: Existing solution mismatched to local implementation context

statement: Provide communication and education about the AI solution to end-users, disadvantaged patient subgroups, and other affected stakeholders at clinical integration.
quote: At the sixth decision point, the focus is on communication and education provided to end-users, members of disadvantaged patient subgroups, and other stakeholders affected by the clinical integration of the AI solution.
hazard: Unaware users perpetuating biases and inequities through AI use

statement: Collect feedback from end-users and affected stakeholders during AI integration.
quote: Moreover, it facilitates the collection of feedback, ultimately advancing progress towards equity objectives.
hazard: Problems experienced by users go unreported

statement: Monitor shifts in health inequities across disadvantaged and advantaged patient subgroups after AI deployment.
quote: The final two decision points involve ongoing monitoring of shifts in health inequities among disadvantaged and advantaged patient subgroups.
hazard: AI deployment widening health inequities unnoticed

statement: Update or decommission the AI solution when monitoring results diverge from equity objectives.
quote: If the monitoring results diverge from these objectives, the AI solution undergoes either updates or decommissioning.
hazard: Continued use of an AI tool that worsens inequities

statement: Assess implementation context, including personnel availability and resources for lifecycle management, separately from algorithmic fairness.
quote: HEAAL includes procedures that focus on components of the AI model, including training data and outcome labels, and components of the implementation context, including personnel availability and resources for lifecycle management.
hazard: Fair models worsening inequity due to unequal resources for follow-up

statement: Default to Safe Harbor de-identification for most AI use cases.
quote: Default to Safe Harbor de-identification for most AI use cases — it is more accessible and does not require expert validation.
hazard: Unnecessary disclosure of identifiable health information.

statement: Reserve Expert Determination for cases where Safe Harbor is too restrictive and the use case justifies the cost.
quote: Reserve Expert Determination for cases where Safe Harbor is too restrictive and the use case clearly justifies the cost.
hazard: Unjustified de-identification costs or loss of data needed for the intended use.

statement: Explore shared de-identification services through HCCNs, regional HIEs, or state hospital associations.
quote: Explore shared service models through HCCNs, regional HIEs, or state hospital associations for pooled de-identification expertise.
hazard: Inadequate de-identification expertise leading to privacy failures.

statement: Work with vendors to accept de-identified data instead of PHI wherever technically feasible.
quote: Work with vendors to accept de-identified data rather than PHI wherever technically feasible, reducing the overall burden.
hazard: Unnecessary vendor access to identifiable patient information.

statement: Implement a formal AI data-request review requiring documented justification for every requested data element.
quote: Implement a formal data request review process requiring documented justification for every data element requested.
hazard: Excessive data collection or sharing beyond the AI use case's needs.

statement: Document why each field is necessary for its intended purpose in the data acquisition register.
quote: Embed minimum necessary assessments into the data acquisition register — each entry should document why each field is needed for the intended purpose.
hazard: Unjustified inclusion of sensitive data in AI datasets.

statement: Use an AI DUA addendum to contractually require vendors to document and justify requested data elements.
quote: Use the AI DUA addendum to contractually require vendors to document and justify the data elements they request.
hazard: Overbroad vendor data requests without enforceable justification requirements.

statement: Require privacy officer or data steward review before AI data exports exceed a defined volume or sensitivity threshold.
quote: Establish a privacy officer or data steward review gate for any AI data export exceeding a defined volume or sensitivity threshold.
hazard: High-volume or sensitive data exports without privacy oversight.

statement: Assign a privacy officer or legal counsel to monitor state privacy law developments.
quote: Designate a privacy officer or legal counsel owner responsible for monitoring state law developments.
hazard: AI data practices becoming noncompliant with changing state privacy laws.

statement: Use modular DUA addenda that allow state-specific provisions to be updated without renegotiating the entire agreement.
quote: Use a modular DUA addendum structure so that state-specific provisions can be updated without renegotiating the full agreement.
hazard: Delayed contractual compliance with changing state privacy obligations.

statement: Subscribe to state privacy law tracking resources or HHS OCR guidance updates.
quote: Subscribe to resources such as the IAPP State Privacy Law Tracker or HHS OCR guidance updates.
hazard: Missed changes to applicable privacy requirements.

statement: Include state law review in the annual AI contract monitoring cycle.
quote: Build state law review into the annual contract monitoring cycle described in the AI DUA addendum.
hazard: Outdated AI contract provisions that fail to address current privacy law.

statement: Prioritize applicable state and federal regulatory requirements, especially for AI solutions meeting the FDA's SaMD definition.
quote: Organizations should prioritize state and federal regulatory requirements, especially for AI solutions that meet the definition of a Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), as defined by the FDA.
hazard: Deployment of AI without satisfying applicable regulatory requirements.

statement: Consult clinical, technical, compliance, ethics, and patient/community advisors familiar with local circumstances when designing and stewarding AI programs.
quote: It is intended to support organizations in thinking through the design and stewardship of their AI programs and should be used in conjunction with from clinical leaders, technical experts, compliance officers, ethicists, patient and community representatives, and other advisors familiar with the specifics of your organization.
hazard: AI governance decisions that overlook clinical, technical, ethical, or community needs.

statement: Obtain vendor commitments to notify the organization of new platform AI features, artifacts, and significant updates before activation.
quote: For this pathway, the primary contractual objective shifts from negotiating bespoke clauses toward two complementary goals: (1) obtaining the vendor's commitment to continually inform the customer of new features, artifacts, and significant updates before they become active; and (2) ensuring that acceptable blanket standard operating procedures (SOPs) govern any solution introduced through the platform.
hazard: Unreviewed AI capabilities becoming active through routine platform updates.

statement: Establish blanket standard operating procedures governing every AI solution introduced through an enterprise platform.
quote: For this pathway, the primary contractual objective shifts from negotiating bespoke clauses toward two complementary goals: (1) obtaining the vendor's commitment to continually inform the customer of new features, artifacts, and significant updates before they become active; and (2) ensuring that acceptable blanket standard operating procedures (SOPs) govern any solution introduced through the platform.
hazard: Embedded AI features bypassing consistent organizational safeguards.

statement: Govern AI solutions across a defined lifecycle for every relevant ingestion modality.
quote: Subdomain 4.1 establishes that AI solutions should be governed across a defined lifecycle for all relevant ingestion modalities.
hazard: Governance gaps across acquisition pathways or lifecycle stages.

statement: Inventory AI features in existing enterprise platforms on a recurring schedule.
quote: Inventory AI features in existing enterprise platforms on a recurring cadence, with explicit owners assigned per platform.
hazard: Undiscovered AI features operating outside organizational oversight.

statement: Assign an explicit owner for AI feature inventory responsibilities on each enterprise platform.
quote: Inventory AI features in existing enterprise platforms on a recurring cadence, with explicit owners assigned per platform.
hazard: Platform AI capabilities going untracked because ownership is unclear.

statement: Review each platform's AI data-processing terms specifically for model training and derivative-use provisions.
quote: Re-read each platform's data processing terms specifically for AI model training and derivative use provisions, which often differ materially from the general terms of service and may be updated independently of the underlying agreement.
hazard: Unrecognized vendor rights to train models on or derive products from organizational data.

statement: Conduct retroactive governance reviews of legacy AI features enabled before the AI governance program existed.
quote: Apply retroactive governance review to legacy AI features that were enabled before an AI governance program existed.
hazard: Previously enabled AI features remaining unassessed.

statement: Keep newly released enterprise-platform AI features off pending governance review wherever the platform permits.
quote: Define a "default-off" posture for newly released AI features on enterprise platforms wherever the platform permits, pending governance review.
hazard: Automatic deployment of AI features before safety and governance review.

statement: Use vendor administration consoles and release notes during recurring sweeps for embedded AI features.
quote: Step 1 - Discover: Recurring sweep across the enterprise platform list. Use vendor admin consoles and release notes.
hazard: Embedded AI features escaping discovery through routine software updates.

statement: Categorize each embedded AI feature by risk.
quote: Step 2 - Triage: Categorize each feature by risk (see Subdomain 4.2: Risk and Impact Assessment playbook).
hazard: High-risk embedded AI receiving insufficient oversight.

statement: Keep existing embedded AI features off while retroactive review is pending wherever the platform permits.
quote: Step 2 - Triage: Categorize each feature by risk (see Subdomain 4.2: Risk and Impact Assessment playbook). Default-off for any feature pending review where the platform permits.
hazard: Continued use of unreviewed legacy AI features.

statement: Assign a named organizational owner to every embedded AI feature.
quote: Step 4 - Assign owner: Every embedded AI feature gets a named org owner.
hazard: Unclear accountability for individual embedded AI features.

statement: Record discovered embedded AI features in the AI Vendor Register.
quote: Step 5 - Document: Add to AI Vendor Register with a recurring re-review cadence.
hazard: Missing records of deployed embedded AI capabilities.

statement: Set a recurring governance re-review schedule for embedded AI features.
quote: Step 5 - Document: Add to AI Vendor Register with a recurring re-review cadence.
hazard: Embedded AI risks becoming outdated or unexamined after initial review.

statement: Invoke contractual change-notification clauses when reviewing embedded AI features.
quote: Step 6 - Invoke contract levers: Use change-notification clauses on the contract agreement; request written confirmation that organization content is not used to train shared models (as needed); request deletion / opt-out (where available).
hazard: Vendor changes occurring without organizational awareness.

statement: Request written confirmation, when needed, that organizational content is not used to train shared models.
quote: Step 6 - Invoke contract levers: Use change-notification clauses on the contract agreement; request written confirmation that organization content is not used to train shared models (as needed); request deletion / opt-out (where available).
hazard: Organizational content being reused for shared-model training without acceptable safeguards.

statement: Request deletion of organizational content under available vendor data provisions.
quote: Step 6 - Invoke contract levers: Use change-notification clauses on the contract agreement; request written confirmation that organization content is not used to train shared models (as needed); request deletion / opt-out (where available).
hazard: Continued vendor retention of organizational content.

statement: Request available opt-outs from vendor AI data uses.
quote: Step 6 - Invoke contract levers: Use change-notification clauses on the contract agreement; request written confirmation that organization content is not used to train shared models (as needed); request deletion / opt-out (where available).
hazard: Unwanted secondary use of organizational data.

statement: Amend existing vendor-management frameworks with AI-specific components rather than restructuring established processes.
quote: CHAI does not recommend that HDOs restructure existing vendor management, legal, compliance, or procurement processes. Instead, this playbook provides guidance on amending or supplementing existing frameworks to incorporate AI-specific components.
hazard: AI-specific risks remaining outside established vendor governance processes.

statement: Add an AI appendix or addendum to new or existing business associate agreements with AI vendors.
quote: This may take the form of: Adding an AI Appendix or AI Addendum to new or existing Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with AI vendors.
hazard: Business associate agreements lacking AI-specific protections.

statement: Add AI disclosure clauses to standard vendor contract templates.
quote: Updating standard vendor contract templates to include disclosure and responsibility clauses.
hazard: Inconsistent vendor disclosure obligations across AI contracts.

statement: Add AI responsibility clauses to standard vendor contract templates.
quote: Updating standard vendor contract templates to include disclosure and responsibility clauses.
hazard: Unallocated responsibilities for AI deployment and associated risks.

statement: Assign AI governance oversight within existing compliance, legal, or clinical informatics functions.
quote: Assigning AI governance oversight responsibilities within existing compliance, legal, or clinical informatics functions.
hazard: AI oversight lacking an accountable organizational function.

statement: Update existing vendor or third-party codes of conduct to include AI-specific expectations.
quote: For HDOs that maintain a vendor or third party code of conduct (e.g., for any vendor handling PHI or operating in clinical workflows), organizations should update this document to incorporate AI-specific expectations.
hazard: Vendor conduct expectations failing to address AI-specific risks.

statement: Include requirements for vendors to maintain responsible AI governance programs in the third-party code of conduct.
quote: This may include: Requirements for vendors to maintain responsible AI governance programs.
hazard: Dependence on vendors without responsible AI governance.

statement: Set vendor transparency expectations covering how AI is developed, tested, and monitored.
quote: Expectations for transparency about how AI is developed, tested, and monitored.
hazard: Insufficient information to assess vendor AI safety and governance.

statement: Include vendor obligations to proactively disclose AI incidents that may affect the organization.
quote: Requirements for vendors to proactively disclose AI incidents that may affect the HDO.
hazard: Delayed awareness of vendor AI incidents affecting organizational operations or patients.

statement: Reference the updated third-party code of conduct in vendor contracts and requests for proposals.
quote: An updated third party code of conduct sets clear expectations at the start of the relationship and can be referenced in vendor contracts and Request for Proposals (RFPs).
hazard: AI vendor expectations not communicated during procurement and contracting.

statement: Engage clinical operations, IT, and business units throughout AI vendor relationships rather than assigning management solely to legal or compliance.
quote: Third party management is inherently cross-functional and should not be treated as solely a legal or compliance responsibility. Effective third party management and governance requires active engagement from clinical operations, IT, business units, among others throughout the vendor relationship lifecycle.
