hazard: Patients lacking information about healthcare AI solutions.

statement: Establish processes for capturing incidents related to healthcare AI solutions.
quote: Subdomain 4.5: Education, Training, and Feedback Playbook defines the approach for educating and training staff, informing patients, and capturing feedback and incidents related to AI solutions in healthcare delivery organizations (HDOs).
hazard: AI-related incidents remaining invisible to organizational oversight.

statement: Maintain a documented process for closing the feedback loop on AI incident reports.
quote: HDOs should implement and maintain a documented process for closing the feedback loop on AI incident reporting, including communicating outcomes and visible follow-up actions to staff.
hazard: Unresolved reports and absent feedback undermine trust and future reporting.

statement: Communicate AI incident outcomes and visible follow-up actions to staff.
quote: HDOs should implement and maintain a documented process for closing the feedback loop on AI incident reporting, including communicating outcomes and visible follow-up actions to staff.
hazard: Staff lose trust when incident reports produce no visible response.

statement: Define mandatory and voluntary reportable AI incidents.
quote: Has your organization defined what constitutes a “mandatory” vs. “voluntary” reportable AI incident, and are those definitions clearly communicated to relevant staff?
hazard: Ambiguous reporting thresholds cause missed or inconsistent incident reports.

statement: Communicate mandatory and voluntary AI incident reporting definitions to relevant staff.
quote: Has your organization defined what constitutes a “mandatory” vs. “voluntary” reportable AI incident, and are those definitions clearly communicated to relevant staff?
hazard: Staff fail to report incidents because reporting criteria are unclear.

statement: Tell everyone involved in an AI incident that each person shares responsibility for reporting it.
quote: Is it explicitly communicated to all parties involved in an AI incident that they share individual responsibility for reporting (not only the most senior person in the chain)?
hazard: Diffusion of responsibility leaves AI incidents unreported.

statement: Notify relevant department heads after every mandatory-reporting AI incident.
quote: Is the head of the relevant department(s) notified after every mandatory reporting incident, and is this notification documented?
hazard: Department leaders remain unaware of incidents requiring corrective action.

statement: Document department-head notifications for mandatory-reporting AI incidents.
quote: Is the head of the relevant department(s) notified after every mandatory reporting incident, and is this notification documented?
hazard: Missing notification records prevent verification of incident handling.

statement: Document the internal notification chain for AI incidents.
quote: Is there a documented internal notification chain, including escalation pathways if the department head is unavailable?
hazard: Unclear notification responsibilities delay incident response.

statement: Establish alternative escalation pathways when the relevant department head is unavailable.
quote: Is there a documented internal notification chain, including escalation pathways if the department head is unavailable?
hazard: An unavailable leader blocks timely escalation of AI incidents.

statement: Capture incident severity, frequency, type, AI involvement, and follow-up contact information in the reporting system.
quote: Does your incident reporting system capture information, such as: (a) severity of the incident; (b) frequency; (c) type of incident; (d) how AI was involved; and (e) contact information for follow-up by a supervisor?
hazard: Incomplete incident records impede triage, investigation, and follow-up.

statement: Define deadlines for internal and applicable regulatory AI incident notifications.
quote: Are time-bound notification requirements defined and enforced (e.g., internal notification within 24 hours, regulatory notification within 72 hours for applicable incidents)?
hazard: Undefined deadlines permit delayed safety responses and regulatory reporting.

statement: Enforce defined AI incident notification deadlines.
quote: Are time-bound notification requirements defined and enforced (e.g., internal notification within 24 hours, regulatory notification within 72 hours for applicable incidents)?
hazard: Missed notification deadlines delay corrective action and create compliance failures.

statement: Provide standard communication templates for common AI incident types.
quote: Are standard communication templates available for common incident types to ensure consistency, appropriate legal framing, and speed of response?
hazard: Improvised incident communications are inconsistent, delayed, or legally inappropriate.

statement: Enable staff to report early AI concerns before they become formal incidents.
quote: Is incident reporting designed to be proactive rather than reactive (e.g., are staff empowered to report early concerns before they escalate to formal incidents)?
hazard: Unreported early warning signs escalate into preventable harm.

statement: Apply relevant federal and state legal protections to information included in AI incident communications.
quote: Control 4.5.5: Ensure information included in AI incident communication falls under relevant federal and state laws and protections.
hazard: Incident communications expose protected information or violate applicable law.

statement: Obtain legal and compliance review of AI incident report contents for HIPAA and applicable state-law compliance.
quote: HDOs should ensure their legal and compliance teams have reviewed what gets documented in AI incident reports and confirmed it aligns with HIPAA and applicable state law.
hazard: Incident reports contain information documented contrary to privacy requirements.

statement: Include AI incident data categories in annual HIPAA risk assessments.
quote: Much of this work can be embedded into existing compliance review cycles: legal teams can add AI incident data categories to their standard annual HIPAA risk assessments, and staff training on incident communication can be updated to include a brief module on what can, and cannot, be shared externally.
hazard: Privacy assessments overlook sensitive data generated during AI incident handling.

statement: Train staff on legal obligations and limits when communicating AI incidents internally and externally.
quote: Are staff trained on their legal obligations, and limitations, when communicating about AI-related incidents internally and externally?
hazard: Staff disclose protected information or fail to meet incident communication obligations.

statement: Identify state-specific mandatory AI and patient-safety reporting obligations.
quote: Have you identified your state-specific mandatory AI or patient safety reporting obligations (e.g., MCARE Act in Pennsylvania, NYPORTS in New York, and similar state regimes)?
hazard: Organizations overlook jurisdiction-specific reporting requirements.

statement: For Pennsylvania hospitals, report serious events to the Pennsylvania Department of Health within 24 hours of confirmation.
quote: Pennsylvania: The Medical Care Availability and Reduction of Error (MCARE) Act of 2002 requires hospitals to report serious events to the Pennsylvania Department of Health within 24 hours of confirmation, while incidents are reported through the Pennsylvania Patient Safety Reporting System administered by the Pennsylvania Patient Safety Authority.
hazard: Delayed serious-event reporting violates state requirements and impedes safety oversight.

statement: Use the Pennsylvania Patient Safety Reporting System to report applicable incidents in Pennsylvania.
quote: Pennsylvania: The Medical Care Availability and Reduction of Error (MCARE) Act of 2002 requires hospitals to report serious events to the Pennsylvania Department of Health within 24 hours of confirmation, while incidents are reported through the Pennsylvania Patient Safety Reporting System administered by the Pennsylvania Patient Safety Authority.
hazard: Incidents fail to reach the state's patient-safety reporting system.

statement: Report adverse events covered by NYPORTS to the New York State Department of Health.
quote: New York: The New York Patient Occurrence Reporting and Tracking System (NYPORTS) requires reporting of certain adverse events to the New York State Department of Health.
hazard: Reportable adverse events are withheld from required state oversight.

statement: Document applicable external regulatory reporting requirements, including FDA requirements for AI classified as Software as a Medical Device.
quote: Are external regulatory reporting requirements identified and documented (e.g., FDA for AI systems classified as Software as a Medical Device)?
hazard: Undocumented regulatory obligations lead to missed incident reports.

statement: Update AI incident communication protocols as new state or federal AI regulations emerge.
quote: Is there a process to review and update incident communication protocols as new AI-specific regulations emerge at the state or federal level?
hazard: Outdated protocols fail to satisfy changing legal requirements.

statement: Provide an accessible AI incident reporting system for staff, patients, and other relevant parties.
quote: HDOs should ensure a robust, accessible incident reporting system is in place. This system should be one that staff, patients, and other relevant parties can use to flag AI-related incidents and concerns.
hazard: People affected by AI cannot report safety concerns.

statement: Audit existing reporting channels to identify systems that staff, patients, and other relevant parties already use and trust.
quote: Review current patient safety platforms, compliance hotlines, and peer review processes to identify which systems staff, patients, and other relevant parties already use and trust.
hazard: Unfamiliar or untrusted reporting channels discourage incident reporting.

statement: Add AI-specific categories to existing reporting tools rather than creating a separate reporting system.
quote: Add AI-specific categories rather than building a new system.
hazard: Parallel reporting systems fragment safety information and increase reporting burden.

statement: Include structured reporting prompts identifying the AI solution, the concern, and surrounding context.
quote: Incorporate an AI-related concern tag or category into existing reporting tools, with a few structured prompts such as which AI solution was involved, what the concern was, and any surrounding context.
hazard: Reports lack the context needed to investigate AI-related failures.

statement: Explain how and where staff can report AI concerns during training, onboarding, and in supporting documentation.
quote: Inform staff of how and where to report AI-related concerns during training, onboarding, and through supporting documentation such as AI fact sheets or model cards.
hazard: Staff do not report concerns because they cannot find the reporting pathway.

statement: Assign an individual or governance body responsibility for reviewing AI reports, identifying patterns, and ensuring follow-up.
quote: Route AI-related reports to a designated individual or governance body responsible for reviewing concerns, identifying patterns, and ensuring follow-up action.
hazard: Unowned reports receive no review, pattern analysis, or corrective follow-up.

statement: Adopt a formal written whistleblower policy explicitly covering AI-related reporting.
quote: Does your organization have a formal, written whistleblower protection policy that explicitly covers AI-related reporting (not just general healthcare incident reporting)?
hazard: General whistleblower policies leave AI reporters uncertain about their protection.

statement: Extend AI whistleblower protections to internal staff and external parties, including patients and vendors.
quote: This control calls on HDOs to extend their whistleblower protection frameworks to explicitly cover AI-related disclosures, ensuring that both HDO staff and external parties (including patients and vendors) can report concerns safely, anonymously, and without fear of retaliation.
hazard: Unprotected external or internal reporters withhold AI safety concerns.

statement: Provide an anonymous AI reporting channel that collects no identifiers or metadata capable of re-identifying the reporter.
quote: A truly anonymous channel (for example, a third party hotline or a no-login web form) accepts a report about an AI system without capturing names, employee IDs, IP addresses, badge data, or any metadata that could re-identify the source.
hazard: Identifiers or metadata reveal reporters who expected anonymity.

statement: Use case codes rather than names to protect reporter anonymity throughout reporting and investigation.
quote: Is anonymity protected throughout the reporting and investigation process (e.g., reporters assigned a case code rather than identified by name to staff handling the report)?
hazard: Investigation workflows expose anonymous reporters' identities.

statement: Restrict access to confidential reporter identities to a narrowly scoped group.
quote: Confidentiality is weaker than anonymity but operationally distinct: the reporter's identity is known to a narrowly scoped group but shielded from disclosure to certain parties (e.g., supervisors).
hazard: Unnecessary disclosure of reporter identities enables retaliation.

statement: Specify that reporter-identifying information will not be shared with AI vendors during root-cause analysis.
quote: Confidentiality protections typically need to specify that identifying information will not be shared with the AI vendor during rootcause analysis, since vendor contracts often create indirect channels back to a reporter's employer.
hazard: Vendor communications indirectly expose reporters to their employers.

statement: Provide written non-retaliation assurances covering good-faith reports, attempted reports, investigation participation, and refusal to use AI reasonably believed unsafe.
quote: Non-retaliation assurances are formal, written commitments by the HDO that no adverse action will be taken against anyone who in good faith reports a concern about a health AI system, attempted to report one, participates in an investigation, or refuses to use an AI solution they reasonably believe is unsafe.
hazard: Fear of adverse employment or contractual consequences suppresses safety reporting.

statement: Explicitly reference AI-related reporting in existing human-resources non-retaliation policies.
quote: Rather than building entirely new infrastructure, much of this can be embedded into what HDOs already have: non-retaliation language can be updated to reference AI specifically within existing HR policies, AI-related reporting categories can be added to current compliance hotline intake forms, and whistleblower protections can be incorporated into the AI modules of onboarding and annual training programs.
hazard: Human-resources policies leave protection for AI-related disclosures ambiguous.

statement: Display explicit non-retaliation protections in the reporting interface, covering dismissal, demotion, harassment, and other adverse actions.
quote: Is non-retaliation explicitly stated in the policy and in the reporting interface itself, covering demotion, dismissal, harassment, and other adverse actions?
hazard: Reporters abandon submissions because protections are not visible when reporting.

statement: Tie AI non-retaliation assurances to applicable whistleblower and anti-retaliation legal frameworks.
quote: Strong programs tie these assurances to existing legal frameworks (e.g., False Claims Act, HIPAA's anti-retaliation provision at 45 CFR 164.530(g), state whistleblower statutes).
hazard: Non-retaliation commitments lack alignment with applicable legal protections.

statement: Publish plain-language disclosures about whistleblower submission data before a report is made.
quote: Clear disclosure of data retention policies means the HDO publishes, in plain language and before a report is made, exactly what happens to the data generated by a whistleblower submission.
hazard: Reporters submit sensitive information without understanding how it will be handled.

statement: Disclose whistleblower data collection, storage, access conditions, retention periods, and destruction methods.
quote: This data or information includes: what is collected (e.g., the report text, attachments, investigation notes, audit logs), where it is stored, who can access it under what conditions, how long each submission is retained, and the method of destruction.
hazard: Undisclosed data handling and retention expose reporters to persistent confidentiality risks.

statement: Define AI incident response service-level agreements by urgency.
quote: Is there a defined response service level agreement (SLA) by urgency level (e.g., critical reports responded to within 24 hours)?
hazard: Critical AI concerns wait too long for a response.

statement: Escalate unresolved AI reports through a defined pathway when their response deadline is missed.
quote: Is there a defined escalation pathway if a report is not addressed within a specified timeframe (e.g., automatic escalation to the Chief AI Officer or similar staff if not responded to within 14 days)?
hazard: Unanswered reports remain stalled without higher-level intervention.

statement: Use semi-automated priority systems to route AI incident reports and prioritize responses.
quote: HDOs may develop semi-automated priority systems for routing and responding to incident reports.
hazard: Manual routing delays urgent reports or sends them to inappropriate reviewers.

statement: Offer multiple reporting channels, including online forms, telephone, and in-person options.
quote: Are multiple channels available for submitting reports (including online forms, telephone, and in-person options) to accommodate reporters with different preferences or accessibility needs?
hazard: A single reporting channel excludes people with different accessibility needs.

statement: Provide reporters a tracking mechanism showing report status, estimated timelines, and escalation paths.
quote: Are reporters provided with a tracking portal or mechanism to follow the status of their report, including estimated timelines and escalation paths?
hazard: Reporters cannot determine whether concerns are progressing or require escalation.

statement: Include explicit acknowledgment of whistleblower protections and reporter obligations in the reporting form.
quote: Does the reporting form include an explicit acknowledgment of protections and reporter obligations (e.g., “I accept” checkbox)?
hazard: Reporters misunderstand their protections or responsibilities.

statement: Include AI whistleblower protections in onboarding and annual staff training.
quote: Rather than building entirely new infrastructure, much of this can be embedded into what HDOs already have: non-retaliation language can be updated to reference AI specifically within existing HR policies, AI-related reporting categories can be added to current compliance hotline intake forms, and whistleblower protections can be incorporated into the AI modules of onboarding and annual training programs.
hazard: Staff remain unaware of protections for reporting AI concerns.

statement: Obtain legal confirmation that AI whistleblower policies address applicable federal anti-retaliation statutes, including the False Claims Act.
quote: Has your legal team confirmed that your whistleblower policy addresses applicable federal anti-retaliation statutes (including the False Claims Act) particularly where AI tools are used in billing, coding, clinical documentation, or prior authorization workflows?
hazard: Whistleblower policies omit legal protections relevant to AI-enabled administrative and clinical workflows.

statement: Target AI training to staff who actually act on the tool's outputs.
quote: Rather than rolling out broad "AI literacy" curricula, training was scoped tightly to the case managers and hospitalists who actually acted on the risk score, and was reinforced in existing multidisciplinary rounds.
hazard: Training resources miss the staff whose decisions depend on AI outputs.

statement: Reinforce AI training during existing multidisciplinary rounds.
quote: Rather than rolling out broad "AI literacy" curricula, training was scoped tightly to the case managers and hospitalists who actually acted on the risk score, and was reinforced in existing multidisciplinary rounds.
hazard: One-time training fails to support safe AI use in routine clinical workflows.

statement: Pilot clinical AI in silent mode against live local EHR data before exposing outputs to clinicians.
quote: Models were piloted in silent mode against live EHR data before alerts were surfaced to clinicians, satisfying the playbook's pre-deployment testing expectation without a dedicated sandbox.
hazard: Untested local behavior affects clinical decisions immediately after activation.

statement: Capture staff feedback within the clinical workflow where AI outputs appear.
quote: Staff feedback was captured in the same rounding and case-management workflow where the score appeared, and concerns were triaged by Parkland Center for Clinical Innovation (PCCI) engineers back into retraining cycles.
hazard: Separate feedback processes miss concerns arising during actual AI use.

statement: Use a dedicated research partner, academic affiliate, or regional collaborative as a peer-to-peer AI feedback channel.
quote: The broader lesson is that smaller HDOs can meet Subdomain 4.5 recommendations and guidance by scoping training narrowly to the people who touch the model, aligning to existing patient-safety reporting, and using a small dedicated research partner (academic affiliate or regional collaborative) as the peer-to-peer feedback channel.
hazard: Resource-constrained organizations lack expert channels for reviewing AI feedback.

statement: Tailor AI training to staff roles and their specific clinical workflows.
quote: Training was role-differentiated: ED nurses were trained on the specific alert triage pathway, physicians received use-case-specific guidance on how COMPOSER differed from the prior rules-based screen, and the model was accompanied by plain-language documentation describing its inputs and known limitations.
hazard: Generic training leaves staff unprepared for their specific AI-related responsibilities.

statement: Explain how newly deployed AI differs from the system or workflow it replaces.
quote: Training was role-differentiated: ED nurses were trained on the specific alert triage pathway, physicians received use-case-specific guidance on how COMPOSER differed from the prior rules-based screen, and the model was accompanied by plain-language documentation describing its inputs and known limitations.
hazard: Clinicians incorrectly transfer assumptions from the previous system to the new AI.

statement: Provide plain-language documentation describing the AI tool's inputs and known limitations.
quote: Training was role-differentiated: ED nurses were trained on the specific alert triage pathway, physicians received use-case-specific guidance on how COMPOSER differed from the prior rules-based screen, and the model was accompanied by plain-language documentation describing its inputs and known limitations.
hazard: Clinicians misunderstand AI inputs or rely on outputs beyond known limitations.

statement: Use a phased go-live for clinical AI deployment.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Immediate broad deployment exposes many patients to unresolved implementation problems.

statement: Log whether clinicians act on, defer, or override AI outputs.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Organizations cannot detect patterns of AI acceptance, deferral, or override.

statement: Review recorded clinician responses to AI outputs through a structured feedback loop.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Collected usage data never informs improvements to deployment or staff support.

statement: Retrain staff when review of clinician feedback identifies a need.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Identified misunderstandings or workflow errors persist after deployment.

statement: Collaborate with trusted partners whose AI governance, testing, data-management, or advisory services align with the CHAI AI Governance Framework.
quote: Collaborate with trusted partners delivering excellence in AI governance, testing, data management, and advisory services - all aligned with the CHAI AI Governance Framework.
hazard: External support lacks alignment with the organization's responsible AI governance framework.

statement: For covered entities, develop a clear, user-friendly notice explaining individuals' health-information rights and organizational privacy practices.
quote: The HIPAA Privacy Rule requires health plans and covered health care providers to develop and distribute a notice that provides a clear, user friendly explanation of individuals’ rights with respect to their personal health information and the privacy practices of health plans and health care providers.
hazard: Patients lack understandable information about health-data rights and privacy practices.

statement: For covered entities, distribute the required notice of health-information rights and privacy practices.
quote: The HIPAA Privacy Rule requires health plans and covered health care providers to develop and distribute a notice that provides a clear, user friendly explanation of individuals’ rights with respect to their personal health information and the privacy practices of health plans and health care providers.
hazard: Patients never receive required information about their health-data rights.

statement: Use the Patient and Family Advisory Councils Blueprint to guide formation and maintenance of a patient and family advisory council.
quote: Use the Patient and Family Advisory Councils Blueprint to help guide your organization through the process of forming and maintaining a successful PFAC.
hazard: Organizations lack a sustained mechanism for patient and family input.

statement: Use cross-sectoral AI RMF profiles to manage risks associated with LLM deployment.
quote: Cross-sectoral profiles can be used to govern, map, measure, and manage risks associated with activities or business processes common across sectors, such as the use of large language models (LLMs), cloud-based services, or acquisition.
hazard: Unmanaged AI risks in organizational activities and business processes.

statement: Tailor generative AI risk measurement to model, system, and use-case characteristics.
quote: These characteristics include but are not limited to GAI model or system architecture, training mechanisms and libraries, data types used for training or fine-tuning, levels of model access or availability of model weights, and application or use case context. Organizations may choose to tailor how they measure GAI risks based on these characteristics.
hazard: Risk assessments that overlook relevant system characteristics or deployment context.

statement: Allocate risk management resources according to the severity and likelihood of harms in the deployment context.
quote: They may additionally wish to allocate risk management resources relative to the severity and likelihood of negative impacts, including where and how these risks manifest, and their direct and material impacts harms in the context of GAI use.
hazard: Insufficient resources to address the most likely or severe harms.

statement: Categorize generative AI risks according to your organization’s approach to risk definition and management.
quote: These risks can be further categorized by organizations depending on their unique approaches to risk definition and management.
hazard: Risk classifications that do not support organizational risk management.

statement: Assess AI chemical and biological design tools for potential misuse in designing harmful agents.
quote: As these models become more eﬃcacious, including for beneficial uses, it will be important to assess their potential to be used for harm, such as the ideation and design of novel harmful chemical or biological agents.
hazard: Misuse of AI-assisted design to create harmful chemical or biological agents.

statement: Monitor AI tools’ ability to facilitate chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear weapons planning.
quote: While some of these described capabilities lie beyond the reach of existing GAI tools, ongoing assessments of this risk would be enhanced by monitoring both the ability of AI tools to facilitate CBRN weapons planning and GAI systems’ connection or access to relevant data and tools.
hazard: Undetected capabilities that enable chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear weapons planning.

statement: Monitor generative AI systems’ connections or access to data and tools relevant to chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear misuse.
quote: While some of these described capabilities lie beyond the reach of existing GAI tools, ongoing assessments of this risk would be enhanced by monitoring both the ability of AI tools to facilitate CBRN weapons planning and GAI systems’ connection or access to relevant data and tools.
hazard: Data and tool access that enables chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear misuse.

statement: Monitor confabulation risks when integrating generative AI into consequential decision-making applications.
quote: Risks of confabulated content may be especially important to monitor when integrating GAI into applications involving consequential decision making.
hazard: Incorrect consequential decisions based on confidently presented false information.

statement: Apply model-output restrictions to limit harmful generated content.
quote: Many current systems restrict model outputs to limit certain content or in response to certain prompts, but this approach may still produce harmful recommendations in response to other less-explicit, novel prompts (also relevant to CBRN Information or Capabilities, Data Privacy, Information Security, and Obscene, Degrading and/or Abusive Content).
hazard: Generation of dangerous, violent, hateful, self-harm, or illegal recommendations.

statement: Assess GAI output accuracy and reliability against ground truth data using varied evaluation methods.
quote: Assess the accuracy, quality, reliability, and authenticity of GAI output by comparing it to a set of known ground truth data and by using a variety of evaluation methods
hazard: Inaccurate or unreliable GAI outputs.

statement: Deploy fact-checking techniques to verify the accuracy of information generated by GAI systems.
quote: Deploy and document fact-checking techniques to verify the accuracy and veracity of information generated by GAI systems, especially when the information comes from multiple (or unknown) sources.
hazard: Generated information is inaccurate or lacks veracity.

statement: Implement regular adversarial testing plans for GAI systems to identify vulnerabilities and misuse potential.
quote: Implement plans for GAI systems to undergo regular adversarial testing to identify vulnerabilities and potential manipulation or misuse.
hazard: Vulnerabilities, manipulation, or misuse of GAI systems.

statement: Evaluate whether GAI operators and end-users can accurately understand content lineage and origin.
quote: Evaluate whether GAI operators and end-users can accurately understand content lineage and origin.
hazard: Users misinterpreting the origin and lineage of AI content.

statement: Adapt existing training programs to include modules on digital content transparency.
quote: Adapt existing training programs to include modules on digital content transparency.
hazard: Lack of understanding of digital content transparency among staff.

statement: Implement systems to continuously monitor and track the outcomes of human-GAI configurations.
quote: Implement systems to continually monitor and track the outcomes of human-GAI configurations for future refinement and improvements.
hazard: Poor outcomes or unforeseen issues from human-AI interactions.

statement: Conduct periodic monitoring of AI-generated content for privacy risks and address sensitive data exposure.
quote: Conduct periodic monitoring of AI-generated content for privacy risks; address any possible instances of PII or sensitive data exposure.
hazard: Exposure of PII or sensitive data in AI-generated content.

statement: Re-evaluate risks when adapting GAI models to new domains.
quote: Re-evaluate risks when adapting GAI models to new domains.
hazard: Unanticipated risks when models are used outside their original domain.

statement: Establish warning systems to detect if a GAI system is used in a new domain.
quote: Additionally, establish warning systems to determine if a GAI system is being used in a new domain where previous assumptions (relating to context of use or mapped risks such as security, and safety) may no longer hold.
hazard: GAI usage in novel contexts invalidating safety and security assumptions.

statement: Detect the presence of PII or sensitive data in generated output text, image, video, or audio.
quote: Leverage approaches to detect the presence of PII or sensitive data in generated output text, image, video, or audio.
hazard: Unintentional generation of PII or sensitive data.

statement: Consider disclosing the use of GAI to end users in relevant contexts.
quote: Consider disclosing use of GAI to end users in relevant contexts, while considering the objective of disclosure, the context of use, the likelihood and magnitude of the risk posed, the audience of the disclosure, as well as the frequency of the disclosures.
hazard: Lack of transparency about AI usage for end users.

statement: Implement continuous monitoring of GAI system impacts to identify whether outputs are equitable across sub-populations.
quote: Implement continuous monitoring of GAI system impacts to identify whether GAI outputs are equitable across various sub-populations.
hazard: Inequitable GAI impacts or biased outputs across different demographic groups.

statement: Review and verify sources and citations in GAI system outputs during pre-deployment and ongoing monitoring.
quote: Review and verify sources and citations in GAI system outputs during predeployment risk measurement and ongoing monitoring activities.
hazard: Hallucinated or incorrect citations and sources in outputs.

statement: Track and document instances of anthropomorphization in GAI system interfaces.
quote: Track and document instances of anthropomorphization (e.g., human images, mentions of human feelings, cyborg imagery or motifs) in GAI system interfaces.
hazard: Users incorrectly attributing human qualities or capabilities to the AI.

statement: Monitor and document instances where human operators or other systems override the GAI's decisions.
quote: Monitor and document instances where human operators or other systems override the GAI's decisions.
hazard: Unidentified flaws in GAI performance that require human intervention.

statement: Verify that GAI system architecture can monitor outputs and handle, recover from, and repair errors.
quote: Verify that GAI system architecture can monitor outputs and performance, and handle, recover from, and repair errors when security anomalies, threats and impacts are detected.
hazard: System inability to recover from security anomalies or errors.

statement: Conduct user surveys to gather satisfaction with AI-generated content and perceptions of authenticity.
quote: Conduct user surveys to gather user satisfaction with the AI-generated content and user perceptions of content authenticity.
hazard: Misalignment between user expectations and AI content quality or authenticity.

statement: Evaluate GAI system performance in real-world scenarios to reveal issues not found in controlled testing.
quote: Evaluate GAI system performance in real-world scenarios to observe its behavior in practical environments and reveal issues that might not surface in controlled and optimized testing environments.
hazard: Unforeseen failures in real-world practical environments.

statement: Decline AI solutions whose risk profiles exceed organizational risk tolerance.
quote: In some cases, it will also determine when an organization chooses not to move forward with a solution, given its risk profile and the organization’s risk tolerance.
hazard: Deployment of solutions with unacceptable residual risk.

statement: Embed AI governance review as a mandatory procurement approval gate.
quote: Embedding your organization's AI governance review (which may consist of initial AI intake, risk assessment, evaluations) as a mandatory gate in the procurement approval workflow.
hazard: Purchasing AI before its risks are assessed.

statement: Link AI governance review to contract negotiation so findings can change terms before execution.
quote: Linking the responsible AI governance review process to contract negotiation, so that any findings, such as model limitations, bias or subgroup performance gaps, or unacceptable risk profiles, can still be used to amend contract terms before execution.
hazard: Losing contractual leverage to address identified AI risks.

statement: Obtain legal or compliance review of the standard AI intake questionnaire before contract sign-off.
quote: For organizations using a standard AI intake questionnaire, ensuring the questionnaire is reviewed by legal and/or compliance before contract sign-off.
hazard: Unresolved legal or compliance risks at contract execution.

statement: Document any contract execution that precedes completion of AI governance review.
quote: If a contract is executed before a full AI governance review can be completed, document this with a defined timeline for completing the review and a process for contract amendment if needed.
hazard: Untracked exceptions to AI governance review.

statement: Set a timeline for completing AI governance review deferred until after contract execution.
quote: If a contract is executed before a full AI governance review can be completed, document this with a defined timeline for completing the review and a process for contract amendment if needed.
hazard: Indefinite deployment without completed governance review.

statement: Define a contract amendment process when governance review is deferred until after execution.
quote: If a contract is executed before a full AI governance review can be completed, document this with a defined timeline for completing the review and a process for contract amendment if needed.
hazard: Inability to remedy risks discovered after signing.

statement: Check AI addenda for conflicts with existing contract terms.
quote: Note that it is important to check that any addenda do not conflict with terms in the existing contract.
hazard: Conflicting terms undermine enforceability of AI protections.

statement: Define what counts as AI within the contractual addendum.
quote: (i) What counts as AI for the purpose of the addendum.
hazard: AI features escape contractual safeguards through ambiguous definitions.

statement: Specify AI data-use restrictions in vendor contracts.

statement: Use completion attestations or awareness checks to validate general AI literacy training.

statement: Use knowledge assessments or scenario-based checks for staff interacting with higher-risk or workflow-changing AI.

hazard: Staff use consequential AI without demonstrating practical understanding.

statement: Include maintenance, monitoring, and performance tracking in training for AI and IT staff.

statement: Include governance policies, regulatory requirements, and audit processes in training for compliance and risk staff.

statement: Include workflow integration, escalations, and patient-facing implications in training for operations staff.

statement: Include report system oversight in training for department leads.

statement: Train ethics personnel on AI-related ethical obligations and alignment with organizational mission and values.

statement: Pilot AI at selected hospitals before expanding across the health system.

hazard: Systemwide rollout occurs before operational problems are understood.

statement: Standardize staffing, training, and documentation infrastructure before scaling AI across hospitals.

statement: Use an intermediary clinical review team when AI alerts create frontline alert fatigue.

statement: Use a two-week pre-go-live shadowing period for clinicians to rehearse AI workflows without affecting patient care.

statement: Hold daily debriefs for at least two weeks after launch to capture feedback and refine AI workflows.
quote: Daily debriefs continued for at least two weeks post-launch to capture feedback and refine workflows.

statement: Gate go-live authorization on formal IT, leadership, administrative, and training readiness criteria.
quote: No hospital was authorized to go live without meeting formal readiness criteria spanning IT, leadership, administrative, and training domains which ensured deployment authorization was a deliberate gate.

statement: Inventory the staff roles that interact with or are affected by each deployed AI system.

statement: Include knowledge-based content and scenario-based exercises with testing or knowledge checks in AI training.

statement: Maintain and periodically review training audits for user adherence and training effectiveness.
quote: Are training audits maintained and reviewed on a recurring basis to ensure users are adherent and the training itself is effective?

statement: Involve end users in piloting before full rollout.
quote: Are end users involved in piloting before full rollout?

statement: Formally collect end-user feedback during pilots.
quote: Are end users involved in piloting before full rollout? Is their feedback formally collected and acted on?

statement: Act on end-user feedback from pilots before full rollout.
quote: Are end users involved in piloting before full rollout? Is their feedback formally collected and acted on?

statement: Document known AI limitations and failure modes before go-live.
quote: Are known limitations and failure modes documented and communicated to staff prior to go-live?

statement: Communicate known AI limitations and failure modes to staff before go-live.
quote: Are known limitations and failure modes documented and communicated to staff prior to go-live?
hazard: Staff unknowingly rely on AI in known failure conditions.

statement: Provide patients with a Notice of Privacy Practices by the first service encounter, subject to applicable exceptions.

statement: Review and update the Notice of Privacy Practices to explicitly describe AI-related patient data use.

statement: Consider updating patient privacy communications to explain AI data safeguards and retained HIPAA rights.

hazard: Patients misunderstand AI data protections or their privacy rights.

statement: Provide the Notice of Privacy Practices as soon as reasonably practicable after emergency treatment when the ordinary deadline does not apply.

statement: Consult legal counsel about applicable exceptions to privacy-notice requirements.

statement: Use clear, user-friendly explanations of privacy practices and patient information rights in privacy notices.

statement: Establish a process to review and update privacy notices when privacy practices materially change, including deployment of new technologies.

statement: Provide staff training or standard documentation for explaining AI-related privacy practices to patients.

statement: Establish a patient transparency and consent process appropriate to relevant AI solutions.

statement: Use material changes to standard care or substitution for clinician judgment as thresholds for formal AI consent.

statement: Use new clinical risks beyond general treatment consent as a threshold for formal AI consent.

statement: Use collection of new patient data categories, such as voice or biometrics, as a threshold for formal AI consent.

hazard: New categories of patient data are collected without appropriate consent.

statement: Use investigational AI or AI within a research protocol as a threshold for formal patient consent.
quote: The AI use is investigational or part of a research protocol.
hazard: Patients participate in investigational AI use without formal consent.

statement: Obtain explicit AI consent when required by applicable state or specialty regulations.
quote: Applicable state or specialty regulation requires explicit consent for the use case (e.g., certain genomic or behavioral health applications).

statement: Inform patients of reasonable non-AI alternatives when AI materially influences a clinical recommendation.

statement: Identify patient-journey touchpoints where patients encounter AI-informed decisions or AI-generated outputs.

statement: Update existing patient workflows and documents with plain-language descriptions of relevant AI use where possible.

statement: Review and update patient transparency materials when deploying new AI systems or materially updating existing systems.

statement: Link appointment confirmation emails to patient portal information about AI use.

statement: Provide a consistent, accessible way for patients to ask AI questions or raise concerns throughout their care episode.

statement: Ensure AI incident communications comply with relevant federal and state laws and protections.

statement: Provide anonymity protections for internal and external AI incident reporters.

statement: Provide confidentiality protections for internal and external AI incident reporting.

statement: Provide non-retaliation assurances for internal and external AI incident reporters.

statement: Clearly disclose data retention policies for internal and external AI incident reporting.

statement: Verify that fine-tuning has not compromised the model's safety and security controls.

statement: Act on patient feedback about AI use.

statement: Include patient or community representatives on AI advisory committees or governance working groups.

statement: Include patients or community members on AI pilot evaluation panels.

statement: Extend existing patient-safety reporting infrastructure with AI-specific fields, tags, categories, and escalation pathways.

statement: Reinforce AI training through recurring briefings.

statement: Maintain AI training records.

statement: Review AI training records on a recurring basis.

hazard: Training gaps and overdue refreshers remain undetected.

statement: Assign clear AI training responsibilities within each department.

hazard: Training obligations are neglected because ownership is unclear.

statement: Consider designating departmental AI Governance Champions for peer support and first-line escalation of staff questions.

hazard: Staff questions and emerging concerns lack an accessible escalation contact.

statement: Make completion of required training a prerequisite for AI system access or use.

statement: Train AI and IT staff on maintenance, monitoring, and system performance tracking.

statement: Interpose a remote nurse review team between AI alerts and frontline clinicians when pilot findings identify alert fatigue.

statement: Conduct a two-week pre-go-live shadowing period for clinicians to rehearse AI-enabled workflows.

statement: Include new clinical risks among thresholds for formal AI consent.

statement: Subject AI red-teaming results to additional analysis before incorporating them into governance decisions and policy updates.

hazard: Governance decisions based on misinterpreted or unrepresentative red-team findings

statement: Have domain experts (e.g., clinicians) modify or verify red-teaming prompts written by general public participants.

statement: Evaluate how users engage with GAI content in decision-making tasks and how they react to overt AI disclosures.

statement: Integrate pre- and post-deployment external user feedback into the monitoring process for generative AI applications.

hazard: Performance changes missed by automated error collection alone

statement: Ensure staff interacting with AI systems understand their roles in reporting AI incidents.

statement: Develop incident reporting guidelines that specify AI actor responsibilities for identifying GAI incidents.

hazard: Inconsistent identification and reporting of GAI incidents

statement: Document and review third-party inputs and plugins connected to LLM systems, including their access controls.
quote: Documentation and review of third-party inputs and plugins for GAI systems is especially important for AI Actors in the context of incident disclosure; LLM inputs and content delivered through these plugins is often distributed, with inconsistent or insuﬃcient access control.
hazard: Data exposure or untraceable incidents via poorly controlled LLM plugins

statement: Log, record, and analyze GAI incidents to facilitate information sharing with relevant parties.
quote: Documentation practices including logging, recording, and analyzing GAI incidents can facilitate smoother sharing of information with relevant AI Actors.
hazard: Incomplete incident records impeding root-cause tracing and response

statement: Maintain change management records, version history, and metadata for generative AI systems to support incident response.
quote: Regular information sharing, change management records, version history and metadata can also empower AI Actors responding to and managing AI incidents.
hazard: Inability to identify which system version caused an incident

statement: Keep the collection of data to a minimum to mitigate the risks associated with data breaches and misuse.
quote: Moreover, the collection of data should be kept to a minimum.

statement: Implement a robust data management system that provides clear ways for patients to grant, deny, or revoke consent.
quote: implementing a robust data management system empowers patients by providing clear ways to grant, deny, or revoke consent for the use of their data
hazard: Unauthorized or non-consensual use of patient data.

statement: Implement appropriate and sufficient policies to ensure AI users act in accordance with the current standard of care.

hazard: Deviations from the standard of care due to unguided AI use.

statement: Disclose and document when AI is utilized in health care decision-making at the point of care.
quote: When AI is utilized in health care decision-making at the point of care, that use should be disclosed and documented
hazard: Hidden use of AI obscuring how decisions impacting patient care are made.

statement: Educate patients about the benefits and risks of consumer-facing large language models, including GPTs.

hazard: Patients acting on false or misleading AI-generated medical advice.

statement: Require human examination of patient records prior to issuing an AI-assisted care denial.

statement: Ensure clinicians engage only with AI that satisfies rigorous standards to advance equity, prioritize safety, and limit risks.

hazard: Adoption of unsafe or inequitable AI applications.

statement: Utilize clinical experts to validate clinical knowledge in AI tools and monitor the technology for clinical validity over time.

statement: Collect only the minimum patient data necessary for the AI tool's intended purpose.

statement: Apply anonymization or pseudonymization to remove or replace personal identifiers in data sets used with AI systems.

statement: Implement a data management system that lets patients grant, deny, or revoke consent for use of their data in AI.

statement: Deploy protections against input manipulation and malicious attacks on AI systems.

statement: Establish organizational policies governing purchase and use of AI tools that ensure use aligns with the current standard of care.

statement: Involve physicians in defining the organization's AI risk tolerance, especially for AI affecting direct patient care.

statement: Permit physicians to use only AI tools that meet rigorous, clearly defined standards for safety, equity, and risk limitation.

statement: Have clinical experts validate the clinical knowledge, pathways, and standards of care embedded in AI tools before use.

statement: Assign clinical experts to monitor AI tools for clinical validity over time as the technology evolves.

hazard: Degraded clinical validity as models change over time

statement: Disclose to patients and physicians when AI is used in health care decision-making at the point of care.
quote: When AI is utilized in health care decision-making at the point of care, that use should be disclosed and documented to limit risks to, and mitigate inequities for, both patients and physicians

statement: Document in the record when AI is used in point-of-care health care decision-making.

statement: Tailor AI transparency disclosures to the needs of the specific end users receiving them.

statement: Design AI disclosure processes that inform patients and physicians without increasing administrative burden.

statement: Mitigate harms resulting from identified algorithmic discrimination in AI tools.

statement: Base AI oversight intensity on risk of harm and benefit, considering intended use, evidence, automation level, transparency, and deployment conditions.

statement: Educate patients, physicians, staff, and administrators on the promise and limitations of health care AI.

statement: Encourage physicians to educate patients about the benefits and risks of consumer-facing LLMs.
quote: encourage physicians to educate patients about the benefits and risks of consumers facing LLMs including GPTs
hazard: Patients harmed by false or misleading LLM-generated medical advice

statement: Require human examination of patient records before any AI-assisted claim or prior authorization denial.

statement: Have AI-assisted claim reviews performed by clinicians with relevant expertise who are not incentivized to deny care.

statement: Ensure AI-assisted claim review uses accurate, up-to-date clinical criteria from specialty society guidelines and peer-reviewed literature.
quote: (1) is based on accurate and up-to-date clinical criteria derived from national medical specialty society guidelines and peer reviewed clinical literature
hazard: Denials based on outdated or inaccurate clinical criteria

statement: Obtain assurance that clinical generative AI tools provide safe, accurate, non-discriminatory answers before deployment.
quote: While generative AI use for clinical applications is relatively limited currently, it is expected to grow and patients and physicians will need assurances that it is providing safe, accurate, non-discriminatory answers to the full extent possible, whether through regulation or generally accepted standards for design, development, and deployment.
hazard: Fabricated, inconsistent, or biased generative AI answers spreading misinformation

statement: Apply appropriate human oversight to the application of AI output in benefits administration.
quote: stating that it must take into account considerations such as appropriate human oversight of the application of the output from AI.

statement: Develop and adopt appropriate policies that anticipate and minimize negative impacts of generative AI.

hazard: Unmanaged risks and negative impacts from generative AI tools.

statement: Ensure all practice staff are educated on the risks and limitations of generative AI tools, including patient privacy concerns.

hazard: Staff lacking understanding of generative AI risks and privacy issues.

statement: Implement appropriate governance policies for generative AI tools prior to adoption.
quote: ...and should have appropriate governance policies in place for its use prior to adoption.

statement: Educate patients about the benefits and risks of using AI-based tools, such as LLMs, for health information.

statement: Do not utilize AI systems introducing overall or disparate risk beyond the organization's capabilities to mitigate.

hazard: Deployment of AI systems with unmanageable risks.

statement: Implement and utilize AI to avoid exacerbating clinician burden and align with clinical workflows.

hazard: AI implementations that increase clinician burden or disrupt workflows.

statement: Disclose AI use impacting medical decisions to physicians and patients in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner.
quote: When AI is used in a manner which impacts access to care or impacts medical decision making at the point of care, that use of AI should be disclosed and documented to both physicians and/or patients in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner.

statement: Allow patients or caregivers to request additional review from a licensed clinician when AI is used.
quote: The opportunity for a patient or their caregiver to request additional review from a licensed clinician should be made available upon request.
hazard: Patients lacking recourse when subjected to AI-influenced decisions.

statement: Document the use of AI in the medical record when it directly impacts patient care, access, or medical decision making.
quote: When AI is used in a manner which directly impacts patient care, access to care, medical decision making, or the medical record, that use of AI should be documented in the medical record.
hazard: Untraceable AI involvement in patient care decisions.

statement: Ensure clinical decisions influenced by AI include specified qualified human intervention points during the decision-making process.

hazard: Fully autonomous AI medical decision making without human oversight.

statement: Maintain a human in the loop capable of intervening or overriding AI model outputs for medical decision making.

statement: Clearly inform patients when they are interacting with an AI tool that serves as their main point of contact.

statement: Tailor AI transparency information to the AI lifecycle stage and to the role or knowledge of each user.

statement: Communicate use of AI that may directly impact medical decision making to all parties involved in that decision.

statement: Give physicians access to information on how an AI tool was trained and validated before use, to assess quality, performance, equity, and utility.

statement: Disclose enough detail about an AI tool for physicians to judge whether it applies to the individual patient being treated.

statement: Consider vendor-provided reported performance, intended use, intended population, and task appropriateness when selecting AI tools.

statement: Develop and adopt organizational policies that anticipate and minimize negative impacts of generative AI use.
quote: To manage risk, health care organizations should develop and adopt appropriate polices that anticipate and minimize negative impacts.
hazard: Unmanaged generative AI risks in clinical and patient care settings

statement: Put governance policies for a generative AI tool in place prior to adopting it in practice.

statement: Encourage physicians to educate patients about benefits and risks of using LLMs for information on health conditions, treatments, or appropriate clinicians.

statement: Avoid using AI tools outside their intended use or intended population, or tools lacking evidence of clinical validation.

statement: Provide user education on data privacy risks specific to LLMs and generative AI tools.

statement: Secure and validate input data to AI tools to prevent malicious inputs from compromising function.

statement: Strengthen deployed AI systems against cybersecurity threats.

statement: Train physicians and staff on the risks of mis- and disinformation when using generative AI.

statement: Make patients aware of the risks of mis- and disinformation when engaging with generative AI.

statement: Require AI vendors to provide mechanisms for reporting mis- and disinformation generated by their products.

statement: Evaluate AI systems with specific focus on mitigating bias so deployment does not exacerbate disparities in access, treatment, or outcomes.

statement: Scale scrutiny, validation, and oversight of each AI system proportionately to its potential for disparate harm.

statement: Specify qualified human intervention points in any clinical decision process influenced by AI.

statement: Staff human intervention points with licensed physicians qualified to provide the same service without AI assistance.

statement: Provide AI-use disclosures in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner.

statement: Allow patients or caregivers to request additional review by a licensed clinician of AI-influenced decisions.

statement: Use structured feedback mechanisms to capture user input about AI-generated content.

statement: Educate all practice staff about generative AI risks and limitations, including patient privacy concerns.

statement: Use AI tools whose performance has been validated in the intended practice setting.

statement: Use AI tools within their intended use.

statement: Use AI tools for their intended patient populations.

statement: Select AI tools with evidence of clinical validation.

statement: Obtain patient authorization for AI uses that require it under HIPAA.

statement: Collect only the minimum information needed for each AI-related purpose.

statement: Educate generative AI users about data privacy.

statement: Assess AI fairness at every adoption stage.

statement: Assess AI reliability at every adoption stage.

statement: Assess AI validity at every adoption stage.

statement: Assess AI transparency at every adoption stage.

statement: Identify experienced partners and subject matter experts to support AI adoption.
quote: Critical to the successful adoption of AI is identifying partners and subject matter experts who can support your health center’s AI development process. Experienced partners can include vendors, leaders from Health Center Controlled Networks (HCCN) and Clinically Integrated Networks (CIN), internal staff, and other health centers with relevant AI experience.
hazard: AI implementation without sufficient expertise or support.

statement: Tier generative AI functions by risk using two axes: degree of independent activity and severity of harm from relying on an incorrect output.

statement: Classify GenAI functions that direct patient or clinician actions as higher risk than functions providing non-directive information.
quote: CDRH is considering treating these “actiondirecting” functions as higher risk functions than GenAI-enabled functions that provide simple non-directive information.

statement: Do not treat 'talk to your doctor' or 'not a medical professional' disclaimers as lowering the risk tier of action-directing patient-facing outputs.

statement: Classify GenAI functions that assign diagnoses, prescribe medications, or initiate order sets as higher risk than informational functions.

statement: Rate patient-facing GenAI informational functions higher on consequence severity than equivalent clinician-facing functions.

statement: Assess elevated risk when generalist clinicians use GenAI tools whose safe use depends on specialist expertise to evaluate outputs.
quote: A function that helps a generalist HCP approach a question typically handled by a specialist may meaningfully extend access to specialty knowledge, while a function whose safe use depends on contextualization by specialist expertise may present elevated risk when used by HCPs lacking that expertise to independently evaluate outputs.
hazard: Generalists unable to recognize incorrect specialist-domain outputs

statement: Evaluate conversational GenAI tools across realistic multi-turn conversation trajectories, not only single-turn function tests.
quote: CDRH is considering an approach for assessing risk of such devices that would consider the device’s behavior across realistic conversational trajectories, not only at the level of individual functions.
hazard: Chatbot drifts from informational to action-directing advice during extended conversations

statement: Evaluate GenAI care-escalation functions for both under-escalation and over-escalation errors.

hazard: Delayed emergency care or unnecessary ED use, anxiety, and eroded trust

statement: Evaluate the final user-facing GenAI system as configured for deployment rather than the foundation model alone.

statement: Scale the rigor and amount of evaluation evidence to the tool's intended use and risk tier.

statement: Monitor the deployed GenAI tool and its underlying foundation model to maintain accuracy, relevance, and reliability for the intended use.

statement: Complement pre-deployment evaluation with ongoing real-world performance monitoring of GenAI tools.

statement: Re-evaluate GenAI tools when the underlying model, prompts, retrieval strategies, guardrails, orchestration logic, or user interface change.

hazard: Unvalidated component changes silently alter tool behavior

statement: Test whether the GenAI tool recognizes safety-critical situations and escalates appropriately.
quote: o S.1 Safety-critical recognition and escalation;

statement: Test whether the GenAI tool stays within its intended scope and adheres to defined boundaries.
quote: o S.2 Scope maintenance and boundary adherence; and

statement: Test the GenAI tool's calibration, communication of uncertainty, and deferral to clinicians when appropriate.
quote: o S.3 Calibration, uncertainty communication, and clinical deferral

statement: Test the communication quality and user comprehension of GenAI outputs.
quote: o E.4 Communication quality and user comprehension
hazard: Users misunderstand outputs and act incorrectly

statement: Test GenAI tool robustness, reliability, and reproducibility across repeated and varied inputs.
quote: o R.1 Robustness, reliability, and reproducibility; and
hazard: Variable outputs to similar inputs produce inconsistent care

statement: Evaluate GenAI tool performance across patient subgroups.
quote: o R.2 Subgroup performance
hazard: Poorer performance for specific populations goes undetected

statement: Prespecify evaluation methods and acceptance criteria before testing a GenAI tool.
quote: CDRH envisions that for benchmarking conducted under a competency-based approach, sponsors would define the scope of testing based on the device’s intended use and risk profile, prespecify evaluation methods, describe and justify scoring rubrics, identify qualified expert adjudicators where applicable, and prespecify and justify acceptance criteria.
hazard: Post hoc selection of favorable metrics masks inadequate performance

statement: Use justified scoring rubrics and qualified expert adjudicators to grade GenAI outputs during evaluation.

statement: Supplement public benchmarks with tests and datasets tailored to the specific tool, accounting for contamination, saturation, and unrepresentativeness.

statement: Maintain an ongoing process to identify decision support tools in use whose input variables measure race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.
