hazard: Invalid rubrics misjudging open-ended output quality for the actual care context

statement: Use expert adjudicators independent of the tool vendor and foundation model developer, with qualifications matching the clinical domain of outputs reviewed.
quote: Where expert adjudication is warranted, it would include adjudicators that are structurally independent from the device sponsor and, where the device incorporates a third-party model, from the developer of that model, and possess qualifications aligned with the clinical domain and complexity of the outputs under review.
hazard: Conflicted or unqualified reviewers overlooking unsafe outputs

statement: Apply the same independence and qualification standards when an LLM serves as the evaluator of another LLM's outputs.
quote: These considerations would still be applicable when the expert adjudicator is itself an LLM.
hazard: Unreliable or biased LLM-as-judge evaluations masking tool failures

statement: Test the tool's clinical knowledge across adjacent clinical domains its outputs may affect, such as comorbidities and drug interactions.
quote: in such cases, it may be appropriate to expect benchmark testing to assess clinical knowledge and analysis across other relevant clinical domains.
hazard: Outputs harming comorbid conditions or causing cross-domain drug interactions

statement: Use evaluation datasets representative of the local deployment contexts where the tool will be used.
quote: Similarly, because a GenAI-enabled device may perform differently depending on its deployment environment, it may be appropriate to expect benchmark datasets to be representative of the deployment contexts in which the device is expected to be used.
hazard: Performance failure in local settings unlike the benchmark environment

statement: Confirm tool performance under real-world or clinically representative conditions in addition to structured benchmark testing.
quote: CDRH is therefore considering that clinical confirmation may be a necessary step in addition to benchmarking to determine whether a GenAI-enabled device performs as intended for its intended population under real-world or clinically representative conditions.
hazard: Benchmarks missing failures arising from real users, workflows, and populations

statement: Evaluate the tool retrospectively on previously collected real patient inputs, comparing outputs to a reference standard or expert adjudication.
quote: The device is applied to previously collected patient inputs, with outputs compared to an established reference standard or to expert clinical adjudication.
hazard: Undetected errors on real patient inputs before go-live

statement: Run a shadow deployment where outputs are hidden from clinicians and patients and compared against actual decisions and outcomes.
quote: The device operates in a live clinical workflow on real patients, but its outputs are not shown to clinicians or patients and do not affect care. Outputs are recorded and compared against decisions actually made and, where appropriate, downstream outcomes.
hazard: Exposing patients to an unvalidated tool in live workflows

statement: Test patient-facing tools with trained patient actors following defined scenarios, evaluating outputs against prospectively defined criteria.
quote: Trained patient actors or representative individuals who could plausibly present as patients are directed to follow defined scenarios, with outputs evaluated against prospectively defined criteria.
hazard: Unsafe conversational behavior with real patients not captured by static tests

statement: Have independent clinicians review real patient inputs blinded to tool outputs and compare their responses with the tool's outputs.
quote: this might take the form of blinded review, in which a clinician reviews real patient inputs without seeing the device’s outputs and independently determines the appropriate response for comparison against the device output
hazard: Anchoring bias in reviewers inflating agreement with tool outputs

statement: Evaluate whether the tool performs consistently across clinically relevant patient subgroups in the intended population.
quote: Across these approaches, relevant considerations might include whether the device performs consistently across clinically relevant subgroups within the intended use population.
hazard: Worse performance for specific subgroups causing inequitable harm

statement: Supplement subgroup evaluation with synthetic data only when it is modeled on real patient data and representative of the deployment environment.
quote: CDRH is considering that synthetically generated data modeled on real patient data could potentially supplement evaluation, assuming such synthetic data is representative of the environment in which the device is intended to be deployed.
hazard: Unrepresentative synthetic data hiding performance gaps in small subgroups

statement: Benchmark open-ended tool outputs against a panel of qualified clinicians reflecting the standard of care or a median practicing clinician.
quote: CDRH is considering that for many GenAI-enabled devices, performance might be compared to that of a panel of qualified clinicians whose consensus reflects the applicable standard of care, or to that of a median clinician in practice.
hazard: Accepting a tool that performs worse than clinicians on the same task

statement: Evaluate performance in the configuration actually used, human-AI team versus fully autonomous, matching the intended workflow.
quote: Considerations for selecting the comparator might include how the device is actually used, including the combined performance of the clinician and device working together as a human-AI team versus the device working in a fully autonomous workflow, depending on the intended use.
hazard: Evaluation not reflecting real workflow, misestimating safety of human-AI use

statement: Reassess the tool against prespecified benchmark thresholds on a defined cadence and after triggering events such as underlying model changes.
quote: The sponsor reassesses the device against the prespecified benchmarking thresholds described in Section V.B, on a defined cadence and after defined triggering events, including changes to the underlying model or other components of the deployment architecture.
hazard: Undetected performance regression after model or architecture updates

statement: Periodically have independent clinicians review samples of real-world inputs and outputs, sampled to reflect the range of presentations encountered.
quote: Qualified, independent clinician adjudicators review samples of real-world inputs and outputs against prospectively defined criteria, sampled to reflect the range of clinically relevant presentations and interaction patterns the device encounters in real-world use.
hazard: Unsafe real-world outputs going unnoticed after deployment

statement: Monitor for performance drift from changes in input population, data environment, or model components using specified analyses and detection thresholds.
quote: The sponsor monitors for performance degradation (e.g., drift) that may result from changes in the input population, the data environment, or underlying model components, specifying the analyses and thresholds to detect such degradation.
hazard: Gradual performance degradation causing harm before detection

statement: Re-benchmark the tool against the same baseline capabilities after any modification to determine whether safety or effectiveness changed.
quote: A GenAIenabled device that has been benchmarked against a defined set of capabilities for premarket authorization could potentially be “re-benchmarked” against the same capabilities following a modification, providing evidence to determine whether the modification has affected safety or effectiveness of the device.
hazard: Modifications silently degrading tool safety or effectiveness

statement: Establish contractual or technical mechanisms to detect and evaluate changes initiated by third-party foundation model developers.
quote: What mechanisms—for example, contractual, technical, or through a PCCP—could provide reasonable assurance that third-party developer-initiated changes do not compromise the safety or effectiveness of the device?
hazard: Unannounced foundation model updates compromising tool safety

statement: Obtain foundation model documentation covering known limitations, healthcare failure modes, subgroup performance, guardrails, update notification commitments, and audit log availability.
quote: evaluation results on healthcare-relevant benchmarks, including performance across clinically meaningful subgroups; safetyrelevant behavioral constraints and guardrails built into the model; update notification commitments; and audit log availability.
hazard: Deploying models with undisclosed limitations, silent updates, or no auditability

statement: Test escalation of safety-critical states using multi-turn simulations measuring time to escalation, handoff quality, and resistance to over-reassurance.
quote: Relevant testing may include multi-turn simulated encounters that assess time to escalation in evolving presentations, the quality of escalation language and handoff information, and resistance to over-reassurance when users minimize symptoms or resist escalation.
hazard: Missed or delayed escalation of emergencies, or false reassurance

statement: Evaluate both under-escalation and over-escalation as failures when testing the tool's safety-critical recognition.
quote: Both under-escalation (failing to escalate when clinically necessary) and over-escalation (escalating when not clinically indicated) are relevant failures.
hazard: Missed emergencies or unnecessary escalations overwhelming care resources

statement: Test scope adherence with adversarial prompting, prompt injection, emotional manipulation, and multi-turn conversations that drift out of scope.
quote: Relevant testing may include adversarial prompting, prompt injection, emotional-manipulation scenarios, and multi-turn conversations in which individual turns appear in-scope but the cumulative interaction drifts out of scope.
hazard: Tool diagnosing or prescribing beyond intended use when manipulated

statement: Verify the tool refuses out-of-scope requests with clinically useful redirection without over-refusing in-scope requests.
quote: Whether the device recognizes when a request exceeds its intended use or clinical scope and responds with appropriate refusal and clinically useful redirection.
hazard: Out-of-scope advice or unhelpful refusals leaving users without guidance

statement: Treat presentation of uncertain, outdated, or contested information with false confidence as a safety failure in evaluation.
quote: Presenting uncertain, outdated, or contested information with false confidence is treated as a safety failure.
hazard: Overconfident incorrect outputs misleading patients or clinicians

statement: Verify the tool defers to a human clinician for overly complex or uncertain situations without over-deferring on answerable questions.
quote: This element also considers whether the device appropriately handles situations that are too complex or uncertain, including deferral to a human clinician, without over-deferring on questions within its knowledge.
hazard: Tool handling cases beyond its competence without human involvement

statement: Test clinical knowledge currency including guidelines, contraindications, drug interactions, and special populations such as pregnant, pediatric, geriatric, and renal/hepatic-impaired patients.
quote: including current guidelines, contraindications, drug interactions, and population-specific considerations, including, for example, those applicable to pregnant patients, pediatric and geriatric patients, and patients with renal or hepatic impairment.
hazard: Inaccurate or outdated advice harming vulnerable patient populations

statement: Test for premature diagnostic closure using scenarios where initially benign information masks a serious condition.
quote: scenarios designed to detect premature diagnostic closure in which initially benign information masks a more serious underlying condition.
hazard: Missed serious diagnoses due to premature closure

statement: Test dosing calculations, unit conversions, lab interpretation, and recognition of implausible values, including conversational inputs with missing units.
quote: This includes clinically relevant calculations such as, for example, weight-based and renal-function-based dosing and unit conversions, interpretation of laboratory and physiologic values against appropriate reference ranges, and recognition of clinically implausible values such as transcription errors or unit confusion
hazard: Dosing errors or misinterpreted lab values from numerical mistakes

statement: Verify intended users across varied health literacy levels understand outputs, limitations, and when escalation is needed.
quote: This element considers whether intended users can actually understand the device’s outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed across varied health literacy levels;
hazard: Users misunderstanding outputs or failing to seek needed care

statement: Evaluate outputs for coercive, emotionally manipulative, or abusive language before deployment.
quote: the avoidance of coercive, emotionally manipulative, or otherwise inappropriate or abusive language;
hazard: Manipulative or abusive language harming patients

statement: Assess risk of automation bias where users accept fluent outputs without appropriate scrutiny.
quote: and the risk of automation bias, in which a user accepts an output without appropriate scrutiny because of the device’s fluency or perceived authority.
hazard: Users uncritically accepting erroneous but fluent outputs

statement: Test reproducibility across repeated runs and paraphrases, treating variation in escalation, refusal, or diagnostic conclusions as failure.
quote: Variation in non-safety-critical phrasing may be acceptable, but variation in safety-critical behaviors such as escalation, refusal, or diagnostic conclusions is treated as a failure.
hazard: Inconsistent safety-critical behavior across equivalent inputs

statement: Scale AI transparency and disclosure to the risks and potential patient harms of each use case.
quote: of the use of AI should be based upon a risk- and impact-based approach that considers the unique circumstance of AI and its use case. The need for transparency and disclosure is greater where the performance of an AI-enabled technology has a greater risk of causing harm to a patient.
hazard: Insufficient disclosure for high-risk AI uses.

statement: Align AI disclosures with ethical standards or norms.
quote: AI disclosur e should align and meet ethical standards or norms.
hazard: Unethical or misleading disclosure of AI use.

statement: Design AI transparency requirements around end-user needs.
quote: T ransparency requirements should be designed to meet the needs of the end users.
hazard: Disclosures that do not support informed use.

statement: Design AI documentation and disclosures to enhance patient and physician knowledge.
quote: Documentation and disclosure should enhance patient and physician knowledge without increasing administrative burden.
hazard: Poor understanding of AI use.

statement: Avoid increasing administrative burden through AI documentation and disclosure requirements.
quote: Documentation and disclosure should enhance patient and physician knowledge without increasing administrative burden.
hazard: Additional administrative workload.

statement: Disclose AI use affecting access to care or point-of-care medical decisions to physicians and/or patients.
quote: W hen AI is used in a manner which impacts access to care or impacts medical decision making at the point of care, that use of AI should be disclosed and documented to both physicians and/or patients in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner.
hazard: Undisclosed AI influence on care access or medical decisions.

statement: Make disclosures of AI use affecting care access or medical decisions culturally appropriate.
quote: W hen AI is used in a manner which impacts access to care or impacts medical decision making at the point of care, that use of AI should be disclosed and documented to both physicians and/or patients in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner.
hazard: Cultural barriers to understanding AI involvement in care.

statement: Make disclosures of AI use affecting care access or medical decisions linguistically appropriate.
quote: W hen AI is used in a manner which impacts access to care or impacts medical decision making at the point of care, that use of AI should be disclosed and documented to both physicians and/or patients in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner.
hazard: Language barriers to understanding AI involvement in care.

statement: Provide additional licensed-clinician review when a patient or caregiver requests it.
quote: The opportunity for a patient or their caregiver to request additional review from a licensed clinician should be made available upon request.
hazard: Patients cannot obtain human reassessment of AI-influenced care.

statement: Document AI use in the medical record when it directly affects patient care, care access, medical decisions, or the record itself.
quote: W hen AI is used in a manner which directly impacts patient care, access to care, medical decision making, or the medical record, that use of AI should be documented in the medical record.
hazard: Untraceable AI contributions to care or clinical documentation.

statement: Obtain physician consent before AI augments or generates records, communications, or other content on that physician's behalf.
quote: AI t ools or systems cannot augment, create, or otherwise generate records, communications, or other content on behalf of a physician without that physician’s consent and final review.
hazard: Unauthorized content attributed to a physician.

statement: Require final physician review of records, communications, or other content AI augments or generates on that physician's behalf.
quote: AI t ools or systems cannot augment, create, or otherwise generate records, communications, or other content on behalf of a physician without that physician’s consent and final review.
hazard: Unreviewed generated content attributed to a physician.

statement: Disclose algorithmic systems affecting patient access, including claims determinations or coverage limits, to impacted parties.
quote: W hen AI or other algorithmic-based systems or programs are utilized in ways that impact patient access to care, such as by payors to make claims determinations or set coverage limitations, use of those systems or programs must be disclosed to impacted parties.
hazard: Hidden algorithmic influence on access to care.

statement: Clearly disclose direct patient interaction with AI at the beginning of the encounter or interaction.
quote: T he use of AI-enabled technologies by hospitals, health systems, physician practices, or other entities, where patients engage directly with AI, should be clearly disclosed to patients at the beginning of the encounter or interaction with the AI-enabled technology.
hazard: Patients mistake AI interaction for human care.

statement: Identify AI-generated patient-facing content as AI-generated within the content.
quote: Where patient-facing content is generated by AI, the use of AI in generating that content should be disclosed or otherwise noted within the content.
hazard: Patients cannot distinguish generated content from human-authored information.

statement: Obtain the AI system's regulatory approval status before purchase or use.
quote: i) R egulatory approval status.
hazard: Uninformed use of systems with unsuitable regulatory status.

statement: Obtain disclosure of consensus standards and clinical guidelines used throughout the AI technology's lifecycle.
quote: ii) A pplicable consensus standards and clinical guidelines utilized in design, development, deployment, and continued use of the technology.
hazard: Deployment without knowledge of applicable clinical and technical standards.

statement: Obtain a clear description of the AI system's problem formulation.
quote: iii) Clear descr iption of problem formulation and intended use accompanied by clear and detailed instructions for use.
hazard: Mismatch between the system's target problem and deployment needs.

statement: Obtain a clear description of the AI system's intended use.
quote: iii) Clear descr iption of problem formulation and intended use accompanied by clear and detailed instructions for use.
hazard: Use outside the system's intended scope.

statement: Obtain clear, detailed instructions for using the AI system.
quote: iii) Clear descr iption of problem formulation and intended use accompanied by clear and detailed instructions for use.
hazard: Incorrect operation or interpretation of the AI system.

statement: Obtain disclosure of the AI system's intended population.
quote: iv) I ntended population and intended practice setting.
hazard: Use in populations for which the system was not intended.

statement: Obtain disclosure of the AI system's intended practice setting.
quote: iv) I ntended population and intended practice setting.
hazard: Deployment in an unsuitable clinical setting.

statement: Obtain a clear description of AI limitations and risks, including possible disparate impacts.
quote: v) Clear descr iption of any limitations or risks for use, including possible disparate impact.
hazard: Unrecognized limitations, safety risks, or unequal effects.

statement: Obtain an account of how impacted populations were engaged throughout the AI lifecycle.
quote: vi) D escription of how impacted populations were engaged during the AI lifecycle.
hazard: Deployment without understanding whether affected populations' perspectives informed the tool.

statement: Obtain disclosure of training-data provenance.
quote: vii) D etailed information regarding data used to train the model: (1) Data provenance.
hazard: Unknown or unsuitable sources underlying model behavior.

statement: Obtain disclosure of training-dataset size and completeness.
quote: (2) Data size and completeness.
hazard: Unrecognized gaps in the data supporting the model.

statement: Obtain disclosure of training-data timeframes.
quote: (3) Data timeframes.
hazard: Reliance on outdated model knowledge.

statement: Obtain disclosure of training-data diversity.
quote: (4) Data diversity.
hazard: Unrecognized population underrepresentation and biased performance.

statement: Obtain disclosure of training-data labeling accuracy.
quote: (5) Data labeling accuracy.
hazard: Model errors arising from inaccurate labeled data.

statement: Obtain evidence of clinical-expert validation for the intended population, practice setting, and clinical outcomes.
quote: viii) Validation Data/Information and evidence of: (1) Clinical expert validation in intended population and practice setting and intended clinical outcomes.
hazard: Deployment without clinically relevant validation.

statement: Obtain evidence that the AI system is constrained to evidence-based outcomes.
quote: (2) C onstraint to evidence-based outcomes and mitigation of “hallucination”/“confabulation” or other output error.
hazard: Unsupported clinical outputs.

statement: Obtain evidence of safeguards mitigating hallucinations, confabulations, and other output errors.
quote: (2) C onstraint to evidence-based outcomes and mitigation of “hallucination”/“confabulation” or other output error.
hazard: Fabricated or erroneous outputs influencing care.

statement: Obtain evidence of algorithmic validation.
quote: (3) Algorithmic validation.
hazard: Deployment of an inadequately validated system.

statement: Obtain information on external validation processes for ongoing performance evaluation, including drift and degradation.
quote: (4) Ex ternal validation processes for ongoing evaluation of the model performance, e.g., accounting for AI model drift and degradation.
hazard: Undetected deterioration in deployed model performance.

statement: Obtain evidence of the comprehensiveness of data supporting the AI system.
quote: (5) Comprehensiveness of data and steps taken to mitigate biased outcomes.
hazard: Unrecognized data gaps affecting performance.

statement: Obtain evidence of steps taken to mitigate biased AI outcomes.
quote: (5) Comprehensiveness of data and steps taken to mitigate biased outcomes.
hazard: Discriminatory or disparate outcomes.

statement: Obtain relevant performance information, including performance at peer institutions or similar practice settings.
quote: (6) O ther relevant performance characteristics, including but not limited to performance characteristics at peer institutions/similar practice settings.
hazard: Assuming performance transfers to the deployment setting without supporting evidence.

statement: Obtain information on post-market surveillance addressing continued safety, performance, and equity.
quote: (7) P ost-market surveillance activities aimed at ensuring continued safety, performance, and equity.
hazard: Unrecognized post-deployment safety, performance, or equity failures.

statement: Obtain the vendor's data-use privacy policy.
quote: ix) Da ta Use Policy: (1) Privacy.
hazard: Unrecognized privacy risks in vendor data use.

statement: Obtain the vendor's data-use security policy.
quote: ix) Da ta Use Policy: (1) Privacy. (2) Security.
hazard: Unrecognized weaknesses in data protection.

statement: Obtain disclosure of special data-use protections for protected populations or groups at increased risk.
quote: (3) Special considerations for protected populations or groups put at increased risk.
hazard: Disproportionate data-related harms to vulnerable populations.

statement: Obtain information about ongoing algorithm maintenance.
quote: x) I nformation regarding maintenance of the algorithm, including any use of active patient data for ongoing training.
hazard: Unknown maintenance practices affecting deployed behavior.

statement: Obtain disclosure of any use of active patient data for ongoing model training.
quote: x) I nformation regarding maintenance of the algorithm, including any use of active patient data for ongoing training.
hazard: Undisclosed reuse of patient data for training.

statement: Obtain disclosure of the design and development team's composition, including diversity.
quote: xi) Disclosur es regarding the composition of design and development team, including diversity and conflicts of interest, and points of physician involvement and review.
hazard: Unknown limitations in development-team representation.

statement: Obtain disclosure of design and development team conflicts of interest.
quote: xi) Disclosur es regarding the composition of design and development team, including diversity and conflicts of interest, and points of physician involvement and review.
hazard: Undisclosed interests influencing system design or claims.

statement: Obtain disclosure of points of physician involvement and review during development.
quote: xi) Disclosur es regarding the composition of design and development team, including diversity and conflicts of interest, and points of physician involvement and review.
hazard: Unrecognized lack of clinical input into the system.

statement: Reconsider purchasing or using AI technologies when developers do not provide the specified disclosures.
quote: P urchasers and/or users (physicians) should carefully consider whether or not to engage with AIenabled health care technologies if this information is not disclosed by the developer.
hazard: Adoption without information needed to assess safety and suitability.

statement: Use generative AI only when organizational policies governing its use and mitigating associated risks are in place.
quote: Generative AI should: (a) only be used where appropriate policies are in place within the practice or other health care organization to govern its use and help mitigate associated risks; and (b) follow applicable state and federal laws and regulations (e.g., HIPAA-compliant Business Associate Agreement).
hazard: Ungoverned generative AI deployment.

statement: Ensure generative AI use complies with applicable state and federal laws and regulations, including applicable HIPAA business associate requirements.
quote: Generative AI should: (a) only be used where appropriate policies are in place within the practice or other health care organization to govern its use and help mitigate associated risks; and (b) follow applicable state and federal laws and regulations (e.g., HIPAA-compliant Business Associate Agreement).
hazard: Unlawful deployment or handling of protected health information.

statement: Develop generative AI governance policies that mitigate incorrect or falsified responses.
quote: Appropriate governance policies should be developed by health care organizations and account for and mitigate risks of: i) Incorrect or falsified responses; lack of ability to readily verify the accuracy of responses or the sources used to generate the response.
hazard: Incorrect or fabricated responses influencing care.

statement: Develop generative AI governance policies addressing difficulty verifying response accuracy and source information.
quote: Appropriate governance policies should be developed by health care organizations and account for and mitigate risks of: i) Incorrect or falsified responses; lack of ability to readily verify the accuracy of responses or the sources used to generate the response.
hazard: Reliance on unverifiable responses or sources.

statement: Address training-data limitations that could produce outdated, incomplete, or inaccurate generative AI responses for any patient population.
quote: ii) Training data set limitations that could result in responses that are out of date or otherwise incomplete or inaccurate for all patients or specific populations.
hazard: Outdated or incomplete responses, including population-specific inaccuracies.

statement: Address gaps in regulatory or clinical oversight of generative AI performance through organizational governance policies.
quote: iii) Lack of regulatory or clinical oversight to ensure performance of the tool.
hazard: Poor performance without effective oversight.

statement: Develop generative AI governance policies mitigating bias, discrimination, stereotypes, and disparate effects on access or outcomes.
quote: iv) Bias, discrimination, promotion of stereotypes, and disparate impacts on access or outcomes.
hazard: Discrimination and unequal access or health outcomes.

statement: Address generative AI data-privacy risks in organizational governance policies.
quote: v) Data privacy.
hazard: Exposure or misuse of private data.

statement: Address generative AI cybersecurity risks in organizational governance policies.
quote: vi) Cybersecurity.
hazard: Cyberattacks compromising generative AI systems or data.

statement: Address physician liability associated with generative AI use in organizational governance policies.
quote: vii) Physician liability associated with the use of generative AI tools.
hazard: Unmanaged physician liability for generative AI use.

statement: Work with AI and health IT developers to implement rigorous validation and verification of datasets informing generative AI models.
quote: Health care organizations should work with their AI and other health information technology (health IT) system developers to implement rigorous data validation and verification protocols to ensure that only –19– accurate, comprehensive, and bias managed datasets inform generative AI models, thereby safeguarding equitable patient care and medical outcomes.
hazard: Inaccurate, incomplete, or biased data producing inequitable care.

statement: Educate physicians and staff about appropriate generative AI use, risks, and benefits.
quote: U se of generative AI should incorporate physician and staff education about the appropriate use, risks, and benefits of engaging with generative AI.
hazard: Unsafe or inappropriate use caused by insufficient understanding.

statement: Use generative AI only when developers provide adequate product information to physicians and other users.
quote: Additionally, physicians and healthcare organizations should engage with generative AI tools only when adequate information regarding the product is provided to physicians and other users by the developers of those tools.
hazard: Use without information needed for informed clinical engagement.

statement: Ensure clinicians understand risks from patients obtaining inaccurate or harmful medical information from generative AI products.
quote: Clinicians should be a ware of the risks of patients engaging with generative AI products that produce inaccurate or harmful medical information (e.g., patients asking chatbots about symptoms) and should be prepared to counsel patients on the limitations of AI-driven medical advice.
hazard: Clinicians overlook harms from patient reliance on unsafe chatbot advice.

statement: Prepare clinicians to counsel patients about the limitations of AI-driven medical advice.
quote: Clinicians should be a ware of the risks of patients engaging with generative AI products that produce inaccurate or harmful medical information (e.g., patients asking chatbots about symptoms) and should be prepared to counsel patients on the limitations of AI-driven medical advice.
hazard: Patients rely on inaccurate or harmful AI medical advice.

statement: Require developers to use contributed data and prompts primarily to improve user experience and tool quality, rather than merely increase market value or revenue.
quote: Da ta and prompts contributed by users should primarily be used by developers to improve the user experience and AI tool quality and not simply increase the AI tool’s market value or revenue generating potential.
hazard: User contributions exploited for commercial gain without corresponding quality benefits.

statement: Allocate AI liability to individuals or entities best positioned to understand risks and prevent or mitigate harm.
quote: C urrent AMA policy states that liability and incentives should be aligned so that the individual(s) or entity(ies) best positioned to know the AI system risks and best positioned to avert or mitigate harm do so through design, development, validation, and implementation.
hazard: Liability allocation that fails to support effective harm prevention.

statement: Align incentives so those best positioned to understand and mitigate AI risks act to prevent harm.
quote: C urrent AMA policy states that liability and incentives should be aligned so that the individual(s) or entity(ies) best positioned to know the AI system risks and best positioned to avert or mitigate harm do so through design, development, validation, and implementation.
hazard: Misaligned incentives discourage risk mitigation.

statement: Assign all applicable liability to the entity or individual mandating AI use when the mandate prevents risk and harm mitigation.
quote: W here a mandated use of AI systems prevents mitigation of risk and harm, the individual or entity issuing the mandate must be assigned all applicable liability.
hazard: Unsafe mandatory AI use without accountability.

statement: Require autonomous clinical AI developers to accept liability for system failure or misdiagnosis in user agreements.
quote: D evelopers of autonomous AI systems with clinical applications (screening, diagnosis, treatment) are in the best position to manage issues of liability arising directly from system failure or misdiagnosis and must accept this liability with measures such as maintaining appropriate medical liability insurance and in their agreements with users.
hazard: Developer accountability displaced onto users for autonomous system failures.

statement: Use appropriate developer medical liability insurance as a measure for addressing autonomous clinical AI liability.
quote: D evelopers of autonomous AI systems with clinical applications (screening, diagnosis, treatment) are in the best position to manage issues of liability arising directly from system failure or misdiagnosis and must accept this liability with measures such as maintaining appropriate medical liability insurance and in their agreements with users.
hazard: Inadequate financial protection for autonomous clinical AI harm.

statement: Do not cover or pay for AI systems subject to nondisclosure agreements concerning flaws, malfunctions, or patient harm.
quote: Health car e AI systems that are subject to non-disclosure agreements concerning flaws, malfunctions, or patient harm (referred to as gag clauses) must not be covered or paid and the party initiating or enforcing the gag clause assumes liability for any harm.
hazard: Contractual suppression of safety problems or patient harm.

statement: Assign liability for harm to the party initiating or enforcing AI safety-related gag clauses.
quote: Health car e AI systems that are subject to non-disclosure agreements concerning flaws, malfunctions, or patient harm (referred to as gag clauses) must not be covered or paid and the party initiating or enforcing the gag clause assumes liability for any harm.
hazard: Suppression of AI safety information without accountability.

statement: Do not hold physicians liable for AI performance when they neither know nor have reason to know of quality or safety concerns.
quote: W hen physicians do not know or have reason to know that there are concerns about the quality and safety of an AI-enabled technology, they should not be held liable for the performance of the technology in question.
hazard: Physicians bear liability for unknowable system defects.

statement: Align physician AI liability protections with current and future AMA medical liability reform policies.
quote: Liabilit y protections for physicians using AI-enabled technologies should align with both current and future AMA medical liability reform policies.
hazard: Inconsistent physician liability protections.

statement: Make information available about the intended health care use and purpose of generative AI.
quote: En tities, e.g., AI developers, should make information available about the intended use of generative AI in health care and identify the purpose of its use.
hazard: Individuals do not understand why generative AI is being used.

statement: Inform individuals how their data will be used or reused in generative AI.
quote: Individuals should know how their data will be used or reused, and the potential risks and benefits.
hazard: Uninformed data use or reuse.

statement: Inform individuals about potential risks and benefits of their data being used or reused in generative AI.
quote: Individuals should know how their data will be used or reused, and the potential risks and benefits.
hazard: Data-sharing decisions made without understanding consequences.

statement: Allow individuals to opt out of generative AI data use, including training and disclosure to other users.
quote: I ndividuals should have the right to opt-out, update, or request deletion of their data from generative AI tools. These rights should encompass AI training data and disclosure to other users of the tool.
hazard: Individuals cannot refuse AI-related use or sharing of their data.

statement: Allow individuals to update their data in generative AI tools, including training data and data disclosed to other users.
quote: I ndividuals should have the right to opt-out, update, or request deletion of their data from generative AI tools. These rights should encompass AI training data and disclosure to other users of the tool.
hazard: Persistent inaccurate or outdated personal data.

statement: Allow individuals to request deletion of their data from generative AI tools, including training data and data disclosed to other users.
quote: I ndividuals should have the right to opt-out, update, or request deletion of their data from generative AI tools. These rights should encompass AI training data and disclosure to other users of the tool.
hazard: Individuals cannot seek removal of personal data.

statement: Prevent generative AI tools from reverse engineering, reconstructing, or reidentifying individuals' originally identifiable data.
quote: G enerative AI tools should not reverse engineer, reconstruct, or reidentify an individual’s originally identifiable data or use identifiable data for nonpermitted uses, e.g., when data are permitted to conduct quality and safety evaluations.
hazard: Reconstruction or reidentification exposes personal information.

statement: Prohibit generative AI tools from using identifiable data for nonpermitted purposes.
quote: G enerative AI tools should not reverse engineer, reconstruct, or reidentify an individual’s originally identifiable data or use identifiable data for nonpermitted uses, e.g., when data are permitted to conduct quality and safety evaluations.
hazard: Unauthorized secondary use of identifiable data.

statement: Use legal frameworks to protect against generative AI reidentification and nonpermitted uses of identifiable data.
quote: Preventive measures should include both legal frameworks and data model protections, e.g., secure enclaves, federated learning, and differential privacy.
hazard: Insufficient legal protection against data misuse.

statement: Implement data-model protections against generative AI reidentification and data misuse, such as secure enclaves, federated learning, or differential privacy.
quote: Preventive measures should include both legal frameworks and data model protections, e.g., secure enclaves, federated learning, and differential privacy.
hazard: Technical exposure or reidentification of personal data.

statement: Provide generative AI user training addressing legal, ethical, and equity considerations.
quote: U sers should be provided with training specifically on generative AI. Education should address: (1) Legal, ethical, and equity considerations.
hazard: Users overlook legal, ethical, or equity risks.

statement: Train generative AI users about data-breach and reidentification risks.
quote: (2) Risks such as data breaches and re-identification.
hazard: Users fail to recognize privacy and reidentification threats.

statement: Train generative AI users about pitfalls of entering sensitive and personal data.
quote: (3) Potential pitfalls of inputting sensitive and personal data.
hazard: Sensitive information exposed through prompts or other inputs.

statement: Train generative AI users about transparency with patients regarding AI use and patient data.
quote: (4) T he importance of transparency with patients regarding the use of generative AI and their data.
hazard: Patients remain unaware of AI use or handling of their data.

statement: Implement strong AI-system protections against input manipulation and malicious attacks.
quote: AI systems must have strong protections against input manipulation and malicious attacks.
hazard: Manipulated inputs or attacks compromise system behavior.

statement: Regularly monitor AI anomalies and performance deviations by comparing outputs with known and normal behavior.
quote: En tities developing or deploying health care AI should regularly monitor for anomalies or performance deviations, comparing AI outputs against known and normal behavior.
hazard: Undetected abnormal or compromised system behavior.

statement: Diligently identify individuals whose personal information is affected by a data breach.
quote: I ndependent of an entity’s legal responsibility to notify a health care provider or organization of a data breach, that entity should also act diligently in identifying and notifying the individuals themselves of breaches that impact their personal information.
hazard: Affected individuals remain unidentified after a breach.

statement: Notify individuals directly when a breach affects their personal information, independently of obligations to notify health care organizations.
quote: I ndependent of an entity’s legal responsibility to notify a health care provider or organization of a data breach, that entity should also act diligently in identifying and notifying the individuals themselves of breaches that impact their personal information.
hazard: Affected individuals cannot respond to exposure of their personal information.

statement: Educate AI users about cybersecurity risks, evolving attacker tactics, threat mitigation, and reporting suspicious behavior or outputs.
quote: U sers should be provided education on AI cybersecurity fundamentals, including specific cybersecurity risks that AI systems can face, evolving tactics of AI cyber attackers, and the user’s role in mitigating threats and reporting suspicious AI behavior or outputs.
hazard: Users fail to recognize, mitigate, or report AI cyber threats.

statement: Obtain developer disclosure of how AI models are trained.
quote: AI dev elopers should ensure transparency and accountability by disclosing how their models are trained and the sources of their training data.
hazard: Unknown training methods undermine assessment of information reliability.

statement: Use mechanisms that detect and flag potentially false or misleading AI content before wide dissemination.
quote: A lgorithms should be developed to detect and flag potentially false and misleading content before it is widely disseminated.
hazard: Wide dissemination of false or misleading medical information.

statement: Require mechanisms for reporting misinformation and disinformation generated or propagated by AI systems.
quote: D evelopers of AI should have mechanisms in place to allow for reporting of mis- and disinformation generated or propagated by AI-enabled systems.
hazard: Harmful misinformation remains unreported.

statement: Select AI developers with policies emphasizing rigorous validation of generated content.
quote: D evelopers of AI systems should be guided by policies that emphasize rigorous validation and accountability for the content their tools generate,
hazard: Unvalidated generated content reaches users.

statement: Require developer policies establishing accountability for AI-generated content.
quote: D evelopers of AI systems should be guided by policies that emphasize rigorous validation and accountability for the content their tools generate,
hazard: No accountable party for harmful generated content.

statement: Require AI developers to accept liability arising directly from system failure or misdiagnosis.
quote: are in the best position to manage issues of liability arising directly from system failure or misdiagnosis and must accept this liability with measures such as maintaining appropriate medical liability insurance and in their agreements with users.
hazard: Developers avoid responsibility for system failures or misdiagnosis.

statement: Establish clear AI-use guidelines for manuscript submissions to organizational academic publications or journals.
quote: A cademic publications and journals should establish clear guidelines to regulate the use of AI in manuscript submissions.
hazard: Unregulated AI use compromises publication integrity.

statement: Require disclosure of AI use in research methods and data collection in academic manuscripts.
quote: These guidelines should include requiring the disclosure that AI was used in research methods and data collection, requiring the exclusion of AI systems as authors, and should outline the responsibility of the authors to validate the veracity of any referenced content generated by AI.
hazard: Undisclosed AI contributions obscure research methods.

statement: Exclude AI systems from authorship in academic publications.
quote: These guidelines should include requiring the disclosure that AI was used in research methods and data collection, requiring the exclusion of AI systems as authors, and should outline the responsibility of the authors to validate the veracity of any referenced content generated by AI.
hazard: Authorship assigned to systems unable to assume responsibility.

statement: Require academic authors to validate the veracity of referenced content generated by AI.
quote: These guidelines should include requiring the disclosure that AI was used in research methods and data collection, requiring the exclusion of AI systems as authors, and should outline the responsibility of the authors to validate the veracity of any referenced content generated by AI.
hazard: False AI-generated content enters the medical literature.

statement: Provide digital-literacy education that helps individuals critically assess online medical information.
quote: E ducation programs are needed to enhance digital literacy, helping individuals critically assess the information they encounter online, particularly in the medical field where mis- and disinformation can have severe consequences.
hazard: Individuals accept harmful medical misinformation or disinformation.

statement: Publicly report automated decision-system use in coverage limits, claims determinations, and benefit design.
quote: U se of automated decision-making systems that determine coverage limits, make claim determinations, and engage in benefit design should be publicly reported, based on easily accessible evidence-based clinical guidelines (as opposed to proprietary payor criteria), and disclosed to both patients and their physician in a way that is easy to understand.
hazard: Opaque automation of coverage and benefits decisions.

statement: Base automated coverage, claims, and benefit decisions on easily accessible evidence-based clinical guidelines rather than proprietary payor criteria.
quote: U se of automated decision-making systems that determine coverage limits, make claim determinations, and engage in benefit design should be publicly reported, based on easily accessible evidence-based clinical guidelines (as opposed to proprietary payor criteria), and disclosed to both patients and their physician in a way that is easy to understand.
hazard: Coverage decisions based on opaque or unsupported criteria.

statement: Disclose automated coverage, claims, and benefit decision-system use to both patients and their physicians.
quote: U se of automated decision-making systems that determine coverage limits, make claim determinations, and engage in benefit design should be publicly reported, based on easily accessible evidence-based clinical guidelines (as opposed to proprietary payor criteria), and disclosed to both patients and their physician in a way that is easy to understand.
hazard: Patients or physicians are unaware of automated coverage decisions.

statement: Make disclosures about automated coverage, claims, and benefit decisions easy for patients and physicians to understand.
quote: U se of automated decision-making systems that determine coverage limits, make claim determinations, and engage in benefit design should be publicly reported, based on easily accessible evidence-based clinical guidelines (as opposed to proprietary payor criteria), and disclosed to both patients and their physician in a way that is easy to understand.
hazard: Incomprehensible disclosures prevent understanding of automated decisions.

statement: Restrict payor automated decision systems to improving coverage or payment efficiency, simplifying administration, and reducing workflow burdens.
quote: P ayors should only use automated decision-making systems to improve or enhance efficiencies in coverage and payment automation, facilitate administrative simplification, and reduce workflow burdens.
hazard: Automation used for purposes that undermine access rather than improve administration.

statement: Prevent payor automated decision systems from creating or worsening overall or disparate barriers to needed benefits.
quote: Automated decision-making systems should never create or exacerbate overall or disparate access barriers to needed benefits by increasing denials, coverage limitations, or limiting benefit offerings.
hazard: Increased denials, coverage limits, or inequitable access barriers.

statement: Preserve individualized assessment of each patient's medical and social circumstances when using payor automated decision systems.
quote: Use of automated decision-making systems should not replace the individualized assessment of a patient’s specific medical and social circumstances and payors’ use of such systems should allow for flexibility to override automated decisions.
hazard: Coverage decisions disregard individual medical or social circumstances.

statement: Allow payor automated decisions to be overridden.
quote: Use of automated decision-making systems should not replace the individualized assessment of a patient’s specific medical and social circumstances and payors’ use of such systems should allow for flexibility to override automated decisions.
hazard: Inappropriate automated decisions cannot be corrected.

statement: Base payor determinations on the patient's particular care needs rather than algorithms developed on similar patients.
quote: Payors should always make determinations based on particular patient care needs and not base decisions on algorithms developed on “similar” or “like” patients.
hazard: Population analogies substitute for the patient's actual care needs.

statement: Disclose payor decision-system training and reference data, including sources and represented demographic attributes.
quote: P ayors using automated decision-making systems should disclose information about any algorithm training and reference data, including where data were sourced and attributes about individuals contained within the training data set (e.g., age, race, gender).
hazard: Hidden data limitations or demographic imbalances in coverage automation.

statement: Provide clear evidence that payor automated decision systems do not discriminate or increase inequities and include bias protections.
quote: Payors should provide clear evidence that their systems do not discriminate, increase inequities, and that protections are in place to mitigate bias.
hazard: Unsubstantiated equity claims conceal discriminatory coverage decisions.

statement: Cite peer-reviewed studies assessing payor automated decision-system accuracy against patient outcomes and the validity of its predictions.
quote: P ayors using automated decision-making systems should identify and cite peer-reviewed studies assessing the system’s accuracy measured against the outcomes of patients and the validity of the system’s predictions.
hazard: Coverage automation lacks credible evidence of accuracy or validity.

statement: Automatically refer AI-recommended care limitations or denials for physician review at both initial review and appeal.
quote: A ny automated decision-making system recommendation that indicates limitations or denials of care, at both the initial review and appeal levels, should be automatically referred for review to a physician
hazard: Unreviewed automated recommendations restrict needed care.

statement: Require physicians reviewing automated care limitations or denials to hold a current, valid, unrestricted license in the state of proposed services.
quote: (a) possessing a current and valid non-restricted license to practice medicine in the state in which the proposed services would be provided if authorized
hazard: Adverse coverage review by physicians without appropriate licensure.

statement: Require physicians reviewing automated care limitations or denials to match the specialty ordinarily managing the condition or providing the requested service.
quote: (b) be of the same specialty as the physician who typically manages the medical condition or disease or provides the health care service involved in the request prior to issuance of any final determination.
hazard: Adverse coverage review lacks relevant clinical expertise.

statement: Complete physician review of automated care-limitation or denial recommendations before issuing a final determination.
quote: (b) be of the same specialty as the physician who typically manages the medical condition or disease or provides the health care service involved in the request prior to issuance of any final determination.
hazard: Final adverse decisions issued before clinical review.

statement: Give the treating physician an opportunity to discuss medical necessity directly with the authorizing physician before an adverse determination.
quote: Prior to issuing an adverse determination, the treating physician must have the opportunity to discuss the medical necessity of the care directly with the physician who will be responsible for determining if the care is authorized.
hazard: Care denied without treating-clinician input on medical necessity.

statement: Give affected patients and physicians access to all relevant automated coverage-decision information, including criteria, determination results, and clinical guidelines.
quote: I ndividuals impacted by a payor’s automated decision-making system, including patients and their physicians, must have access to all relevant information (including the coverage criteria, results that led to the coverage determination, and clinical guidelines used).
hazard: Affected parties cannot understand or challenge coverage determinations.

statement: Regularly audit payor automated decision systems for increased overall or disparate denials, coverage limitations, or reduced care access.
quote: P ayors using automated decision-making systems should be required to engage in regular system audits to ensure use of the system is not increasing overall or disparate claims denials or coverage limitations, or otherwise decreasing access to care.
hazard: Undetected worsening of care access or coverage inequities.

statement: Publish readily accessible approval, denial, and appeal statistics with patient demographics for payor automated decision systems.
quote: Payors using automated decision-making systems should make statistics regarding systems’ approval, denial, and appeal rates available on their website (or another publicly available website) in a readily accessible format with patient population demographics to report and contextualize equity implications of automated decisions.
hazard: Public cannot assess coverage automation's access and equity effects.

statement: Ensure payor automated decision-system use conforms to all relevant state and federal laws.
quote: Payor use of automated decision-making systems must conform to all relevant state and federal laws.
hazard: Unlawful automated coverage or benefits decisions.

statement: Use AI systems that enhance patients' experience of care.
quote: AI systems should enhance the patient experience of care and outcomes, improve population health, reduce overall costs for the health care system while increasing value, and support the professional satisfaction of physicians and the health care team.
hazard: AI deployment worsens patient experience.

statement: Use AI systems that improve patient outcomes.
quote: AI systems should enhance the patient experience of care and outcomes, improve population health, reduce overall costs for the health care system while increasing value, and support the professional satisfaction of physicians and the health care team.
hazard: Deployment without patient outcome benefit.

statement: Use AI systems that improve population health.
quote: AI systems should enhance the patient experience of care and outcomes, improve population health, reduce overall costs for the health care system while increasing value, and support the professional satisfaction of physicians and the health care team.
hazard: Deployment fails to advance population health.

statement: Use AI systems that reduce overall health care costs while increasing value.
quote: AI systems should enhance the patient experience of care and outcomes, improve population health, reduce overall costs for the health care system while increasing value, and support the professional satisfaction of physicians and the health care team.
hazard: Higher health care costs without improved value.

statement: Use AI systems that support professional satisfaction among physicians and the health care team.
quote: AI systems should enhance the patient experience of care and outcomes, improve population health, reduce overall costs for the health care system while increasing value, and support the professional satisfaction of physicians and the health care team.
hazard: AI deployment undermines workforce satisfaction.

statement: Evaluate the device on previously collected real patient inputs by comparing outputs to an established reference standard or expert clinical adjudication.
quote: The device is applied to previously collected patient inputs, with outputs compared to an established reference standard or to expert clinical adjudication.
hazard: Device performs poorly on real patient data.

statement: Operate the device in a live clinical workflow without showing outputs to clinicians or patients, recording and comparing outputs against actual clinical decisions.
quote: The device operates in a live clinical workflow on real patients, but its outputs are not shown to clinicians or patients and do not affect care. Outputs are recorded and compared against decisions actually made
hazard: The device produces harmful or inaccurate outputs in a live clinical environment.

statement: Evaluate device outputs against prospectively defined criteria by directing trained patient actors or representative individuals to follow defined scenarios.
quote: Trained patient actors or representative individuals who could plausibly present as patients are directed to follow defined scenarios, with outputs evaluated against prospectively defined criteria.
hazard: Device interacts unsafely or inappropriately in real-world patient scenarios.

statement: Have qualified, independent clinicians review samples of real patient inputs and device outputs against prospectively defined criteria.
quote: Qualified, independent clinicians review samples of real patient inputs and device outputs against prospectively defined criteria.
hazard: Device produces clinically incorrect or inappropriate outputs for real patient cases.

statement: Periodically have qualified, independent clinician adjudicators review samples of real-world inputs and outputs to monitor post-deployment device performance.
quote: Periodic sample-based clinician review: Qualified, independent clinician adjudicators review samples of real-world inputs and outputs against prospectively defined criteria, sampled to reflect the range of clinically relevant presentations and interaction patterns
hazard: Device performance degrades or handles real-world interactions unsafely over time.

statement: Monitor the device for performance degradation resulting from changes in the input population, data environment, or underlying model components.
quote: The sponsor monitors for performance degradation (e.g., drift) that may result from changes in the input population, the data environment, or underlying model components, specifying the analyses and thresholds to detect such degradation.
hazard: Unnoticed performance drift due to shifts in input data or underlying models.

statement: Test the device's boundary adherence and scope maintenance using adversarial prompting, prompt injection, and emotional-manipulation scenarios.
quote: Relevant testing may include adversarial prompting, prompt injection, emotional-manipulation scenarios, and multi-turn conversations in which individual turns appear in-scope but the cumulative interaction drifts out of scope.
hazard: Device responds to requests exceeding its clinical scope or intended use.

statement: Ensure expert adjudicators evaluating outputs are structurally independent from the device sponsor and the underlying third-party model developer.
quote: Where expert adjudication is warranted, it would include adjudicators that are structurally independent from the device sponsor and, where the device incorporates a third-party model, from the developer of that model
hazard: Biased evaluation of device performance due to conflicts of interest.

statement: Ensure benchmark datasets are representative of the deployment contexts in which the generative AI device is expected to be used.
quote: because a GenAI-enabled device may perform differently depending on its deployment environment, it may be appropriate to expect benchmark datasets to be representative of the deployment contexts in which the device is expected to be used.
hazard: The device performs poorly due to mismatched benchmark testing contexts.

statement: Supplement evaluation with synthetically generated data modeled on real patient data for subgroups where real-world data is limited.
quote: Where subgroup evaluation would be difficult, particularly for small or hard-to-sample subgroups where real-world data is limited, CDRH is considering that synthetically generated data modeled on real patient data could potentially supplement evaluation
hazard: Inadequate performance testing for small or hard-to-sample patient subgroups.

statement: Evaluate the device using multi-turn simulated encounters to assess time to clinical escalation, handoff quality, and resistance to user over-reassurance.
quote: Relevant testing may include multi-turn simulated encounters that assess time to escalation in evolving presentations, the quality of escalation language and handoff information, and resistance to over-reassurance when users minimize symptoms or resist escalation.
hazard: Device fails to appropriately escalate safety-critical clinical states.

statement: Re-benchmark the generative AI device against its original defined set of capabilities following any modifications to evaluate impact.
quote: A GenAIenabled device that has been benchmarked against a defined set of capabilities for premarket authorization could potentially be “re-benchmarked” against the same capabilities following a modification, providing evidence to determine whether the modification has affected safety or effectiveness of the device.
hazard: Unnoticed negative impacts on safety or effectiveness following a device modification.

statement: Compare device performance to a panel of qualified clinicians reflecting the standard of care when true outputs are open-ended.
quote: performance might be compared to that of a panel of qualified clinicians whose consensus reflects the applicable standard of care, or to that of a median clinician in practice.
hazard: Using inappropriate performance thresholds for open-ended generative AI outputs.

statement: Document trade-offs, decision processes, measurements, and feedback supporting acceptance of risks within organizational tolerance.
quote: Document trade-oﬀs, decision processes, and relevant measurement and feedback results for risks that do not surpass organizational risk tolerance, for example, in the context of model release: Consider diﬀerent approaches for model release, for example, leveraging a staged release approach.
hazard: Unaccountable acceptance of residual risks.

statement: Consider staged releases of generative AI models.
quote: Consider diﬀerent approaches for model release, for example, leveraging a staged release approach.
hazard: Broad exposure to risks before deployment experience reveals them.

statement: Select release approaches in light of the model and its projected use cases.
quote: Consider release approaches in the context of the model and its projected use cases.
hazard: Release strategies mismatched to intended uses and risks.

statement: Mitigate, transfer, or avoid risks exceeding organizational risk tolerances.
quote: Mitigate, transfer, or avoid risks that surpass organizational risk tolerances.
hazard: Deployment with risks exceeding organizational acceptance limits.

statement: Monitor the robustness and effectiveness of risk controls and mitigation plans.
quote: Monitor the robustness and eﬀectiveness of risk controls and mitigation plans (e.g., via red-teaming, field testing, participatory engagements, performance assessments, user feedback mechanisms).
hazard: Ineffective or deteriorating safeguards remaining undetected.

statement: Test generated content against predefined organizational risk tolerances, guidelines, and principles.
quote: Compare GAI system outputs against pre-defined organization risk tolerance, guidelines, and principles, and review and test AI-generated content against these guidelines.
hazard: Generated content violating organizational safety standards.

statement: Document training data sources to support tracing the provenance of generated content.
quote: Document training data sources to trace the origin and provenance of AIgenerated content.
hazard: Inability to trace generated content to its data origins.

statement: Evaluate feedback loops connecting content provenance information and human reviewers.
quote: Evaluate feedback loops between GAI system content provenance and human reviewers, and update where needed.
hazard: Provenance information failing to inform human review.

statement: Update content-provenance feedback loops when evaluation identifies a need.
quote: Evaluate feedback loops between GAI system content provenance and human reviewers, and update where needed.
hazard: Known weaknesses in provenance review persisting.

statement: Monitor content provenance protocols in real time to verify their continued effectiveness.
quote: Implement real-time monitoring systems to aﬃrm that content provenance protocols remain eﬀective.
hazard: Undetected failure of content provenance safeguards.

statement: Evaluate generative AI content and data for representational biases.
quote: Evaluate GAI content and data for representational biases and employ techniques such as re-sampling, re-ranking, or adversarial training to mitigate biases in the generated content.
hazard: Biased representation of people or groups in generated content.

statement: Mitigate representational bias in generated content using applicable techniques such as re-ranking.
quote: Evaluate GAI content and data for representational biases and employ techniques such as re-sampling, re-ranking, or adversarial training to mitigate biases in the generated content.
hazard: Biased generated content reaching users.

statement: Analyze generative AI outputs for harmful content, misinformation, CBRN-related content, and nonconsensual intimate imagery.
quote: Engage in due diligence to analyze GAI output for harmful content, potential misinformation, and CBRN-related or NCII content.
hazard: Dissemination of harmful, misleading, or abusive generated content.

statement: Use feedback from internal and external stakeholders, users, individuals, and communities to assess generated-content impacts.
quote: Use feedback from internal and external AI Actors, users, individuals, and communities, to assess impact of AI-generated content.
hazard: Content-related harms overlooked by internal assessments.

statement: Use real-time auditing tools when demonstrated to support validation of generated-data lineage and authenticity.
quote: Use real-time auditing tools where they can be demonstrated to aid in the tracking and validation of the lineage and authenticity of AI-generated data.
hazard: Unauthenticated or untraceable generated data.

statement: Establish structured user feedback mechanisms to detect shifts in generated-content quality or alignment with community values.
quote: Use structured feedback mechanisms to solicit and capture user input about AIgenerated content to detect subtle shifts in quality or alignment with community and societal values.
hazard: Subtle quality degradation or value misalignment remaining undetected.

statement: Maintain incident response and recovery plans for generative AI systems.
quote: Develop and update GAI system incident response and recovery plans and procedures to address the following:
hazard: Unprepared or ineffective responses to AI incidents.

statement: Maintain incident-related policies and procedures that account for newly encountered uses.
quote: Review and maintenance of policies and procedures to account for newly encountered uses;
hazard: New uses falling outside established incident safeguards.

statement: Maintain policies and procedures for detecting unanticipated uses.
quote: Review and maintenance of policies and procedures for detection of unanticipated uses;
hazard: Unanticipated system uses remaining undetected.

statement: Verify that incident response and recovery plans cover the generative AI value chain.
quote: Verify response and recovery plans account for the GAI system value chain;
hazard: Incident response gaps across suppliers and downstream dependencies.

statement: Keep downstream incident communication details current, including points of contact, contact information, and notification formats.
quote: Verify response and recovery plans are updated for and include necessary details to communicate with downstream GAI system Actors: Points-of-Contact (POC), Contact information, notification format.
hazard: Delayed or failed notification of downstream stakeholders.

statement: Assign responsibilities for superseding, disengaging, or deactivating systems whose performance or outcomes conflict with intended use.
quote: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
hazard: Unsafe systems remaining active because shutdown responsibilities are unclear.

statement: Maintain stakeholder communication plans for system deactivation, including reasons, workarounds, access removal, alternative processes, and contacts.
quote: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc.
hazard: Disrupted workflows or continued use after system deactivation.

statement: Escalate incidents to organizational risk authorities when deactivation or disengagement criteria are met.
quote: Establish and maintain procedures for escalating GAI system incidents to the organizational risk management authority when specific criteria for deactivation or disengagement is met for a particular context of use or for the GAI system as a whole.

statement: Maintain procedures for remediating issues that trigger incident response.
quote: Establish and maintain procedures for the remediation of issues which trigger incident response processes for the use of a GAI system, and provide stakeholders timelines associated with the remediation plan.
hazard: Incident-causing issues remaining unresolved.

statement: Provide stakeholders with remediation timelines.
quote: Establish and maintain procedures for the remediation of issues which trigger incident response processes for the use of a GAI system, and provide stakeholders timelines associated with the remediation plan.
hazard: Stakeholders lacking information needed to manage ongoing incident risks.

statement: Maintain regularly reviewed deactivation criteria aligned with organizational risk tolerances and appetites.
quote: Establish and regularly review specific criteria that warrants the deactivation of GAI systems in accordance with set risk tolerances and appetites.
hazard: Inconsistent or delayed deactivation of unsafe systems.

statement: Regularly monitor risks and benefits associated with third-party AI resources.
quote: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented.

statement: Document risk controls applied to third-party AI resources.
quote: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented.

statement: Apply organizational risk tolerances to third-party datasets, fine-tuned models, and models adapted to new domains.

statement: Apply organizational risk controls to third-party generative AI resources.

statement: Assess the credentials and qualifications of personnel involved with third-party generative AI resources.
quote: Apply organizational risk tolerances and controls (e.g., acquisition and procurement processes; assessing personnel credentials and qualifications, performing background checks; filtering GAI input and outputs, grounding, fine tuning, retrieval-augmented generation) to third-party GAI resources:
hazard: Unqualified personnel managing third-party AI risks.

statement: Use personnel background checks as a risk control for third-party generative AI resources.
quote: Apply organizational risk tolerances and controls (e.g., acquisition and procurement processes; assessing personnel credentials and qualifications, performing background checks; filtering GAI input and outputs, grounding, fine tuning, retrieval-augmented generation) to third-party GAI resources:
hazard: Personnel-related security risks in the AI value chain.

statement: Filter inputs to third-party generative AI resources as a risk control.
quote: Apply organizational risk tolerances and controls (e.g., acquisition and procurement processes; assessing personnel credentials and qualifications, performing background checks; filtering GAI input and outputs, grounding, fine tuning, retrieval-augmented generation) to third-party GAI resources:
hazard: Problematic inputs reaching third-party generative AI systems.

statement: Ground outputs from third-party generative AI resources as a risk control.
quote: Apply organizational risk tolerances and controls (e.g., acquisition and procurement processes; assessing personnel credentials and qualifications, performing background checks; filtering GAI input and outputs, grounding, fine tuning, retrieval-augmented generation) to third-party GAI resources:
hazard: Unsupported or inaccurate generated outputs.

statement: Consider retrieval-augmented generation as a risk control for third-party generative AI resources.
quote: Apply organizational risk tolerances and controls (e.g., acquisition and procurement processes; assessing personnel credentials and qualifications, performing background checks; filtering GAI input and outputs, grounding, fine tuning, retrieval-augmented generation) to third-party GAI resources:
hazard: Generated responses lacking relevant supporting information.

statement: Test generative AI value-chain risks, including security vulnerabilities, labor practices, privacy compliance, data localization, and geopolitical alignment.
