hazard: Supply-chain vulnerabilities and compliance failures propagating into deployment.

statement: Reassess model risks after fine-tuning or implementing retrieval-augmented generation.
quote: Re-assess model risks after fine-tuning or retrieval-augmented generation implementation and for any third-party GAI models deployed for applications and/or use cases that were not evaluated in initial testing.
hazard: Model modifications introducing unevaluated risks.

statement: Reassess third-party model risks for applications or use cases absent from initial testing.
quote: Re-assess model risks after fine-tuning or retrieval-augmented generation implementation and for any third-party GAI models deployed for applications and/or use cases that were not evaluated in initial testing.
hazard: Reliance on testing that does not cover the deployed use case.

statement: Implement measures to prevent, flag, or otherwise address outputs reproducing protected training content.
quote: Implement reasonable measures to prevent, flag, or take other action in response to outputs that reproduce particular training data (e.g., plagiarized, trademarked, patented, licensed content or trade secret material).
hazard: Disclosure or unauthorized reproduction of protected training material.

statement: Review system cards, model cards, and other transparency artifacts for third-party models.
quote: Review various transparency artifacts (e.g., system cards and model cards) for third-party models.

statement: Apply explainable AI techniques during continuous improvement to address risks from unexplained system behavior.

statement: Use AI systems to improve population health.
quote: AI systems should enhance the patient experience of care and outcomes, improve population health, reduce overall costs for the health care system while increasing value, and support the professional satisfaction of physicians and the health care team.
hazard: AI deployment fails to advance population health.

statement: Use AI systems to reduce overall health system costs while increasing value.
quote: AI systems should enhance the patient experience of care and outcomes, improve population health, reduce overall costs for the health care system while increasing value, and support the professional satisfaction of physicians and the health care team.
hazard: AI increases costs without delivering corresponding value.

statement: Use AI systems to support physicians' and health care team members' professional satisfaction.
quote: AI systems should enhance the patient experience of care and outcomes, improve population health, reduce overall costs for the health care system while increasing value, and support the professional satisfaction of physicians and the health care team.
hazard: AI deployment undermines workforce satisfaction.

statement: Prespecify test methods and acceptance criteria for evaluating an AI tool before testing begins.
quote: Consistent with expectations for non-clinical performance testing across devices,19 test methods and acceptance criteria would be prespecified prior to testing.
hazard: Post hoc selection of metrics or thresholds that overstates tool performance

statement: Ground output-scoring rubrics in established clinical guidelines or qualified expert validation, fitted to the local patient population, clinical setting, and intended use.
quote: Where device outputs are evaluated against scoring rubrics, such rubrics would be grounded in established clinical guidelines or validated through qualified expert input and fit-for-use within the assessment context, including with respect to the specific patient population, clinical setting, and intended use of the device.
hazard: Invalid rubrics that misjudge open-ended output quality for the deployment context

statement: Use clinically qualified expert adjudicators who are independent of the vendor and of any underlying foundation model developer.
quote: Where expert adjudication is warranted, it would include adjudicators that are structurally independent from the device sponsor and, where the device incorporates a third-party model, from the developer of that model, and possess qualifications aligned with the clinical domain and complexity of the outputs under review.
hazard: Biased or unqualified evaluation of AI outputs due to conflicts of interest

statement: Apply the same independence and qualification requirements when an LLM serves as the evaluator of another model's outputs.
quote: These considerations would still be applicable when the expert adjudicator is itself an LLM.
hazard: LLM-as-judge evaluations that share blind spots with or favor the evaluated model

statement: Test the tool's clinical knowledge across adjacent clinical domains its outputs could affect, such as comorbidities and drug interactions.
quote: in such cases, it may be appropriate to expect benchmark testing to assess clinical knowledge and analysis across other relevant clinical domains.
hazard: Harmful outputs affecting comorbid conditions or interacting medications outside the primary domain

statement: Use evaluation datasets representative of the local deployment contexts where the tool will be used.
quote: Similarly, because a GenAI-enabled device may perform differently depending on its deployment environment, it may be appropriate to expect benchmark datasets to be representative of the deployment contexts in which the device is expected to be used.
hazard: Performance failure in local settings not reflected in benchmark data

statement: Confirm tool performance under real-world or clinically representative conditions in addition to structured benchmark testing.
quote: CDRH is therefore considering that clinical confirmation may be a necessary step in addition to benchmarking to determine whether a GenAI-enabled device performs as intended for its intended population under real-world or clinically representative conditions.
hazard: Benchmark success masking failures with real users, workflows, and patient populations

statement: Evaluate the tool retrospectively on previously collected real patient inputs, comparing outputs with a reference standard or expert clinical adjudication.
quote: The device is applied to previously collected patient inputs, with outputs compared to an established reference standard or to expert clinical adjudication.
hazard: Undetected errors on real patient inputs before go-live

statement: Run the tool in shadow mode on live patients with outputs hidden from clinicians and patients, comparing outputs against actual decisions and outcomes.
quote: The device operates in a live clinical workflow on real patients, but its outputs are not shown to clinicians or patients and do not affect care. Outputs are recorded and compared against decisions actually made and, where appropriate, downstream outcomes.
hazard: Exposing patients to unvalidated outputs in live workflows

statement: Test patient-facing tools with trained patient actors following defined scenarios, evaluating outputs against prospectively defined criteria.
quote: Trained patient actors or representative individuals who could plausibly present as patients are directed to follow defined scenarios, with outputs evaluated against prospectively defined criteria.
hazard: Unsafe conversational behavior with real patients not captured by static tests

statement: Conduct blinded clinician review where clinicians independently determine the appropriate response to real inputs for comparison with tool outputs.
quote: this might take the form of blinded review, in which a clinician reviews real patient inputs without seeing the device’s outputs and independently determines the appropriate response for comparison against the device output
hazard: Anchoring bias inflating apparent agreement with AI outputs

statement: Assess whether the tool performs consistently across clinically relevant subgroups of the intended patient population.
quote: Across these approaches, relevant considerations might include whether the device performs consistently across clinically relevant subgroups within the intended use population.
hazard: Worse performance for specific patient subgroups going undetected

statement: Supplement limited real patient inputs with synthetic inputs modeled on real patient data only with documented justification.
quote: Where real patient inputs are limited, synthetically generated inputs modeled on real patient data might, with appropriate justification, supplement this evaluation.
hazard: Unrepresentative synthetic data giving false assurance of performance

statement: Compare open-ended tool outputs against a qualified clinician panel reflecting the standard of care or a median practicing clinician.
quote: CDRH is considering that for many GenAI-enabled devices, performance might be compared to that of a panel of qualified clinicians whose consensus reflects the applicable standard of care, or to that of a median clinician in practice.
hazard: No valid standard for judging open-ended outputs, accepting substandard performance

statement: Evaluate combined clinician-plus-AI team performance when the tool will be used with human review rather than autonomously.
quote: Considerations for selecting the comparator might include how the device is actually used, including the combined performance of the clinician and device working together as a human-AI team versus the device working in a fully autonomous workflow, depending on the intended use.
hazard: Evaluation mismatched to actual workflow, missing human-AI interaction failures

statement: Re-benchmark the tool against prespecified thresholds on a defined cadence and after triggering events such as underlying model changes.
quote: The sponsor reassesses the device against the prespecified benchmarking thresholds described in Section V.B, on a defined cadence and after defined triggering events, including changes to the underlying model or other components of the deployment architecture.
hazard: Undetected performance regression after model or architecture updates

statement: Have independent qualified clinicians periodically review representative samples of real-world inputs and outputs against prospectively defined criteria.
quote: Qualified, independent clinician adjudicators review samples of real-world inputs and outputs against prospectively defined criteria, sampled to reflect the range of clinically relevant presentations and interaction patterns the device encounters in real-world use.
hazard: Unsafe real-world outputs going unnoticed after deployment

statement: Monitor for performance drift from changes in input population, data environment, or model components using specified analyses and thresholds.
quote: The sponsor monitors for performance degradation (e.g., drift) that may result from changes in the input population, the data environment, or underlying model components, specifying the analyses and thresholds to detect such degradation.
hazard: Gradual performance degradation after deployment

statement: Establish contractual or technical mechanisms to detect, evaluate, and respond promptly to updates initiated by third-party foundation model developers.
quote: How can a manufacturer detect, evaluate, and respond to such changes in a timely manner? What mechanisms—for example, contractual, technical, or through a PCCP—could provide reasonable assurance that third-party developer-initiated changes do not compromise the safety or effectiveness of the device?
hazard: Silent upstream model changes compromising tool safety

statement: Obtain from foundation model vendors documentation of safety guardrails, update notification commitments, and audit log availability.
quote: safetyrelevant behavioral constraints and guardrails built into the model; update notification commitments; and audit log availability.
hazard: Lack of visibility into model safeguards, updates, and audit trails

statement: Test whether the tool recognizes safety-critical states and escalates in a timely, clear, actionable way, measuring both under- and over-escalation.
quote: Whether the device recognizes safety-critical clinical states and initiates escalation that is timely, clear, actionable, and appropriately empathetic. Both under-escalation (failing to escalate when clinically necessary) and over-escalation (escalating when not clinically indicated) are relevant failures.
hazard: Missed emergencies or unnecessary escalation burdening care

statement: Use multi-turn simulated encounters to test resistance to over-reassurance when users minimize symptoms or resist escalation.
quote: Relevant testing may include multi-turn simulated encounters that assess time to escalation in evolving presentations, the quality of escalation language and handoff information, and resistance to over-reassurance when users minimize symptoms or resist escalation.
hazard: Tool falsely reassuring patients who downplay serious symptoms

statement: Test that the tool refuses out-of-scope requests and provides clinically useful redirection without over-refusing in-scope requests.
quote: Whether the device recognizes when a request exceeds its intended use or clinical scope and responds with appropriate refusal and clinically useful redirection.
hazard: Tool diagnosing or prescribing beyond its intended use

statement: Conduct adversarial testing including prompt injection, emotional manipulation, and multi-turn conversations that gradually drift out of scope.
quote: Relevant testing may include adversarial prompting, prompt injection, emotional-manipulation scenarios, and multi-turn conversations in which individual turns appear in-scope but the cumulative interaction drifts out of scope.
hazard: Manipulation or cumulative drift causing unsafe out-of-scope outputs

statement: Test whether the tool expresses appropriate uncertainty rather than presenting uncertain, outdated, or contested information with false confidence.
quote: Presenting uncertain, outdated, or contested information with false confidence is treated as a safety failure.
hazard: Users acting on overconfident incorrect or outdated information

statement: Test whether the tool defers overly complex or uncertain situations to a human clinician without over-deferring on questions within its knowledge.
quote: This element also considers whether the device appropriately handles situations that are too complex or uncertain, including deferral to a human clinician, without over-deferring on questions within its knowledge.
hazard: Tool handling cases beyond its competence without human involvement

statement: Test the tool's knowledge of current guidelines, contraindications, drug interactions, and special populations such as pregnant, pediatric, geriatric, and renally impaired patients.
quote: Whether the device possesses accurate, current, and applicable clinical knowledge for its intended scope, including current guidelines, contraindications, drug interactions, and population-specific considerations, including, for example, those applicable to pregnant patients, pediatric and geriatric patients, and patients with renal or hepatic impairment.
hazard: Clinically inaccurate outputs harming vulnerable patient populations

statement: Include test scenarios designed to detect premature diagnostic closure when benign initial information masks a serious condition.
quote: scenarios designed to detect premature diagnostic closure in which initially benign information masks a more serious underlying condition
hazard: Missed serious diagnoses due to premature closure

statement: Test dosing calculations, unit conversions, lab interpretation, and detection of implausible values, including conversationally reported or unit-less measurements.
quote: This includes clinically relevant calculations such as, for example, weight-based and renal-function-based dosing and unit conversions, interpretation of laboratory and physiologic values against appropriate reference ranges, and recognition of clinically implausible values such as transcription errors or unit confusion, including when measurements are reported conversationally or with missing units.
hazard: Dosing errors and misinterpretation of numerical clinical data

statement: Test whether intended users across health literacy levels understand the tool's outputs, limitations, and when escalation is needed.
quote: whether intended users can actually understand the device’s outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed across varied health literacy levels
hazard: Users misunderstanding outputs or failing to seek needed care

statement: Test that the tool avoids coercive, emotionally manipulative, inappropriate, or abusive language.
quote: the avoidance of coercive, emotionally manipulative, or otherwise inappropriate or abusive language
hazard: Manipulative or abusive language harming patients

statement: Assess the risk that users accept tool outputs without appropriate scrutiny because of fluency or perceived authority.
quote: the risk of automation bias, in which a user accepts an output without appropriate scrutiny because of the device’s fluency or perceived authority
hazard: Automation bias leading to uncritical acceptance of erroneous outputs

statement: Test consistency of escalation, refusal, and diagnostic conclusions across repeated runs and paraphrased inputs, treating safety-critical variation as failure.
quote: Variation in non-safety-critical phrasing may be acceptable, but variation in safety-critical behaviors such as escalation, refusal, or diagnostic conclusions is treated as a failure.
hazard: Nondeterministic outputs producing inconsistent safety-critical behavior

statement: Define the outcomes ambient-scribe deployment is intended to improve.
quote: To answer these questions, leaders need a clear understanding of what outcomes (e.g., reduced clinician burnout, improved productivity) they are attempting to address and how to measure the performance of ambient scribes and the financial value of their improvements against those outcomes.
hazard: Deployment without clear objectives or criteria for success.

statement: Select ambient-scribe performance measures aligned with the intended outcomes.
quote: To answer these questions, leaders need a clear understanding of what outcomes (e.g., reduced clinician burnout, improved productivity) they are attempting to address and how to measure the performance of ambient scribes and the financial value of their improvements against those outcomes.
hazard: Performance assessments that do not establish whether deployment objectives were achieved.

statement: Measure the financial value of ambient-scribe improvements against the intended outcomes.
quote: To answer these questions, leaders need a clear understanding of what outcomes (e.g., reduced clinician burnout, improved productivity) they are attempting to address and how to measure the performance of ambient scribes and the financial value of their improvements against those outcomes.
hazard: Unrecognized financial underperformance or unsupported claims of value.

statement: Start ambient-scribe implementation in primary care.
quote: Approaches to ambient scribe implementation have varied across health system participants, but most have focused on primary care as the first use case.
hazard: An unfocused initial rollout across heterogeneous clinical settings.

statement: Use standardized metrics to assess ambient scribes' impact on clinicians.
quote: Standardized metrics would improve the ability to understand how these solutions impact the system, including (1) clinician impact, (2) patient impact, and (3) financial impact.
hazard: Inconsistent or incomparable assessments of clinician impact.

statement: Use standardized metrics to assess ambient scribes' impact on patients.
quote: Standardized metrics would improve the ability to understand how these solutions impact the system, including (1) clinician impact, (2) patient impact, and (3) financial impact.
hazard: Inconsistent or overlooked assessments of patient impact.

statement: Use standardized metrics to assess ambient scribes' financial impact.
quote: Standardized metrics would improve the ability to understand how these solutions impact the system, including (1) clinician impact, (2) patient impact, and (3) financial impact.
hazard: Incomparable financial evaluations that undermine purchasing and scaling decisions.

statement: Use standardized methodologies to evaluate ambient-scribe performance.
quote: Critically, there is a need for more standardized methodologies and metrics to understand performance across a range of indicators and for more research to understand their long-term impact on efficiency.
hazard: Heterogeneous evaluation methods that prevent reliable interpretation of performance.

statement: Evaluate the long-term effects of ambient scribes on efficiency.
quote: Critically, there is a need for more standardized methodologies and metrics to understand performance across a range of indicators and for more research to understand their long-term impact on efficiency.
hazard: Assuming early impressions establish sustained efficiency gains.

statement: Involve clinical workflow, operational, technology, and financial leaders in AI integration, governance, and oversight.
quote: Such discussions underscore the importance of collaboration between clinical workflow, operational, technology, and financial leaders to effectively integrate, govern, and oversee these new tools.
hazard: Siloed decisions that overlook clinical, operational, technical, or financial consequences.

statement: Measure physician burnout using validated instruments such as the Maslach Burnout Inventory or Mini-Z Survey.
quote: Physician burnout is typically measured using validated survey instruments, including the Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI) and the Mini-Z Survey, among others.
hazard: Unreliable measurement of burnout and changes attributed to deployment.

statement: Inventory existing people, processes, and technology when assessing administrative efficiency for AI deployment.
quote: As a result, “why does it cost X to do Y?” is a question that requires an inventory of how people, process, and technology currently work.
hazard: Deploying technology without understanding existing operational costs and dependencies.

statement: Ensure AI-related productivity improvements do not come at the expense of workforce well-being.
quote: Health system leaders see clinician burnout as a central challenge to address, which means that productivity or efficiency cannot come at the expense of workforce well-being. Optimal solutions support both.
hazard: Productivity gains that worsen burnout and associated patient-safety risks.

statement: Map the existing workflows that AI-based administrative solutions will replace, reorganize, or augment.
quote: Any strategy focused on reducing administrative burden must deeply understand what existing workflows they are replacing, reorganizing, or augmenting with AI-based solutions.
hazard: Workflow disruption or added administrative burden from poorly understood implementation changes.

statement: Establish data infrastructure that supports evaluating whether AI implementation produces intended changes.
quote: If you want to know whether a change is working, you need baseline architecture that will enable you to pose, and answer, those questions.
hazard: Inability to determine whether implementation improves outcomes.

statement: Implement robust cybersecurity measures for systems supporting AI deployment.
quote: The integration of disparate IT systems, the need for robust cybersecurity measures, and the management of vast amounts of data are just a few of the hurdles facing health systems today.
hazard: Unauthorized access, data compromise, or disruption of healthcare systems.

statement: Establish common data pipelines as the organization incorporates AI-enabled tools.
quote: As systems incorporate more AI-enabled tools, establishing common data pipelines and interoperable enterprise systems is essential.
hazard: Fragmented data flows that compound existing inefficiencies.

statement: Establish interoperable enterprise systems to support AI-enabled tools.
quote: As systems incorporate more AI-enabled tools, establishing common data pipelines and interoperable enterprise systems is essential.
hazard: Disconnected systems that obstruct workflows and outcome tracking.

statement: Fund technology infrastructure needed to support AI implementation.
quote: Overall, these challenges necessitate significant investment in technology, skilled personnel to manage and improve existing systems, and change-management teams.
hazard: Infrastructure limitations that undermine deployment and compound operational inefficiencies.

statement: Invest in skilled personnel to manage and improve systems supporting AI deployment.
quote: Overall, these challenges necessitate significant investment in technology, skilled personnel to manage and improve existing systems, and change-management teams.
hazard: Insufficient expertise to maintain and improve systems supporting AI.

statement: Fund change-management teams to support AI implementation.
quote: Overall, these challenges necessitate significant investment in technology, skilled personnel to manage and improve existing systems, and change-management teams.
hazard: Poorly managed implementation changes and unsuccessful adoption.

statement: Obtain patient consent before recording conversations with an ambient scribe.
quote: With consent, providers use a mobile application to capture conversations with a patient without interrupting the natural flow of a patient visit.
hazard: Recording patient conversations without consent.

statement: Pilot ambient-scribe technologies within the health system.
quote: All the health systems participating in the PHTI Taskforce — including public and private systems; academic medical centers; and regional, multistate, and national delivery systems — have piloted or scaled AI-based ambient scribe technologies.
hazard: Deployment without experience of how the technology performs locally.

statement: Specify the IT and operational resources committed to ambient-scribe implementation.
quote: What level of IT and operations resources will we contribute to this?
hazard: Implementation plans that exceed available technical and operational capacity.

statement: Decide whether to prioritize ambient-scribe vendors already in the organization's technology ecosystem.
quote: Should we prioritize developers in our current technology ecosystem?
hazard: Vendor selection without considering compatibility with existing technology relationships.

statement: Decide whether to pilot more than one ambient-scribe vendor.
quote: Should we pilot with more than one vendor?
hazard: Vendor selection without an explicit approach to comparing alternatives.

statement: Decide whether to procure a custom ambient-scribe tool or an off-the-shelf product.
quote: Do we want a custom tool or a product off the shelf?
hazard: Procurement of a product whose customization approach does not match organizational needs.

statement: Decide whether to offer ambient scribes broadly to interested clinicians or restrict access to a smaller group.
quote: Should we offer the product broadly to all who want or reserve for a smaller group?
hazard: An unplanned rollout scope that does not match organizational implementation capacity.

statement: Decide whether to offer ambient scribes across all specialties or roll out by service area.
quote: Should we offer to all specialties or roll out by service area?
hazard: Deployment sequencing that does not account for differences among clinical services.

statement: Choose whether to actively drive ambient-scribe adoption or let clinician interest determine uptake.
quote: Should we be intentional about driving adoption — or let interest drive adoption?
hazard: Unplanned adoption patterns that undermine implementation goals.

statement: Prioritize evaluation metrics according to their importance to key stakeholders.
quote: Which of the metrics matter most? To what key stakeholders?
hazard: Evaluation findings that overlook outcomes important to decision-makers and affected users.

statement: Identify which users currently benefit most from ambient scribes.
quote: Who is experiencing the most benefit from the tool today? How might this change?
hazard: Assuming all users experience the same benefits.

statement: Assess how the users benefiting most from ambient scribes might change.
quote: Who is experiencing the most benefit from the tool today? How might this change?
hazard: Assuming early patterns of benefit will remain unchanged.

statement: Use clinician satisfaction to inform decisions about scaling ambient scribes.
quote: Why did we scale? The doctors were immensely happy and that was enough of a strategy early on for our executive team.
hazard: Scaling tools without considering clinician acceptance.

statement: Use clear, plain language in patient education materials generated with ambient scribes.
quote: Ambient scribes also support develop- ment of patient education materials in clear, plain language.
hazard: Patient education materials that patients cannot readily understand.

statement: Establish policies governing ambient-scribe use.
quote: However, with robust policies and governance, emphasis on note review by clinicians, and ongoing enhancements to underlying AI models, leaders broadly agree that risks associated with ambient scribe can be largely mitigated or accepted.
hazard: Unmanaged documentation, privacy, and security risks.

statement: Establish governance oversight for ambient-scribe deployment.
quote: However, with robust policies and governance, emphasis on note review by clinicians, and ongoing enhancements to underlying AI models, leaders broadly agree that risks associated with ambient scribe can be largely mitigated or accepted.
hazard: Inadequate organizational oversight of ambient-scribe risks.

statement: Have clinicians review notes generated by ambient scribes.
quote: However, with robust policies and governance, emphasis on note review by clinicians, and ongoing enhancements to underlying AI models, leaders broadly agree that risks associated with ambient scribe can be largely mitigated or accepted.
hazard: Documentation omissions or errors entering patient records unchecked.

statement: Enable patients to review ambient-scribe summaries.
quote: There are important potential benefits for patient experience by enabling clinicians to pay more attention to the interaction itself rather than documenting it, as well as summaries that patients could review.
hazard: Patients lacking access to review summaries of their clinical encounters.

statement: Select AI tools that integrate seamlessly into clinical workflows.
quote: Technologies that fail to integrate seamlessly into clinical workflows — no matter how advanced — face challenges in gaining traction within health systems.
hazard: Workflow disruption and poor adoption despite technical capability.

statement: Integrate ambient scribes with the EHR to populate clinical documentation directly.
quote: Ambient scribe developers have established deep integrations with leading EHR platforms, enabling them to create custom templates and directly populate clinical documentation.
hazard: Disconnected documentation workflows that undermine adoption and efficiency.

statement: Consider prioritizing vendors offering integrated platforms over stand-alone point solutions.
quote: Moving forward, this may be more complex; companies that bundle integrations (e.g., AI applications and cloud-based services) may have a competitive advantage as organizations consider prioritizing vendors who offer platform solutions, rather than one-off, point-solution applications.
hazard: Growing integration complexity from disconnected point solutions.

statement: Collaborate with ambient-scribe vendors to customize note structure and templates to clinicians' needs.
quote: Developers often work closely with health systems to customize note structure and templates, ensuring the ambient scribe support its clinicians’ needs.
hazard: Generated documentation that does not fit clinicians' workflows or documentation needs.

statement: Provide onboarding for clinicians adopting ambient scribes.
quote: As such, while onboarding and training are still important, they are relatively straightforward.
hazard: Clinicians beginning use without adequate implementation support.

statement: Train clinicians to use ambient scribes.
quote: As such, while onboarding and training are still important, they are relatively straightforward.
hazard: Incorrect or ineffective use caused by inadequate user preparation.

statement: Include a disclaimer indicating generative AI generated each patient clinical communication, unless a licensed or certified human health care provider has read and reviewed it.
quote: (1) A disclaimer that indicates to the patient that the communication was generated by generative artificial intelligence.
hazard: Patients mistaking AI-generated clinical communications for human-authored communications.

statement: Place AI-generation disclaimers prominently at the beginning of occasional written patient clinical messages, unless read and reviewed by a licensed or certified human provider.
quote: (A) For written communications involving physical and digital media, including letters, emails, and other occasional messages, the disclaimer shall appear prominently at the beginning of each communication.
hazard: Patients overlooking AI-generation disclosures in written clinical messages.

statement: Display AI-generation disclaimers prominently throughout continuous online patient clinical interactions, unless read and reviewed by a licensed or certified human provider.
quote: (B) For written communications involving continuous online interactions, including chat-based telehealth, the disclaimer shall be prominently displayed throughout the interaction.
hazard: Patients losing awareness of AI generation during ongoing online clinical interactions.

statement: Verbally disclose AI generation at the start of audio patient clinical interactions, unless read and reviewed by a licensed or certified human provider.
quote: (C) For audio communications, the disclaimer shall be provided verbally at the start and the end of the interaction.
hazard: Patients beginning audio clinical interactions unaware that communications are AI-generated.

statement: Verbally disclose AI generation at the end of audio patient clinical interactions, unless read and reviewed by a licensed or certified human provider.
quote: (C) For audio communications, the disclaimer shall be provided verbally at the start and the end of the interaction.
hazard: Patients finishing audio clinical interactions without recognizing that communications were AI-generated.

statement: Display AI-generation disclaimers prominently throughout video patient clinical interactions, unless read and reviewed by a licensed or certified human provider.
quote: (D) For video communications, the disclaimer shall be prominently displayed throughout the interaction.
hazard: Patients overlooking AI generation during video clinical interactions.

statement: Provide clear instructions for contacting a human provider, employee, or other appropriate person in AI-generated patient clinical communications unless read and reviewed by a licensed or certified provider.
quote: (2) Clear instructions describing how a patient may contact a human health care provider, employee of the health facility, clinic, physician’s office, or office of a group provider, or other appropriate person.
hazard: Patients not knowing how to reach a human after receiving AI-generated clinical communications.

statement: Use reading and review by a licensed or certified human health care provider to exempt AI-generated patient clinical communications from disclaimer and human-contact-instruction requirements.
quote: (b) If a communication is generated by generative artificial intelligence and read and reviewed by a human licensed or certified health care provider, the requirements of subdivision (a) do not apply.
hazard: Unreviewed AI-generated clinical communications being exempted from disclosure and human-contact instructions.

statement: Ensure AI-generated patient communications pertaining to clinical information include a disclaimer indicating the use of generative AI.
quote: ensure that those communications include both (1) a disclaimer that indicates to the patient that a communication was generated by generative artificial intelligence
hazard: Patients mistaking AI-generated clinical information for human-generated communications.

statement: Provide clear instructions in AI-generated communications describing how a patient may contact a human healthcare provider or employee.
quote: (2) Clear instructions describing how a patient may contact a human health care provider, employee of the health facility, clinic, physician’s office, or office of a group provider, or other appropriate person.
hazard: Patients being unable to reach a human when confused or concerned by AI communications.

statement: Place the AI disclaimer prominently at the beginning of written communications involving physical and digital media.
quote: For written communications involving physical and digital media, including letters, emails, and other occasional messages, the disclaimer shall appear prominently at the beginning of each communication.
hazard: Patients missing AI disclosures in letters, emails, or other occasional messages.

statement: Display the AI disclaimer prominently throughout the interaction for continuous online interactions like chat-based telehealth.
quote: For written communications involving continuous online interactions, including chat-based telehealth, the disclaimer shall be prominently displayed throughout the interaction.
hazard: Patients forgetting or missing AI disclosures during ongoing chat sessions.

statement: Provide the AI disclaimer verbally at the start and end of audio interactions.
quote: For audio communications, the disclaimer shall be provided verbally at the start and the end of the interaction.
hazard: Patients being unaware that an audio interaction is AI-generated.

statement: Display the AI disclaimer prominently throughout video interactions.
quote: For video communications, the disclaimer shall be prominently displayed throughout the interaction.
hazard: Patients being unaware that video content is generated by AI.

statement: Exempt AI-generated communications from patient disclosure requirements if they are read and reviewed by a licensed or certified human health care provider.
quote: If a communication is generated by generative artificial intelligence and read and reviewed by a human licensed or certified health care provider, the requirements of subdivision (a) do not apply.
hazard: Unnecessary friction or alarm from disclosing AI use when a licensed human has reviewed the content.

statement: Evaluate whether AI communications show empathy appropriate to the intended user, clinical context, and risk level.
quote: Whether the device communicates in a manner appropriate to its intended user, clinical context, and risk level, including empathy, linguistic construction, health literacy, and therapeutic appropriateness.
hazard: Communication that is emotionally inappropriate for the user or clinical situation.

statement: Evaluate whether AI communications use linguistic construction appropriate to the intended user, clinical context, and risk level.
quote: Whether the device communicates in a manner appropriate to its intended user, clinical context, and risk level, including empathy, linguistic construction, health literacy, and therapeutic appropriateness.
hazard: Misinterpretation caused by language unsuitable for the intended user or clinical context.

statement: Evaluate the therapeutic appropriateness of AI communications for the intended clinical context.
quote: Whether the device communicates in a manner appropriate to its intended user, clinical context, and risk level, including empathy, linguistic construction, health literacy, and therapeutic appropriateness.
hazard: Communications that undermine appropriate therapeutic interactions.

statement: Test whether intended users across health literacy levels understand AI outputs.
quote: This element considers whether intended users can actually understand the device’s outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed across varied health literacy levels; the avoidance of coercive, emotionally manipulative, or otherwise inappropriate or abusive language; and the risk of automation bias, in which a user accepts an output without appropriate scrutiny because of the device’s fluency or perceived authority.
hazard: Misunderstanding AI outputs because of differences in health literacy.

statement: Test whether intended users across health literacy levels understand the limitations of AI outputs.
quote: This element considers whether intended users can actually understand the device’s outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed across varied health literacy levels; the avoidance of coercive, emotionally manipulative, or otherwise inappropriate or abusive language; and the risk of automation bias, in which a user accepts an output without appropriate scrutiny because of the device’s fluency or perceived authority.
hazard: Reliance on AI outputs without understanding their limitations.

statement: Test whether intended users across health literacy levels understand when escalation is needed.
quote: This element considers whether intended users can actually understand the device’s outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed across varied health literacy levels; the avoidance of coercive, emotionally manipulative, or otherwise inappropriate or abusive language; and the risk of automation bias, in which a user accepts an output without appropriate scrutiny because of the device’s fluency or perceived authority.
hazard: Delayed escalation because users do not recognize when additional care or review is needed.

statement: Evaluate AI outputs for coercive, emotionally manipulative, inappropriate, or abusive language.
quote: This element considers whether intended users can actually understand the device’s outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed across varied health literacy levels; the avoidance of coercive, emotionally manipulative, or otherwise inappropriate or abusive language; and the risk of automation bias, in which a user accepts an output without appropriate scrutiny because of the device’s fluency or perceived authority.
hazard: Emotional harm or compromised user autonomy from harmful generated language.

statement: Assess whether AI fluency or perceived authority causes users to accept outputs without appropriate scrutiny.
quote: This element considers whether intended users can actually understand the device’s outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed across varied health literacy levels; the avoidance of coercive, emotionally manipulative, or otherwise inappropriate or abusive language; and the risk of automation bias, in which a user accepts an output without appropriate scrutiny because of the device’s fluency or perceived authority.
hazard: Automation bias leading users to accept incorrect or unsafe outputs.

statement: Evaluate whether safety and clinical proficiency remain consistent across foreseeable runtime conditions.
quote: Whether the safety and clinical proficiency properties hold consistently across foreseeable variation in inputs, runtime conditions, and conversational contexts.
hazard: Unsafe performance when deployment conditions differ from evaluation conditions.

statement: Treat variation in safety-critical escalation, refusal, or diagnostic conclusions as an evaluation failure.
quote: Variation in non-safety-critical phrasing may be acceptable, but variation in safety-critical behaviors such as escalation, refusal, or diagnostic conclusions is treated as a failure.

statement: Treat measurement and signal-processing functions as potentially higher risk when users cannot independently evaluate the basis of outputs.

statement: Consider higher consequence ratings for patient-facing functions when patients lack the knowledge to independently evaluate outputs.

hazard: Patients acting on incorrect clinical information they cannot recognize as erroneous.

statement: Assess elevated deployment risk when safe use requires specialist expertise that intended clinician users lack.

hazard: Clinicians relying on specialist-domain outputs without sufficient expertise to evaluate them.

statement: Assess conversational GenAI risk across realistic multi-turn trajectories rather than isolated functions.
quote: CDRH is considering an approach for assessing risk of such devices that would consider the device’s behavior across realistic conversational trajectories, not only at the level of individual functions.
hazard: Conversations drifting from non-directive information into higher-risk action-directing advice.

statement: Include under-escalation errors in risk assessments of care-escalation functions.
quote: CDRH notes that for GenAI-enabled functions involving care escalation decisions, such as advising whether to seek emergency care, both under-escalation and over-escalation can impact assessment of risk of such functions.
hazard: Delayed or missed necessary care.

statement: Include over-escalation errors in risk assessments of care-escalation functions.
quote: CDRH notes that for GenAI-enabled functions involving care escalation decisions, such as advising whether to seek emergency care, both under-escalation and over-escalation can impact assessment of risk of such functions.
hazard: Unnecessary emergency care, procedures, anxiety, resource burden, and erosion of patient trust.

statement: Evaluate GenAI devices through supervised practice.
quote: Patel and Blumenthal14 argue that GenAI is too broad, adaptive, and opaque to be evaluated effectively through current medical device regulatory frameworks and instead propose competency-based regulation modeled on medical training, licensure examinations, supervised practice, periodic reevaluation, and public reporting.
hazard: Clinical failures emerging without supervision during practical use.

statement: Reevaluate deployed GenAI devices periodically.

statement: Publicly report GenAI device performance.

statement: Define a scope of practice for autonomous GenAI systems.

statement: Assign explicit accountability to developers and deploying institutions for autonomous GenAI systems.

statement: Establish accountability mechanisms with consequences when GenAI devices fail to meet expected standards.

statement: Conduct non-clinical device benchmarking before deployment.

statement: Obtain clinical confirmation of GenAI device performance before deployment.

statement: Define benchmarking test scope from the device’s intended use and risk profile.
quote: CDRH envisions that for benchmarking conducted under a competency-based approach, sponsors would define the scope of testing based on the device’s intended use and risk profile, prespecify evaluation methods, describe and justify scoring rubrics, identify qualified expert adjudicators where applicable, and prespecify and justify acceptance criteria.

statement: Identify qualified expert adjudicators for benchmarking where applicable.

statement: Fit scoring rubrics to the intended patient population, clinical setting, and device use.

statement: Benchmark knowledge and analysis in other clinical domains affected by the device’s intended actions.

statement: Use benchmark datasets representative of the device’s expected deployment contexts.

statement: Supplement benchmarking with clinical confirmation in real-world or clinically representative conditions for the intended population.

statement: Document clinical adjudicators’ independence from the device manufacturer and applicable foundation model developer.

statement: Record outputs generated during shadow deployment.

statement: Compare shadow-deployment outputs with actual clinical decisions and, where appropriate, downstream outcomes.

statement: Evaluate defined scenarios with trained patient actors or representative individuals against prospectively defined criteria.

statement: Use blinded clinician review of real patient inputs to establish independent responses for comparison with device outputs.

statement: Use unblinded clinician review of full interaction records to assess output quality and appropriateness.
