hazard: False reassurance that discourages necessary clinical care.

statement: Test whether the device recognizes requests outside its intended use or clinical scope.
quote: Whether the device recognizes when a request exceeds its intended use or clinical scope and responds with appropriate refusal and clinically useful redirection.
hazard: Unrecognized requests for unsupported clinical functions.

statement: Evaluate whether out-of-scope requests receive clinically useful redirection.
quote: Whether the device recognizes when a request exceeds its intended use or clinical scope and responds with appropriate refusal and clinically useful redirection.
hazard: Users left without an appropriate next step after a refusal.

statement: Assess both failure to refuse out-of-scope requests and inappropriate refusal of in-scope requests.
quote: Both under-refusal (producing outputs beyond the device’s intended use, such as diagnosing or prescribing when not designed to do so) and over-refusal (declining requests that fall within the device’s intended use) are relevant failures.
hazard: Unsupported clinical advice or unjustified denial of intended assistance.

statement: Test scope maintenance using adversarial prompting.
quote: Relevant testing may include adversarial prompting, prompt injection, emotional-manipulation scenarios, and multi-turn conversations in which individual turns appear in-scope but the cumulative interaction drifts out of scope.
hazard: Adversarial requests inducing unsupported or unsafe clinical outputs.

statement: Test resistance to prompt injection that attempts to bypass intended-use boundaries.
quote: Relevant testing may include adversarial prompting, prompt injection, emotional-manipulation scenarios, and multi-turn conversations in which individual turns appear in-scope but the cumulative interaction drifts out of scope.
hazard: Injected instructions overriding clinical scope and safety boundaries.

statement: Test scope maintenance under emotional-manipulation scenarios.
quote: Relevant testing may include adversarial prompting, prompt injection, emotional-manipulation scenarios, and multi-turn conversations in which individual turns appear in-scope but the cumulative interaction drifts out of scope.
hazard: Emotional pressure inducing unsafe exceptions to intended-use boundaries.

statement: Test multi-turn conversations whose individually in-scope turns cumulatively drift beyond the device’s intended scope.
quote: Relevant testing may include adversarial prompting, prompt injection, emotional-manipulation scenarios, and multi-turn conversations in which individual turns appear in-scope but the cumulative interaction drifts out of scope.
hazard: Gradual conversational drift into unsupported clinical activities.

statement: Evaluate whether outputs accurately communicate confidence, limitations, and uncertainty when evidence is contested, evolving, or beyond reliable knowledge.
quote: Whether the device accurately represents the confidence and limits of its outputs, expressing appropriate uncertainty when evidence is contested, evolving, or beyond its reliable knowledge.
hazard: Users treating uncertain or unsupported information as established fact.

statement: Treat false confidence in uncertain, outdated, or contested information as an evaluation failure.
quote: Presenting uncertain, outdated, or contested information with false confidence is treated as a safety failure.
hazard: Unsafe decisions based on confidently presented unreliable information.

statement: Test appropriate human-clinician deferral for complex or uncertain cases without excessive deferral on answerable questions.
quote: This element also considers whether the device appropriately handles situations that are too complex or uncertain, including deferral to a human clinician, without over-deferring on questions within its knowledge.
hazard: Unsupported autonomous advice or unnecessary reliance on clinician intervention.

statement: Test clinical knowledge against current guidelines, contraindications, and drug interactions within the intended scope.
quote: Whether the device possesses accurate, current, and applicable clinical knowledge for its intended scope, including current guidelines, contraindications, drug interactions, and population-specific considerations, including, for example, those applicable to pregnant patients, pediatric and geriatric patients, and patients with renal or hepatic impairment.
hazard: Incorrect or outdated clinical advice, including contraindicated treatments and drug interactions.

statement: Test population-specific clinical knowledge for pregnant, pediatric, geriatric, renally impaired, and hepatically impaired patients.
quote: Whether the device possesses accurate, current, and applicable clinical knowledge for its intended scope, including current guidelines, contraindications, drug interactions, and population-specific considerations, including, for example, those applicable to pregnant patients, pediatric and geriatric patients, and patients with renal or hepatic impairment.
hazard: Clinical advice that overlooks population-specific contraindications or care needs.

statement: Test acknowledgment of knowledge limitations and uncertainty about evidence absent from model training.
quote: This element also considers whether the device is aware of its own knowledge limitations and acknowledges uncertainty for evidence not reflected in its training.
hazard: Confident claims about evidence the model does not reliably know.

statement: Evaluate handling of incomplete, evolving, or ambiguous clinical information within appropriate clinical parameters.
quote: Whether the device can gather, integrate, and act on incomplete, evolving, or ambiguous clinical information within appropriate clinical parameters.
hazard: Inappropriate clinical conclusions from incomplete or changing information.

statement: Assess generated differential diagnoses for completeness and appropriate prioritization of serious diagnoses.
quote: Relevant testing may include differential diagnosis generation assessed for completeness and appropriate prioritization of serious diagnoses, multi-turn simulated encounters scored for the quality and sequencing of follow-up questions, and scenarios designed to detect premature diagnostic closure in which initially benign information masks a more serious underlying condition.
hazard: Omitted or insufficiently prioritized serious diagnoses.

statement: Score follow-up-question quality and sequencing in multi-turn simulated encounters.
quote: Relevant testing may include differential diagnosis generation assessed for completeness and appropriate prioritization of serious diagnoses, multi-turn simulated encounters scored for the quality and sequencing of follow-up questions, and scenarios designed to detect premature diagnostic closure in which initially benign information masks a more serious underlying condition.
hazard: Poor information gathering that misses clinically important details.

statement: Test for premature diagnostic closure using initially benign presentations that conceal serious conditions.
quote: Relevant testing may include differential diagnosis generation assessed for completeness and appropriate prioritization of serious diagnoses, multi-turn simulated encounters scored for the quality and sequencing of follow-up questions, and scenarios designed to detect premature diagnostic closure in which initially benign information masks a more serious underlying condition.
hazard: Missed serious illness after early commitment to a benign explanation.

statement: Test appropriate deferral when information is insufficient without over-deferral when adequate information is available.
quote: This element also considers whether the device defers appropriately when information is insufficient, without over-deferring when adequate information is available.
hazard: Unsupported clinical action or unnecessary deferral despite sufficient information.

statement: Test interpretation of numerical and measurement inputs under noisy or ambiguous real-world conditions.
quote: Whether the device correctly interprets and acts on numerical and measurement information, including under the noisy or ambiguous input conditions common in real-world interactions.
hazard: Clinical errors caused by misinterpreted numerical inputs.

statement: Test weight-based and renal-function-based dosing calculations.
quote: This includes clinically relevant calculations such as, for example, weight-based and renal-function-based dosing and unit conversions, interpretation of laboratory and physiologic values against appropriate reference ranges, and recognition of clinically implausible values such as transcription errors or unit confusion, including when measurements are reported conversationally or with missing units.
hazard: Incorrect medication doses caused by calculation errors.

statement: Test clinically relevant unit conversions.
quote: This includes clinically relevant calculations such as, for example, weight-based and renal-function-based dosing and unit conversions, interpretation of laboratory and physiologic values against appropriate reference ranges, and recognition of clinically implausible values such as transcription errors or unit confusion, including when measurements are reported conversationally or with missing units.
hazard: Treatment or interpretation errors caused by incorrect unit conversion.

statement: Evaluate interpretation of laboratory and physiologic values against appropriate reference ranges.
quote: This includes clinically relevant calculations such as, for example, weight-based and renal-function-based dosing and unit conversions, interpretation of laboratory and physiologic values against appropriate reference ranges, and recognition of clinically implausible values such as transcription errors or unit confusion, including when measurements are reported conversationally or with missing units.
hazard: Misclassification of clinically important laboratory or physiologic abnormalities.

statement: Test recognition of implausible measurements, including transcription errors, unit confusion, and conversational reports with missing units.
quote: This includes clinically relevant calculations such as, for example, weight-based and renal-function-based dosing and unit conversions, interpretation of laboratory and physiologic values against appropriate reference ranges, and recognition of clinically implausible values such as transcription errors or unit confusion, including when measurements are reported conversationally or with missing units.
hazard: Clinical action based on erroneous or ambiguous measurements.

statement: Evaluate communication appropriateness for intended users, clinical context, and risk, including empathy, linguistic construction, and therapeutic appropriateness.
quote: Whether the device communicates in a manner appropriate to its intended user, clinical context, and risk level, including empathy, linguistic construction, health literacy, and therapeutic appropriateness.
hazard: Communication that is confusing, insensitive, or clinically inappropriate.

statement: Test whether users across health literacy levels understand outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed.
quote: This element considers whether intended users can actually understand the device’s outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed across varied health literacy levels; the avoidance of coercive, emotionally manipulative, or otherwise inappropriate or abusive language; and the risk of automation bias, in which a user accepts an output without appropriate scrutiny because of the device’s fluency or perceived authority.
hazard: Misunderstood advice, limitations, or escalation instructions among users with different health literacy levels.

statement: Evaluate whether outputs avoid coercive, emotionally manipulative, inappropriate, or abusive language.
quote: This element considers whether intended users can actually understand the device’s outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed across varied health literacy levels; the avoidance of coercive, emotionally manipulative, or otherwise inappropriate or abusive language; and the risk of automation bias, in which a user accepts an output without appropriate scrutiny because of the device’s fluency or perceived authority.
hazard: Psychological harm or compromised autonomy from manipulative or abusive outputs.

statement: Assess automation bias caused by fluent or authoritative-seeming device outputs.
quote: This element considers whether intended users can actually understand the device’s outputs, their limitations, and when escalation is needed across varied health literacy levels; the avoidance of coercive, emotionally manipulative, or otherwise inappropriate or abusive language; and the risk of automation bias, in which a user accepts an output without appropriate scrutiny because of the device’s fluency or perceived authority.
hazard: Uncritical acceptance of incorrect outputs because they sound fluent or authoritative.

statement: Test safety and clinical proficiency across foreseeable variations in inputs, runtime conditions, and conversational contexts.
quote: Whether the safety and clinical proficiency properties hold consistently across foreseeable variation in inputs, runtime conditions, and conversational contexts.
hazard: Safety failures triggered by ordinary variations in use or runtime conditions.

statement: Treat inconsistent safety-critical escalation, refusal, or diagnostic conclusions as evaluation failures.
quote: Variation in non-safety-critical phrasing may be acceptable, but variation in safety-critical behaviors such as escalation, refusal, or diagnostic conclusions is treated as a failure.
hazard: Unreliable clinical outcomes despite clinically equivalent inputs.

statement: Evaluate reproducibility across repeated runs.
quote: Relevant considerations include 26 reproducibility across repeated runs, consistency across semantically equivalent paraphrases reflecting differences in user health literacy and emotional framing,
hazard: Unstable performance concealed by single-run evaluation.

statement: Test consistency across semantically equivalent paraphrases varying in health literacy and emotional framing.
quote: Relevant considerations include 26 reproducibility across repeated runs, consistency across semantically equivalent paraphrases reflecting differences in user health literacy and emotional framing,
hazard: Clinically inconsistent responses driven by wording, literacy, or emotional presentation.

statement: Define benchmarking scope according to the device’s intended use and risk profile.
quote: CDRH envisions that for benchmarking conducted under a competency-based approach, sponsors would define the scope of testing based on the device’s intended use and risk profile, prespecify evaluation methods, describe and justify scoring rubrics, identify qualified expert adjudicators where applicable, and prespecify and justify acceptance criteria.
hazard: Evaluation that misses clinically important capabilities or risks.

statement: Prespecify evaluation methods before testing.
quote: Consistent with expectations for non-clinical performance testing across devices,19 test methods and acceptance criteria would be prespecified prior to testing.
hazard: Post hoc selection of methods that exaggerates performance.

statement: Document the rationale for scoring rubrics used in benchmarking.
quote: CDRH envisions that for benchmarking conducted under a competency-based approach, sponsors would define the scope of testing based on the device’s intended use and risk profile, prespecify evaluation methods, describe and justify scoring rubrics, identify qualified expert adjudicators where applicable, and prespecify and justify acceptance criteria.
hazard: Unsupported scoring rules that misrepresent clinical performance.

statement: Prespecify acceptance criteria before testing.
quote: Consistent with expectations for non-clinical performance testing across devices,19 test methods and acceptance criteria would be prespecified prior to testing.
hazard: Retrospective threshold changes that permit unsafe performance.

statement: Document the justification for evaluation acceptance criteria.
quote: CDRH envisions that for benchmarking conducted under a competency-based approach, sponsors would define the scope of testing based on the device’s intended use and risk profile, prespecify evaluation methods, describe and justify scoring rubrics, identify qualified expert adjudicators where applicable, and prespecify and justify acceptance criteria.
hazard: Acceptance thresholds lacking a defensible clinical basis.

statement: Use synthetic-data generation or simulation tools to standardize device testing.
quote: CDRH recognizes that there could be opportunities for sponsors to leverage methodologies such as synthetic data generation and simulation tools, including virtual patient avatars, to conduct testing in a manner that is predictable, standardized, and amenable to automation.
hazard: Inconsistent or difficult-to-repeat evaluation conditions.

statement: Ground scoring rubrics in established clinical guidelines or qualified expert validation.
quote: Where device outputs are evaluated against scoring rubrics, such rubrics would be grounded in established clinical guidelines or validated through qualified expert input and fit-for-use within the assessment context, including with respect to the specific patient population, clinical setting, and intended use of the device.
hazard: Scoring that rewards clinically incorrect or inappropriate outputs.

statement: Verify that scoring rubrics fit the intended patient population, clinical setting, and device use.
quote: Where device outputs are evaluated against scoring rubrics, such rubrics would be grounded in established clinical guidelines or validated through qualified expert input and fit-for-use within the assessment context, including with respect to the specific patient population, clinical setting, and intended use of the device.
hazard: Evaluation criteria that do not reflect deployment conditions.

statement: Use expert adjudicators structurally independent of the device sponsor and any underlying third-party model developer.
quote: Where expert adjudication is warranted, it would include adjudicators that are structurally independent from the device sponsor and, where the device incorporates a third-party model, from the developer of that model, and possess qualifications aligned with the clinical domain and complexity of the outputs under review.
hazard: Conflicts of interest that bias performance assessments.

statement: Select adjudicators with qualifications matching the clinical domain and complexity of evaluated outputs.
quote: Where expert adjudication is warranted, it would include adjudicators that are structurally independent from the device sponsor and, where the device incorporates a third-party model, from the developer of that model, and possess qualifications aligned with the clinical domain and complexity of the outputs under review.
hazard: Clinical errors missed by inadequately qualified reviewers.

statement: Apply expert-adjudicator independence and qualification standards to LLM adjudicators.
quote: These considerations would still be applicable when the expert adjudicator is itself an LLM.
hazard: Biased or clinically unreliable LLM-based evaluation.

statement: Benchmark relevant clinical domains beyond the primary indication when comorbidities or medication interactions could affect safety.
quote: For example, a GenAIenabled device intended to prescribe medications for cardiovascular conditions may prescribe medications that can affect comorbid diseases in other clinical domains or interact with medications prescribed for non-cardiovascular conditions; in such cases, it may be appropriate to expect benchmark testing to assess clinical knowledge and analysis across other relevant clinical domains.
hazard: Missed comorbidity effects or cross-specialty medication interactions.

statement: Use benchmark datasets representative of anticipated deployment contexts.
quote: Similarly, because a GenAI-enabled device may perform differently depending on its deployment environment, it may be appropriate to expect benchmark datasets to be representative of the deployment contexts in which the device is expected to be used.
hazard: Benchmark performance that fails to generalize to actual deployment.

statement: Supplement benchmarking with clinical confirmation in real-world or clinically representative conditions.
quote: CDRH is therefore considering that clinical confirmation may be a necessary step in addition to benchmarking to determine whether a GenAI-enabled device performs as intended for its intended population under real-world or clinically representative conditions.
hazard: Workflow, user, or population failures missed by structured benchmarks.

statement: Match clinical-confirmation evidence rigor to the device’s intended use and risk profile.
quote: the type and rigor of evidence consistent with the device’s intended use and 19 See, e.g., FDA guidance Recommended Content and Format of Non-Clinical Bench Performance Testing Information in Premarket Submissions. 15 proportionate to its risk profile, potentially utilizing the two-axis risk framework described in Section IV.
hazard: Insufficient clinical evidence for high-risk uses.

statement: Consider the type of patient data processed when selecting a clinical-confirmation approach.
quote: The appropriate approach may also depend on the type of patient data the device acts on.
hazard: Confirmation methods poorly matched to the device’s clinical inputs.

statement: Evaluate previously collected patient inputs against an established reference standard or expert clinical adjudication.
quote: The device is applied to previously collected patient inputs, with outputs compared to an established reference standard or to expert clinical adjudication.
hazard: Clinically incorrect outputs undetected before live use.

statement: Use multi-clinician consensus to establish expert clinical reference judgments.
quote: Expert clinical adjudication might be established through multi-clinician consensus, with adjudicator independence from the device manufacturer and foundation model developer (as applicable) documented.
hazard: Reference judgments distorted by individual clinician error or preference.

statement: Document clinical adjudicators’ independence from the device manufacturer and foundation model developer.
quote: Expert clinical adjudication might be established through multi-clinician consensus, with adjudicator independence from the device manufacturer and foundation model developer (as applicable) documented.
hazard: Undisclosed conflicts of interest in clinical evaluation.

statement: Supplement limited real-patient inputs with justified synthetic inputs modeled on real patient data.
quote: Where real patient inputs are limited, synthetically generated inputs modeled on real patient data might, with appropriate justification, supplement this evaluation.
hazard: Insufficient evaluation coverage when real patient inputs are scarce.

statement: Conduct shadow deployment with outputs hidden from clinicians and patients and excluded from care decisions.
quote: The device operates in a live clinical workflow on real patients, but its outputs are not shown to clinicians or patients and do not affect care.
hazard: Patient exposure to unconfirmed device performance during evaluation.

statement: Compare recorded shadow-deployment outputs with actual clinical decisions and, where appropriate, downstream outcomes.
quote: Outputs are recorded and compared against decisions actually made and, where appropriate, downstream outcomes.
hazard: Unrecognized disagreement with real-world care or patient outcomes.

statement: Evaluate standardized patient interactions using defined scenarios and prospectively specified criteria.
quote: Trained patient actors or representative individuals who could plausibly present as patients are directed to follow defined scenarios, with outputs evaluated against prospectively defined criteria.
hazard: Interaction failures missed by static or nonrepresentative test inputs.

statement: Use clinician assessments blinded to device outputs as reference responses for real patient cases.
quote: Depending on the device, this might take the form of blinded review, in which a clinician reviews real patient inputs without seeing the device’s outputs and independently determines the appropriate response for comparison against the device output, or unblinded review of full interaction records to assess the quality and appropriateness of outputs.
hazard: Clinician reference judgments influenced by the device’s own output.

statement: Have clinicians review complete real-case interaction records for output quality and appropriateness.
quote: Depending on the device, this might take the form of blinded review, in which a clinician reviews real patient inputs without seeing the device’s outputs and independently determines the appropriate response for comparison against the device output, or unblinded review of full interaction records to assess the quality and appropriateness of outputs.
hazard: Context-dependent clinical errors missed by isolated-output review.

statement: Use a prospective clinical study, including a randomized trial where appropriate, to confirm clinical performance.
quote: Depending on the device, a prospective clinical study, and in some instances a randomized controlled clinical trial, might be the appropriate confirmatory method.
hazard: Unconfirmed safety or effectiveness under actual clinical use.

statement: Evaluate performance consistency across clinically relevant subgroups in the intended-use population.
quote: Across these approaches, relevant considerations might include whether the device performs consistently across clinically relevant subgroups within the intended use population.
hazard: Subgroup-specific performance failures concealed by aggregate results.

statement: Supplement data-scarce subgroup evaluations with synthetic patient data representative of the intended deployment environment.
quote: Where subgroup evaluation would be difficult, particularly for small or hard-to-sample subgroups where real-world data is limited, CDRH is considering that synthetically generated data modeled on real patient data could potentially supplement evaluation, assuming such synthetic data is representative of the environment in which the device is intended to be deployed.
hazard: Unevaluated safety and performance in small or underrepresented subgroups.

statement: Compare open-ended output performance with qualified-clinician consensus reflecting the applicable standard of care.
quote: CDRH is considering that for many GenAI-enabled devices, performance might be compared to that of a panel of qualified clinicians whose consensus reflects the applicable standard of care, or to that of a median clinician in practice.
hazard: Inappropriate performance standards for outputs without one uniquely correct response.

statement: Consider median practicing-clinician performance as a comparator for open-ended outputs.
quote: CDRH is considering that for many GenAI-enabled devices, performance might be compared to that of a panel of qualified clinicians whose consensus reflects the applicable standard of care, or to that of a median clinician in practice.
hazard: Performance judgments lacking a relevant clinical comparator.

statement: Use an established ground truth or clinical reference standard when one is available and appropriate.
quote: For other GenAI-enabled devices, a more traditional ground truth or clinical reference standard may be available and appropriate, e.g., a diagnosis confirmed by biopsy or by adjudicated expert consensus.
hazard: Accuracy assessments based on unreliable reference answers.

statement: Select performance comparisons that reflect whether intended deployment uses a clinician–AI team or autonomous AI.
quote: Considerations for selecting the comparator might include how the device is actually used, including the combined performance of the clinician and device working together as a human-AI team versus the device working in a fully autonomous workflow, depending on the intended use.
hazard: Evaluation results that misrepresent the intended human–AI workflow.

statement: Use qualified, independent third parties to conduct or evaluate competency-based assessments.
quote: Conducting or evaluating the competency-based assessment of a GenAIenabled device (or portions of the competency assessment) and issuing a determination (or a certificate) that CDRH could consider in its review of the device;
hazard: Biased assessment caused by insufficient separation between development and testing.

statement: Use third-party-maintained, sequestered evaluation datasets and benchmarks developed independently of the device manufacturer.
quote: Maintaining sequestered evaluation datasets and benchmarks that are developed independently from the device manufacturer;
hazard: Contaminated or manufacturer-optimized benchmarks that overstate real-world performance.

statement: Scale postdeployment monitoring scope to the device’s risk profile.
quote: CDRH recognizes that there may be a variety of different approaches to postmarket monitoring of GenAI-enabled devices, and that the scope, frequency, and level of evidence of such approaches might vary in proportion to the risk profile of the device.
hazard: Monitoring that overlooks important risks in higher-risk deployments.

statement: Set postdeployment monitoring frequency in proportion to the device’s risk profile.
quote: CDRH recognizes that there may be a variety of different approaches to postmarket monitoring of GenAI-enabled devices, and that the scope, frequency, and level of evidence of such approaches might vary in proportion to the risk profile of the device.
hazard: Delayed detection of failures in higher-risk deployments.

statement: Scale the evidentiary rigor of postdeployment monitoring to the device’s risk profile.
quote: CDRH recognizes that there may be a variety of different approaches to postmarket monitoring of GenAI-enabled devices, and that the scope, frequency, and level of evidence of such approaches might vary in proportion to the risk profile of the device.
hazard: Weak monitoring evidence that fails to establish continued safe performance.

statement: Re-benchmark deployed devices on a defined schedule against prespecified performance thresholds.
quote: The sponsor reassesses the device against the prespecified benchmarking thresholds described in Section V.B, on a defined cadence and after defined triggering events, including changes to the underlying model or other components of the deployment architecture.
hazard: Undetected deterioration after initial evaluation.

statement: Re-benchmark after predefined triggers, including underlying-model or deployment-architecture changes.
quote: The sponsor reassesses the device against the prespecified benchmarking thresholds described in Section V.B, on a defined cadence and after defined triggering events, including changes to the underlying model or other components of the deployment architecture.
hazard: Safety or effectiveness regressions introduced by deployment changes.

statement: Periodically have qualified, independent clinicians review sampled real-world inputs and outputs against prospectively defined criteria.
quote: Periodic sample-based clinician review: Qualified, independent clinician adjudicators review samples of real-world inputs and outputs against prospectively defined criteria, sampled to reflect the range of clinically relevant presentations and interaction patterns the device encounters in real-world use.
hazard: Clinically significant output failures missed after deployment.

statement: Sample postdeployment reviews to represent clinically relevant presentations and real-world interaction patterns.
quote: Periodic sample-based clinician review: Qualified, independent clinician adjudicators review samples of real-world inputs and outputs against prospectively defined criteria, sampled to reflect the range of clinically relevant presentations and interaction patterns the device encounters in real-world use.
hazard: Monitoring blind spots caused by unrepresentative case sampling.

statement: Monitor performance degradation associated with changes in patient populations, data environments, or underlying model components.
quote: The sponsor monitors for performance degradation (e.g., drift) that may result from changes in the input population, the data environment, or underlying model components, specifying the analyses and thresholds to detect such degradation.
hazard: Undetected performance drift during real-world use.

statement: Specify the analyses used to detect postdeployment performance degradation.
quote: The sponsor monitors for performance degradation (e.g., drift) that may result from changes in the input population, the data environment, or underlying model components, specifying the analyses and thresholds to detect such degradation.
hazard: Inconsistent or ineffective detection of deteriorating performance.

statement: Specify thresholds for detecting postdeployment performance degradation.
quote: The sponsor monitors for performance degradation (e.g., drift) that may result from changes in the input population, the data environment, or underlying model components, specifying the analyses and thresholds to detect such degradation.
hazard: Ambiguous detection criteria that delay recognition of unsafe degradation.

statement: Document postdeployment device changes in a quality management system.
quote: CDRH is considering several possible approaches to the oversight of postmarket changes to GenAI-enabled devices, with requirements that may range from documentation in a sponsor’s quality management system to FDA authorization before changes are implemented.
hazard: Untracked modifications that compromise safety or effectiveness.

statement: Use a Predetermined Change Control Plan to manage eligible device modifications.
quote: A Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP)22 could be one mechanism to facilitate certain device changes without requiring a new premarket submission.
hazard: Uncontrolled changes to a deployed medical device.

statement: Establish device-specific safety and effectiveness even when the underlying foundation model has a master file.
quote: Under such an approach, submission of a Foundation Model MAF would not constitute authorization of the underlying model for any device intended use, and sponsors would remain responsible for independently demonstrating the safety and effectiveness of their own device built on a foundation model.
hazard: Assuming foundation-model documentation establishes safety for a specific clinical application.

statement: Test recognition of safety-critical clinical states.
quote: Whether the device recognizes safety-critical clinical states and initiates escalation that is timely, clear, actionable, and appropriately empathetic.
hazard: Failure to recognize a clinical emergency.

statement: Evaluate escalation messages for clarity, actionability, and appropriate empathy.
quote: Whether the device recognizes safety-critical clinical states and initiates escalation that is timely, clear, actionable, and appropriately empathetic.
hazard: Escalation messages that users cannot understand or act upon.

statement: Test for both missed clinically necessary escalation and clinically unnecessary escalation.
quote: Both under-escalation (failing to escalate when clinically necessary) and over-escalation (escalating when not clinically indicated) are relevant failures.

statement: Measure time to escalation in multi-turn simulated encounters with evolving clinical presentations.
quote: Relevant testing may include multi-turn simulated encounters that assess time to escalation in evolving presentations, the quality of escalation language and handoff information, and resistance to over-reassurance when users minimize symptoms or resist escalation.

statement: Assess the quality of handoff information produced during escalation.

statement: Test resistance to over-reassurance when users minimize symptoms or resist escalation.

statement: Test medication-safety knowledge, including contraindications and drug interactions.

hazard: Unsafe medication advice involving contraindications or interactions.

statement: Test population-specific clinical knowledge for pregnancy, pediatric and geriatric care, and renal or hepatic impairment.
quote: Whether the device possesses accurate, current, and applicable clinical knowledge for its intended scope, including current guidelines, contraindications, drug interactions, and population-specific considerations, including, for example, those applicable to pregnant patients, pediatric and geriatric patients, and patients with renal or hepatic impairment.

statement: Test whether the device acknowledges uncertainty about evidence not reflected in its training.

statement: Validate that intended users receive key information in relevant use contexts.

statement: Validate that intended users functionally understand key information in relevant use contexts.

quote: Stakeholders in implementation of AI tools in clinical practice should therefore familiarize themselves with the relevant methods and metrics for clinical evaluation and devise strategies to verify performance claims prior to tool introduction
hazard: Deployment of AI tools that fail to meet advertised clinical safety claims

statement: Continuously monitor the performance of AI systems during routine usage.
quote: and should continuously monitor performance during routine usage (64).
hazard: Undetected AI performance drift over time

statement: Test the AI model on local data using local systems and workflows to ensure accuracy at deployment.
quote: testing the AI model on local data, with the local systems and workflows used in practice, is essential to ensure accuracy and relevance when the model is deployed.
hazard: Inaccurate model predictions due to incompatible local workflows

statement: Calculate an enhanced detection rate based on the combined true positive results of the radiologist and AI.
quote: Secondly, calculate an “Enhanced Detection Rate,” the optimized detection that could be obtained through a combined detection of radiologist plus AI true positive results.
hazard: Underestimating the clinical impact of radiologist and AI augmentation

statement: Identify impressive or "WOW cases" during evaluation to demonstrate AI model value to stakeholders.
quote: Thirdly, impressive, or “WOW cases,” should be identified to demonstrate the AI model’s value to users and stakeholders.
hazard: Poor user adoption due to unperceived model value

statement: Categorize false positive and false negative cases to set radiologist expectations and improve model acceptance.
quote: Fourthly, categorizing AI false positives and, when possible, false negative cases can set radiologist expectations and improve their acceptance of an imperfect AI model
hazard: Clinician rejection of AI tools due to misunderstood error patterns

statement: Utilize clinical evaluation data alongside change management to set user expectations before AI implementation.
quote: Utilizing information from the above 5-step clinical evaluation for radiologist education, coupled with change management, is vital to set user expectations before AI model implementation.
hazard: User dissatisfaction and misuse from mismatched performance expectations

statement: Establish ongoing AI performance oversight as a core function of the local AI governance process.
quote: institutions using AI should establish ongoing performance oversight as one function of a local AI governance process (78).
hazard: Lack of accountability for degrading model accuracy

statement: Determine case-by-case the requirements for sufficient monitoring of each specific algorithm.
quote: It is incumbent on the local AI oversight group to determine on a case by case basis what sufficient monitoring looks like in a particular algorithm.
hazard: Inadequate oversight due to rigid, one-size-fits-all monitoring policies

statement: Tailor real-world monitoring strategies to the AI model type and the risk to patient safety.
quote: Strategies for real-world monitoring of AI in clinical practice should take into account the type of AI model being used and the risk to patient safety if the model performance declines.
hazard: Misaligned monitoring intensity causing missed critical AI failures

statement: Deploy robust monitoring solutions prior to running unsupervised, autonomously-functioning AI algorithms.
quote: However, when unsupervised autonomously-functioning AI algorithms emerge, robust monitoring solutions will be required to ensure patient safety.
hazard: Patient harm originating from unchecked autonomous AI errors

statement: Develop an escalation and resolution strategy detailing notifications and operational modes for when monitoring detects model failures.
quote: Institutions should develop a clearly defined escalation and resolution strategy when monitoring detects model failure or performance drift occurs that defines the notification and action plan, and the mode of operation while the model performance is being assessed and the cause of model failure determined.
hazard: Delayed clinical response to failing AI systems endangering patients

statement: Re-evaluate static AI model performance at least annually if real-time data gathering is limited.
quote: Re-evaluation of AI model performance using updated local data sets at specified intervals, but at least annually, may be an appropriate monitoring mechanism for models where gathering real-time data on model performance is limited
hazard: Long-term undetected performance drift in non-monitored static models

statement: Define baseline input data characteristics upon model acceptance to continuously monitor for data drift.
quote: institutions could elect to define baseline input data characteristics at the time of model acceptance and then monitor for data drift against that baseline state specific to each AI model (82).
hazard: Undetected data drift degrading overall AI model predictions

statement: Incorporate available patient demographic information from DICOM headers into continuous AI monitoring data collection.
quote: Limited patient demographic information may also be found in the DICOM header and should be incorporated in the data collection.
hazard: Inability to detect biased performance across demographic subpopulations

statement: Formalize local AI governance oversight and associated processes for clinical AI deployment.
quote: Given the complexity of managing all aspects of the AI lifecycle in clinical environments, provider entities engaging in the use of clinical AI are well served by formalizing local AI governance oversight and associated processes (78).
hazard: Uncoordinated and risky deployment of clinical AI tools

statement: Assimilate, orient, and train new clinical staff in available AI tools and associated work processes.
quote: As new users arrive in a local practice, they need to be properly assimilated, oriented, and trained in the available AI tools and associated work processes, to become effective participants in this technology-assisted care delivery paradigm.
hazard: Errors caused by untrained clinical staff misusing AI systems

statement: Require robust continuous performance monitoring for continuous-learning AI models prior to deployment.
quote: Robust continuous performance monitoring will be needed prior to deployment of any autonomously functioning AI algorithms and required for continuous-learning AI models.
hazard: Unpredictable degradation of self-updating models over time

statement: Include at minimum yearly re-evaluations of AI model performance in monitoring strategies to ensure safety.
quote: Monitoring strategies should include at minimum yearly re-valuation the performance of all AI models being used in clinical practice so that appropriate measures can be taken to ensure patient safety.
hazard: Prolonged exposure of patients to degraded AI performance

statement: Educate radiologists and other end-users on AI principles, including the limits and potential risks of the AI models they use.
quote: To ensure safe operation of AI models in Radiology, it is essential to educate radiologists and other potential end-users about the principles of AI and teach them the limits and potential risks when using AI models (15, 16).
hazard: Unsafe use of AI by users unaware of its limitations and risks

statement: Evaluate AI model accuracy on the target patient population before introducing it into clinical practice.
quote: It is also important to evaluate the accuracy of AI models on the target population before introducing them into clinical practice, and after that introduction, their performance should be monitored to detect drifts in accuracy.
hazard: Deploying models that underperform on the local population

statement: Monitor AI model performance after deployment to detect drifts in accuracy.
quote: It is also important to evaluate the accuracy of AI models on the target population before introducing them into clinical practice, and after that introduction, their performance should be monitored to detect drifts in accuracy.
hazard: Undetected performance drift over time

statement: Design AI integration to avoid exposing radiologists to multiple complex separate interfaces.
quote: In this context, attention should be paid to the interface design. Exposing radiologists to an increasing number of complex interfaces is undesirable, and is liable to diminish utility and acceptance of AI tools (18).
hazard: Interface complexity reducing utility and acceptance of AI tools

statement: Obtain appropriate patient consent for use of patient data by AI systems.
quote: Ensuring that this data is used ethically involves maintaining patient privacy, obtaining informed consent for data use, and ensuring data security.
hazard: Unethical use of patient data without consent

statement: Maintain patient privacy and data security for data used in AI training and operation.
quote: Ensuring that this data is used ethically involves maintaining patient privacy, obtaining informed consent for data use, and ensuring data security.
hazard: Privacy breaches and insecure patient data

statement: Consider potential harms to patients such as discrimination, insurance costs and humiliation when making AI data-related decisions.
quote: Potential harms, such as discrimination, insurance costs and humiliation, must be considered when data-related decisions are made.
hazard: Discrimination, insurance, or humiliation harms from data use

statement: Maintain anonymity of patient data used by AI systems.
quote: The anonymity of patient data is also an important but complex consideration and, if not maintained, is another source of risk.
hazard: Re-identification of patients

statement: Assess whether AI training data are representative of the patient population on which the system will be used.
quote: In particular, AI systems rely on training data, lack context and are more likely to exhibit bias if the data used to train the AI system are not representative of the patient population on which the AI system will be used.
hazard: Biased outputs for underrepresented patient groups

statement: Account for radiologist fatigue and limited workforce capacity, which heighten automation bias, when planning supervision of AI output.
quote: This automation bias may be accentuated when a radiologist is fatigued or there is a limited radiology workforce and therefore limited capacity to supervise AI output.
hazard: Automation bias leading to acceptance of incorrect AI output

statement: Increase assessment and monitoring intensity for autonomous AI systems or systems that continue learning after deployment.
quote: Risks to patient safety will also be higher when autonomous AI systems are implemented or the AI system continues to learn and adapt over time. In these situations, the need for assessment and monitoring of AI system performance becomes commensurately greater.
hazard: Higher patient safety risk from autonomous or adaptive AI

statement: Provide deployers clear information on the AI system's intended purpose, capabilities, limitations, operating conditions, and expected accuracy.
quote: Transparency requires provision of clear information about an AI system’s capabilities and limitations, in particular the purpose for which the systems are intended, the conditions under which they can be expected to function as intended and the expected level of accuracy in achieving the specified purpose.
hazard: Use of AI outside intended conditions or with misplaced trust

statement: Inform patients when AI systems are being used in their care.
quote: The concept of transparency should also extend to patients being made aware if AI systems are being used.
hazard: Patients unaware of AI involvement in their care

statement: Balance transparency and explainability disclosures against risks of privacy loss, proprietary information loss, and malicious attacks.
quote: Opinions differ, but the need for transparency, interpretability and explainability should be balanced against potential harm relating to loss of privacy, loss of proprietary information and malicious attacks.
hazard: Privacy loss or malicious attacks enabled by disclosure

statement: Assign ultimate responsibility and accountability for AI use to its human designers and operators.
quote: Ultimate responsibility and accountability for AI remains with its human designers and operators.
hazard: Unclear accountability for AI-related harms

statement: Identify and manage conflicts of interest where clinicians or health systems are involved with commercial AI vendors.
quote: Conflicts of interest may also arise where radiologists, other healthcare professionals or healthcare systems are engaged by or otherwise involved with commercial entities marketing AI systems (28).
hazard: Biased AI selection or evaluation due to conflicts of interest

statement: Plan integration of AI systems into clinical workflow and with other technology before deployment.
quote: In order to achieve optimal performance and patient safety, consideration must be given to successful integration of AI systems into workflow and with other technology, and education of those using such systems.
hazard: Poor integration compromising performance and patient safety

statement: Educate users of AI systems before and during deployment.
quote: In order to achieve optimal performance and patient safety, consideration must be given to successful integration of AI systems into workflow and with other technology, and education of those using such systems.
hazard: Unsafe use by inadequately trained users

statement: Develop AI products that target unmet clinical needs rather than available technology and datasets.
quote: New products should target unmet clinical needs rather than focus on existing technology and datasets.
hazard: Tools lacking clinical utility

statement: Involve clinicians as early as possible in AI tool design and development.
quote: In the absence of an existing Use Case reference, or an application that is not a direct derivative evolution of an existing application, developers should involve clinicians as early as possible in the design and development process to gain insights into the feasibility and practicality of proposals, well before substantial investments in time and developer resources have been made.
hazard: Impractical or infeasible tools poorly suited to clinical workflow

statement: Determine baseline clinical performance and compare AI performance against existing software or radiologist multi-reader control data.
quote: In situations where no such open data exist, developers should determine the baseline clinical performance, and compare the AI performance with existing or approved software, or radiologist multi-reader control data.
hazard: Deploying tools not superior to existing practice

statement: Require external or multi-centre test data and prospective real-world evaluation for AI models with poor transparency or explainability.
quote: in situations where model transparency and explainability are poor, a higher standard of empirical evidence of performance may be required, including external or multi-centre test data to prove model generalizability, and prospective real-world evaluation, used in clinical settings that most resemble the clinical setting in which the product is most likely to be deployed.
hazard: Poor generalizability of black-box models

statement: Require vendors to report a range of expected performance and specific failure conditions, not a single summary accuracy figure.
quote: Two common errors in solution performance reporting include a failure to report a range of expected performance—lower quality solutions often report a single summary accuracy figure—and not reporting specific failure conditions and errors, with lower quality solutions selectively highlighting the best diagnoses made by their systems.
hazard: Overstated performance claims hiding failure modes

statement: Request Model Cards or System Cards reporting limitations, errors, and biases from AI vendors.
quote: In the broader AI safety community, there is a strong embrace of Model Cards or System Cards, in which in-depth analyses of limitations, errors, and biases are explicitly reported, often entirely separate from the primary report of system performance (44, 45).
hazard: Undisclosed limitations, errors, and biases

statement: Maintain human co-supervision of AI decisions in clinical imaging, including declarations of stability or normality.
quote: The patient implications of decision making required in clinical medical imaging, even declarations of stability or normality, often have dramatic direct implications on patient care, which we suspect will require human co-supervision for some time.
hazard: Harm from unsupervised autonomous AI decisions

statement: Require an explicit post-market quality assurance plan for AI solutions.
quote: Regulators should be particularly attuned to ensuring that solutions have an explicit post-market quality assurance plan.
hazard: Lack of post-deployment safety assurance

statement: Re-check AI performance for concept drift after patient population changes or software version upgrades.
quote: The importance of this has several aspects, but mainly relates to the issues caused by concept drift, due to changes in the patient population or occasionally even differences due to upgrades of successive new versions of AI software (49).
hazard: Performance changes after population shifts or software upgrades

statement: Monitor month-to-month diagnostic event frequencies and raise alerts when values exceed normal bounds.
quote: In practice, what this may entail is prospective performance monitoring of the AI model, for example monitoring for major deviations in month-to-month diagnostic event frequencies, with alerts raised when normal bounds are exceeded
hazard: Undetected concept drift

statement: Routinely evaluate the algorithm on a constant held-out control set of difficult or borderline cases.
quote: or a control sample approach where a constant reserved held-out set of test case examples is routinely evaluated with the algorithm, to ensure no major deviations on known difficult or borderline cases (50).
hazard: Degradation on difficult cases going unnoticed

statement: Establish an easily accessible procedure for clinicians to report unexpected AI errors to the vendor, with named responsible contacts.
quote: At a very minimum, a clear reporting procedure for unexpected errors to the vendor, with named responsible contact personnel, should be established and made easily accessible to clinical end users.
hazard: Unreported AI errors persisting

statement: Define the AI tool's intended use, main beneficiaries, associated risks, and potential economic impact before purchase.
quote: What is the intended use of the AI, who will most benefit from its use, which risks are associated with its use and what is the potential economic impact?
hazard: Purchasing tools without clear purpose or risk understanding

statement: Plan how the AI tool will integrate into institutional workflows before purchase.
quote: How will the AI tool be integrated into the institutions’ workflows and how can the commercial claims be verified and monitored?
hazard: Poor workflow integration

statement: Establish how vendor commercial claims will be verified and monitored after purchase.
quote: How will the AI tool be integrated into the institutions’ workflows and how can the commercial claims be verified and monitored?
hazard: Reliance on unverified vendor claims

statement: Define user training requirements for the AI tool before implementation.
quote: How do users need to be trained and which psychological effects need to be considered with regard to human-AI-interaction?
hazard: Untrained users misusing AI tools

statement: Assess psychological effects of human-AI interaction, such as automation bias, before implementing the tool.
quote: How do users need to be trained and which psychological effects need to be considered with regard to human-AI-interaction?
hazard: Automation bias and other human-AI interaction errors

statement: Verify whether regulatory clearance accuracy data reflect accuracy on local data and whether local accuracy suffices for institutional use.
quote: Is the FDA (or other agency) approval/clearance data reflective of accuracy on local data? Is that accuracy on local data sufficient for use in that institution and will users accept and hence engage with the AI results?
hazard: Regulatory accuracy not transferring to local setting

statement: Identify areas needing improvement and define relevant key performance indicators before integrating an AI tool.
quote: For any AI tool to be successfully integrated into clinical practice, stakeholders should first clearly identify areas that need improvement and define relevant key performance indicators (52, 53).
hazard: Unmeasurable or unjustified AI adoption

statement: Confirm the AI tool solves a real, specific problem the institution has before adopting it.
quote: In either case, as outlined in Section 4A, it is essential to determine whether or not the tool solves a real, specific problem that the institution has; tools are solutions, and a solution to a non-existent problem has no value.
hazard: Investing in tools of no value to the institution

statement: Set objective, quantifiable goals to measure the AI tool's positive impact.
quote: For the positive impact of an AI tool to be measurable, objective and quantifiable goals should be set.
hazard: Inability to measure AI benefit

statement: Estimate the proportion of cases or patients the AI tool will affect and the magnitude of impact per case.
quote: It may be useful to consider both what proportion of cases or patients an AI tool is expected to impact, and what the magnitude of impact on each case or patient is expected to be.
hazard: Overestimating AI benefit

statement: Plan and conduct return-on-investment and cost–benefit analyses before AI integration.
quote: Return on investment (RoI) and cost–benefit analyses should be planned and carried out to ensure the viability of the planned AI integration.
hazard: Financially unviable AI deployments

statement: Include capital and recurrent costs and implementation risks in AI purchase analysis.
quote: Lastly, potential costs (both capital and recurrent) and risks associated with the implementation and usage of an AI system are essential components of any purchase analysis and decision.
hazard: Underestimated total cost and risk

statement: Consult vendor regulatory risk matrices and risk–benefit analyses while recognizing risks not covered there.
quote: In part, risk assessment can be facilitated by consulting the risk matrix and the risk–benefit analysis provided in the regulatory files by vendors. However, some risks may not be addressed in such regulatory filings or only become apparent during use.
hazard: Unrecognized deployment risks

statement: Evaluate vendor reliability as a partner and staying power in a consolidating market before purchase.
quote: Other essential factors in making an informed decision include evaluating the vendor’s compatibility as a reliable partner, the vendor’s staying power in a competitive environment with limited payor reimbursement (even more important in this era of AI vendor consolidation), optimized model pricing, and opportunities for collaboration beyond product purchase, such as co-development and product resale.
hazard: Vendor failure leaving unsupported tools

statement: Perform a statistically rigorous evaluation of AI performance on the site's own local data before implementation.
quote: Ideally, each site considering implementation would perform a statistically rigorous evaluation of performance on their own local data (a method for this evaluation is presented in the Clinical Evaluation Section below).
hazard: Local error rates differing from reported testing

statement: At minimum, compare local data characteristics (e.g., scanner manufacturer, protocols, demographics) with vendor test data characteristics.
quote: At a minimum, the characteristics of local data should be compared with those of the test data (a typical example might be where a model has been tested only on one manufacturer’s MRI scanner, but will be used on a scanner made by a different manufacturer).
hazard: Performance degradation from data distribution mismatch

statement: Avoid or proceed with great caution when local population differs from test data, such as off-label pediatric use of adult-tested algorithms.
quote: Where these are similar, the reported performance metrics may be relied upon with some confidence; where they are not (e.g., an algorithm tested only on adults being considered for off-label use in a pediatric hospital) one should proceed with great caution, if at all.
hazard: Unsafe off-label use on unvalidated populations

statement: Assess, for each anticipated AI error type, the probability that people in the workflow will detect it.
quote: One should consider the detectability of the errors that are anticipated. That is, for each error, what is the probability that people in the workflow will notice that the AI has produced an erroneous output?
hazard: Undetected AI errors reaching patients

statement: Assess risk of AI errors by jointly considering error frequency, detectability, correctability, and patient impact.
quote: The consideration together of error frequency, detectability, correctability and impact provides a framework for assessing the direct risk of algorithmic errors.
hazard: Underestimating harm from uncorrected algorithmic errors

statement: Clarify over-reliance and under-reliance biases that can affect radiologist–AI interpretation.
quote: These biases need to be both clarified and managed to ensure the AI’s output does not negatively influence the radiologist’s judgment. There are two general types of bias that can be introduced in a human–computer system, over-reliance, and under-reliance.
hazard: False-positive and false-negative interpretations caused by inappropriate reliance on AI.

statement: Mitigate over-reliance and under-reliance biases in radiologist–AI interpretation.
quote: These biases need to be both clarified and managed to ensure the AI’s output does not negatively influence the radiologist’s judgment. There are two general types of bias that can be introduced in a human–computer system, over-reliance, and under-reliance.
hazard: Acceptance of incorrect AI results or rejection of accurate AI results.

statement: Optimize the diagnostic performance of the combined radiologist–AI system.
quote: Ultimately, the output of the combination of radiologist plus the AI system must be optimized.
hazard: Poor diagnostic performance arising from interactions between radiologists and AI.

statement: Provide continuous radiologist education about AI capabilities and limitations.
quote: A robust approach to mitigating biases and challenges related to reliance involves continuous radiologist education about AI capabilities and limitations.
hazard: Diagnostic errors caused by misunderstanding AI capabilities or limitations.

statement: Provide radiologists with comprehensive information about AI decision-making.
quote: Providing comprehensive information about AI decision-making, its results, and confidence levels can enhance transparency and help radiologists make informed judgments.
hazard: Uninformed diagnostic judgments caused by opaque AI decision-making.

statement: Provide radiologists with comprehensive information about AI results.
quote: Providing comprehensive information about AI decision-making, its results, and confidence levels can enhance transparency and help radiologists make informed judgments.
hazard: Misinterpretation of AI results because of insufficient information.

statement: Provide radiologists with information about AI confidence levels.
quote: Providing comprehensive information about AI decision-making, its results, and confidence levels can enhance transparency and help radiologists make informed judgments.
hazard: Inappropriate trust in uncertain AI outputs.

statement: Categorize scenarios in which AI assistance may fail.
quote: In addition, categorizing scenarios where AI assistance may falter, and integrating that information into a robust training program, can empower radiologists to recognize and rectify errors.
hazard: Failure-prone AI use scenarios remaining unrecognized.

statement: Incorporate scenarios where AI assistance may fail into radiologist training.
quote: In addition, categorizing scenarios where AI assistance may falter, and integrating that information into a robust training program, can empower radiologists to recognize and rectify errors.
hazard: Radiologists failing to recognize or correct AI errors.

statement: Identify the most accurate AI model for radiologist augmentation.
quote: The accuracy of the AI system also affects rad-AI bias—bias is decreased by more accurate AI results (87). Hence, identifying the most accurate AI model has clinical relevance.
hazard: Increased radiologist–AI bias from inaccurate AI results.

statement: Monitor the diagnostic accuracy of the combined radiologist–AI system.
quote: Ultimately, the successful implementation of AI in radiology relies on an understanding of its implications, and proactive measures, including radiologist education, AI explainability, and radiologist-AI accuracy monitoring to address safety and ethical concerns.
hazard: Undetected diagnostic inaccuracies in combined radiologist–AI performance.

statement: Provide directed feedback on combined radiologist–AI accuracy.
quote: Finally, the measurement of rad-AI accuracy, along with directed feedback, can further refine the system’s performance.
hazard: Persistent radiologist–AI performance problems without corrective feedback.

statement: Assess how AI augmentation affects resource allocation for training and retaining subspecialist radiologists in resource-constrained settings.
quote: However, the reliance on AI may lead to a dilemma where the presence of AI might influence the allocation of resources for training and retaining subspecialists. Careful consideration is needed to balance the ethical implications of AI augmentation in resource-constrained environments.
hazard: AI adoption undermining investment in subspecialist training and retention.

statement: Apply stringent reliability and accuracy standards to autonomous diagnostic AI.
quote: Autonomous AI should be subject to stringent performance standards and comprehensive and continuous testing to ensure its reliability and accuracy.
hazard: Unreliable or inaccurate diagnostic decisions without direct human oversight.

statement: Conduct comprehensive, continuous testing of autonomous diagnostic AI for reliability and accuracy.
quote: Autonomous AI should be subject to stringent performance standards and comprehensive and continuous testing to ensure its reliability and accuracy.
hazard: Undetected autonomous AI inaccuracies or reliability failures.

statement: Critically assess autonomous AI failure modes across real-world environments rather than relying solely on regulatory or vendor accuracy statistics.
quote: It is essential to critically assess the system’s failure modes, considering that statistics from regulatory approval or vendor-provided accuracy rates might not adequately reflect real-world performance across various environments.
hazard: Unrecognized real-world failures concealed by unrepresentative approval or vendor performance statistics.

statement: Establish a rigorous ongoing monitoring program to detect autonomous AI errors promptly.
quote: For autonomous AI, a rigorous ongoing monitoring program is imperative to detect and rectify errors promptly (11).
hazard: Autonomous diagnostic errors continuing undetected.

statement: Promptly rectify errors detected during autonomous AI operation.
quote: For autonomous AI, a rigorous ongoing monitoring program is imperative to detect and rectify errors promptly (11).
hazard: Continued patient exposure to known autonomous AI errors.

statement: Train healthcare professionals to recognize autonomous AI failure modes.
quote: Training healthcare professionals in recognizing failure modes and offering a simple mechanism to disable autonomous AI when necessary is essential to avoid unchecked errors that could jeopardize patient care.
hazard: Unchecked autonomous AI errors jeopardizing patient care.

statement: Provide healthcare professionals with a simple mechanism to disable autonomous AI when necessary.
quote: Training healthcare professionals in recognizing failure modes and offering a simple mechanism to disable autonomous AI when necessary is essential to avoid unchecked errors that could jeopardize patient care.
hazard: Inability to stop autonomous AI producing unsafe results.

statement: Use input-data assessment tools, such as training-distribution checks, to obtain early indications of autonomous AI accuracy.
quote: To gain earlier insights into AI’s accuracy, additional tools for assessing expected AI outcomes based on input data (e.g., determining whether the input data falls within or outside the training data distribution) or comparing the results of one AI model to those of other AI models simultaneously can be employed (88).
hazard: Delayed detection of inaccurate outputs caused by unfamiliar input data.

statement: Compare autonomous AI outputs with simultaneous outputs from other AI models to obtain early indications of accuracy.
quote: To gain earlier insights into AI’s accuracy, additional tools for assessing expected AI outcomes based on input data (e.g., determining whether the input data falls within or outside the training data distribution) or comparing the results of one AI model to those of other AI models simultaneously can be employed (88).
hazard: Delayed recognition of inaccurate autonomous AI results.

statement: Make actions initiated by autonomous AI transparent, identifiable, and discoverable.
quote: Autonomous AI should be designed to initiate actions that are transparent, identifiable, and discoverable.
hazard: Autonomous AI actions occurring without being recognized or understood.

statement: Ensure autonomous AI can be disabled swiftly and effectively in the event of failure.
quote: The capacity to disable the AI system swiftly and effectively in the event of failure is crucial for patient safety.
hazard: Patient harm during delayed or ineffective shutdown of failed autonomous AI.

statement: Establish a streamlined process for addressing autonomous AI failures to prevent their recurrence.
quote: A streamlined process to address and mitigate failures should be in place to prevent repeating mistakes.
hazard: Repeated autonomous AI failures because incidents are not effectively addressed.

statement: Balance improved access with preservation of diagnostic quality when deploying autonomous AI where radiology services are scarce.
quote: In communities where radiology services are scarce, the deployment of autonomous AI raises complex ethical questions. While autonomous AI can provide diagnostic insights in the absence of skilled radiologists, decisions made by AI systems could potentially lack nuanced human judgment. Striking a balance between accessible healthcare and maintaining diagnostic quality becomes a critical ethical concern.
hazard: Improved access coming at the expense of diagnostic quality in underserved communities.

statement: Align AI development, promotion, and clinical adoption with benefits for the patients on whom the tools will be used.
quote: Development, promotion and clinical adoption of AI tools must be aligned with benefit for those on whom these tools will be used (89).
hazard: AI development or adoption serving interests other than patient benefit.

statement: Consider commercial interests when developing or adopting AI tools.
quote: Inevitably, commercial interests must be considered when developing and adopting AI tools, but these interests should not take primacy.
hazard: AI development or adoption decisions overlooking relevant commercial interests.

statement: Prevent commercial interests from taking priority in AI development and adoption decisions.
quote: Inevitably, commercial interests must be considered when developing and adopting AI tools, but these interests should not take primacy.
hazard: Commercial incentives overriding patient benefit.

statement: Make patient and societal safety and well-being the primary drivers of AI lifecycle decisions.
quote: In this multisociety paper, we have endeavoured to provide guidance for developers, purchasers and users of AI in radiology to ensure that the practical issues that surround all stages of AI from conception to long-term integration in healthcare are clear, understood and addressed, and that patient and societal safety and well-being are the primary drivers of all decisions.
hazard: AI lifecycle decisions subordinating patient or societal safety and well-being.

statement: Perform clinical evaluation studies at multiple sites to assess performance and interoperability across clinical workflows before deployment.
quote: Except for AI tools intended for single centres, the clinical evaluation studies should be performed at several sites to assess performance and interoperability across clinical workflows.46
hazard: The AI tool fails to generalize or interoperate when deployed at new clinical sites.

statement: Evaluate AI tools for local clinical validity to ensure they fit local clinical workflows and perform well on local populations before deployment.
quote: Therefore, to ensure trust at each site, the AI tools should be evaluated for their local clinical validity.17
hazard: Model performance degrades due to site-specific population or workflow differences.

statement: Maintain a risk management file and continuously monitor risks and their mitigation measures throughout the AI tool's lifecycle.
quote: Throughout the AI tool’s lifecycle, the multidisciplinary development team shall analyse potential risks, assess each risk’s likelihood, effects and risk-benefit balance, define risk mitigation measures, monitor the risks and mitigations continuously, and maintain a risk management file.
hazard: Unmitigated or evolving risks cause harm during AI operation.

statement: Implement risk mitigation measures such as user warnings, system shutdowns, or reverting to human judgment when necessary.
quote: Mitigation measures might include warnings to the users, system shutdown, reprocessing of the input data, the acquisition of new input data, or the use of an alternative procedure or human judgment only.
hazard: AI failures or misuse harm patients without technical fail-safes in place.

statement: Use feedback channels like customer complaints and logged real-world performance to continuously monitor and reassess AI risks.
quote: Monitoring and reassessment of risk might involve the use of various feedback channels, such as customer feedback and complaints, as well as logged real world performance and issues
hazard: Unnoticed adverse events or real-world performance issues persist undetected.

statement: Provide an information leaflet to inform citizens and healthcare professionals about the AI tool's intended use, risks, and instructions.
quote: adequate documentation should be created and maintained for the AI tool,48 which might include (a) an AI information leaflet to inform citizens and healthcare professionals about the tool’s intended use, risks (eg, biases) and instructions for use;
hazard: End users misunderstand the AI tool's capabilities, limitations, and operational risks.

statement: Deploy the AI tool with mechanisms for continuous monitoring and quality control of its inputs and outputs.
quote: The AI tool should be developed and deployed with mechanisms for continuous monitoring and quality control of the AI inputs and outputs,47
hazard: Missing, out-of-range, or erroneous inputs lead to unsafe or implausible AI outputs.

statement: Provide calibrated uncertainty estimates to inform end users about the degree of confidence in the AI decisions.
quote: For quality control of the AI decisions, uncertainty estimates should be provided (and calibrated53) to inform the end users about the degree of confidence in the results.54
hazard: Users overrely on uncertain or incorrect AI predictions without knowing the confidence level.

statement: Deploy the AI tool with a configurable system for periodic auditing to identify data drift and performance degradation.
quote: The AI tool should be developed and deployed with a configurable system for periodic auditing,47 which should define the datasets and timelines for periodic evaluations (eg, every year).
hazard: AI model performance degrades over time due to unmonitored data or concept drift.

statement: Apply necessary updates to AI models or tools based on the results of periodic auditing.

statement: Implement and regularly evaluate measures to protect the AI tool against malicious or adversarial attacks.
quote: Furthermore, the manufacturers and deployers should implement and regularly evaluate measures for protecting the AI tool against malicious or adversarial attacks, such as by using system level cybersecurity solutions or application specific defence mechanisms (eg, attack detection or mitigation).76
hazard: Exploitation of the AI system by malicious actors compromising safety or privacy.

statement: Benchmark model performance against reference AI tools or standard practice to enable comparative assessment.
quote: Finally, benchmarking with respect to reference AI tools or standard practice should be performed to enable comparative assessment of model performance.
hazard: Adopting an AI tool that performs worse than existing tools or standard practice.

statement: Identify and address all application-specific ethical, social, and societal issues during development and deployment.
