quote: AI developers, domain specialists, and professional ethicists should identify, discuss, and address all application specific ethical, social, and societal issues as an integral part of the development and deployment of the AI tool.79
hazard: Unintended societal harms or ethical breaches caused by the AI application.

statement: Proceed with great caution, or not at all, when the local intended-use population or equipment differs from the population on which the algorithm was tested.
quote: where they are not (e.g., an algorithm tested only on adults being considered for off-label use in a pediatric hospital) one should proceed with great caution, if at all.
hazard: Off-label use on dissimilar populations yielding unreliable performance

statement: Before deployment, estimate the probability that users in the workflow will detect each anticipated AI error.
quote: One should consider the detectability of the errors that are anticipated.
hazard: Undetected algorithmic errors reaching patients

statement: Assess AI error risk by jointly considering error frequency, detectability, correctability and impact on patients.
quote: The consideration together of error frequency, detectability, correctability and impact provides a framework for assessing the direct risk of algorithmic errors.
hazard: Underestimating risk by considering error frequency alone

statement: Assess the risk that relying on the AI tool will de-skill radiologists for tasks they must perform manually when the tool fails.
quote: This risk is particularly problematic if the radiologist is expected to perform the task manually when the tool fails, but may no longer be skilled enough to do so adequately.
hazard: Radiologist de-skilling leaving no competent fallback when AI fails

statement: Assess, before deployment, the potential for the AI tool to create or exacerbate healthcare disparities.
quote: A final aspect of risk that must be considered is the potential for AI to create or exacerbate healthcare disparities.
hazard: AI perpetuating historical inequities embedded in training data

statement: Actively search for and mitigate biases in AI tools inherited from training data.
quote: it is incumbent upon us as physicians and data scientists to think about, search for and mitigate these biases; if these questions are unasked, they will most certainly remain unanswered.
hazard: Unidentified bias causing disparate performance across patient groups

statement: Use imaging AI to classify study and series contents (e.g., body part, IV contrast) for data orchestration instead of relying on DICOM metadata.
quote: A more robust option is to use imaging AI to determine the data contents at the studies and series level and use that output for orchestration.
hazard: Wrong images sent to AI due to incomplete or variable DICOM headers

statement: Educate referring physicians about AI model details and accuracy before making AI results visible to them in PACS.
quote: This limited integration not only allows visualization of AI results by referring physicians, which may not be optimal if these physicians haven’t been educated about the details and accuracy of the AI model, but also has been shown to increase automation bias among radiologists (59).
hazard: Uneducated referring physicians misinterpreting AI results; automation bias

statement: Configure PACS so radiologists can interact with and modify AI results.
quote: To optimize AI results management and integration, a PACS should enable the radiologist to interact with and modify the AI results and, if results are changed, empower the AI to immediately reprocess a new output.
hazard: Uncorrectable erroneous AI outputs persisting in the record

statement: Enable the AI to immediately reprocess and produce a new output when a radiologist changes AI results.
quote: To optimize AI results management and integration, a PACS should enable the radiologist to interact with and modify the AI results and, if results are changed, empower the AI to immediately reprocess a new output.
hazard: Stale AI outputs inconsistent with radiologist corrections

statement: Provide radiologist-corrected AI results back to the AI vendor for future model improvement.
quote: In addition, the updated AI result should be provided to the AI vendor so it can be used for future model improvement.
hazard: Recurring model errors not fed back for correction

statement: Store AI results together with radiologist feedback to support continuous monitoring of AI accuracy.
quote: Additionally, the ability to accept and store AI results along with radiologist feedback, optimize data security, and continuously monitor AI accuracy are crucial technical aspects that are facilitated in cloud-native systems.
hazard: Inability to track AI accuracy over time

statement: Integrate AI tools into the usual clinical workflow and information systems so users need not switch between applications.
quote: Whatever the integration, ideally AI tools should be well integrated into the usual clinical workflow and information systems in order to avoid additional workload by requiring users to switch between applications.
hazard: Added workload and poor adoption from fragmented workflows

statement: Validate the AI tool's performance on a local dataset prior to clinical implementation.
quote: purchasers should consider validation of the AI’s performance on a local dataset, and adjust parameters if needed prior to implementation in clinical practice.
hazard: AI not performing locally as advertised

statement: Adjust AI parameters such as decision thresholds based on local validation before clinical implementation.
quote: purchasers should consider validation of the AI’s performance on a local dataset, and adjust parameters if needed prior to implementation in clinical practice.
hazard: Miscalibrated thresholds producing unacceptable diagnostic accuracy

statement: Repeat local validation whenever relevant changes are made to the AI software or the equipment used with it.
quote: This process should be repeated whenever relevant changes are made to the AI software or the equipment used in combination with the AI.
hazard: Performance shifts after software or equipment updates

statement: Recalibrate decision thresholds after AI tool updates that change output rates such as recall rate.
quote: In the example of a commercially available breast screening AI model an update of the AI tool resulted in a substantially different recall rate, requiring recalibration of the decision threshold to ensure continued usage with clinically acceptable diagnostic accuracy (61).
hazard: Changed recall rates after vendor update degrading accuracy

statement: Ensure implementation stakeholders learn the relevant methods and metrics for clinical evaluation of AI tools.
quote: Stakeholders in implementation of AI tools in clinical practice should therefore familiarize themselves with the relevant methods and metrics for clinical evaluation and devise strategies to verify performance claims prior to tool introduction, and should continuously monitor performance during routine usage (64).
hazard: Inability to critically evaluate AI performance

statement: Verify vendor performance claims prior to introducing the AI tool.
quote: Stakeholders in implementation of AI tools in clinical practice should therefore familiarize themselves with the relevant methods and metrics for clinical evaluation and devise strategies to verify performance claims prior to tool introduction, and should continuously monitor performance during routine usage (64).
hazard: Reliance on unverified premarket performance claims

statement: Continuously monitor AI performance during routine clinical usage.
quote: Stakeholders in implementation of AI tools in clinical practice should therefore familiarize themselves with the relevant methods and metrics for clinical evaluation and devise strategies to verify performance claims prior to tool introduction, and should continuously monitor performance during routine usage (64).
hazard: Undetected performance degradation during clinical use

statement: Educate users and stakeholders about automation bias and algorithmic aversion in human-AI interaction.
quote: These findings highlight the need for further education on those topics to increase awareness amongst users and stakeholders and allow for safe and successful implementation of AI into clinical routine (76).
hazard: Over- or under-reliance on AI output impairing oversight

statement: Evaluate AI user interface configuration (e.g., image overlays versus text-only output) for its effect on reader performance.
quote: For example, while many radiologists preferred image overlays to detect pulmonary nodules, it was found that this configuration of the UI did not improve reader performance, while a minimalistic setup with text-only UI output did (74).
hazard: UI design degrading reader performance despite user preference

statement: Test the AI model on local data using local systems and workflows before deployment.
quote: testing the AI model on local data, with the local systems and workflows used in practice, is essential to ensure accuracy and relevance when the model is deployed.
hazard: Regulatory clearance data not reflecting local accuracy

statement: Compare AI performance on local data against regulatory authority documentation during clinical evaluation.
quote: The first step involves comparing the AI model’s performance on local data against regulatory authority documentation, specifically evaluating accuracy through the lens of radiologist acceptance and engagement with the AI tool.
hazard: Local performance falling short of documented performance

statement: Report local positive and negative predictive values at local disease prevalence rather than only AUC or sensitivity/specificity.
quote: Hence, parameters that are radiologist-facing, including positive and negative predictive values for the disease prevalence are more relevant than overall accuracy, Area Under the Curve (AUC), or sensitivity/specificity.
hazard: Misleading metrics hiding high local false-positive burden

statement: Calculate an Enhanced Detection Rate combining radiologist plus AI true positives during local evaluation.
quote: Secondly, calculate an “Enhanced Detection Rate,” the optimized detection that could be obtained through a combined detection of radiologist plus AI true positive results.
hazard: Failure to quantify added value of AI to radiologists

statement: Identify high-value cases where AI detected impressive findings to demonstrate the model's value to users.
quote: Thirdly, impressive, or “WOW cases,” should be identified to demonstrate the AI model’s value to users and stakeholders.
hazard: Poor user acceptance of an imperfect model

statement: Categorize AI false positives and, when possible, false negatives from local evaluation to set radiologist expectations.
quote: Fourthly, categorizing AI false positives and, when possible, false negative cases can set radiologist expectations and improve their acceptance of an imperfect AI model (all AI models are imperfect).
hazard: Unrealistic expectations of AI and miscalibrated trust

statement: Review all local evaluation findings to decide whether the AI model is worthy of clinical deployment.
quote: Finally, all the findings should be reviewed to determine if the AI model is worthy of clinical deployment.
hazard: Deploying models unsuitable for local practice

statement: Restrict AI deployment to exam subsets with higher disease prevalence (e.g., inpatient CXRs for pneumothorax) to reduce false positives.
quote: Hence, some AI models may be deployed on a subset of exams because disease prevalence in that exam subset is increased from baseline.
hazard: Excessive false positives in low-prevalence populations limiting acceptance

statement: Use local clinical evaluation findings for radiologist education, coupled with change management, before AI implementation.
quote: Utilizing information from the above 5-step clinical evaluation for radiologist education, coupled with change management, is vital to set user expectations before AI model implementation.
hazard: Misaligned user expectations of AI performance

statement: Designate a local AI champion to promote AI adoption among radiologists.
quote: A local AI champion plays a significant role in promoting AI adoption among radiologists.
hazard: Poor adoption and engagement with deployed AI

statement: Provide continuous user education throughout the lifecycle of AI use.
quote: Finally, continuous user education throughout the lifecycle of AI utilization and monitoring radiologist AI usage and the combined accuracy of radiologist plus AI are instrumental in ensuring optimal patient care.
hazard: Knowledge decay leading to unsafe AI use

statement: Monitor radiologists' usage of the AI tool during clinical deployment.
quote: Finally, continuous user education throughout the lifecycle of AI utilization and monitoring radiologist AI usage and the combined accuracy of radiologist plus AI are instrumental in ensuring optimal patient care.
hazard: Unnoticed misuse or non-use of AI tools

statement: Monitor the combined accuracy of radiologist plus AI in clinical practice.
quote: Finally, continuous user education throughout the lifecycle of AI utilization and monitoring radiologist AI usage and the combined accuracy of radiologist plus AI are instrumental in ensuring optimal patient care.
hazard: Human-AI team performing worse than expected

statement: Plan for static AI model performance to decline over time due to data, equipment, protocol and population shifts.
quote: End users should expect the performance of static (also known as “locked algorithms”) AI model performance to decline over time, due to shifts in local input data, changes to imaging equipment or protocols, acquisition software updates influencing source image parameters such as noise levels, or naturally occurring changes in patient populations and demographics (77).
hazard: Unanticipated performance drift of locked algorithms

statement: Establish ongoing AI performance oversight as a function of the local AI governance process.
quote: Therefore, as the use of AI becomes more prevalent and the AI tools being deployed become more diverse, institutions using AI should establish ongoing performance oversight as one function of a local AI governance process (78).
hazard: Undetected performance degradation harming patient safety

statement: Ensure monitoring systems for locally adaptive AI provide baseline and longitudinal feedback to continuously learning algorithms.
quote: In a potential future state where adaptive intelligence enables local model refinement, monitoring systems must be able to provide both baseline and longitudinal feedback information to continuously learning AI algorithms (77).
hazard: Uncontrolled drift in continuously learning models

statement: Compare real-time AI performance data against local, regional or national benchmarks when feasible.
quote: An ideal monitoring solution collects real time data on model performance, aggregates and analyses results comparing against expected performance at the local, regional or national benchmark level when feasible.
hazard: Performance degradation going unrecognized without benchmarks

statement: For triage AI models, monitor concordance or discordance between radiologist reports and model outputs.
quote: One common approach with triage type AI models that are tuned to identify findings which are also reported by radiologists would be an analysis of concordance or discordance between radiologist reports and model inference output.
hazard: Undetected triage model accuracy decline

statement: Monitor changes in input metadata, examination parameters and patient demographics against manufacturer specifications.
quote: Other targets for monitoring include changes in input metadata (e.g. equipment manufacturer, magnetic field strength or number of CT detectors), other relevant examination parameters and relevant demographic data about individual patients, since deviation of any or several of these from manufacturer specifications can result in degraded performance.
hazard: Out-of-specification inputs degrading AI performance

statement: Have the local AI oversight group define, per algorithm, what sufficient monitoring looks like.
quote: It is incumbent on the local AI oversight group to determine on a case by case basis what sufficient monitoring looks like in a particular algorithm.
hazard: Inadequate or inappropriate monitoring for specific algorithms

statement: Have radiologists confirm absence of imaging artifacts that would interfere with AI processing, especially for quantitative outputs.
quote: In all cases, but especially when using quantitative models, radiologists may be able to determine the general validity of the AI output by confirming the absence of relevant imaging artifacts that would interfere with AI processing.
hazard: Invalid AI outputs from artifact-degraded images

statement: Tailor real-world monitoring strategies to the AI model type and the patient safety risk if performance declines.
quote: Strategies for real-world monitoring of AI in clinical practice should take into account the type of AI model being used and the risk to patient safety if the model performance declines.
hazard: Under-monitoring of high-risk models

statement: Implement robust monitoring solutions before deploying unsupervised autonomously functioning AI algorithms.
quote: Robust continuous performance monitoring will be needed prior to deployment of any autonomously functioning AI algorithms and required for continuous-learning AI models.
hazard: Autonomous AI failures reaching patients without human detection

statement: Require robust continuous performance monitoring for continuous-learning AI models.
quote: Robust continuous performance monitoring will be needed prior to deployment of any autonomously functioning AI algorithms and required for continuous-learning AI models.
hazard: Uncontrolled performance changes in continuously learning models

statement: Understand failure modes and establish safety net processes before implementing autonomous AI.
quote: In future autonomous AI implementation, thorough understanding of failure modes and associated safety net processes may become paramount.
hazard: Unmitigated autonomous AI failures without human review

statement: Define a notification and action plan for when monitoring detects model failure or performance drift.
quote: Institutions should develop a clearly defined escalation and resolution strategy when monitoring detects model failure or performance drift occurs that defines the notification and action plan, and the mode of operation while the model performance is being assessed and the cause of model failure determined.
hazard: Uncoordinated response to detected model failure

statement: Define the mode of clinical operation while a failing or drifting model's performance and root cause are being assessed.
quote: Institutions should develop a clearly defined escalation and resolution strategy when monitoring detects model failure or performance drift occurs that defines the notification and action plan, and the mode of operation while the model performance is being assessed and the cause of model failure determined.
hazard: Continued unsafe use of failing model during investigation

statement: Re-evaluate the performance of all clinically used AI models at least yearly.
quote: Monitoring strategies should include at minimum yearly re-valuation the performance of all AI models being used in clinical practice so that appropriate measures can be taken to ensure patient safety.
hazard: Undetected performance degradation over time

statement: For periodic re-evaluation, build an up-to-date local evaluation dataset similar in size and parameters to the initial validation set.
quote: Such a system requires that a new up-to-date evaluation data set be created using an appropriate number of clinical cases and parameters similar to the initial validation set to re-evaluate the performance of the model under current conditions.
hazard: Re-evaluation not reflecting current local conditions

statement: Re-evaluate local model performance when the manufacturer issues a new model version rather than assuming benefits generalize.
quote: It cannot be simply assumed by user sites that intended benefits introduced by a manufacturer’s deployment of the latest version of a model automatically generalize to the local practice.
hazard: New vendor versions performing worse locally

statement: Define baseline input data characteristics at model acceptance and monitor for data drift against that baseline per model.
quote: institutions could elect to define baseline input data characteristics at the time of model acceptance and then monitor for data drift against that baseline state specific to each AI model (82).
hazard: Input data drift degrading AI performance unnoticed

statement: Trigger model performance re-evaluation when monitoring detects relevant changes in input parameters associated with data drift.
quote: Monitoring for changes in parameters known to be associated with input data drift could trigger more frequent re-evaluations.
hazard: Delayed detection of drift-related degradation

statement: Increase re-evaluation frequency based on patient risk from model failure and clinical decision relevance of the AI output.
quote: The need for more frequent re-evaluations should also be considered based on patient risk in the event of model failure and clinical decision relevance of a specific AI output.
hazard: Insufficient monitoring of high-risk AI outputs

statement: Use the interpreting radiologist's final report as a surrogate for model accuracy in continuous monitoring.
quote: While real-time determinations of statistical parameters such as sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value are not possible during continuous monitoring, the algorithm’s performance compared to the interpreting radiologist’s final report, where possible, can be used as a surrogate for model accuracy.
hazard: No real-time accuracy signal for deployed AI

statement: Harvest examination metadata including equipment manufacturer, protocol, radiation dose and patient demographics as part of continuous monitoring.
quote: As explained above, harvesting of metadata about the examination should form part of this monitoring, and should include equipment manufacturer, protocol used, radiation dose and patient demographics.
hazard: Inability to attribute performance changes to their causes

statement: Automatically compare NLP-extracted findings from radiologist reports against AI outputs as a background accuracy measure.
quote: Ideally this data collection could occur in the background, comparing information automatically extracted via suitable natural language processing methods against the radiologists’ reports as an AI accuracy measure, and data contained in the DICOM header to monitor the compliance of examination parameters with AI manufacturer specification of input data whenever feasible.
hazard: Labor-intensive monitoring leading to no monitoring

statement: Use DICOM header data to monitor examination parameter compliance with the AI manufacturer's input specifications.
quote: Ideally this data collection could occur in the background, comparing information automatically extracted via suitable natural language processing methods against the radiologists’ reports as an AI accuracy measure, and data contained in the DICOM header to monitor the compliance of examination parameters with AI manufacturer specification of input data whenever feasible.
hazard: Out-of-specification inputs producing unreliable AI outputs

statement: Incorporate patient demographic information from DICOM headers into monitoring data collection.
quote: Limited patient demographic information may also be found in the DICOM header and should be incorporated in the data collection.
hazard: Undetected subgroup performance disparities

statement: Collect expanded patient demographics to support robust bias detection in AI monitoring.
quote: More robust monitoring and bias detection solutions may require expanded patient demographics.
hazard: Bias undetectable due to missing demographic data

statement: Record AI model performance information in a dedicated AI data registry enabling multi-site reports.
quote: Relevant information about AI model performance should be recorded in a dedicated AI data registry that allows generation of reports across multiple sites and geographies.
hazard: Local degradation and drift sources going unidentified

statement: Systematically analyze cases the AI fails to process as a monitoring target.
quote: Systematic analysis of cases that are not processed represent another important monitoring target.
hazard: Silent acquisition or transfer failures preventing AI inference

statement: Share aggregated multi-institution AI performance data with developers to identify performance gaps.
quote: Aggregation of data from multiple institutions using the same AI models could provide information to developers to identify performance gaps that can be addressed in future versions of the algorithm, as well as meeting any future post-market surveillance regulatory requirements.
hazard: Performance gaps persisting across model versions

statement: For autonomous AI, spot-monitor performance by intermittently sampling a predetermined number of cases against ground truth.
quote: Therefore, one could imagine that performance monitoring could include intermittent random sampling of a pre-determined number of cases with ground truth comparison to spot-monitor performance over time.
hazard: Undetected autonomous AI performance decline

statement: Include robust real-time performance monitoring and patient-risk mitigation measures in any AI change control plan.
quote: Any change control plan must include robust real-time AI model performance and measures that mitigate patient risk.
hazard: Harm from unmonitored locally tuned or modified models

statement: Formalize local AI governance oversight and associated processes across the AI lifecycle.
quote: Given the complexity of managing all aspects of the AI lifecycle in clinical environments, provider entities engaging in the use of clinical AI are well served by formalizing local AI governance oversight and associated processes (78).
hazard: Unmanaged lifecycle risks of clinical AI

statement: Establish an orderly process to replace deployed AI products with updates or alternative products.
quote: and an orderly process to replace currently deployed products with future updates or alternative products.
hazard: Disruptive or unsafe product transitions

statement: Orient and train newly arriving users in available AI tools and associated work processes.
quote: As new users arrive in a local practice, they need to be properly assimilated, oriented, and trained in the available AI tools and associated work processes, to become effective participants in this technology-assisted care delivery paradigm.
hazard: Staff turnover leaving untrained AI users

statement: Share responsibility between vendors and local governance leaders for keeping stakeholders competent in AI use.
quote: Ensuring that all local stakeholders are up to date and competent in the use of AI technology is a shared responsibility between vendors and the leaders of local institutional governance and oversight.
hazard: Incompetent or outdated AI use by staff

statement: Identify and manage human-AI biases so AI output does not negatively influence radiologist judgment.
quote: These biases need to be both clarified and managed to ensure the AI’s output does not negatively influence the radiologist’s judgment.
hazard: Automation bias or under-reliance increasing false positives and negatives

statement: Optimize the combined output of radiologist plus AI system rather than AI performance alone.
quote: Ultimately, the output of the combination of radiologist plus the AI system must be optimized.
hazard: Human-AI team performing worse than either alone

statement: Have the interdisciplinary team identify possible types and sources of bias for the AI tool at the design phase.
quote: At the design phase, the interdisciplinary AI development team (see glossary) should identify possible types and sources of bias for their AI tool.
hazard: Unrecognized biases leading to unequal performance across patient groups

statement: Collect individual attributes such as sex, gender, age, ethnicity, risk factors, comorbidities, and disabilities to enable bias identification.
quote: To identify biases and apply measures for increased fairness, relevant attributes of the individuals, such as sex, gender, age, ethnicity, risk factors, comorbidities, or disabilities, should be collected.
hazard: Inability to detect subgroup performance disparities

statement: Subject collection of individual demographic and clinical attributes to informed consent and ethics committee approval.
quote: This should be subject to informed consent and approval by ethics committees to ensure an appropriate balance between the benefits of non-discrimination and the risks of reidentification.
hazard: Patient reidentification and privacy harm from collecting sensitive attributes

statement: Systematically collect dataset metadata including acquisition centre, machine used, and preprocessing and annotation processes.
quote: Furthermore, relevant information about the datasets, such as the centres where they were acquired, the machine used, the preprocessing and annotation processes, should be systematically collected to address technical and human biases.
hazard: Undetected technical and human biases from data acquisition differences

statement: Apply bias detection using fairness metrics such as true positive rates, statistical parity, and equalised odds when attributes are available.
quote: When possible—that is, the individuals’ and data attributes are available—bias detection methods should be applied by using fairness metrics such as true positive rates, statistical parity, group fairness, and equalised odds.
hazard: Deploying tools with undetected subgroup performance disparities

statement: Test bias mitigation measures for identified biases and verify their impact on both fairness and model accuracy.
quote: To correct for any identified biases, mitigation measures should be tested, such as data resampling, bias free representations, and equalised odds postprocessing,36 37 38 39 40 to verify their impact on both the tool’s fairness and the model’s accuracy.
hazard: Persistent bias or accuracy loss from untested corrections

statement: Document and report any remaining bias to inform end users and citizens.
quote: Importantly, any remaining bias should be documented and reported to inform the end users and citizens (see traceability 2).
hazard: Users unaware of residual biases misapplying outputs to affected groups

statement: Specify the clinical settings where the AI tool will be applied, such as primary care, hospitals, home care, or resource levels.
quote: At the design phase, the development team should specify the clinical settings in which the AI tool will be applied (eg, primary healthcare centres, hospitals, home care, low versus high resource settings, one or several countries), and anticipate potential obstacles to universality (eg, differences in end users, clinical definitions, medical equipment or IT infrastructures across settings).
hazard: Using tools in settings they were not designed for

statement: Anticipate cross-setting obstacles such as differences in end users, clinical definitions, equipment, and IT infrastructure.
quote: At the design phase, the development team should specify the clinical settings in which the AI tool will be applied (eg, primary healthcare centres, hospitals, home care, low versus high resource settings, one or several countries), and anticipate potential obstacles to universality (eg, differences in end users, clinical definitions, medical equipment or IT infrastructures across settings).
hazard: Failure to generalize across sites with differing infrastructure or users

statement: Require AI tools to be built on existing community defined standards such as SNOMED CT, OMOP, DICOM, and FHIR.
quote: To ensure the quality and interoperability of the AI tool, it should be developed based on existing community defined standards.
hazard: Poor interoperability and quality from nonstandard definitions and interfaces

statement: Perform technical validation using external datasets distinct from those used for model training.
quote: To assess generalisability, technical validation of the AI tools should be performed with external datasets that are distinct from those used for model training.45
hazard: Overestimated performance that fails to generalize

statement: Conduct clinical evaluation studies at several sites unless the tool is intended for a single centre.
quote: Except for AI tools intended for single centres, the clinical evaluation studies should be performed at several sites to assess performance and interoperability across clinical workflows.46
hazard: Performance and workflow failures across different clinical sites

statement: Apply and test mitigation measures such as transfer learning or domain adaptation when generalisability is limited.
quote: If the tool’s generalisability is limited, mitigation measures (eg, transfer learning or domain adaptation) should be applied and tested.
hazard: Degraded performance in new populations or sites

statement: Evaluate the AI tool's local clinical validity at each deployment site.
quote: Therefore, to ensure trust at each site, the AI tools should be evaluated for their local clinical validity.17
hazard: Poor performance at a site due to local population or workflow differences

statement: Verify that the AI tool fits local clinical workflows and performs well on the local population.
quote: In particular, the AI tool should fit the local clinical workflows and perform well on the local populations.
hazard: Workflow misfit and poor local performance

statement: Recalibrate and retest the AI model, for example by fine tuning, when local performance is decreased.
quote: If the performance is decreased when evaluated locally, recalibration of the AI model should be performed and tested (eg, through model fine tuning).
hazard: Deploying a model with degraded local accuracy

statement: Analyse potential risks throughout the lifecycle, assessing each risk's likelihood, effects, and risk-benefit balance.
quote: Throughout the AI tool’s lifecycle, the multidisciplinary development team shall analyse potential risks, assess each risk’s likelihood, effects and risk-benefit balance, define risk mitigation measures, monitor the risks and mitigations continuously, and maintain a risk management file.
hazard: Unassessed risks causing patient harm

statement: Define risk mitigation measures for each identified AI risk.
quote: Throughout the AI tool’s lifecycle, the multidisciplinary development team shall analyse potential risks, assess each risk’s likelihood, effects and risk-benefit balance, define risk mitigation measures, monitor the risks and mitigations continuously, and maintain a risk management file.
hazard: Known risks left unmitigated

statement: Continuously monitor identified risks and the effectiveness of their mitigations.
quote: Throughout the AI tool’s lifecycle, the multidisciplinary development team shall analyse potential risks, assess each risk’s likelihood, effects and risk-benefit balance, define risk mitigation measures, monitor the risks and mitigations continuously, and maintain a risk management file.
hazard: Emerging risks or failing mitigations going undetected

statement: Maintain a risk management file for the AI tool.
quote: Throughout the AI tool’s lifecycle, the multidisciplinary development team shall analyse potential risks, assess each risk’s likelihood, effects and risk-benefit balance, define risk mitigation measures, monitor the risks and mitigations continuously, and maintain a risk management file.
hazard: Lack of accountability and traceability of risk decisions

statement: Include misuse risks in risk assessment: not following instructions, insufficient training, use outside target population, and use by non-target users.
quote: Other risks to consider include human factors that might lead to misuse of the AI tool (eg, not following the instructions, receiving insufficient training), application of the AI tool to individuals who are not within the target population, use of the tool by others than the target end users (eg, technician instead of physician)
hazard: Harm from misuse, off-label populations, or unqualified users

statement: Use mitigation measures such as user warnings, system shutdown, input reprocessing, or fallback to alternative procedures or human judgment only.
quote: Mitigation measures might include warnings to the users, system shutdown, reprocessing of the input data, the acquisition of new input data, or the use of an alternative procedure or human judgment only.
hazard: Continued reliance on failing AI outputs without a fallback

statement: Monitor and reassess risk using feedback channels such as customer complaints and logged real world performance and issues.
quote: Monitoring and reassessment of risk might involve the use of various feedback channels, such as customer feedback and complaints, as well as logged real world performance and issues (see traceability 5).
hazard: Real world failures and complaints going unaddressed

statement: Provide an AI information leaflet informing citizens and healthcare professionals of the tool's intended use, risks including biases, and instructions for use.
quote: adequate documentation should be created and maintained for the AI tool,48 which might include (a) an AI information leaflet to inform citizens and healthcare professionals about the tool’s intended use, risks (eg, biases) and instructions for use;
hazard: Users unaware of intended use and risks misapplying the tool

statement: Obtain technical documentation covering model properties, training and testing data, evaluation results, biases, limitations, and periodic audits and updates.
quote: (b) a technical document to inform AI developers, health organisations, and regulators about the AI model’s properties (eg, hyperparameters), training and testing data, evaluation criteria and results, biases and other limitations, and periodic audits and updates49 50 51;
hazard: Organizations deploying tools without understanding their limitations

statement: Deploy continuous quality control of AI inputs to flag missing or out-of-range variables, inconsistent formats or units, and incorrect preprocessing.
quote: The AI tool should be developed and deployed with mechanisms for continuous monitoring and quality control of the AI inputs and outputs,47 such as to identify missing or out-of-range input variables, inconsistent data formats or units, incorrect annotations or data preprocessing, and erroneous or implausible AI outputs.
hazard: Erroneous outputs from bad or malformed input data

statement: Deploy continuous quality control of AI outputs to detect erroneous or implausible results.
quote: The AI tool should be developed and deployed with mechanisms for continuous monitoring and quality control of the AI inputs and outputs,47 such as to identify missing or out-of-range input variables, inconsistent data formats or units, incorrect annotations or data preprocessing, and erroneous or implausible AI outputs.
hazard: Implausible AI outputs reaching clinical decisions

statement: Provide calibrated uncertainty estimates with AI outputs to inform end users of confidence in results.
quote: For quality control of the AI decisions, uncertainty estimates should be provided (and calibrated53) to inform the end users about the degree of confidence in the results.54
hazard: Overreliance on low-confidence AI results

statement: Implement a configurable periodic auditing system that defines datasets and timelines for periodic evaluations, e.g., yearly.
quote: The AI tool should be developed and deployed with a configurable system for periodic auditing,47 which should define the datasets and timelines for periodic evaluations (eg, every year).
hazard: Undetected performance degradation over time

statement: Use periodic audits to identify data or concept drift, new biases, performance degradation, and changes in end user decision making.
quote: The periodic auditing should enable the identification of data or concept drifts, newly occurring biases, performance degradation or changes in the decision making of the end users.55
hazard: Drift, emerging bias, or automation effects going unnoticed

statement: Apply necessary updates to AI models or tools based on periodic audit findings.
quote: Accordingly, necessary updates to the AI models or AI tools should be applied.56
hazard: Continued use of degraded or outdated models

statement: Implement a logging system that records AI tool usage.
quote: Implement a logging system for usage recording
hazard: Inability to trace AI use and investigate incidents

statement: Establish mechanisms for AI governance.
quote: Establish mechanisms for AI governance
hazard: Lack of accountability for deployed AI tools

statement: Define intended use and user requirements from an early stage.
quote: Define intended use and user requirements from an early stage
hazard: Tools misaligned with clinical needs or used beyond intended purpose

statement: Establish mechanisms for human-AI interaction and human oversight of the AI tool.
quote: Establish mechanisms for human-AI interactions and oversight
hazard: Unchecked AI errors affecting patient care

statement: Provide training materials and activities such as tutorials and hands-on sessions for end users.
quote: Provide training materials and activities (eg, tutorials, hands-on sessions)
hazard: Misuse from insufficient user training

statement: Evaluate user experience and acceptance with independent end users.
quote: Evaluate user experience and acceptance with independent end users
hazard: Poor usability leading to errors or non-adoption

statement: Evaluate clinical utility and safety, including effectiveness, harm, and cost-benefit, before deployment.
quote: Evaluate clinical utility and safety (eg, effectiveness, harm, cost-benefit)
hazard: Deploying tools that are ineffective or harmful

statement: Evaluate and optimise robustness of the AI tool against real world data variations.
quote: Evaluate and optimise robustness against real world variations
hazard: Failure under real world data variation

statement: Define explainability needs and requirements together with end users.
quote: Define the need and requirements for explainability with end users
hazard: Opaque outputs users cannot interpret or trust

statement: Evaluate explainability with end users, including correctness of explanations and impact on users.
quote: Evaluate explainability with end users (eg, correctness, impact on users)
hazard: Misleading explanations causing incorrect decisions

statement: Engage interdisciplinary stakeholders throughout the AI lifecycle.
quote: Engage interdisciplinary stakeholders throughout the AI lifecycle
hazard: Tools misaligned with needs of patients, clinicians, and organizations

statement: Implement measures for data privacy and security.
quote: Implement measures for data privacy and security
hazard: Data breaches and privacy violations

statement: Define an adequate evaluation plan specifying datasets, metrics, and reference methods.
quote: Define adequate evaluation plan (eg, datasets, metrics, reference methods)
hazard: Inadequate or biased evaluation of AI tools

statement: Identify and comply with applicable AI regulatory requirements.
quote: Identify and comply with applicable AI regulatory requirements
hazard: Legal noncompliance and unsafe deployment

statement: Investigate and address application specific ethical issues of the AI tool.
quote: Investigate and address application specific ethical issues
hazard: Ethical harms specific to the application

statement: Investigate and address social and societal issues raised by the AI tool.
quote: Investigate and address social and societal issues
hazard: Negative societal impacts such as widening inequalities

statement: Educate radiologists and other potential end users about AI principles.
quote: To ensure safe operation of AI models in Radiology, it is essential to educate radiologists and other potential end-users about the principles of AI and teach them the limits and potential risks when using AI models (15, 16).
hazard: Unsafe use caused by inadequate understanding of AI.

statement: Teach end users the limitations of AI models.
quote: To ensure safe operation of AI models in Radiology, it is essential to educate radiologists and other potential end-users about the principles of AI and teach them the limits and potential risks when using AI models (15, 16).
hazard: Reliance on AI beyond its capabilities.

statement: Teach end users the potential risks of using AI models.
quote: To ensure safe operation of AI models in Radiology, it is essential to educate radiologists and other potential end-users about the principles of AI and teach them the limits and potential risks when using AI models (15, 16).
hazard: Unrecognized AI-related patient safety risks.

statement: Evaluate AI accuracy on the target population before introducing the model into clinical practice.
quote: It is also important to evaluate the accuracy of AI models on the target population before introducing them into clinical practice, and after that introduction, their performance should be monitored to detect drifts in accuracy.
hazard: Deployment of models that perform inadequately in the intended patient population.

statement: Monitor AI performance after clinical introduction to detect accuracy drift.
quote: It is also important to evaluate the accuracy of AI models on the target population before introducing them into clinical practice, and after that introduction, their performance should be monitored to detect drifts in accuracy.
hazard: Undetected deterioration in AI accuracy.

statement: Limit the number and complexity of AI interfaces presented to radiologists.
quote: In this context, attention should be paid to the interface design. Exposing radiologists to an increasing number of complex interfaces is undesirable, and is liable to diminish utility and acceptance of AI tools (18).
hazard: Interface burden that reduces AI utility and user acceptance.

statement: Distribute the benefits and harms of radiology AI fairly among stakeholders.
quote: AI in radiology should promote well-being, minimize harm, and ensure that the benefits and harms are distributed among stakeholders in a just manner.
hazard: Inequitable distribution of AI benefits and harms.

statement: Design AI systems for dependability.
quote: It should be designed for maximum transparency and dependability.
hazard: Unreliable AI operation in clinical practice.

statement: Keep ultimate responsibility and accountability for AI with its human designers and operators.
quote: Ultimate responsibility and accountability for AI remains with its human designers and operators.
hazard: Accountability gaps when AI causes harm.

statement: Develop AI codes of ethics and practice that prioritize patients and the common good.
quote: The radiology community should develop codes of ethics and practice for AI that promote any use that helps patients and the common good, and block use of radiology data and algorithms for financial gain without those two attributes.
hazard: AI deployment driven by interests that do not benefit patients or the public.

statement: Block use of radiology data and algorithms for financial gain when it does not help patients and the common good.
quote: The radiology community should develop codes of ethics and practice for AI that promote any use that helps patients and the common good, and block use of radiology data and algorithms for financial gain without those two attributes.
hazard: Commercial exploitation of radiology data or algorithms without patient and public benefit.

statement: Conduct research on how best to deploy AI in clinical practice.
quote: There is a need for extensive research to understand how to best deploy AI in clinical practice.
hazard: Deployment approaches unsupported by clinical implementation evidence.

statement: Maintain patient privacy when using patient data for AI.
quote: Ensuring that this data is used ethically involves maintaining patient privacy, obtaining informed consent for data use, and ensuring data security.
hazard: Exposure or misuse of private patient information.

statement: Obtain informed consent for patient-data use in AI.
quote: Ensuring that this data is used ethically involves maintaining patient privacy, obtaining informed consent for data use, and ensuring data security.
hazard: Use of patient data without informed authorization.

statement: Ensure the security of patient data used by AI systems.
quote: Ensuring that this data is used ethically involves maintaining patient privacy, obtaining informed consent for data use, and ensuring data security.
hazard: Unauthorized access to or compromise of patient data.

statement: Consider whether patient-data anonymity is maintained when making AI data-use decisions.
quote: The anonymity of patient data is also an important but complex consideration and, if not maintained, is another source of risk.
hazard: Identification of patients through AI-related data use.

statement: Consider discrimination, insurance costs, humiliation, and other potential harms when making data-related decisions.
quote: Potential harms, such as discrimination, insurance costs and humiliation, must be considered when data-related decisions are made.
hazard: Discrimination, financial harm, or humiliation resulting from patient-data use.

statement: Increase performance assessment for autonomous AI systems and systems that continue learning or adapting during use.
quote: Risks to patient safety will also be higher when autonomous AI systems are implemented or the AI system continues to learn and adapt over time. In these situations, the need for assessment and monitoring of AI system performance becomes commensurately greater.
hazard: Insufficient evaluation of higher-risk autonomous or adapting AI.

statement: Increase performance monitoring for autonomous AI systems and systems that continue learning or adapting during use.
quote: Risks to patient safety will also be higher when autonomous AI systems are implemented or the AI system continues to learn and adapt over time. In these situations, the need for assessment and monitoring of AI system performance becomes commensurately greater.
hazard: Undetected unsafe behavior in autonomous or continually adapting AI.

statement: Provide deployers with clear information about AI capabilities and limitations.
quote: Transparency requires provision of clear information about an AI system’s capabilities and limitations, in particular the purpose for which the systems are intended, the conditions under which they can be expected to function as intended and the expected level of accuracy in achieving the specified purpose.
hazard: Misuse or overreliance caused by misunderstanding AI capabilities and limitations.

statement: Disclose the intended purpose of each AI system.
quote: Transparency requires provision of clear information about an AI system’s capabilities and limitations, in particular the purpose for which the systems are intended, the conditions under which they can be expected to function as intended and the expected level of accuracy in achieving the specified purpose.
hazard: Use of AI for purposes outside its intended scope.

statement: Disclose the conditions under which an AI system can be expected to function as intended.
quote: Transparency requires provision of clear information about an AI system’s capabilities and limitations, in particular the purpose for which the systems are intended, the conditions under which they can be expected to function as intended and the expected level of accuracy in achieving the specified purpose.
hazard: Deployment under conditions where AI performance is unreliable.

statement: Disclose an AI system’s expected accuracy for its specified purpose.
quote: Transparency requires provision of clear information about an AI system’s capabilities and limitations, in particular the purpose for which the systems are intended, the conditions under which they can be expected to function as intended and the expected level of accuracy in achieving the specified purpose.
hazard: Unrealistic expectations of AI accuracy.

statement: Make patients aware when AI systems are being used.
quote: The concept of transparency should also extend to patients being made aware if AI systems are being used.
hazard: Undisclosed AI involvement that undermines patient autonomy and trust.

statement: Provide patients and medical professionals with information about how AI decisions are made.
quote: Although difficult to achieve with some deep learning systems, provision of information about how decisions are made results in greater comprehensibility and trust amongst patients and medical professionals.
hazard: Poor understanding of AI decisions and reduced trust.

statement: Balance AI transparency, interpretability, and explainability against privacy, proprietary-information, and malicious-attack risks.
quote: Opinions differ, but the need for transparency, interpretability and explainability should be balanced against potential harm relating to loss of privacy, loss of proprietary information and malicious attacks.
hazard: Privacy breaches, proprietary-information exposure, or attacks enabled by excessive disclosure.

statement: Plan AI integration into clinical workflows during implementation.
quote: In order to achieve optimal performance and patient safety, consideration must be given to successful integration of AI systems into workflow and with other technology, and education of those using such systems.
hazard: Workflow incompatibility that compromises AI performance or patient safety.

statement: Consider integration with existing technology when implementing AI systems.
quote: In order to achieve optimal performance and patient safety, consideration must be given to successful integration of AI systems into workflow and with other technology, and education of those using such systems.
hazard: Technical integration failures that impair safe clinical operation.

statement: Include user education in AI implementation planning.
quote: In order to achieve optimal performance and patient safety, consideration must be given to successful integration of AI systems into workflow and with other technology, and education of those using such systems.
hazard: Implementation without adequate preparation of AI users.

statement: Develop AI ethical guidelines collaboratively with clinicians, patients, AI developers, and ethicists.
quote: Addressing ethical issues in AI will require a combination of technical solutions, government activity, regulatory oversight, and ethical guidelines developed in collaboration with a wide range of stakeholders, including clinicians, patients, AI developers, and ethicists.
hazard: Ethical guidelines that overlook patient perspectives or relevant stakeholder expertise.

statement: Develop AI products that improve the quality or efficiency of existing clinical workflows.
quote: New products should improve the quality or efficiency of existing workflows in terms of lesion detection, segmentation, diagnosis, or prediction of clinical outcomes.
hazard: Introduction of AI products without meaningful workflow benefit.

statement: Target unmet clinical needs rather than allowing available technology and datasets to determine the AI product.
quote: New products should target unmet clinical needs rather than focus on existing technology and datasets.
hazard: Development of technically feasible AI products without clinical utility.

statement: Use society-developed use-case resources to assess whether proposed AI technology meets genuine clinical needs.
quote: Society-developed resources, such as the ACR DSI Define-AI directory, often serve as a good starting place to ensure the technology being developed meets genuine clinical needs (30).
hazard: Selection of AI applications disconnected from genuine clinical needs.

statement: Involve clinicians early when designing AI without an existing use-case reference or direct predecessor, before substantial investment.
quote: In the absence of an existing Use Case reference, or an application that is not a direct derivative evolution of an existing application, developers should involve clinicians as early as possible in the design and development process to gain insights into the feasibility and practicality of proposals, well before substantial investments in time and developer resources have been made.
hazard: Investment in AI proposals that are clinically impractical or infeasible.

statement: Determine baseline clinical performance when open competition data are unavailable for evaluating a proposed AI solution.
quote: In situations where no such open data exist, developers should determine the baseline clinical performance, and compare the AI performance with existing or approved software, or radiologist multi-reader control data.
hazard: AI performance claims without an appropriate clinical baseline.

statement: Compare AI performance with existing or approved software or radiologist multi-reader controls when open competition data are unavailable.
quote: In situations where no such open data exist, developers should determine the baseline clinical performance, and compare the AI performance with existing or approved software, or radiologist multi-reader control data.
hazard: Deployment without evidence of performance relative to existing clinical tools.

statement: Use well-designed multi-reader diagnostic accuracy studies to evaluate claims of AI superiority.
quote: Well-designed multi-reader diagnostic accuracy studies are a common method of reporting AI solution superiority, though they can be both difficult and expensive to perform effectively.
hazard: Unsupported claims that AI improves diagnostic performance.

statement: Account for first-reader, concurrent-reader, second-reader, or triage use when analyzing AI-assisted reader performance.
quote: When human readers are assisted by AI, different modes of algorithm use, such as first-reader, concurrent reader, second-reader, or triage modes, may affect how relative performance is analyzed (33).
hazard: Performance estimates that do not reflect the intended AI reading workflow.

statement: Combine visualizations with generated text to improve the interpretability of AI diagnoses.
quote: There has been much comment about the black box nature of AI models, with early efforts focused on heat map and saliency visualizations; some researchers have called for a combination of visualizations and generated text to improve interpretability of diagnoses (35–37).
hazard: Poor interpretability of AI diagnostic outputs.

statement: Use external or multicentre test data to establish generalizability when model transparency and explainability are poor.
quote: in situations where model transparency and explainability are poor, a higher standard of empirical evidence of performance may be required, including external or multi-centre test data to prove model generalizability, and prospective real-world evaluation, used in clinical settings that most resemble the clinical setting in which the product is most likely to be deployed.
hazard: Unrecognized lack of generalizability in opaque AI models.

statement: Prospectively evaluate poorly explainable AI in real-world clinical settings resembling the intended deployment setting.
quote: in situations where model transparency and explainability are poor, a higher standard of empirical evidence of performance may be required, including external or multi-centre test data to prove model generalizability, and prospective real-world evaluation, used in clinical settings that most resemble the clinical setting in which the product is most likely to be deployed.
hazard: Failure of opaque AI models under actual deployment conditions.

statement: Report AI evaluation studies according to established scientific reporting standards.
quote: Regulators should pay close attention to ensure that the reported information complies with the highest standards of practice; studies should ideally adhere to criteria defined by the multiple established scientific reporting standards (39–43).
hazard: Incomplete study reporting that prevents reliable assessment of AI evidence.

statement: Report a range of expected AI performance rather than only a single summary accuracy figure.
quote: Two common errors in solution performance reporting include a failure to report a range of expected performance—lower quality solutions often report a single summary accuracy figure—and not reporting specific failure conditions and errors, with lower quality solutions selectively highlighting the best diagnoses made by their systems.
hazard: Misleading certainty about AI accuracy.

statement: Report specific AI failure conditions and errors rather than selectively highlighting successful diagnoses.
quote: Two common errors in solution performance reporting include a failure to report a range of expected performance—lower quality solutions often report a single summary accuracy figure—and not reporting specific failure conditions and errors, with lower quality solutions selectively highlighting the best diagnoses made by their systems.
hazard: Hidden failure modes and inflated perceptions of diagnostic reliability.

statement: Document in-depth analyses of AI limitations, errors, and biases in model cards or system cards.
quote: In the broader AI safety community, there is a strong embrace of Model Cards or System Cards, in which in-depth analyses of limitations, errors, and biases are explicitly reported, often entirely separate from the primary report of system performance (44, 45).
hazard: Undocumented model limitations, errors, and biases.

statement: Retain human co-supervision of clinical imaging AI decisions, including declarations of stability or normality.
quote: The patient implications of decision making required in clinical medical imaging, even declarations of stability or normality, often have dramatic direct implications on patient care, which we suspect will require human co-supervision for some time.
hazard: Unsupervised AI decisions that adversely affect patient care.

statement: Establish an explicit post-market quality assurance plan for each AI solution.
quote: Regulators should be particularly attuned to ensuring that solutions have an explicit post-market quality assurance plan.
hazard: Post-deployment performance changes without planned quality assurance.

statement: Monitor month-to-month diagnostic event frequencies for major deviations.
quote: In practice, what this may entail is prospective performance monitoring of the AI model, for example monitoring for major deviations in month-to-month diagnostic event frequencies, with alerts raised when normal bounds are exceeded
hazard: Undetected shifts in diagnostic output patterns.

statement: Raise alerts when monitored diagnostic event frequencies exceed normal bounds.
quote: In practice, what this may entail is prospective performance monitoring of the AI model, for example monitoring for major deviations in month-to-month diagnostic event frequencies, with alerts raised when normal bounds are exceeded
hazard: Delayed recognition of potentially unsafe changes in AI diagnostic behavior.

statement: Routinely evaluate AI on a fixed held-out control set to detect deviations on known difficult or borderline cases.
quote: a control sample approach where a constant reserved held-out set of test case examples is routinely evaluated with the algorithm, to ensure no major deviations on known difficult or borderline cases (50).
hazard: Undetected performance regression on difficult or borderline cases.

statement: Establish a clear procedure for reporting unexpected AI errors to the vendor.
quote: At a very minimum, a clear reporting procedure for unexpected errors to the vendor, with named responsible contact personnel, should be established and made easily accessible to clinical end users.
hazard: Unexpected AI errors remaining unreported to the vendor.

statement: Name responsible contacts for reporting unexpected AI errors.
quote: At a very minimum, a clear reporting procedure for unexpected errors to the vendor, with named responsible contact personnel, should be established and made easily accessible to clinical end users.
hazard: Error reports lacking an identifiable responsible recipient.

statement: Make the AI error-reporting procedure easily accessible to clinical end users.
quote: At a very minimum, a clear reporting procedure for unexpected errors to the vendor, with named responsible contact personnel, should be established and made easily accessible to clinical end users.
hazard: Underreporting of AI errors because reporting procedures are difficult to access.

statement: Determine the intended use of an AI tool before purchase.
quote: What is the intended use of the AI, who will most benefit from its use, which risks are associated with its use and what is the potential economic impact?
hazard: Procurement without a clearly defined deployment purpose.

statement: Plan how to verify vendors’ commercial claims before implementing an AI tool.
quote: How will the AI tool be integrated into the institutions’ workflows and how can the commercial claims be verified and monitored?
hazard: Procurement based on unverified vendor claims.

statement: Plan ongoing monitoring of whether an AI tool delivers its claimed commercial benefits.
quote: How will the AI tool be integrated into the institutions’ workflows and how can the commercial claims be verified and monitored?
hazard: Continued use of AI that does not deliver its claimed benefits.

statement: Consider psychological effects of human–AI interaction when planning deployment.
quote: How do users need to be trained and which psychological effects need to be considered with regard to human-AI-interaction?
hazard: Unsafe human reliance on or rejection of AI assistance.

statement: Determine whether AI accuracy on local data is sufficient for institutional use.
quote: Is the FDA (or other agency) approval/clearance data reflective of accuracy on local data? Is that accuracy on local data sufficient for use in that institution and will users accept and hence engage with the AI results?
hazard: Local deployment despite inadequate accuracy.

statement: Assess whether intended users will accept and engage with AI results.
quote: Is that accuracy on local data sufficient for use in that institution and will users accept and hence engage with the AI results?
hazard: Implementation failure because users do not engage with AI outputs.

statement: Identify areas of clinical practice needing improvement before selecting AI tools.
quote: For any AI tool to be successfully integrated into clinical practice, stakeholders should first clearly identify areas that need improvement and define relevant key performance indicators (52, 53).
hazard: AI procurement that does not address institutional priorities.

statement: Define relevant key performance indicators for the proposed AI integration.
quote: For any AI tool to be successfully integrated into clinical practice, stakeholders should first clearly identify areas that need improvement and define relevant key performance indicators (52, 53).
hazard: Inability to evaluate whether AI integration improves clinical practice.

statement: Integrate AI deployment into a broader strategy for achieving institutional goals.
quote: The integration of an AI tool may then be part of a larger strategy devised to attain the goal set for the institution.
hazard: Isolated AI implementation disconnected from institutional improvement goals.

statement: Confirm that the proposed AI tool solves a real, specific institutional problem.
quote: In either case, as outlined in Section 4A, it is essential to determine whether or not the tool solves a real, specific problem that the institution has; tools are solutions, and a solution to a non-existent problem has no value.
hazard: Purchasing AI with no relevant institutional use case.

statement: Set objective, quantifiable goals for the intended impact of an AI tool.
quote: For the positive impact of an AI tool to be measurable, objective and quantifiable goals should be set.
hazard: Unverifiable claims of benefit after AI implementation.

statement: Estimate the proportion of cases or patients expected to be affected by the AI tool.
quote: It may be useful to consider both what proportion of cases or patients an AI tool is expected to impact, and what the magnitude of impact on each case or patient is expected to be.
hazard: Overestimation of the population-level reach of AI benefits.

statement: Estimate the expected magnitude of AI impact on each affected case or patient.
quote: It may be useful to consider both what proportion of cases or patients an AI tool is expected to impact, and what the magnitude of impact on each case or patient is expected to be.
hazard: Overestimation of the benefit delivered to individual patients.

statement: Consider AI beneficiaries beyond the radiology department, including patients, the institution, and wider society.
quote: Purchasers should be aware that the beneficiary of the AI tools’ potential for improvement does not always need to be the radiologist or the radiology department alone. Ideally, all stakeholders involved, from the patient requiring a service to the respective institution and even the wider society could benefit from AI being successfully implemented in a clinical workflow.
hazard: Procurement decisions that overlook benefits or consequences outside radiology.

statement: Weigh expected AI benefits against immediate, medium-term, and long-term economic impacts in the local healthcare setting.
quote: Depending on the local circumstances and healthcare system in place, such potential benefits need to be carefully weighed against their immediate and mid- or long-term economic impact.
hazard: Economically unsustainable AI implementation.

statement: Conduct a return-on-investment analysis before planned AI integration.
quote: Return on investment (RoI) and cost–benefit analyses should be planned and carried out to ensure the viability of the planned AI integration.
hazard: AI investment without evidence of financial viability.

statement: Conduct a cost–benefit analysis before planned AI integration.
quote: Return on investment (RoI) and cost–benefit analyses should be planned and carried out to ensure the viability of the planned AI integration.
hazard: AI costs exceeding the value of expected benefits.

statement: Establish a viable payment mechanism for AI use when relevant to the healthcare system.
quote: Depending on the healthcare system, establishment of a viable payment mechanism for AI use may be critical.
hazard: Inability to sustain AI use because payment arrangements are inadequate.

statement: Include both capital and recurrent AI costs in purchase analyses.
quote: Lastly, potential costs (both capital and recurrent) and risks associated with the implementation and usage of an AI system are essential components of any purchase analysis and decision.
hazard: Underbudgeting for implementation and ongoing AI operation.

statement: Assess risks associated with AI implementation and use before making a purchase decision.
quote: Lastly, potential costs (both capital and recurrent) and risks associated with the implementation and usage of an AI system are essential components of any purchase analysis and decision.
hazard: Procurement without understanding deployment and operational risks.

statement: Consult the vendor’s regulatory risk matrix and risk–benefit analysis when assessing AI risks.
quote: In part, risk assessment can be facilitated by consulting the risk matrix and the risk–benefit analysis provided in the regulatory files by vendors.
hazard: Failure to consider documented product risks during procurement.

statement: Include contracting, integration, training, infrastructure, maintenance, and monitoring in AI ownership-cost estimates.
quote: Other sources of cost include contracting and legal agreements, IT effort and professional services for integration with existing systems, training for users and administrators, infrastructure for running the AI, and on-going maintenance and monitoring.
hazard: Underestimation of AI ownership costs beyond licensing fees.

statement: Evaluate the AI vendor’s compatibility as a reliable institutional partner.
quote: Other essential factors in making an informed decision include evaluating the vendor’s compatibility as a reliable partner, the vendor’s staying power in a competitive environment with limited payor reimbursement (even more important in this era of AI vendor consolidation), optimized model pricing, and opportunities for collaboration beyond product purchase, such as co-development and product resale.
hazard: Dependence on an incompatible or unreliable AI supplier.

statement: Evaluate the AI vendor’s staying power in its competitive and reimbursement environment.
quote: Other essential factors in making an informed decision include evaluating the vendor’s compatibility as a reliable partner, the vendor’s staying power in a competitive environment with limited payor reimbursement (even more important in this era of AI vendor consolidation), optimized model pricing, and opportunities for collaboration beyond product purchase, such as co-development and product resale.
hazard: Loss of product support or continuity because the vendor cannot remain viable.

statement: Evaluate opportunities to optimize AI model pricing before purchase.
quote: Other essential factors in making an informed decision include evaluating the vendor’s compatibility as a reliable partner, the vendor’s staying power in a competitive environment with limited payor reimbursement (even more important in this era of AI vendor consolidation), optimized model pricing, and opportunities for collaboration beyond product purchase, such as co-development and product resale.
hazard: Avoidable procurement costs that undermine implementation viability.

statement: Evaluate opportunities for vendor collaboration beyond purchase, such as co-development or product resale.
quote: Other essential factors in making an informed decision include evaluating the vendor’s compatibility as a reliable partner, the vendor’s staying power in a competitive environment with limited payor reimbursement (even more important in this era of AI vendor consolidation), optimized model pricing, and opportunities for collaboration beyond product purchase, such as co-development and product resale.
hazard: Incomplete assessment of potential vendor partnership value.

statement: Perform a statistically rigorous evaluation of AI performance on the implementing site’s own local data.
quote: Ideally, each site considering implementation would perform a statistically rigorous evaluation of performance on their own local data (a method for this evaluation is presented in the Clinical Evaluation Section below).
hazard: Local performance failures masked by results from other settings.

statement: Compare local data characteristics with the data used to test the AI model, at minimum.
quote: At a minimum, the characteristics of local data should be compared with those of the test data (a typical example might be where a model has been tested only on one manufacturer’s MRI scanner, but will be used on a scanner made by a different manufacturer).
hazard: Unrecognized mismatch between local inputs and model test conditions.

statement: Proceed with great caution, or avoid deployment, when local data differ from the AI model’s test data.
quote: Where these are similar, the reported performance metrics may be relied upon with some confidence; where they are not (e.g., an algorithm tested only on adults being considered for off-label use in a pediatric hospital) one should proceed with great caution, if at all.
hazard: Unsafe extrapolation of AI performance to untested populations or conditions.

statement: Include expected algorithmic error frequency in AI risk assessments.
quote: The consideration together of error frequency, detectability, correctability and impact provides a framework for assessing the direct risk of algorithmic errors.
hazard: Risk estimates that ignore how often AI errors occur.

statement: Assess the probability that workflow participants will detect each anticipated AI error.
quote: One should consider the detectability of the errors that are anticipated. That is, for each error, what is the probability that people in the workflow will notice that the AI has produced an erroneous output?
hazard: AI errors escaping detection within the clinical workflow.

statement: Assess the probability that each detected AI error will be corrected.
quote: For each detected error, what is the probability that the error will be corrected?
hazard: Detected AI errors remaining uncorrected.

statement: Assess the expected impact of undetected or uncorrected AI errors on patients and other stakeholders.
quote: Finally, if an error is not detected or not corrected, what is the expected impact on patients or other stakeholders?
hazard: Underestimation of harm from errors that reach patients or other stakeholders.

statement: Evaluate the AI tool’s impact on radiologist performance as part of risk assessment.
quote: Another key component of risk is the impact of an AI tool on radiologist performance.
hazard: AI assistance that degrades radiologist performance.

statement: Evaluate AI tool robustness under real-world variations such as test-retest and multivendor datasets before deployment.
quote: Evaluate robustness under real world variations
hazard: Performance degradation under real-world data variation such as different scanners or vendors

statement: Evaluate AI tool robustness under simulated variations such as synthetic noise and artefacts.
quote: Evaluate robustness under simulated variations
hazard: Unrecognized fragility to noise, artefacts, or input perturbations

statement: Evaluate AI tool robustness against variations in end users, such as different technicians or annotators.
quote: Evaluate robustness against variations in end users
hazard: Inconsistent performance depending on which operator uses the tool

statement: Assess whether AI explanations are clinically meaningful through expert panel review and alignment with clinical guidelines.
quote: Assess if explanations are clinically meaningful
hazard: Explanations that point to shortcuts or are clinically meaningless

statement: Assess AI explainability quantitatively using objective measures such as fidelity, consistency, and completeness.
quote: Assess explainability quantitatively using objective measures
hazard: Unfaithful or inconsistent explanations misleading users
