hazard: Residual bias remaining unrecorded and unavailable for oversight.

statement: Inform end users and citizens about any remaining AI bias.
quote: Importantly, any remaining bias should be documented and reported to inform the end users and citizens (see traceability 2).
hazard: Users relying on AI without awareness of unequal performance.

statement: Provide AI driven medical care equally to all citizens.
quote: AI driven medical care should be provided equally for all citizens.
hazard: Inequitable access to AI supported medical care.

statement: Specify the clinical settings in which the AI tool will be used during the design phase.
quote: At the design phase, the development team should specify the clinical settings in which the AI tool will be applied (eg, primary healthcare centres, hospitals, home care, low versus high resource settings, one or several countries), and anticipate potential obstacles to universality (eg, differences in end users, clinical definitions, medical equipment or IT infrastructures across settings).
hazard: Deployment in settings outside the tool’s intended scope.

statement: Anticipate cross-setting barriers involving users, clinical definitions, equipment, and IT infrastructure during AI design.
quote: At the design phase, the development team should specify the clinical settings in which the AI tool will be applied (eg, primary healthcare centres, hospitals, home care, low versus high resource settings, one or several countries), and anticipate potential obstacles to universality (eg, differences in end users, clinical definitions, medical equipment or IT infrastructures across settings).
hazard: Failure to transfer safely between clinical environments.

statement: Use existing community defined standards when developing the AI tool.
quote: To ensure the quality and interoperability of the AI tool, it should be developed based on existing community defined standards.
hazard: Inconsistent clinical definitions and incompatible data or system interfaces.

statement: Validate AI generalisability using external datasets distinct from the model’s training data.
quote: To assess generalisability, technical validation of the AI tools should be performed with external datasets that are distinct from those used for model training.45
hazard: Overestimated performance that does not generalise beyond development data.

statement: Consider reference or benchmarking datasets that approximate expected real world variations when assessing generalisability.
quote: These might include reference or benchmarking datasets that are representative for the task in question (ie, approximating the expected real world variations).
hazard: Validation results that fail to reflect real world conditions.

statement: Evaluate AI performance and workflow interoperability across multiple sites unless the tool is intended for a single centre.
quote: Except for AI tools intended for single centres, the clinical evaluation studies should be performed at several sites to assess performance and interoperability across clinical workflows.46
hazard: Site-specific failures hidden by single-centre evaluation.

statement: Apply mitigation measures when the AI tool’s generalisability is limited.
quote: If the tool’s generalisability is limited, mitigation measures (eg, transfer learning or domain adaptation) should be applied and tested.
hazard: Continued use despite inadequate generalisability.

statement: Test measures introduced to improve limited AI generalisability.
quote: If the tool’s generalisability is limited, mitigation measures (eg, transfer learning or domain adaptation) should be applied and tested.
hazard: Unverified adaptations failing to improve performance in new settings.

statement: Evaluate AI performance on the local patient population at each deployment site.
quote: Therefore, to ensure trust at each site, the AI tools should be evaluated for their local clinical validity.17 In particular, the AI tool should fit the local clinical workflows and perform well on the local populations.
hazard: Poor performance on patients who differ from evaluation populations.

statement: Evaluate whether the AI tool fits local clinical workflows.
quote: Therefore, to ensure trust at each site, the AI tools should be evaluated for their local clinical validity.17 In particular, the AI tool should fit the local clinical workflows and perform well on the local populations.

statement: Explicitly cover autonomous actions in the permissible and non-permissible use list for agentic solutions.

statement: Extend responsible AI principles to mandate transparency of the reasoning trace within an agent's autonomous decision space.
quote: RAI principles should extend to the agent's autonomous decision space (e.g., transparency of the agent's reasoning trace, the scope of tool access, and the reversibility of actions).
hazard: Opaque agentic decision-making obscuring the causes of errors or biased actions.

statement: Monitor agentic solutions for action drift, tracking the specific types of actions the agent takes.
quote: Monitoring must extend beyond model output drift to action drift (e.g., the actions the agent takes, tool-call success / failure rates, hallucinated tool invocations, and unexpected action sequences).
hazard: Unnoticed deviation in the types of actions an autonomous agent executes.

statement: Monitor tool-call success and failure rates to detect action drift in agentic solutions.
quote: Monitoring must extend beyond model output drift to action drift (e.g., the actions the agent takes, tool-call success / failure rates, hallucinated tool invocations, and unexpected action sequences).
hazard: Failing to detect malfunctioning or degraded tools used by autonomous agents.

statement: Monitor agentic solutions for hallucinated tool invocations and unexpected action sequences.
quote: Monitoring must extend beyond model output drift to action drift (e.g., the actions the agent takes, tool-call success / failure rates, hallucinated tool invocations, and unexpected action sequences).
hazard: Agents attempting to use non-existent tools or executing harmful, illogical sequences.

statement: Utilize run traces and replay logs as key monitoring artifacts for auditing agentic solutions.

hazard: Inability to audit or debug unexpected autonomous actions.

statement: Monitor for automation bias and overreliance indicators specifically when deploying agents that can act autonomously.

statement: Train intended users to interpret an agent's proposed action plan.

statement: Train intended users to verify an agent's proposed action plan.
quote: Training should cover how to interpret and verify an agent's proposed action plan, where humans can/should intervene, and how to safely abort or roll back agent actions.

statement: Train intended users to identify where humans can or should intervene in agent actions.
quote: Training should cover how to interpret and verify an agent's proposed action plan, where humans can/should intervene, and how to safely abort or roll back agent actions.
hazard: Missed opportunities for human intervention before harmful autonomous actions.

statement: Train intended users to safely abort agent actions.
quote: Training should cover how to interpret and verify an agent's proposed action plan, where humans can/should intervene, and how to safely abort or roll back agent actions.
hazard: Continuation of harmful agent actions because users cannot safely stop them.

statement: Train intended users to safely roll back agent actions.
quote: Training should cover how to interpret and verify an agent's proposed action plan, where humans can/should intervene, and how to safely abort or roll back agent actions.
hazard: Persistent harm from agent actions that users cannot safely reverse.

statement: Educate intended users on the difference between recommendation-only AI and action-taking AI.
quote: Intended users need explicit education on the difference between recommendation-only AI and action-taking AI, and on the boundaries of the agent's tool access.

statement: Educate intended users on the boundaries of an agent's tool access.

statement: Establish processes for model recalibration when the patient population changes.

statement: Consider the level of an agent's decision-making authority when categorizing its risks.
quote: Within these domains, organizations should also consider risk modifiers such as level of agent decision-making authority, scope creep potential, and the presence/quality of defined stop conditions.

statement: Include the difficulty of reversing an agent's actions as a risk domain.
quote: These may include: Autonomy: The level of independent decision-making authority granted to the agent. Irreversibility: The difficulty or impossibility of reversing actions an agent has taken. Agent-to-Agent: Risks arising from interactions or hand-offs between multiple AI agents.
hazard: Underestimated harm from agent actions that are difficult or impossible to reverse.

statement: Include risks from interactions or hand-offs between AI agents in risk categorization.
quote: These may include: Autonomy: The level of independent decision-making authority granted to the agent. Irreversibility: The difficulty or impossibility of reversing actions an agent has taken. Agent-to-Agent: Risks arising from interactions or hand-offs between multiple AI agents.

statement: Consider an agent's potential for scope creep when categorizing its risks.
quote: Within these domains, organizations should also consider risk modifiers such as level of agent decision-making authority, scope creep potential, and the presence/quality of defined stop conditions.
hazard: Agent activity expanding beyond its intended scope without appropriate oversight.

statement: Assess the adequacy of defined agent stop conditions, including whether they exist, when categorizing risks.
quote: Within these domains, organizations should also consider risk modifiers such as level of agent decision-making authority, scope creep potential, and the presence/quality of defined stop conditions.
hazard: Uncontrolled continuation of agent actions because stop conditions are absent or inadequate.

statement: Adjust claims-based risk outputs using local social determinants of health through a rule-based algorithm.

hazard: Utilization-based predictions underestimate care needs in disadvantaged populations.

statement: Send care-management teams a weekly roster of high-risk patients identified at enrollment or re-determination.

statement: Prioritize care-management outreach using risk predictions together with program eligibility criteria.

hazard: Outreach fails to reach patients with elevated risk and relevant program eligibility.

statement: Prioritize care-management resource allocation using risk predictions together with program eligibility criteria.
quote: Each care management program will receive a list of high and moderate risk members in accordance with model predictions and other eligibility criteria (e.g. specific diagnosis required, disability status, etc.) and will use this list to prioritize resource allocation and outreach to members for further evaluation to determine final eligibility for specialty care management program enrollment.
hazard: Limited care-management resources are allocated without considering patient risk and eligibility.

statement: Begin further care-management evaluation with a review of the patient's profile.
quote: enhanced care management program to conduct further evaluation, beginning first with review of patient profile.
hazard: Risk classifications substitute for assessment of individual care-coordination needs.

statement: Interview high-risk members to assess eligibility for enhanced care-management services.
quote: Upon contact with members, enhanced care management staff conduct additional interviews to determine if a high-risk individual is eligible for services based on a rule-based decision tree.
hazard: High predicted utilization is mistaken for a confirmed need for enhanced care management.

statement: Apply a rule-based decision tree when determining enhanced care-management eligibility after risk-model screening.
quote: Upon contact with members, enhanced care management staff conduct additional interviews to determine if a high-risk individual is eligible for services based on a rule-based decision tree.
hazard: Care-management enrollment decisions rely solely on predicted risk rather than eligibility criteria.

statement: Deidentify patient, medical claims, and pharmacy claims data used in the care-management risk-model workflow.
quote: Patient data, medical, and pharmacy claims data must be deidentified and automatically flow from claims data storage.
hazard: Identifiable patient information is unnecessarily exposed during claims-based risk prediction.

statement: Automate the flow of patient and claims data from claims storage into the care-management risk-model workflow.
quote: Patient data, medical, and pharmacy claims data must be deidentified and automatically flow from claims data storage.

statement: Require one to two years of available data before generating future care-management risk predictions.

statement: Generate member-level predictions and update care-management risk categories monthly.
quote: 3. Model produces member-level output for predicted values and stratifies members into risk categories (monthly).

statement: Use probability cut-offs to assign patients to high-, moderate-, and low-risk care-management groups.

statement: Contact moderate-risk members next in the care-management outreach prioritization sequence.
quote: 7. Moderate-risk members are contacted next in prioritization order.

statement: Assign the claims-based high-risk category to the top 5% of individuals when prioritizing limited care-coordination resources.

statement: Re-tune the claims-based care-management model to the local patient sample.
quote: The model must be re-tuned to the local sample to avoid errors and inconsistencies in performance.
hazard: Population differences cause prediction errors and inconsistent local performance.

statement: Reevaluate the care-management algorithm when changing its use context or target population beyond the intended or initially evaluated use.

statement: Evaluate whether ambiguity or uncertainty aversion causes nonuse or improper use of the care-management risk model.

statement: Evaluate whether algorithm aversion causes nonuse or improper use of the care-management risk model.
quote: Some notable end-user tendencies that could alter model effectiveness and performance and should be evaluated include: • Ambiguity/uncertainty aversion can lead to lack of use or improper use. • Algorithm aversion can lead to lack of use or improper use.
hazard: Algorithm aversion prevents appropriate use of risk predictions.

statement: Evaluate whether staff accept care-management predictions or risk categories without further assessment because of automation bias.
quote: Automation bias (defaulting to using AI-generated predictions or risk categories without further evaluation) may lead to inappropriate or ineffective use.
hazard: Uncritical acceptance of risk categories leads to inappropriate care-management decisions.

statement: Categorize prior-authorization requests by complexity before selecting the authorization pathway.
quote: The triage engine categorizes the request according to complexity.
hazard: Complex authorization requests receive an inappropriate level of automation.

statement: Use rules-based decision-making for simple first-level prior-authorization requests.

statement: Have clinicians and payers review prior-authorization interpretations alongside AI outputs.

statement: Route very-high-complexity prior-authorization requests to providers for manual review, using AI only to organize the facts.

statement: Validate prior-authorization algorithms through objective public review.

statement: Certify prior-authorization algorithms against clinical cases juried by national clinical leaders.
quote: It validates the algorithm from an objective public review and certification against a panel of clinical cases juried by national clinical leaders.
hazard: Clinically inappropriate authorization decisions escape evaluation before deployment.

statement: Use the targeted NGS tumor-profiling assay for previously diagnosed cancer patients with solid malignant neoplasms.

statement: Limit professional use of tumor-profiling results to qualified healthcare professionals.

statement: Use tumor-profiling results in accordance with professional guidelines.

statement: Do not treat broad-panel tumor gene-alteration findings as conclusive or prescriptive for labeled use of a specific therapeutic product.

statement: Clearly explain the association between identified genetic variants and suggested treatment options in genomic reports.

statement: Make genomic-treatment reports understandable to both clinicians and patients.

statement: Explain to patients how genomic-data handling adheres to personal-data-protection legislation.
quote: Information about genomics-data ownership and adherence to personal-data-protection legislation need to be properly presented to patients, particularly as patients may receive care from different professionals and institutions along their treatment journey.

statement: Have a medical professional manually review genomic variant results for quality and accuracy.

statement: Add relevant companion-diagnostic information to approved genomic results before release.

statement: Merge companion-diagnostic annotations with patient demographics and additional testing-laboratory information before releasing genomic results.

statement: Have the laboratory director or designee review and sign off genomic-treatment reports for accuracy.

statement: Automatically upload genomic alterations to a portal supporting data mining and interpretation.

statement: Document the data entry mechanism, update criteria, update cadence, and designated approvers in the register for continuously learning or periodically retrained models.

statement: Create a distinct data register entry documenting access controls, retention periods, and BAA coverage for agentic systems that maintain persistent memory stores across sessions.

statement: Document all systems, databases, and external APIs an agentic AI is authorized to query at runtime within the data acquisition register.

statement: For AI models ingesting live runtime data, document how the model behaves or is handled when expected input fields are missing or anomalous.

statement: For continuously learning or periodically retrained models, document the cadence and criteria for model updates.

statement: For continuously learning or periodically retrained models, designate and document who is responsible for approving model updates.

statement: Where AI outputs feed back into retraining, calibration, or performance scoring, document the secondary data flow, its legal basis, and whether it generates new data types.

statement: For AI systems whose data scope shifts over time or at runtime, implement comprehensive logging of actual data access to complement the data register.

statement: Define a retention period for each agentic AI persistent memory store.

statement: Confirm BAA coverage for any agentic AI persistent memory store containing patient data.

statement: Block deployment of continuously adaptive or self-calibrating AI unless the vendor specifies whether calibration changes trigger risk recategorization.

hazard: Continued use of an AI tool that actively worsens health inequities.

statement: Conduct proactive outreach to provide appropriate workup and diagnosis for all high-risk patients to mitigate inequitable underdiagnosis.
quote: Prospective implementation of the AI solution with proactive outreach to conduct appropriate workup and diagnosis for all high- risk patients will be required to assess the impact on health equity.
hazard: AI predictions failing to benefit systematically underdiagnosed disadvantaged populations.

statement: Review medical-image header metadata for patient identifiers before sharing images.
quote: Medical images (e.g., DICOM files) need particular care: metadata embedded in image headers often contains patient identifiers beyond the 18 HIPAA Safe Harbor fields (such as institution name, acquisition date, equipment identifiers, and operator names) and must be reviewed and stripped before images are shared or used for AI training.
hazard: Disclosure of patient identifiers embedded in medical-image metadata.

statement: Strip identifying header metadata from medical images before sharing them.
quote: Medical images (e.g., DICOM files) need particular care: metadata embedded in image headers often contains patient identifiers beyond the 18 HIPAA Safe Harbor fields (such as institution name, acquisition date, equipment identifiers, and operator names) and must be reviewed and stripped before images are shared or used for AI training.
hazard: Patient re-identification through residual image-header identifiers.

statement: Treat potentially identifying pixel-level image data as re-identifiable patient data.
quote: Pixel-level data in certain image types, including full-face photographs and some dermatology, ophthalmology, or plastic surgery images, may directly reidentify patients and should be treated accordingly.
hazard: Patient re-identification from image pixels despite metadata removal.

statement: Evaluate ambient AI performance across language subgroups when serving primarily non-English-speaking patients.
quote: For example, a CHC that serves primarily non-English speakers, may want to look at how their Ambient AI solution performs by language subgroups, and may want to capture metadata associated with data language.
hazard: Unequal ambient AI performance for patients speaking different languages.

statement: Capture language metadata for ambient AI data.
quote: For example, a CHC that serves primarily non-English speakers, may want to look at how their Ambient AI solution performs by language subgroups, and may want to capture metadata associated with data language.
hazard: Inability to identify language-specific ambient AI performance gaps.

statement: Align traditional machine-learning data cleaning with the intended deployment data environment.
quote: Data cleaning should be done to ensure data integrity while maintaining alignment with the intended model deployment data environment.
hazard: Performance degradation when data-cleaning assumptions do not match production data.

statement: Document rules for reconciling conflicting predictive-model input values across EHR modules, facilities, and encounter types.
quote: How to resolve inconsistencies across data sources: document rules for reconciling conflicting values from different EHR modules, facilities, or encounter types.
hazard: Inconsistent model inputs and unreliable predictions across clinical data sources.

statement: Define when categorical predictive-model inputs use one-hot encoding, label encoding, or learned embeddings.
quote: Categorical variables: define when to use one-hot encoding vs. label encoding vs. learned embeddings.
hazard: Inconsistent categorical encoding that undermines model reliability and reproducibility.

statement: Document clinical-code mapping rules for predictive-model inputs.
quote: Clinical codes (ICD, CPT, SNOMED, RxNorm): document code mapping, aggregation, and normalization rules.
hazard: Incorrect clinical-code interpretation and inconsistent model inputs.

statement: Document clinical-code aggregation rules for predictive-model inputs.
quote: Clinical codes (ICD, CPT, SNOMED, RxNorm): document code mapping, aggregation, and normalization rules.
hazard: Inconsistent clinical-code aggregation that changes predictions.

statement: Document clinical-code normalization rules for predictive-model inputs.
quote: Clinical codes (ICD, CPT, SNOMED, RxNorm): document code mapping, aggregation, and normalization rules.
hazard: Inconsistent clinical-code normalization and unreliable model behavior.

statement: Define temporal-feature encoding rules, including handling dates for patients over age 89 under HIPAA Safe Harbor.
quote: Temporal features: define how dates, times, and time intervals are encoded, including handling of dates for patients over age 89 (HIPAA Safe Harbor requirement).
hazard: Temporal-input inconsistencies and disclosure of identifying date information.

statement: Document which continuous model inputs are normalized or standardized and the method used for each.
quote: Document which continuous variables are normalized or standardized and by what method (min-max scaling, z-score standardization, log transformation).
hazard: Unreproducible preprocessing and inconsistent model inputs.

statement: Calculate normalization parameters exclusively from training data.
quote: Critical rule: normalization parameters (min, max, mean, standard deviation) must be calculated only on training data and then applied to validation and test data.
hazard: Data leakage that inflates validation and test performance.

statement: Apply training-derived normalization parameters to validation and test data.
quote: Critical rule: normalization parameters (min, max, mean, standard deviation) must be calculated only on training data and then applied to validation and test data.
hazard: Misleading evaluation caused by inconsistent preprocessing across datasets.

statement: Use test data from a later period than training data to simulate deployment on future patients.
quote: Temporal separation: The test set should use data from a later time period than training, simulating the real-world deployment condition where the model will be applied to future patients.
hazard: Overestimated performance from evaluations that fail to represent future deployment conditions.

statement: Keep each patient's data out of either the training set or the test set to prevent overlap.
quote: Patient-level separation: The same patient’s data must not appear in both training and test sets.
hazard: Inflated performance from evaluating models on patients represented in training.

statement: Hold out data from one or more sites for external validation in multi-site organizations.
quote: Site-level separation: For multi-site organizations, consider holding out data from one or more sites for external validation.
hazard: Undetected performance failures when models are deployed at different sites.

statement: Document train, validation, and test split ratios and the rationale for the partitioning approach.
quote: Document split ratios (e.g., 70/15/15 train/validate/test) and the rationale for the chosen approach.
hazard: Unverifiable evaluation design and irreproducible performance estimates.

statement: Document which systems, APIs, and data sources each agentic AI system is authorized to query.
quote: Define and document which systems, APIs, and data sources an agentic AI system is authorized to query — this is the agentic equivalent of a training data inventory.
hazard: Unauthorized agent access to systems or sensitive data.

statement: Restrict agentic data access to systems relevant to the agent's authorized task.
quote: Establish least-privilege data access: agents should only be able to query systems relevant to the specific task they are authorized to perform.
hazard: Excessive agent permissions exposing unrelated systems and sensitive information.

statement: Require explicit justification for agentic cross-system data aggregation.
quote: Cross-system data aggregation should require explicit justification.
hazard: Unjustified combination of sensitive information across systems.

statement: Document how agentic tool-call outputs are validated before use in further reasoning.
quote: Document how tool-call outputs are validated before being used in further reasoning — unvalidated external outputs can introduce errors or adversarial content into the agent's reasoning chain.
hazard: Errors or adversarial content entering an agent's reasoning through external tool outputs.

statement: Specify logging requirements for all agentic tool calls and data queries, not only final outputs.
quote: Specify logging requirements for all tool calls and data queries made by agentic systems — not just final outputs.
hazard: Inability to audit agent actions or reconstruct incidents.

statement: Log human approvals and overrides of agentic actions for audit.
quote: Access to different data sources, human approvals/override (where relevant), should be logged for audit purposes.
hazard: Missing accountability for human authorization and intervention in agentic workflows.

statement: Apply formal access controls to persistent agent memory.
quote: Govern agentic memory: if the agent maintains persistent memory across sessions, that memory store must be brought under formal data governance (access controls, retention policies, BAA coverage).
hazard: Unauthorized access to sensitive information retained across agent sessions.

statement: Establish retention policies for persistent agent memory.
quote: Govern agentic memory: if the agent maintains persistent memory across sessions, that memory store must be brought under formal data governance (access controls, retention policies, BAA coverage).
hazard: Uncontrolled retention of sensitive information in persistent agent memory.

statement: Bring persistent agent memory under BAA coverage.
quote: Govern agentic memory: if the agent maintains persistent memory across sessions, that memory store must be brought under formal data governance (access controls, retention policies, BAA coverage).
hazard: Sensitive agent memory remaining outside contractual privacy protections.

statement: Tailor agentic human oversight to system risk and data sensitivity.
quote: Establish type of human oversight requirements and access controls: Human oversight may need to take risk of the system and sensitivity of the data in mind.
hazard: Insufficient oversight of high-risk agent behavior or sensitive-data access.

statement: Define which high-risk agentic actions or sensitive-data accesses require human review or confirmation before execution.
quote: For agentic AI systems operating on or with access sensitive data or that fall under higher-risk (e.g. access to patient data/PHI, payment data, or integrated into clinical workflows) define which types of actions/access require human review or confirmation before execution.
hazard: Unsafe autonomous actions or unauthorized sensitive-data access without human confirmation.

statement: Review agentic behavior meaningfully during initial deployment before reducing human oversight.
quote: Even where full automation is the operational goal, initial deployment phases should include meaningful review to validate that the system is behaving as expected before reducing oversight.
hazard: Premature automation before safe agent behavior has been demonstrated.

statement: Define conditions under which agentic systems should pause.
quote: Establish escalation and halt procedures: Define conditions under which an agentic system should pause, escalate to a human reviewer, or decline to take action.
hazard: Continued autonomous operation under unsafe or unexpected conditions.

statement: Define conditions under which agentic systems should escalate to a human reviewer.
quote: Establish escalation and halt procedures: Define conditions under which an agentic system should pause, escalate to a human reviewer, or decline to take action.
hazard: High-risk or unexpected situations proceeding without human judgment.

statement: Define conditions under which agentic systems should decline to act.
quote: Establish escalation and halt procedures: Define conditions under which an agentic system should pause, escalate to a human reviewer, or decline to take action.
hazard: Execution of unsafe actions with potentially irreversible consequences.

statement: Clearly document the escalation path for agentic systems.
quote: Document the escalation path clearly, and ensure that frontline users and operators know how to initiate escalation or halt the system.
hazard: Delayed intervention because escalation responsibilities or routes are unclear.

statement: Ensure frontline users and operators know how to initiate escalation for agentic systems.
quote: Document the escalation path clearly, and ensure that frontline users and operators know how to initiate escalation or halt the system.
hazard: Delayed human review because staff cannot initiate escalation.

statement: Ensure frontline users and operators know how to halt agentic systems.
quote: Document the escalation path clearly, and ensure that frontline users and operators know how to initiate escalation or halt the system.
hazard: Unsafe agent actions continuing because staff cannot stop the system.

statement: Have clinical staff review predictive-model rules for handling missing laboratory values.
quote: For example, rules for handling missing lab values, encoding diagnosis codes, or selecting date windows should be reviewed with clinical staff to ensure they reflect clinical reality.
hazard: Clinically inappropriate handling of missing laboratory data producing unreliable predictions.

statement: Have clinical staff review predictive-model diagnosis-code encoding rules.
quote: For example, rules for handling missing lab values, encoding diagnosis codes, or selecting date windows should be reviewed with clinical staff to ensure they reflect clinical reality.
hazard: Diagnosis-code encoding that misrepresents clinical meaning.

statement: Have clinical staff review predictive-model date-window selection rules.
quote: For example, rules for handling missing lab values, encoding diagnosis codes, or selecting date windows should be reviewed with clinical staff to ensure they reflect clinical reality.
hazard: Clinically inappropriate date windows excluding relevant information or incorporating misleading data.

statement: Have clinical staff review preparation of data whose clinical meaning depends on time-series or trends rather than single time points.
quote: For example, rules for handling missing lab values, encoding diagnosis codes, or selecting date windows should be reviewed with clinical staff to ensure they reflect clinical reality. This is also true of data that is clinically meaningful as a time-series or trend versus a single time-point.
hazard: Loss of clinically meaningful temporal patterns during data preparation.

statement: Document applicable FDA reporting requirements for AI systems classified as Software as a Medical Device.
quote: Are external regulatory reporting requirements identified and documented (e.g., FDA for AI systems classified as Software as a Medical Device)?
hazard: Missed mandatory device incident reports and regulatory noncompliance.

statement: Scope predictive risk-score training to the staff who act on the scores.
quote: Rather than rolling out broad "AI literacy" curricula, training was scoped tightly to the case managers and hospitalists who actually acted on the risk score, and was reinforced in existing multidisciplinary rounds.
hazard: Staff acting on risk scores without relevant operational training.

statement: Reinforce predictive risk-score training during existing multidisciplinary rounds.
quote: Rather than rolling out broad "AI literacy" curricula, training was scoped tightly to the case managers and hospitalists who actually acted on the risk score, and was reinforced in existing multidisciplinary rounds.
hazard: Inconsistent application of risk-score training in clinical workflows.

statement: Pilot predictive models in silent mode against live EHR data before surfacing alerts to clinicians.
quote: Models were piloted in silent mode against live EHR data before alerts were surfaced to clinicians, satisfying the playbook's pre-deployment testing expectation without a dedicated sandbox.
hazard: Unvalidated predictions influencing clinical decisions through live alerts.

statement: Capture staff feedback within the rounding and case-management workflows where predictive risk scores appear.
quote: Staff feedback was captured in the same rounding and case-management workflow where the score appeared, and concerns were triaged by Parkland Center for Clinical Innovation (PCCI) engineers back into retraining cycles.
hazard: Risk-score problems remaining undetected because feedback channels are disconnected from clinical use.

statement: Have engineers triage staff concerns about deployed risk scores into model retraining cycles.
quote: Staff feedback was captured in the same rounding and case-management workflow where the score appeared, and concerns were triaged by Parkland Center for Clinical Innovation (PCCI) engineers back into retraining cycles.
hazard: Persistent predictive-model problems despite staff reports.

statement: Train emergency department nurses on the specific triage pathway for predictive sepsis alerts.
quote: Training was role-differentiated: ED nurses were trained on the specific alert triage pathway, physicians received use-case-specific guidance on how COMPOSER differed from the prior rules-based screen, and the model was accompanied by plain-language documentation describing its inputs and known limitations.
hazard: Delayed or incorrect responses to predictive sepsis alerts.

statement: Give physicians use-case-specific guidance explaining how a predictive sepsis model differs from the previous rules-based screen.
quote: Training was role-differentiated: ED nurses were trained on the specific alert triage pathway, physicians received use-case-specific guidance on how COMPOSER differed from the prior rules-based screen, and the model was accompanied by plain-language documentation describing its inputs and known limitations.
hazard: Misinterpreting predictive alerts using assumptions from a previous rules-based screen.

statement: Provide clinicians with plain-language documentation of the predictive sepsis model's inputs.
quote: Training was role-differentiated: ED nurses were trained on the specific alert triage pathway, physicians received use-case-specific guidance on how COMPOSER differed from the prior rules-based screen, and the model was accompanied by plain-language documentation describing its inputs and known limitations.
hazard: Clinical use without understanding the information underlying sepsis predictions.

statement: Provide clinicians with plain-language documentation of the predictive sepsis model's known limitations.
quote: Training was role-differentiated: ED nurses were trained on the specific alert triage pathway, physicians received use-case-specific guidance on how COMPOSER differed from the prior rules-based screen, and the model was accompanied by plain-language documentation describing its inputs and known limitations.
hazard: Overreliance on sepsis predictions outside the model's known capabilities.

statement: Use a phased go-live when activating predictive sepsis alerts.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Widespread exposure to alerting problems during an uncontrolled rollout.

statement: Log whether clinicians act on, defer, or override predictive sepsis alerts.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Unrecognized patterns of alert deferral or override.

statement: Have the development team review logged dispositions of predictive sepsis alerts.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Alert-use problems remaining unaddressed despite recorded clinician responses.

statement: Recalibrate predictive sepsis alert thresholds using development-team review of logged alert dispositions.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Inappropriate alert thresholds persisting despite evidence from clinical use.

statement: Retrain staff when review of predictive sepsis alert dispositions identifies a need.
quote: The research and operational teams ran COMPOSER in silent mode before activation, used a phased go-live, and established a structured clinician feedback loop in which alert disposition (acted on, deferred, or overridden) was logged and reviewed by the development team to recalibrate thresholds and retrain staff where needed.
hazard: Persistent gaps in staff interpretation or handling of predictive sepsis alerts.

statement: Prospectively evaluate the health-equity impact of predictive models targeting conditions underdiagnosed in disadvantaged subgroups.
quote: Prospective implementation of the AI solution with proactive outreach to conduct appropriate workup and diagnosis for all high- risk patients will be required to assess the impact on health equity.
hazard: Misleading equity assessments caused by undiagnosed positive cases in historical data.

statement: Conduct proactive outreach for appropriate workup and diagnosis of all high-risk patients when deploying models targeting inequitably underdiagnosed conditions.
quote: Prospective implementation of the AI solution with proactive outreach to conduct appropriate workup and diagnosis for all high- risk patients will be required to assess the impact on health equity.
hazard: Persistent underdiagnosis and unequal access to diagnostic workup among high-risk patients.

statement: For models targeting inequitably overdiagnosed conditions, set an equity objective of reducing event rates in both disadvantaged and advantaged subgroups.
quote: However, systemic racism may be entangled in the diagnosis process and the equity objective can be to reduce event rates across both disadvantaged and advantaged subgroups.
hazard: Perpetuation of inequitable overdiagnosis and associated harmful interventions.

statement: During prospective deployment of models targeting inequitably overdiagnosed conditions, proactively provide medical support to all high-risk patients.
quote: Prospective implementation of the AI solution with proactive outreach to provide medical and social support for all high-risk patients can improve health equity.
hazard: Unmet medical needs and persistent inequities among high-risk patients.

statement: During prospective deployment of models targeting inequitably overdiagnosed conditions, proactively provide social support to all high-risk patients.
quote: Prospective implementation of the AI solution with proactive outreach to provide medical and social support for all high-risk patients can improve health equity.
hazard: Unmet social needs and persistent inequities among high-risk patients.

statement: Require prospective implementation with proactive outreach for diagnosis of high-risk patients to assess equity impacts when facing inequitable underdiagnosis.
quote: Prospective implementation of the AI solution with proactive outreach to conduct appropriate workup and diagnosis for all high- risk patients will be required to assess the impact on health equity.
hazard: Inaccurately estimating model performance on historical data due to underdiagnosis.

statement: Prospectively implement AI solutions with proactive outreach to provide support for all high-risk patients to mitigate inequitable overdiagnosis.
quote: Prospective implementation of the AI solution with proactive outreach to provide medical and social support for all high-risk patients can improve health equity.
hazard: Exacerbating inequities through overdiagnosis linked to systemic racism.

statement: Ensure payor automated decision-making systems for coverage and claims do not override physicians' clinical judgment.
quote: Steps should be taken to ensure that these systems do not override clinical judgment.
hazard: Automated algorithmic denials overriding clinical judgment and withholding needed care

statement: Inform patients and physicians when payor automated decision-making is used and provide a means for them to question its determinations.
quote: Patients and physicians should be informed and empowered to question a payor’s automated decision-making.
hazard: Opaque, unchallengeable automated coverage denials limiting patient access to care

statement: Limit AI-enabled automated decision-making to lower-risk, less complex care decisions governed by clear guidelines.
quote: With clear guidelines, AI-enabled decision-making systems may also be appropriate for use in some lower-risk, less complex care decisions.
hazard: Automated systems making complex, high-risk care decisions without individualized review

statement: Deploy payor automated decision-making systems only for purposes that improve coverage and payment efficiency, simplify administration, and reduce workflow burden.
quote: Payors should leverage automated decision-making systems that improve or enhance efficiencies in coverage and payment automation, facilitate administrative simplification, and reduce workflow burdens.
hazard: Automated systems used to deny care rather than reduce administrative burden

statement: Require AI incident reports to reference the active model version and data vintage to enable traceability of drift and updates.
quote: AI incident reports should reference the model version and data vintage active at the time of the incident to enable traceability.
hazard: Inability to trace incidents to specific model versions or data drift.

statement: Trigger re-certification or refresher training for staff whenever an AI system undergoes material updates.
quote: Whenever a system undergoes material updates, a re-certification or refresher training should be triggered to ensure continued competency.
hazard: Staff making errors by using outdated workflows on materially updated AI models.

statement: Ensure vendor contracts explicitly obligate proactive incident notification, performance reporting, and communication of model changes.
quote: Organizations should ensure vendor contracts include explicit obligations for proactive incident notification, performance reporting, and communication of model changes.
hazard: Vendors silently updating models or failing to notify the healthcare organization of performance issues.

statement: Reserve formal consent for AI uses that materially change standard of care, introduce clinical risk, or collect new patient data categories.
quote: Formal consent should be reserved for AI uses that materially change the standard of care, introduce discrete clinical risk, or require collection of a new category of patient data.
hazard: Collecting sensitive patient data like ambient voice recordings without explicit informed consent.

statement: Train staff in non-patient simulation environments to assess performance, surface limitations, and safely interact with the AI before live patient care.
quote: When able, training staff in non-patient environments (e.g., sandbox systems, test EHR instances, or simulation settings) allows organizations to assess system performance, surface known limitations and failure modes, and train end users on how to interact with the solution before patient safety is at stake.
hazard: Staff encountering dangerous AI failure modes for the first time during live patient care.

statement: Interpose a remote review team between predictive AI algorithms and frontline clinicians to evaluate alerts and mitigate clinician alert fatigue.

hazard: Frontline clinician alert fatigue causing them to ignore critical predictive risk warnings.

statement: Institute a mandatory shadowing period showing alerts to clinicians for workflow practice in a simulation environment before full AI go-live.
quote: Important to note, KPNC instituted a mandatory two-week shadowing period before each hospital's go-live, during which alerts were shown to selected clinicians for workflow practice runs (functioning as a simulation environment where staff could rehearse the system before patient safety was at stake).
hazard: Poor clinical integration of predictive risk alerts disrupting workflows and patient care.

statement: Escalate AI data drift or bias incidents through data governance channels with data stewards engaged in root cause analysis.
quote: Data incidents should trigger escalation through the HDO’s data governance channel alongside the AI Governance Committee, with data stewards engaged in root cause analysis.
hazard: Failing to adequately investigate and remediate data drift or population shift errors.

statement: Require EHR developers supplying predictive decision support interventions to disclose specified source attributes of those tools to users.
quote: Starting in 2025, EHR developers that supply Predictive DSIs as part of the developer’s EHR offering must disclose specific attributes and inform users if patient demographic, social determinants of health, or health assessment data are used in the Predictive DSI.
hazard: Clinicians misunderstanding how predictive tools work, their bias potential, and limitations

statement: Require EHR vendors to inform users whether demographic, social determinants of health, or health assessment data are inputs to a predictive decision support tool.
quote: Starting in 2025, EHR developers that supply Predictive DSIs as part of the developer’s EHR offering must disclose specific attributes and inform users if patient demographic, social determinants of health, or health assessment data are used in the Predictive DSI.
hazard: Undisclosed use of demographic or social data introducing bias into predictions

statement: Apply risk management practices covering design, development, training, and evaluation to predictive decision support tools in the EHR.
quote: EHRs will be subject to regulatory requirements regarding the design, development, training, and evaluation of Predictive DSIs along with mandated risk management practices.
hazard: Poorly designed or evaluated predictive tools harming patients

statement: Make reasonable efforts to identify discrimination by clinical algorithms, such as race-adjusted algorithms, before and during use.
quote: The final rule prohibits discrimination by clinical algorithms and requires physicians, hospitals, health systems, and others to use “reasonable efforts” to both identify algorithmic discrimination and to mitigate resulting harms.
hazard: Discriminatory harms from biased or race-adjusted clinical algorithms

statement: Mitigate harms resulting from identified discrimination by clinical algorithms.
quote: The final rule prohibits discrimination by clinical algorithms and requires physicians, hospitals, health systems, and others to use “reasonable efforts” to both identify algorithmic discrimination and to mitigate resulting harms.
hazard: Ongoing patient harm from discriminatory algorithm outputs

statement: Require developers of autonomous clinical AI for screening, diagnosis, or treatment to maintain appropriate medical liability insurance.
quote: Specifically, developers of autonomous AI systems with clinical applications (screening, diagnosis, treatment) are in the best position to manage issues of liability arising directly from system failure or misdiagnosis and must accept this liability with measures such as maintaining appropriate medical liability insurance and in their agreements with users.
hazard: Uncompensated harm and misplaced liability from autonomous system failure or misdiagnosis

statement: Include developer acceptance of liability for system failure or misdiagnosis in contracts for autonomous clinical AI systems.
quote: Specifically, developers of autonomous AI systems with clinical applications (screening, diagnosis, treatment) are in the best position to manage issues of liability arising directly from system failure or misdiagnosis and must accept this liability with measures such as maintaining appropriate medical liability insurance and in their agreements with users.
hazard: Clinicians bearing liability for autonomous AI failures outside their control

statement: Base AI-assisted claims and prior authorization review on accurate, up-to-date clinical criteria from specialty society guidelines and peer-reviewed literature.
quote: (1) is based on accurate and up-to-date clinical criteria derived from national medical specialty society guidelines and peer reviewed clinical literature;
hazard: Inappropriate care denials from automated tools using outdated or invalid criteria

statement: Have AI-assisted claim denials reviewed by clinicians with relevant expertise who are not incentivized to deny care.
quote: (2) includes reviews by doctors and other health care professionals who are not incentivized to deny care and with expertise for the service under review; and
hazard: Faulty automated denials of care to patients

statement: Require human examination of patient records before any AI-assisted care or prior authorization denial.
quote: (3) requires such reviews include human examination of patient records prior to a care denial.
hazard: Wrongful denials issued with seconds of review by automated decision tools

statement: Require physicians to review and approve ambient AI-generated clinical notes before they are finalized in the record.
quote: Physicians must review and approve AI-generated notes, ensuring clinical accuracy and accountability.
hazard: Inaccurate or incomplete ambient-drafted notes entering the medical record

statement: Require human review to validate and interpret AI-generated patient risk predictions before acting on them.
quote: Human oversight is essential to validate and interpret AI-generated predictions, maintain objective and balanced data collection, ensure data privacy, and take appropriate action based on insights.
hazard: Acting on incorrect or misinterpreted risk predictions

statement: Assign human oversight to keep data collection for predictive risk models objective and balanced.
quote: Human oversight is essential to validate and interpret AI-generated predictions, maintain objective and balanced data collection, ensure data privacy, and take appropriate action based on insights.
hazard: Biased or unbalanced input data skewing risk predictions

statement: Monitor predictive model outputs for inaccuracies arising from poor data quality that could produce flawed patient risk assessments.
quote: Remember: AI predictions rely on data quality. It’s important to carefully monitor for inaccuracies that could lead to flawed or incorrect assessments.
hazard: Flawed or incorrect risk assessments from data quality problems

statement: Validate AI-generated personalized care intervention recommendations with clinician judgment before applying them.
quote: Validate AI recommendations with human judgment; regularly monitor for errors and unintended outcomes.
hazard: Inappropriate tailored interventions from erroneous AI recommendations

statement: Regularly monitor AI care-recommendation tools for errors and unintended outcomes.
quote: Validate AI recommendations with human judgment; regularly monitor for errors and unintended outcomes.

statement: Conduct subgroup performance audits of population health AI models to ensure balanced performance across patient groups.

hazard: Models trained on nonrepresentative data worsening access and outcome gaps

statement: Integrate data from multiple sources when building or deploying population health AI models to reduce nonrepresentative-data bias.
quote: To mitigate these risks, strategies like integrating data from multiple sources and conducting subgroup performance audits are recommended to ensure balanced model performance.
hazard: Nonrepresentative data reinforcing existing health gaps

statement: Ensure AI tools are validated for performance within your specific practice setting before engaging with them.
quote: physicians will need to be diligent in ensuring that they engage with AI tools where performance has been validated in their practice setting.
hazard: Poor model performance in untested clinical environments.

statement: Select AI tools that have evidence of clinical validation and use them only within their intended population and use case.
quote: Negligent selection of an AI tool, including using tools outside their intended use or intended population, or choosing a tool where there is no evidence of clinical validation, could be decisions that expose a physician to a liability claim.
hazard: Patient harm from unvalidated AI or off-label use.

statement: Require purchasers to consider vendor-provided information regarding reported performance, intended use, intended population, and task appropriateness when selecting AI tools.
quote: Developers and vendors should provide this information about their products, and physicians and other purchasers should consider this information when selecting the AI tools they use.

statement: Require specified, qualified human intervention points capable of overriding AI output during clinical decision-making processes.
quote: Clinical decisions influenced by AI must be made with specified qualified human intervention points during the decision-making process.

statement: Do not deploy AI systems that introduce overall or disparate risk beyond the organization's capability to mitigate.

statement: Design and deploy AI in harmony with clinical workflows to avoid exacerbating clinician burden.

hazard: Increased clinician burnout from poor AI workflow integration.

statement: Disclose and document the use of AI to physicians and patients in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner when it impacts medical decision-making.

statement: Provide patients or caregivers the opportunity to request additional review from a licensed clinician when AI impacts their care.

statement: Document the use of AI in the medical record when it directly impacts patient care, medical decision making, or access to care.

statement: Ensure automated decision-making systems used by payors do not override clinical judgment.
quote: Steps should be taken to ensure that these systems do not override clinical judgment.
hazard: Denied patient care due to automated overrides of clinician decisions.

statement: Inform and empower patients and physicians to question a payor's automated decision-making regarding claims and coverage.
quote: Patients and physicians should be informed and empowered to question a payor’s automated decision-making.
hazard: Unchallenged algorithmic denials of insurance coverage.

statement: Clearly inform patients when they are interacting with an AI tool as their main point of contact in health care.
quote: when AI is the main point of contact in health care, it is ACR’s position that patients should be clearly informed that they are interacting with an AI tool.
hazard: Deceptive interactions where patients believe they speak to humans.

statement: Keep the collection of data to a minimum to mitigate risks associated with data breaches and misuse.
quote: Moreover, the collection of data should be kept to a minimum.

statement: Implement a robust data management system that empowers patients by providing clear ways to grant, deny, or revoke consent.

hazard: Unauthorized use of patient data without consent

statement: Use reasonable efforts to identify algorithmic discrimination and to mitigate resulting harms from clinical algorithms.

hazard: Discriminatory harms caused by biased algorithms

statement: Require developers of autonomous AI systems with clinical applications to accept liability with measures such as maintaining appropriate medical liability insurance.
quote: Specifically, developers of autonomous AI systems with clinical applications (screening, diagnosis, treatment) are in the best position to manage issues of liability arising directly from system failure or misdiagnosis and must accept this liability with measures such as maintaining appropriate medical liability insurance and in their agreements with users.
hazard: Unassigned liability from system failure or misdiagnosis

statement: Require human examination of patient records prior to a care denial when using AI for reviewing patient claims and prior authorization requests.
quote: requires such reviews include human examination of patient records prior to a care denial.
hazard: Inappropriate denials of care or limitations on coverage

statement: Implement appropriate and sufficient policies to ensure users act in accordance with the current standard of care when utilizing AI technologies.
quote: purchasers and users of these technologies should have appropriate and sufficient policies in place to ensure they are acting in accordance with the current standard of care.
hazard: Operating AI tools below the accepted standard of clinical care

statement: Disclose and document the use of AI when it is utilized in health care decision-making at the point of care.
quote: When AI is utilized in health care decision-making at the point of care, that use should be disclosed and documented
hazard: Hidden decision-making points and unaccountable points of error

statement: Define the specific goals an ambient scribe deployment is meant to achieve before adoption, so later judgments of whether it is working reference those goals.

statement: Require clinicians to review ambient scribe-generated notes before they are finalized in the record.

hazard: Omissions or errors in ambient scribe summaries entering the medical record

statement: Establish organizational policies and governance for ambient scribe use covering summary errors, omissions, and data privacy and security risks.

statement: Work with the ambient scribe developer to customize note structure and templates to clinicians' needs during deployment.

statement: Disclose to impacted parties any algorithmic system used to make claims determinations or set coverage limitations affecting patient access to care.

statement: Publicly report use of automated decision-making systems that determine coverage limits, claim determinations, or benefit design.

statement: Base automated coverage decision systems on easily accessible evidence-based clinical guidelines rather than proprietary payor criteria.

hazard: Inappropriate denials based on non-evidence-based proprietary criteria

statement: Disclose use of automated coverage decision systems to both patients and their physicians in easy-to-understand language.

hazard: Patients and physicians unaware of or unable to understand automated coverage decisions

statement: Ensure automated coverage decisions do not replace individualized assessment and allow reviewers flexibility to override automated decisions.

hazard: Rigid algorithmic denials ignoring individual patient medical and social circumstances

statement: Make coverage determinations based on the particular patient's care needs, not on algorithms developed on similar or like patients.
quote: Payors should always make determinations based on particular patient care needs and not base decisions on algorithms developed on “similar” or “like” patients.

statement: Disclose algorithm training and reference data sources and demographic attributes (e.g., age, race, gender) of individuals in the training data.
quote: P ayors using automated decision-making systems should disclose information about any algorithm training and reference data, including where data were sourced and attributes about individuals contained within the training data set (e.g., age, race, gender).
hazard: Unrepresentative training data producing biased automated decisions

statement: Provide clear evidence that automated decision-making systems do not discriminate or increase inequities, and that bias mitigation protections are in place.
quote: Payors should provide clear evidence that their systems do not discriminate, increase inequities, and that protections are in place to mitigate bias.
hazard: Discriminatory automated decisions widening health inequities

statement: Identify and cite peer-reviewed studies assessing the automated system's accuracy against patient outcomes and the validity of its predictions.
quote: P ayors using automated decision-making systems should identify and cite peer-reviewed studies assessing the system’s accuracy measured against the outcomes of patients and the validity of the system’s predictions.
hazard: Use of unvalidated predictive systems making inaccurate coverage determinations

statement: Automatically refer any automated recommendation to limit or deny care, at initial review and appeal, to a physician licensed in the relevant state before final determination.

hazard: Care denials issued by algorithm without physician review

statement: Ensure the physician reviewing automated denial recommendations is of the same specialty as the physician who typically manages the condition or provides the service.

statement: Conduct regular audits of automated decision-making systems to verify they are not increasing overall or disparate denials, coverage limitations, or access barriers.

hazard: Automated systems progressively increasing denials or disparate access barriers undetected

statement: Publish automated system approval, denial, and appeal rates with patient demographics on a publicly accessible website to contextualize equity impacts.

hazard: Unnoticed exacerbation of access barriers or disparate denial rates over time due to automated systems.

statement: Publish statistics regarding automated systems' approval, denial, and appeal rates alongside patient demographics to contextualize equity implications.

statement: Regularly monitor health care AI for anomalies or performance deviations by comparing outputs against known and normal behavior.

statement: Deeply understand existing workflows before replacing, reorganizing, or augmenting them with AI-based solutions.

statement: Establish common data pipelines and interoperable enterprise systems to support the integration of AI-enabled tools.

statement: Obtain patient consent before using mobile applications to capture conversations for ambient scribing.

statement: Customize ambient scribe note structures and templates to ensure they support specific clinician needs.

statement: Use standardized metrics to evaluate the impact of AI solutions on clinicians, patients, and financial outcomes.
